*rin po che’i mchog*, Skt. *rin po che’i mchog*, Birthplace of the buddha Gaṇimuktirāja.

## best of men
*mi mchog*, Skt. *puruṣottama*, An epithet of the Buddha.

## Best of Mountains
*ri rab*, Skt. *ri rab*, Attendant of the buddha Ketuprabha.

## Best of those who walk on two feet
A common epithet of the Buddha.

## Bestower of Nourishment
*zas sbyin ma*, Skt. *annadāyinī*, One of the twelve names or epithets of Mahāśrī in The Sūtra of Mahāśrī (Toh 740/1005) and The Twelve Names of the Great Goddess Śrī.

## betel
Areca catechu.

## bewildering rite
A particular class of tantric ritual.

## bewilderment
*’khrul pa*, Skt. *bhrānti*, Bewilderment is the confusion arising from the subject-object dichotomy and fundamental ignorance, on the basis of which rebirth in cyclic existence is perpetuated.

## Beyond Abiding
*gnas pa las ’das pa*, Skt. *gnas pa las ’das pa*, Father of the buddha Padmahastin.

## Beyond All Sorrow and Harm
*mya ngan dang gnod pa thams cad las ’das pa*, Skt. *mya ngan dang gnod pa thams cad las ’das pa*, Name of the world system of the thus-gone one Branch Guru. Alternative name for the world system Liberation from All Sorrow and Harm.

## Beyond All Suffering and Harm
*mya ngan dang gnod pa thams cad las rgal ba*, Skt. *mya ngan dang gnod pa thams cad las rgal ba*, A buddha realm.

## Beyond All Utterances, Speech, and Sounds
*sgrar rjod pa dang dbyangs dang nga ro thams cad las ’das pa*, Skt. *sgrar rjod pa dang dbyangs dang nga ro thams cad las ’das pa*, The name of a bodhisattva in the Buddha’s audience.

## Beyond All Worlds
*’gro ba thams cad las ’das*, Skt. *’gro ba thams cad las ’das*, A buddha.

## Beyond Doubt
*yid gnyis las ’das pa*, Skt. *yid gnyis las ’das pa*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Ratnābhacandra (731 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## beyond duality
*gnyis su med pa*, Skt. *advaya*, Also rendered here as “without duality,” “nonduality,” “nondual.”

## Beyond Incense
*spos ’das*, Skt. *spos ’das*, A buddha realm.

## Beyond Mind
*yid bral*, Skt. *yid bral*, A buddha realm.

## beyond sequence
*snrel zhi*, Skt. *vyatyasta*, A meditative stability. See also .

## beyond signs
*mtshan ma med pa*, Skt. *animitta*, See “signlessness.”

## Beyond Stain
*dri ’das*, Skt. *dri ’das*, A buddha realm.

## beyond suffering
*mya ngan ’da’*, See “pass into nirvāṇa.”

## Beyond the Mind
*blo ’das*, Skt. *blo ’das*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Smṛtīndra.

## Beyond the Senses
A bodhisattva in the Buddha’s retinue.

## Beyond the World
*’jig rten ’das*, Skt. *’jig rten ’das*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Pūritāṅga.

## beyond wishes
*smon pa med pa*, Skt. *apraṇihita*, See “wishlessness.”

## bezoar
*gi wang*, Skt. *sarocanā*, As this is distinguished from gorocanā (“cow bezoar”), this may be bezoar obtained from the head of an elephant, in distinction from that obtained from a cow. Used in Āyurveda for both external and oral application in treating worm infestation, pruritus (itching), psychiatric disorders, low digestion strength, and more.

## Bhaṭṭā
*rje btsun ma*, Skt. *bhaṭṭā*, A yakṣiṇī invoked in magical rites.

## Bhūṣaṇī
*rgyan can ma*, Skt. *bhūṣaṇī*, The name of an apsaras.

## Ābha
*snang ba*, Skt. *ābha*, Fifth of the sixteen god realms of form that correspond to the four meditative concentrations, meaning “Radiance.”

## Bhaṭa
*dpa’ bo*, Skt. *bhaṭa*, One of the two brothers in Mathurā who are predicted by the Buddha to build a monastery in the future.

## Bhīṣaṇa
*’jigs mdzad*, Skt. *bhīṣaṇa*, The 627th buddha in the first list, 626th in the second list, and 619th in the third list.

## Bhīṣaṇaka
*’jigs ’jigs*, Skt. *bhīṣaṇaka*, One of the five yakṣa generals.

## Bhaṭakunire
The name of a city.

## Bhaṇḍanā
*b+hAN+Da nA*, Skt. *bhaṇḍanā*, A mountain off Videha.

## Bhaṇḍapurī
The name of a city.

## bhadanta
*btsun pa*, Skt. *bhadanta*, “Venerable One.” A term of respect used for Buddhist monks.

## Bhaddāli
Skt. *bhaddāli*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhaddālin
*legs ldan*, Skt. *bhaddālin*, A monk.

## Bṛhaddruma
*sdong chen*, Skt. *bṛhaddruma*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Bṛhaddyuti
*yangs pa’i ’od*, Skt. *bṛhaddyuti*, A potter who was the Buddha in a former life.

## Bhadrā
*bzang po*, Skt. *bhadrā*, Lit. “Good.” Name of four lotus ponds, each located in one of the four gardens of the residence of the bodhisattva great being Dharmodgata, in the city of Gandhavatī.

## Bhadra
Known as “Bhadra the illusionist,” he was a powerful magician of Rājagṛha whose attempts to fool the Buddha go awry in The Prophecy for Bhadra the Illusionist.

## Bhadraśaila
*brag bzang*, Skt. *bhadraśaila*, A mountain king.

## Bhadrabala
*bzang po’i stobs*, Skt. *bhadrabala*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Bhadradatta
*bzang byin*, Skt. *bhadradatta*, The 326th buddha in the first list, 325th in the second list, and 320th in the third list.

## Bhadradeva
*lha bzang*, Skt. *bhadradeva*, A householder in the Buddha Dīpaṅkara’s time.

## Bhadraka
*bzang po*, Skt. *bhadraka*, Our present eon in which over a thousand buddhas will appear. The meaning is “good” because of the number of buddhas that will appear. In this sūtra it is usually called bhadraka.

## Bhadrakalpika
*skal bzang yod*, Skt. *bhadrakalpika*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhadrakanyā
*bu mo bzang mo*, Skt. *bhadrakanyā*, A woman who was Mahā­maudgalyāyana’s mother in her previous life and was reborn in Marīcika World. See also .

## Bhadrakarṇa
*rna ba bzang*, Skt. *bhadrakarṇa*, A yakṣa general.

## Bhadraṃkara
*bzang byed*, Skt. *bhadraṃkara*, A city.

## Bhadrakālī
*nag mo bzang mo*, Skt. *bhadrakālī*, One of the goddesses invited to partake in the oblation offering.

## Bhadrakānta
*bzang sdug*, Skt. *bhadrakānta*, A nāga king.

## Bhadrakāra
The inhabitants of the city of Bhadrakāra, also known as Śākala, which was the capital city of the Madra kingdom and which has been identified as present-day Sialkot in northern Punjab.

## Bhadramati
*bzang po’i blo gros*, Skt. *bhadramati*, The queen of a cakravartin in the distant past, a previous life of the night goddess Pramudita­nayana­jagad­virocanā.

## Bhadrapadā
Skt. *bhadrapadā*, The name of a pair of nakṣatras.

## Bhadrapada
The name of a lunar mansion and a lunar month.

## bhadrapatralatā
An unidentified plant ingredient used in ritual and alchemical preparations.

## Bhadrapāṇi
Skt. *bhadrapāṇi*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhadrapāla
*bzang skyong*, Skt. *bhadrapāla*, One of “the sixteen excellent men.” A bodhisattva who appears prominently in certain sūtras, such as The Samādhi of the Presence of the Buddhas, and perhaps also the merchant of that name who is the principal interlocutor in The Questions of Bhadrapāla the Merchant (tshong dpon bzang skyong gyis zhus pa zhes bya ba theg pa chen po’i mdo, toh 83).

## Bhadra­pāla
*bzang skyong*, Skt. *bhadra­pāla*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Bhadrapura
*grong khyer bzung*, Skt. *bhadrapura*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Bhadraśrī
*dpal bzang po*, Skt. *bhadraśrī*, Bhadraśrī (Excellent Glory) is a buddha who inhabits the buddhafield Padmaśrī.

## Bhadra­śrī (the buddha)
*bzang po’i dpal*, Skt. *bhadra­śrī*, A buddha in a world realm in the eastern direction.

## Bhadra­śrī (the upāsaka)
*bzang po’i dpal*, Skt. *bhadra­śrī*, An upāsaka in Dhanyākara.

## Bhadra­śrī (the upāsikā)
*dge ba’i dpal*, Skt. *bhadra­śrī*, An upāsikā in Dhanyākara.

## Bhadrarāja
A god whose name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Bhadra­śrī­meru­tejas
*dpal gyi ri bo gzi brjid bzang po*, Skt. *bhadra­śrī­meru­tejas*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Bhadrasena
*sde bzang po*, Skt. *bhadrasena*, One of the generals of Māra.

## Bhadraśrī
*bzang po’i dpal*, Skt. *bhadraśrī*, “Glorious Goodness,” the bodhisattva who resides at a place called Jyotiṣprabha.

## Bṛhadratha
*shing rta che*, Skt. *bṛhadratha*, A yakṣa general.

## Bhadravairocana
*rnam par snang byed bzang po*, Skt. *bhadra­vairocana*, A bodhisattva who comes from the realm of the Buddha Jitendriya­viśāla­netra to the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

## Bhadravaktra
*zhal bzangs*, Skt. *bhadravaktra*, A buddha who is not listed in the first or second list but is 862nd in the third list.

## Bhadrikā
*bzang po can*, Skt. *bhadrikā*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Bhadrika
*bzang ldan*, Skt. *bhadrika*, One of the five excellent companions, with whom Siddhārtha Gautama practiced asceticism near the Nairañjanā River and who later heard the [Buddha](#buddha) first teach the Four Noble Truths at the Deer [Park](#park) in Sarnath.

## Bhadrikarāja
*bzang ldan rgyal po*, Skt. *bhadrikarāja*, Supreme among the upper-class monks. He became an arhat in the first rainy season. One of the first group of Śākya princes to become a monk. He is said to have been a king in many successive previous lifetimes, which is why the title of “king” is added after his name in the sūtra. He is not to be confused with the Bhadrika who was one of the Buddha’s first five pupils.

## Bhadrottamā
*bzang mchog*, Skt. *bhadrottamā*, Lit. “Best.” Name of four lotus ponds, each located in one of the four gardens of the residence of the bodhisattva great being Dharmodgata, in the city of Gandhavatī.

## Bhadrottama
*bzang mchog*, Skt. *bhadrottama*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Bhadrāśva
*rta bzangs*, Skt. *bhadrāśva*, A city or village.

## bhaga
*bha+ga*, Skt. *bhaga*, In this text, it mostly refers to the female sexual and reproductive organs. However, this term encompasses several meanings, including “good fortune,” “happiness,” and “majesty.” It forms the root of the word bhagavat (Blessed One). A number of Buddhist esoteric scriptures are set within the bhaga of a female deity from the Buddhist pantheon.

## bhagavat
*bcom ldan ’das*, Skt. *bhagavat*, Literally “one who has bhaga,” which has many diverse meanings including “good fortune,” “happiness,” and “majesty.” In the Buddhist context, it means “one who has the good fortune of attaining enlightenment.” The Tibetan translation has three syllables defined to mean “one who has conquered (the māras), possesses (the qualities of enlightenment), and has transcended (saṃsāra, or both saṃsāra and nirvāṇa).”

## bhagavatī
*bcom ldan ’das ma*, Skt. *bhagavatī*, Also rendered as “Blessed Lady.”

## Bhagavān
*bcom ldan 'das*, an epithet of the [Buddha](#buddha). He who has vanquished (*bcom*) the [four demons](#four-demons), possess (*ldan*) all the qualities of realization, and is beyond (*das*) [saṃsāra](#saṃsāra) and [nirvāṇa](#nirvāṇa).

## Bhagga
A small tribal oligarchy belonging to the Vṛji confederacy located between ancient Vaiśālī and Śrāvastī.

## Bhaginī
*sring mo*, Skt. *bhaginī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bhagīratha
The king of the “solar race,” from Puranic narratives, who is said to have brought down the river Gaṅgā from the heavens. He is identified in Buddhist texts as an ancestor of the buddha Śākyamuni; also, the name of a previous buddha.

## Bhaiṣajyadatta
*sman sbyin*, Skt. *bhaiṣajyadatta*, A bodhisattva. (Toh 555: sman gtong)

## Bhaiṣajya­guru
*sman gyi lha*, Skt. *bhaiṣajya­guru*, A short form of the name of Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha, the Medicine Buddha.

## Bhaiṣajyaguru Vaidūryaprabharāja
*sman gyi bla bai du rya’i ’od*, Skt. *bhaiṣajya­guru vaidūrya­prabharāja*, Teacher of Medicine, King of Vaiḍūrya Light.

## Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha
*sman gyi lha bai DUr+ya’i ’od*, Skt. *bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha*, The Medicine Buddha, the thus-gone one residing in the buddhafield Vaiḍūrya­nirbhāsa. Also called Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha­rāja.

## Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha­rāja
*sman gyi lha bai DUr+ya’i ’od kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha­rāja*, The Medicine Buddha, the thus-gone one residing in the buddhafield Vaiḍūrya­nirbhāsa. Also called Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha.

## Bhaiṣajyarāja
*sman gyi rgyal po*, Skt. *bhaiṣajyarāja*, Lit. “King of Healers.” In the story of Śākyamuni’s former life in this sūtra, he is the tathāgata of the universe Mahāvyūha, during the eon called Vicaraṇa, who taught Prince Candracchattra about Dharma-worship. In later Buddhism, this buddha is believed to be the supernatural patron of healing and medicine.

## Bhaiṣajya­rāja­jyotirvi­mala
*sman gyi rgyal po skar ma dri ma med*, Skt. *bhaiṣajya­rāja­jyotirvimala*, The bodhisattva name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha gives to Mahābalavegadhārin, the youngest of the Veda-reciting pupils of the brahmin Samudrareṇu. The Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies that he will be the Buddha Roca, the thousand and fifth and the last buddha in the Bhadraka eon.

## Bhaiṣajyasamudgata
*sman yang dag ’phags*, Skt. *bhaiṣajya­samudgata*, One of the bodhisattva great beings.

## Bhaiṣajya­samudgata
*sman yang dag ’phags*, Skt. *bhaiṣajya­samudgata*, A bodhisattva present at the sūtra’s teaching.

## Bhaiṣajyasena
A lineage of kings.

## bhairavī
A female among a class of beings known to be “fearsome,” and perhaps associated with Bhairava, the wrathful form of Śiva.

## Bhairava
*’jigs byed*, Skt. *bhairava*, This name usually refers to the wrathful aspect of Śiva.

## Bhairavatī
*’jigs ldan*, Skt. *bhairavatī*, The western realm in which the bodhisattva Prajñārciḥ­saṃkopita­daṣṭa became the Buddha Sūrya­garbhārci­vimalendra.

## Bhairavī
*’jigs byed ma*, Skt. *bhairavī*, Fierce and terrifying Hindu goddess identified as the consort of Bhairava.

## Bhakṣaka
*za byed*, Skt. *bhakṣaka*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Bhallika
*bzang po*, Skt. *bhallika*, One of the two brother merchants, the other being Trapuṣa, who met and made offerings to the Buddha near the Bodhi tree, seven weeks after his awakening.

## Bhīṣamāṇa
“Frightening.” The name of a muhūrta.

## Bhandani
The name of a town.

## bhandu
An unidentified ritual substance.

## Bṛhannalā
Skt. *bṛhannalā*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bṛhantā
*chen mo nyid*, Skt. *bṛhantā*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bharaṇī
*bra nye*, Skt. *bharaṇī*, A constellation in the north, personified as a semidivine being. Here called upon for protection.

## Ābharaṇacchatra­nirghoṣa­rāja
*rgyan dang gdugs kyi dbyangs kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *ābharaṇacchatra­nirghoṣa­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Bharadvaja-Tree Bark
*b+ha ra dwa dza shing shun can*, Skt. *b+ha ra dwa dza shing shun can*, A ṛṣi present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Bharadvāja
*bha ra dwa dza*, Skt. *bharadvāja*, One of the principal śrāvaka pupils of Śākyamuni. It is said that his previous lives had been in hells and then as a human he had only stones to eat because of his mistreatment of his mother in one lifetime.

## Bharadvājasa
*bha ra dwa dza*, Skt. *bharadvājasa*, The name of a long enduring family in the distant past in which twenty thousand buddhas appeared.

## Bharata
*bha ra ta*, Skt. *bharata*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Jñānakrama.

## Bharata Abode
*bha ra ta’i gnas pa*, Skt. *bharata*, An island beyond Videha.

## Bhargava
*skal yod*, Skt. *bhargava*, A deity.

## Bhargavajra
*bhar ga rdo rje*, Skt. *bhar ga rdo rje*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Prajñākūṭa (538 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Bhargodeva
“God of Splendor.” The name of a muhūrta.

## Bhaṭṭārikā
*rje btsun ma*, Skt. *bhaṭṭārikā*, An epithet meaning “noble lady” commonly associated with the goddess Tārā in Buddhist literature, it is also applied to other goddesses in the Buddhist and Hindu pantheons. In The Maṇḍala Rites of Noble Mārīcī, the term appears as either an epithet of the goddess Durgā or perhaps Mārīcī.

## Bharo Chakdum
Bharo “Maimed Hand,” the Newar master and who was one of Ra Lotsāwa’s main teachers. His work with Ra Lotsāwa, locates him in the eleventh to twelfth centuries.

## Bharuka
*gso ba po*, Skt. *bharuka*, A yakṣa general.

## Bharukaccha
An ancient trade city on the west coast of the Indian subcontinent, presently known as Bharuch in the state of Gujarat.

## Bhasma
*thal ba*, Skt. *bhasma*, The younger brother of the king Samudragupta.

## Bhasmakrodha
*khro ba bcom*, Skt. *bhasmakrodha*, The 653rd buddha in the first list, 652nd in the second list, and 644th in the third list.

## Bhasmāntikā
*thal bar nye gnas ma*, Skt. *bhasmāntikā*, One of the great piśācīs.

## Bhasmodgirā
*thal ba za ma*, Skt. *bhasmodgirā*, One of the great piśācīs.

## Bṛhaspati
*phur bu*, Skt. *bṛhaspati*, The planet Jupiter. The Tibetan translation phur bu reflects the Sanskrit Kīlaka, which is also a name for the planet Jupiter.

## Bṛhaspatideva
*phur bu’i lha*, Skt. *bṛhaspatideva*, Name of a past king, a former incarnation of the Buddha while he was a practicing bodhisattva.

## Bṛhaspati’s Science of Grammar
*phur bu sgra rig*, Skt. *phur bu sgra rig*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Bṛhat
*che ba*, Skt. *bṛhat*, Thirteenth of the sixteen god realms of form that correspond to the four meditative concentrations, meaning “Great.”

## Bṛhatphala
*’bras bu che*, Skt. *bṛhatphala*, Lit. “Those in the Great Result.” The twelfth of the seventeen heavens of the form realm; also the name of the gods living there. In the form realm, which is structured according to the four concentrations and pure abodes‍, or Śuddhāvāsa‍, it is listed as the third of the three heavens that correspond to the fourth of the four concentrations.

## Bṛhat­phala
*’bras bu che*, Skt. *bṛhat­phala*, Twefth god realm of form, meaning “great fruition.”

## Bhava
*’byor pa*, Skt. *bhava*, A householder and the father of Pūrṇa from Sūrpāraka.

## Bhavadatta
*srid pa byin pa*, Skt. *bhavadatta*, An ancient king of Kāmarūpa.

## Bhavadeva
*srid pa’i lha*, Skt. *bhavadeva*, The king of Nandivardhana.

## Bhavanandin
*’byor dga’*, Skt. *bhavanandin*, A son of Bhava and half brother of Pūrṇa from Sūrpāraka.

## Bhavapuṣpa
*srid me tog*, Skt. *bhavapuṣpa*, The 982nd buddha in the first list, 981st in the second list, and 972nd in the third list.

## Bhava­tṛṣṇā­mala­prahīṇa
*srid pa’i sred pa dri ma spangs pa*, Skt. *bhava­tṛṣṇā­mala­prahīṇa*, The 833rd buddha in the first list, 832nd in the second list, and 822nd in the third list.

## Bhavatrāta
*’byor skyob*, Skt. *bhavatrāta*, A son of Bhava and half brother of Pūrṇa from Sūrpāraka.

## Bhavila
*’byor len*, Skt. *bhavila*, A son of Bhava and half brother of Pūrṇa from Sūrpāraka.

## Bhavānta
*rgyu mtha’*, Skt. *bhavānta*, One of the pratyeka­buddhas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhavāntadarśin
*srid mtha’ gzigs pa*, Skt. *bhavāntadarśin*, The 127th buddha in the first list, 127th in the second list, and 128th in the third list.

## Bhavānta­maṇi­gandha
*srid mtha’ nor bu’i spos*, Skt. *bhavānta­maṇi­gandha*, The 347th buddha in the first list, 346th in the second list, and 341st in the third list.

## Bhavāntikā
Skt. *bhavāntikā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhavyaghoṣa
The name of a king.

## Bhayaṃkara
*’jigs byed*, Skt. *bhayaṃkara*, One of the sons of Māra present at the eve of Prince Siddhārtha’s awakening.

## Bhayaṅkara
*’jigs mdzad*, Skt. *bhayaṅkara*, A buddha.

## Bhūbhāsa
*sa ’od*, Skt. *bhūbhāsa*, One of the kings of Nepal.

## Bhūbhṛt
*sa ’dzin*, Skt. *bhūbhṛt*, A nāga king; a member of the Buddha’s retinue.

## Bhūbhṛta
*sa ’dzin*, Skt. *bhūbhṛta*, A king, former incarnation of the Buddha.

## bhūcarī
*sa spyod*, Skt. *bhūcarī*, A type of ḍākinī (literally, “earth traveller”).

## Bhādrapadā
Refers to the two asterisms Pūrvabhādrapadā and Uttarabhādrapadā.

## Bhādrapada
The sixth lunar month, which falls within the period of August–September, when the full moon is in the Bhādrapadā asterisms.

## Bhīduram
*b+hI dU raM*, Skt. *bhīduram*, A town in Videha.

## bherī drum
*rnga*, Skt. *bherī*, As specified in the Sanskrit, a conical or bowl-shaped kettledrum, with an upper surface that is beaten with sticks. The Tibetan and Chinese are not specific about the kind of drum it is.”

## Bheraṇḍa
*e raN+Da*, Skt. *bheraṇḍa*, One of the mahoraga kings.

## Bheruṇḍa
*te raN+Da*, Skt. *bheruṇḍa*, One of the mahoraga kings.

## Bhesakalā grove
A deer park in the city of Suṃsumāragiri, the capital of the tribal oligarchy of the Bhaggas (Skt. Bhargas). The Tibetan translators interpreted this name as a compound where bhesakalā was rendered as sman (“medicine”) and vana as nags (“forest”). On the meaning of the Pali name, see in the translation.

## Bhṛṅgin
Skt. *bhṛṅgin*, A great ṛṣi.

## Bhṛṅgirasa
*ngan spong dga’*, Skt. *bhṛṅgirasa*, A great ṛṣi.

## Bhāgiratha
*skal ldan shing rta*, Skt. *bhāgiratha*, A great ṛṣi.

## Bhṛṅgiriṭi
*b+h+ring gi ri ti*, Skt. *bhṛṅgiriṭi*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi; also, one of the personal attendants on Śiva.

## Bhṛṅgāra
*b+h+ring ga ra*, Skt. *bhṛṅgāra*, One of the rāśis.

## Bhāṅgīrasi
A buddha in the distant past.

## Bhāgīrathī
*chu klung skal ldan shing rta*, Skt. *bhāgīrathī*, Another name for the river Gaṇgā, mentioned by the teacher [Sañjayin](#sañjayin-the-teacher) in encouraging [Śāriputra](#śāriputra) and [Maudgalyāyana](#maudgalyāyana) to seek out the [Buddha](#buddha) who was born on its banks.

## Bhāgīratha
*skal shing rta*, Skt. *bhāgīratha*, The 950th buddha in the first list, 949th in the second list, and 940th in the third list.

## Bhāgīrathi
*skal ldan shing rta*, Skt. *bhāgīrathi*, The 315th buddha in the first list, 314th in the second list, and 309th in the third list.

## Bhāgīrāthī
*gang gA*, Skt. *bhāgīrāthī*, One of the three branches of the river Gaṅgā in its early course.

## Bhṛgu
*ngan spong*, Skt. *bhṛgu*, One of the seven great rishis of ancient India. The founder of Indian astrology.

## Bhāgupta
*sa srung*, Skt. *bhāgupta*, One of the kings of Nepal.

## bhikṣu
*dge slong*, Skt. *bhikṣu*, The term bhikṣu, which is often translated as “monk,” refers to the highest type among the eight types of prātimokṣa vows that make one part of the Buddhist assembly. The term is explained as having at least three possible meanings: (1) someone who begs; (2) someone who has taken the highest level of Buddhist ordination; and (3) someone who has destroyed mental afflictions.

## bhikṣuṇī
*dge slong ma*, Skt. *bhikṣuṇī*, A fully ordained nun. Also rendered here simply as “nun.”

## Bāhiliko
*ba hi li ko*, Skt. *bāhiliko*, A land to the north of Jambudvīpa.

## Bhākrama
*pha rol gnon*, Skt. *bhākrama*, One of the kings of Nepal.

## Bhṛkuṭī
*khro gnyer ma*, Skt. *bhṛkuṭī*, One of the deified female bodhisattvas; one of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bhṛkuṭi
*khro gnyer can*, Skt. *bhṛkuṭi*, A yakṣa. (Toh 555: khro gnyer)

## Bhṛkuṭīmukha
*khro gnyer gdong*, Skt. *bhṛkuṭīmukha*, A mahoraga lord.

## Bhṛkuti
*khro gnyer*, Skt. *bhṛkuti*, A yakṣa.

## Bāhlika
*ba lhi ka*, Skt. *bāhlika*, Appears in The Hundred Deeds as the name of a king and a people dwelling in the “barbaric outlying region” west of Jambudvīpa.

## Bāhlīka
The name of the Bactrian people, who lived in the Balkh region of northern Afghanistan, north of the Hindu Kush. In later times the people from this region also settled in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent.

## Bhīmā
*’jigs med*, Skt. *bhīmā*, The name of various goddesses; one of the deities in the maṇḍala of Avalokiteśvara-Amoghapāśa and in some of the maṇḍalas of Avalokiteśvara.

## Bhīma
*skrag byed*, Skt. *bhīma*, A nāga king.

## Bhīṣma
*’jigs byed*, Skt. *bhīṣma*, A great ṛṣi.

## Bhūma
*sa pa*, Skt. *bhūma*, A yakṣa general who dwells on the earth.

## Bhīṣmagarjitanirghoṣasvara
*sgra dbyangs mi zad par sgrogs pa*, Skt. *bhīṣma­garjita­nirghoṣa­svara*, The buddha as whom Dharmodgata was reborn.

## Bhīṣma­garjita­nirghoṣa­svara
*sgra dbyangs mi bzad par sgrogs pa*, Skt. *bhīṣma­garjita­nirghoṣa­svara*, Lit. “Who Roared the Fearsome Roar.” A buddha, presumably in another realm, in the presence of whom the bodhisattva great being Sadāprarudita is practicing celibacy.

## Bhīṣma­garjita­svara­rāja
*’jigs bsgrags dbyangs kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *bhīṣma­garjita­svara­rāja*, The names of millions of buddhas within one eon in the distant past, and also the name of a particular buddha in chapter 19.

## Bhīmaka
*skrag byed*, Skt. *bhīmaka*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Bhīṣmamātaṅga
*’jigs byed glang po*, Skt. *bhīṣmamātaṅga*, A great ṛṣi.

## Bhīmasena
*’jigs sde*, Skt. *bhīmasena*, One of the five Pāṇḍava brothers. Son of Vāyu.

## Bhīṣmayaśas
*’jigs par grags pa*, Skt. *bhīṣmayaśas*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## bhūmi
*sa*, Skt. *bhūmi*, This is literally the “ground” in which qualities grow like plants, and it also means a “level.” As an untranslated term, bhūmi is used specifically to refer to levels of enlightenment, especially the seven or ten levels of the enlightened bodhisattvas. Sūtras such as the Perfection of Wisdom sūtras teach the seven bhūmis. The teaching of ten bhūmis was found in the Mahāsāṃghika tradition and particularly in the Daśa­bhūmika Sūtra (Toh 44, ch. 31, Ten Bhūmi Sūtra ), which is the thirty-first chapter in the Tibetan version of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra.

## Bhūmikampa
*sa g.yo byed*, Skt. *bhūmikampa*, A yakṣa. (Toh 555: sa kun g.yo ba)

## bhūmilatā
This is either a type of ground creeping vine or perhaps a term for an earthworm.

## Bhūmipati
*sa’i bdag po*, Skt. *bhūmipati*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa. See .

## Bhūmiprāpaṭī
*sa thob par ’gro ba*, Skt. *bhūmiprāpaṭī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## bhūmividārī
*bhu mi bi dA rI*, Skt. *bhūmividārī*, Same as bhūmisphoṭa (?); Agaricus campestris (?)

## Bhīṣmottara
*’jigs pa’i bla ma*, Skt. *bhīṣmottara*, The name of both a previous life of Buddha Śākyamuni as a king (translated as ’jigs pa’i bla ma) and the name of one of the buddhas (translated as ’jigs mchog) that Śākyamuni received the samādhi teaching from in a previous life.

## Bhīṣmottara­nirghoṣa
*’jigs mchog dbyangs*, Skt. *bhīṣmottara­nirghoṣa*, A ṛṣi, the kalyāṇamitra of chapter 11.

## Bhānugupta
Skt. *bhānugupta*, A sixth century king of the imperial Gupta dynasty.

## Bhānumat
*nyi ma lta bur gshegs pa*, Skt. *bhānumat*, The 810th buddha in the first list, 809th in the second list, and 798th in the third list.

## Bhānuprabhā
*nyi ma’i ’od*, Skt. *bhānuprabhā*, A merchant’s daughter, a previous life of Gopā.

## Bhogavatī
*longs spyod ldan ma*, Skt. *bhogavatī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bhogavān
*longs spyod ldan*, Skt. *bhogavān*, A nāga king.

## Bhogāvalī
*longs spyod phreng ma*, Skt. *bhogāvalī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bhojya
The name of a people in central India, whose kingdom, Bhoja, was situated in the Vidarbha region below the Vindhya mountain range.

## Bhojyadeva
An individual famous for attaining siddhi in the city of Mālavī.

## Bhoktrī
*longs spyod ma*, Skt. *bhoktrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## bhoṭārālā
An unidentified ritual ingredient.

## Bhrū
*smin ma*, Skt. *bhrū*, One of the vidyārājñīs attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhāradvāja
*b+ha ra dwA dza*, Skt. *bhāradvāja*, A brahmin who scolded the Buddha but subsequently became a monk.

## Bhramaṇa
*’khor*, Skt. *bhramaṇa*, One of the muhūrtas.

## Bhramarī
*bung ba ma*, Skt. *bhramarī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Bhramara
*bung ba*, Skt. *bhramara*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Bhraṣṭolā
*yul gnyid ’grogs*, Skt. *bhraṣṭolā*, A country.

## Bhārgava
One of the sublineages connected with the Vātsya lineage of the brahmanical tradition.

## Bhārgavīya
The name of a family lineage.

## Bhrikuti
*jo mo khro gnyer can*, one of the forms of [Tārā](#tārā) the female [Bodhisattva](#bodhisattva) of compassion. The name [means](#means) literally "She who has a wrathful frown."

## Bhrāmaṇa
*’khor bar byed pa nyid*, Skt. *bhrāmaṇa*, One of the muhūrtas.

## Bhrāmarī
*bung ba’i bu ma*, Skt. *bhrāmarī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi; one of the great piśācīs.

## Ābhāsaraśmi
*snang ba’i ’od zer*, Skt. *ābhāsaraśmi*, The 649th buddha in the first list, 648th in the second list, and 640th in the third list.

## Bhāsarāja
*snang ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *bhāsarāja*, A buddha.

## Bhāskara­deva
*nyi ma’i lha*, Skt. *bhāskara­deva*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Bhāskara­pradīpa
*nyi ma’i sgron ma*, Skt. *bhāskara­pradīpa*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Ābhāsvara
*’od gsal*, Skt. *ābhāsvara*, Lit. “Clear Light.” The sixth of the seventeen heavens of the form realm; also the name of the gods living there. In the form realm, which is structured according to the four concentrations and pure abodes‍, or Śuddhāvāsa‍, it is listed as the third of the three heavens that correspond to the second of the four concentrations.

## Bhāsvat
*’od ldan*, Skt. *bhāsvat*, One of the kings of Nepal.

## bhūtā
A female bhūta.

## bhūtī
A female bhūta.

## bhūta
*’byung po*, Skt. *bhūta*, This term in its broadest sense can refer to any being, whether human, animal, or nonhuman. However, it is often used to refer to a specific class of nonhuman beings, akin to spirits, who haunt dangerous and wild places. They are regularly mentioned alongside other nonhuman beings such as rākṣasas, piśācas, and pretas, and are especially prominent in Buddhist tantras. Their leader is traditionally regarded to be Rudra-Śiva (also known by the name Bhūta), thus bhūtas are also common in Śaivism.

## Bhūta (a brahmin)
*’byung po*, Skt. *bhūta*, The name of a certain brahmin who lived in Rājagṛha. Not to be confused with Bhūta, the name of a merchant and a dog, and a certain class of evil beings.

## Bhūta (the merchant and the dog)
*’byung po*, Skt. *bhūta*, The name of a certain householder’s dog and the name given to the lost infant it carried home to its owner one night, which would one day be reunited with his birth mother. Also the name of a certain brahmin who lived in Rājagṛha, and the name of a certain class of evil beings.

## bhūtagraha
*’byung po’i gdon*, Skt. *bhūtagraha*, A general term for classes of spirits and demonic beings who possess humans and cause illnesses.

## Bhūtaḍāmara
*’byung po ’dul ba*, Skt. *bhūtaḍāmara*, ‟Tamer of Spirits,” the titular deity of the Bhūtaḍāmara Tantra; a wrathful form of Vajrapāṇi.

## Bhūtamātṛ
*sems can rnams kyi ma*, Skt. *bhūtamātṛ*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Bhūtamukha
*’byung po’i gdong*, Skt. *bhūtamukha*, A yakṣa general.

## Bhūtamuni
Skt. *bhūtamuni*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhūtarāśi
*’byung ba’i phung po*, Skt. *bhūtarāśi*, One of the uṣṇīṣa kings attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bhūtavatī
*’byung po ldan ma*, Skt. *bhūtavatī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bhūtādhipati
Skt. *bhūtādhipati*, Epithet of Rudra; also of Maheśvara.

## Bhūteśvara
*’byung po’i bdag po*, Skt. *bhūteśvara*, ‟Lord of Bhūtas,” one of the eight bhūta kings.

## Bhūti
*mi ’byung ba*, Skt. *bhūti*, ‟Prosperity,” one of the eight goddesses of offerings in the Bhūtaḍāmara maṇḍala. Note that the Tibetan translation does not accord with the Sanskrit Bhūti.

## Bhūtika
*’byung ba pa*, Skt. *bhūtika*, One of the rāśis.

## Bhūtinī
*’byung mo*, Skt. *bhūtinī*, A female bhūta or any nonhuman female being; in some mantras it seems to be used as a proper name.

## Bhūtāntaścara
*’byung ba’i nang spyod*, Skt. *bhūtāntaścara*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Bhūtāntakarī
*’byung po mthar byed ma*, Skt. *bhūtāntakarī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Bhūtāntakara
*’byung po mthar byed*, Skt. *bhūtāntakara*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bāhu
*lag pa*, Skt. *bāhu*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi; one of the kings of asuras.

## Bhujaṅga
*lag ’gro*, Skt. *bhujaṅga*, A deity.

## Bhujaṃgama
*lag ’gro*, Skt. *bhujaṃgama*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## bhujaṅgapodadhika
A group of people opposed to Rāma and his supporters in the Rāmāyaṇa.

## Bhāvatī
Skt. *bhāvatī*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Bṛhāvatī
*yangs pa*, Skt. *bṛhāvatī*, A city.

## Bhāvaviveka
*legs ldan ’byed*, Skt. *bhāvaviveka*, (c. a.d. 400). A major Indian philosopher, a master of the Mādhyamika school of Buddhism, who founded a sub-school known as Svātantrika.

## Bhāvikī
*sgom pa ma*, Skt. *bhāvikī*, One of the subtle channels in the body.

## Bhāṇḍāyana
One of the sublineages connected with the Māṇḍavya lineage of the brahmanical tradition.

## bichiliocosm
*stong gnyis pa bar ma’i ’jig rten gyi khams*, Skt. *dvitīyamadhyama sāhasralokadhātu*, Equal to a thousand universes of a thousand worlds (i.e., a universe of a million worlds).

## big action
*byed pa chen po*, Skt. *byed pa chen po*, A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## big black mouth
A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## big pearl
A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## big water life
A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## bignonia
*skya snar*, Skt. *pāṭalā*, Bignonia suaveolens. The Indian species of bignonia. They have trumpet-shaped flowers and the small trees are common throughout India.

## Bile
*mkhris pa*, one of the three humours of the body, whose imbalance creates the different kinds of illness. See also [wind](#wind), [phlegm](#phlegm).

## bile disorders
*mkhris pa’i nad*, Skt. *paittikāvyādhi*, Second of the four kinds of disease.

## billion trillionth
*bye ba khrag khrig stong gi cha*, Skt. *bye ba khrag khrig stong gi cha*, Ten to the power of -21. A “hundred billion trillionth” (bye ba khrag khrig rgya phrag stong gi cha) is ten to the power of -23.

## billions
*bye ba khrag khrig phrag ’bum*, Skt. *koṭiniyuta­śatasahasra*, The number of grains of sand of the river Ganges is a favored analogy for immense numbers in the sūtras. Literally 10 million x 100 million x 100 thousand; i.e., 1019 or 10 quintillion.

## billion-world galaxy
*stong gsum gyi stong chen po’i ’jig rten gyi khams*, Skt. *trisāhasra­mahā­sāhasra­loka­dhātu*, Lit. “three-thousand-great-thousand-world realm.” Each of these is composed of one thousand realms, each of which contains one thousand realms, each of which contains one thousand realms = one thousand to the third power = one billion worlds.

## Billowing Waters
*chu g.yo ba*, Skt. *chu g.yo ba*, A river on Great Slope.

## Billowing Waves
*rlabs g.yo ba*, Skt. *rlabs g.yo ba*, A lake on Equal Peaks.

## bilva
Aegle marmelos. The bel tree, also known as the Bengal quince.

## Bilvaka of Sumeru
*lhun po’i bi lwa kaH*, Skt. *bilvaka*, An island in the vicinity of Jambudvīpa.

## bimbā
*bim pa*, Skt. *bimbā*, Momordica monadelpha. A perennial climbing plant, the fruit of which is a bright red gourd. Because of its color it is frequently used in poetry as a simile for lips.

## Bimbī
*btsun mo gzugs can, gzugs can*, Skt. *bimbī, rājñī bimbī*, The queen, wife of King [Mahāpadma](#mahāpadma) and mother of [Bimbisāra](#bimbisāra).

## bimba
*bim pa*, Skt. *bimba*, Momordica monadelpha. A perennial climbing plant, the fruit of which is a bright red gourd. Because of its color it is frequently used in poetry as a simile for lips.

## Bimbika
*bim pi ka*, Skt. *bimbika*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Bimbisāra
*gzugs can snying po*, Skt. *bimbisāra*, The king of [Magadha](#magadha) and a great patron of Śākyamūni [Buddha](#buddha). His birth coincided with the [Buddha](#buddha)’s. His father, mistakenly attributing the brilliant light that marked the [Buddha](#buddha)’s birth to the birth of his son by Queen [Bimbī](#bimbī) (Goldie), named him ‘[Essence](#essence) of Gold.’

## bindi
*thig le*, Skt. *tilaka*, An ornamental dot painted between the eyebrows.

## binding
*bcing ba*, Skt. *bandhana*, A type of ritual action.

## Bindu
*thig le*, lit. a circle, sphere, point or drop, but also with a range of more abstract meanings. We have used this Sanskrit term in the chapter on the [transference](#transference) of consciousness to underline the fact that the [levels](#levels) of meaning are multiple; in other contexts we have translated the same word as [essence](#essence).

## Bindusāra
*snying po thig le*, Skt. *bindusāra*, The second Mauryan emperor, son of Candragupta.

## biographies
*rtogs pa brjod pa’i sde*, Skt. *avadāna*, One of the twelve branches of Buddhist scriptures.

## birch bark
A medium for writing texts and mantras. Mahākāla’s Sovereign Tantra prescribes using birch bark to copy down the text.

## Bird Throat
*bya mgrin*, Skt. *bya mgrin*, An asura king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Bird’s Beak
*bya mchu can*, Skt. *bya mchu can*, A preta king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## birth
*skye ba*, Skt. *jāti*, The four types of birth are birth from a womb, birth from an egg, birth from warmth and moisture, and miraculous birth.

## birth from a womb
*mngal gyi gnas*, Skt. *mngal gyi gnas*, Existence in which one is born from a womb. This is one of four types of birth listed in treatises such as the Abhidharmakośa : (1) birth from a womb (mammals, human beings), (2) from an egg (birds, reptiles, fish, etc.), (3) from heat and moisture (maggots, etc.), (4) and spontaneous or miraculous birth (gods, pretas, hell beings, intermediate state beings, etc.).

## birth from heat and moisture
*drod gsher las skyes*, Skt. *saṃsvedaja*, Third of the four modes of birth.

## Birth of Happy Mind
*yid bde skyes*, Skt. *yid bde skyes*, Son of the buddha Asaṅga.

## birth story
*skyes pa’i rabs*, Skt. *jātaka*, The Buddha’s accounts of his own previous lifetimes, listed as one of the twelve aspects of the wheel of Dharma.

## birth totem gods
*lhan cig skyes pa'i lha*, Skt. *devatā sahajā*, [Yakṣa](#yakṣa) and other spirits that appear at the same time a person is born in order to protect them.

## birthlessness
*mi skye ba*, Skt. *anutpādatva*, This refers to the ultimate nature of reality, to the fact that, ultimately, nothing has ever been produced or born nor will it ever be because birth and production can occur only on the relative, or superficial, level. Hence “birthlessness” is a synonym of “voidness,” “reality,” “absolute,” “ultimate,” “infinity,” etc.

## bisakṣīla
*pad ma’i rtsa ba’i ’o ma*, Skt. *bisakṣīla*, The juice of lotus roots.

## bitter
*kha*, Skt. *tikta*, One of the eight supreme flavors. Also one of the six tastes of the Āyurveda and Tibetan medical traditions.

## bitter gourd
*in dra ba ru na*, Skt. *indrāvaruṇi*, Cucumis trigonus; colocynth, a wild bitter gourd, Cucumis colocynthis; the favorite plant of Indra and Varuṇa.

## Bījadhara
*sa bon ’chang*, Skt. *bījadhara*, A great bodhisattva.

## Bālā
*stobs*, Skt. *bālā*, One of the five goddesses personifying the five “hooks of gnosis.”

## Bāla
*byis*, Skt. *bāla*, One of the Gupta emperors, the successor of king Skanda.

## Bālabhañja
The name of a city located just north of Mount Sumeru.

## Black (a brahmin)
*nag po*, Skt. *kāla*, A certain dark-complected brahmin youth who became a sage, then heard the Dharma from the Buddha, became ordained, and manifested arhatship. Not to be confused with Black the yakṣa who also appears in his story, nor with Kāla the nāga king (whose name in Tib. is the same nag po).

## Black (a yakṣa)
*nag po*, Skt. *kāla*, A certain yakṣa tamed by the Buddha and subsequently sworn to protect the people of Rājagṛha. Not to be confused with Black the brahmin who also appears in his story, nor with Kāla the nāga king.

## Black Acala
*mi g.yo ba nag po*, Skt. *kṛṣṇācala*, Acala corresponding to Buddha Akṣobhya in the center of the maṇḍala.

## black begging bowl carriers
*lhung bzed nag pa can*, Skt. *kālapātrika*, A euphemism for those who seek [alms](#alms), understood to refer to Buddhist monks.

## Black Belly
*nag po gsus pa*, Skt. *kālodara*, (1) An area in Kuru (nag po gsus pa). 2. One of sixteen realms that surround the Hell of Ultimate Torment. (lto gnag), also called Raven’s Belly.

## Black Bhūta
A graha.

## Black Cord
*thig nag*, Skt. *kālasūtra*, One of the eight hot hells.

## Black Defeater
The name of one of the eighteen primary emanations of the goddess described in this text.

## black earth
*sa nag po*, Skt. *kṛṣṇamṛttikā*, A type of soil (?)

## black face
*gdong gnag*, Skt. *gdong gnag*, A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## black faction
*nag po’i phyogs*, Skt. *kṛṣṇapakṣa*, The army, divisions, or factions of Māra, the deity who personifies spiritual death; from Māra’s point of view, this is the “white faction.” Also refers to the dark fortnight of the lunar month.

## black gram
A type of bean used in ritual preparations. Most often identified as black gram (Vigna mungo).

## black head
*mgo nag*, Skt. *mgo nag*, A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## Black Indrāṇī
The name of one of the eighteen primary emanations of the goddess described in this text.

## Black Kapālin

## Black Mountains
The Kāla Mountains of Bhāratvarṣa (i.e., India) are listed in the Mahābhārata as the mountain ranges Vindhya (separating the Deccan from north India), Mahendra (the eastern Ghats), Malaya (southern half of the Western Ghats), Sahya (the northern half of the Western Ghats), Rakṣavat (northeast extension of the Vindhya), Pāripātra, and the Sūktimat (or Śuktimat), which is presumably another name for the one remaining significant mountain range, the Arbuda in the northwest.

Emmerick, based on the Nobel edition, separates the compound into two: patra (leaf) and śaileya. Toh 555: spra ba.

It is one of seven types of pride, which include (1) pride (Tib. nga rgyal; Skt. māna), (2) excessive pride (Tib. lhag pa’i nga rgyal; Skt. adhimāna), (3) outrageous pride (Tib. nga rgyal las kyang nga rgyal; Skt. mānātimāna), (4) egoistic pride (Tib. nga’o snyam pa’i nga rgyal; Skt. asmimāna), (5) blatant pride (Tib. mngon pa’i nga rgyal; Skt. abhimāna), (6) pride of feeling inferior (Tib. cung zad snyam pa’i nga rgyal; Skt. ūnamāna), and (7) unfounded pride (Tib. log pa’i nga rgyal; Skt. mithyāmāna).

## blessed lady
*bcom ldan ’das ma*, Skt. *bhagavatī*, The female form of the epithet commonly applied to buddhas and other awakened beings. The Sanskrit word bhaga means, among other factors, “good fortune,” “happiness,” “prosperity,” and “excellence.” The suffix -vat indicates possession. A common English translation is thus “blessed one” or “fortunate one.” The three syllables of the Tibetan translation mean that the being has “overcome” or “conquered” (Tib. bcom), is “endowed [with qualities]” (Tib. ldan), and has “gone beyond [saṃsāra]” (Tib. ’das).

## Blessed Lord
*bcom ldan ’das*, Skt. *bhadanta­bhagavan*, See “Blessed One.”

## Blessed Mārīcī’s Supreme Secret
*bcom ldan ’das ma mchog tu gsang ba*, The name of a text mentioned in The Maṇḍala Rites of Noble Mārīcī. The name of this text appears as the source for an excerpted chapter titled “The Mantra Wheel: A Jewel That Fulfills Every Wish.”

## blessed one
*bcom ldan ’das*, Skt. *bhagavān*, In Buddhist literature, an epithet applied to buddhas, most often to Śākyamuni. The Sanskrit term generally means “possessing fortune,” but in specifically Buddhist contexts it implies that a buddha is in possession of six auspicious qualities (bhaga) associated with complete awakening. The Tibetan term—where bcom is said to refer to “subduing” the four māras, ldan to “possessing” the great qualities of buddhahood, and ’das to “going beyond” saṃsāra and nirvāṇa—possibly reflects the commentarial tradition where the Sanskrit bhagavat is interpreted, in addition, as “one who destroys the four māras.” This is achieved either by reading bhagavat as bhagnavat (“one who broke”), or by tracing the word bhaga to the root √bhañj (“to break”).

## Blue
*sngon po*, Skt. *sngon po*, Blue (the color), also the name of an ocean off Jambudvīpa.

## blue beryl
*bai DUr+ya*, Skt. *vaiḍūrya*, Although vaiḍūrya—particularly in the context of Bhaiṣajya­guru—has often been translated as lapis lazuli, blue beryl is overall a better match for the descriptions and references in the Sanskrit and Tibetan literature. The equivalent Pāli form of vaiḍūrya is veḷuriya. The Prākrit form verulia is the source for the English word “beryl.” There are white, yellow, and green beryls (green beryl is generally called “emerald”), but in this case blue beryl needs to be specified to match traditional descriptions. Vaiḍūrya may nevertheless have been taken to designate different gems at different times and places, and no single equivalent in English is entirely satisfactory.

## bodhi
*byang chub*, Skt. *bodhi*, In general the Sanskrit means “awakening,” as from sleep, but in the Buddhist context it is the awakening from ignorance, i.e., the direct realization of truth.

## Bodhi tree
*byang chub kyi shing*, Skt. *bodhivṛkṣa*, Lit. “tree of awakening.” Name of the tree under which the Buddha Śākyamuni attained awakening in Bodhgayā. It is a kind of fig tree, the Ficus religiosa, known in Sanskrit as aśvattha or pippala. It is also mentioned as the tree beneath which every buddha will manifest the attainment of buddhahood.

## bodhicitta
In normative Mahāyāna doctrine, bodhicitta refers to the aspiration for awakening, in both its relative and absolute aspects. In tantric thought it frequently refers to semen in the context of its generation through sexual yoga, its use as a ritual substance, and its manipulation through practices dealing with the chanels and centers of the body.

## bodhimaṇḍa
*snying po byang chub*, Skt. *bodhimaṇḍa*, The exact place where every buddha in this world will manifest the attainment of buddhahood. In our world, it is the spot beneath the Bodhi tree in the village presently known as Bodhgaya. Literally, “the essence of enlightenment.” Also translated elsewhere as byang chub kyi snying po.

*byang chub dam pa’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *bodhimaṇḍacūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

*snying po byang chub rnam par sangs rgyas pa’i dpal gyi zla ba*, Skt. *bodhi­maṇḍa­vibuddha­śrī­candra*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Bodhimati
*byang chub blo gros*, Skt. *bodhimati*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Bodhimitra
A Kashmiri paṇḍita who was invited to Tibet during the late eight and early ninth centuries. He worked with several Tibetan translators on the translation of a number of sūtras.

## Bodhirāja
*byang chub rgyal po*, Skt. *bodhirāja*, The 574th buddha in the first list, 574th in the second list, and 567th in the third list.

## Bodhisattva
*byang chub kyi sems*, lit. the mind of [enlightenment](#enlightenment). On the relative level, it is the wish to attain Buddhahood for the sake of all beings, as well as the practice of the [path](#path) of love, compassion, the [six transcendent perfections](#six-transcendent-perfections), etc., necessary for achieving that goal. On the absolute level, it is the direct insight into the ultimate nature.

## Bodhisattva Abbot
the title by which [Śāntarakṣita](#śāntarakṣita) is sometimes known.

## bodhisattva basket
*byang chub sems pa'i sde snod*, Skt. *bodhisattva­piṭaka*, A collection of the Great Vehicle teachings.

## bodhisattva collection
*byang chub sems dpa’i sde snod*, Skt. *bodhisattva­piṭaka*, In this text, the bodhisattva collection refers to the realization of all phenomena as well as the qualities of ordinary beings, learning, that which is beyond learning, hearers, solitary buddhas, bodhisattvas, and buddhas.

## bodhisattva conduct
*byang chub sems dpa’i spyod pa*, Skt. *bodhisattva­caryā*, The proper conduct of a committed bodhisattva is a topic addressed in many Mahāyāna sūtras, as wells as the commentarial literature.

## bodhisattva great being
*byang chub sems dpa’ chen po*, Skt. *bodhisattva­mahāsattva*, A bodhisattva who has attained the highest level next to the Buddha.

## bodhisattva level
The ten levels or stages traversed by a bodhisattva that culminate in buddhahood: (1) Joyful (pramuditā; rab tu dga’ ba), (2) Stainless (vimalā; dri ma med pa), (3) Luminous (prabhākarī; ’od byed pa), (4) Radiant (arciṣmatī; ’od ’phro can), (5) Invincible (sudurjayā; shin tu sbyang dka’ ba), (6) Facing Directly (abhimukhī; mngon du gyur), (7) Far-Reaching (dūraṅgamā; ring du song ba), (8) Immovable (acalā; mi g.yo ba), Auspicious Intellect (sādhumatī; legs pa’i blo gros), and (10) Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā; chos kyi sprin).

## Bodhisattva levels
*phags pa'i sa*, lit. [sublime levels](#sublime-levels), Skt. *bhūmi*. The ten [levels](#levels) of realization reached by [Bodhisattvas](#bodhisattva) on the [path](#path)s of seeing, meditation and beyond learning. In some classifications additional [levels](#levels) are added. "These [levels](#levels) are sublime because they are far beyond ordinary beings." DICT.

## bodhisattva mahāsattva
*byang chub sems dpa’ sems dpa’ chen po*, Skt. *bodhisattvamahāsattva*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva is a bodhisattva who has completed the seventh bhūmi and is on the eighth, ninth, or tenth bhūmi prior to becoming a buddha. These bodhisattvas have several special qualities that bodhisattvas on the lower bhūmis do not have.

## bodhisattva of great courage
A common epithet of great bodhisattvas, the precise meaning of which is contested but that seems to describe someone as possessing great courage, magnanimity, and great strength of character. The term is explained in the *Mahā­prajñā­pāramitopadeśa, which has a short chapter on this term, also as a being who possesses great love and great compassion.

## Bodhisattva Vehicle
*byang chub sems dpa’i theg pa*, Skt. *bodhisattvayāna*, A synonym for the Mahāyāna, the Great Vehicle.

## Bodhisattva­piṭaka
Skt. *bodhisattva­piṭaka*, “Basket” or “Collected Teachings for Bodhisattvas,” refers to the sūtras and teachings of the bodhisattva yāna in general.

## Bodhisattvasamuccayā
*byang chub yang dag par bsdus pa*, Skt. *Bodhi­sattva­samuccayā*, A goddess. In Toh 555 called “goddess of the Bodhi tree.”

## Bodhisattva­yāna
*byang chub sems dpa’i theg pa*, Skt. *bodhisattva­yāna*, This is the way (yāna) of the bodhisattva, the teachings of the Mahāyāna sūtras.

## Bodhākṣa
*shes mig*, Skt. *bodhākṣa*, One of the māras.

## Bodhnath (stūpa)
*bya rung kha shor*, pronounced "Jarungkashor", one of the two great [stūpa](#stūpa)s in the Kathmandu valley. The story of its construction is related to the advent of Buddhism in Tibet and described in the *History of the Jarungkhashor Stūpa*, a terma discovered by Śākya Zangpo (translated by Keith Downam as *The Legend of the Great Stūpa*, berkeley, [Dharma](#dharma) Publishing, 1973).

## Bodhyaṅgā
*byang chub yan lag ma*, Skt. *bodhyaṅgā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Bodhyaṅgapuṣpa
*byang chub kyi yan lag gi me tog*, Skt. *bodhyaṅgapuṣpa*, Lit. “Limbs of Awakening Flower.” Name that a hundred thousand one hundred million billion beings will bear when they become buddhas after sixty-four eons.

## bodhyaṅgavatin
*byang chub kyi yan lag yod pa*, Skt. *bodhyaṅgavatin*, Lit. “endowed with the limbs of awakening.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Bodhyaṅgā­laṃkāra
*byang chub yan lag brgyan*, Skt. *bodhyaṅgā­laṃkāra*, A buddha realm.

## Bodily Array of Qualities
*yon tan bkod pa’i lus*, Skt. *yon tan bkod pa’i lus*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Ratnapāṇi.

## bodily essences
*snying sna*, The exact identification of these substances is not explicitly stated in The Tantra of Glorious Mahākāla. The Suśrutasaṁhitā refers to seven “bodily essences” (Skt. sāra). These are vital fluid (Skt. sattva, perhaps signifying the amniotic fluid), semen (Skt. śukra), marrow (Skt. majjan), bone (Skt. asthi), lymph (Skt. medas), flesh (Skt. māṃsa), and blood (Skt. rakta). It is entirely possible, however, that these “bodily essences” correspond to the various bodily fluids that often accompany offerings of the five types of meat in the performance and maintenance of samaya.

## Bodong Paṇchen Choklé Namgyal
*bo dong paN chen phyogs las rnam rgyal*, Skt. *bo dong paN chen phyogs las rnam rgyal*, 1376–1451. Prolific scholar and abbot of the Bodong E monastery.

## body anointed with the fragrance of moral discipline
*tshul khrims kyi spos kyis lus byugs pa*, Skt. *śīla­gandhānulipta­gātra*, There are many references in the sūtras to a pleasant fragrance that is the result of moral discipline. Although it is not stated in these exact words, this description echoes some of the eighty excellent signs (asītyānuvyañjana), a subset of the 112 physical characteristics of both buddhas and cakravartins. For example, the list found in the Perfection of Wisdom in Ten Thousand Lines (Toh 11, 2.33) describes these signs: “(34) Their body is immaculate and without unpleasant odors”; and (later down the list) “(40) The pores of their body all emit a pleasant odor.”

## body consciousness constituent
*lus kyi rnam par shes pa’i khams*, Skt. *kāyavijñānadhātu*, One of the eighteen constituents.

## body of emanation

## body of reality
In distinction to the rūpakāya, or form body of a buddha, this is the eternal, imperceivable realization of a buddha. In origin it was a term for the presence of the Dharma, and it has since become synonymous with the true nature.

*sku, gsung, thugs, yon tan, phrin las*, five aspects of Buddhahood. Sometimes referred to as the [five kāyas](#five-kāyas). See also [five families](#five-families).

## born from sacred spaces
A class of yoginī or ḍākinī who takes birth in a human form. Buddhist and non-Buddhist literature lists multiple classes of such beings, with Buddhist literature often employing a threefold typology: those born from sacred spaces (kṣetrajā or pīṭhajā), those born from mantra (mantrajā), and those born from the natural state (sahajā).

## Bothar
The first Degé king, Bothar Lodrö Topden (late fourteenth to mid-fifteenth century), was the head of the house of Degé in its thirty-first generation. He is remembered for establishing the site that would later become the center of the Degé kingdom. He had two sons, Lama Palden Sengé and Gyaltsen Bum. For more on his life see his entry at The Treasury of Lives.

A gathering of all the monks within these boundaries constitutes a “[consensus](#consensus),” during which formal [act](#act)s of [saṅgha](#saṅgha) may be performed.

## Bāṣpa
*rlangs pa*, Skt. *bāṣpa*, One of the monks attending this teaching in Śrāvastī, at Jeta’s Grove. He was one of the five companions who joined Prince Siddhārtha while practicing austerities and attended his first turning of the wheel of Dharma at the Deer Park, after the Buddha’s awakening.

*tshang pa’i gnas*, Skt. *brahmavihāra*, See “abodes of Brahmā.”

## brahmā abodes
Here refers to the brahmā heavens of the form realm, in which brahmā deities and the supreme deity, Brahmā, lord of the Sahā world, abide. Elsewhere the four brahmā abodes, or the “four immeasurables,” refer to the practices of limitless love, compassion, joy, and equanimity, which lead to rebirth in the brahmā realms.

## Brahmā and the gods of his realm
A term for the heavenly realm of Brahmā and the gods who dwell there.

*tshangs pa’i tog*, Skt. *tshangs pa’i tog*, Birthplace of the buddha Hutārci.
