*kak+ko Ta*, Skt. *karkoṭaka*, One of the kings of the nāgas.

## Karkoṭakamukhī
*karkote mu khi*, Skt. *karkoṭakamukhī*, “One with the Face of Karkoṭa.” One of the eight nāga queens.

## Karālī
*lag ’gro ma*, Skt. *karālī*, A great rākṣasī.

## Karāladantī
*so brod ma*, Skt. *karāladantī*, A great rākṣasī.

## Karma
*las*. We have generally preferred to say "the [effects of actions](#effects-of-actions)," "actions and their effects" or the "[principle of cause and effect](#principle-of-cause-and-effect)." Karma literally [means](#means) simply "action," but is often used loosely to mean the result produced by past actions (*las kyi 'bras bu,* Skt. *karmaphala*).

## Karma Chagme
*karma chags med* (16th century), famous [lama](#lama) of the [Kagyupa](#kagyupa) school who united the teaching of his school and those of the [Nyingmapas](#nyingmapa) and was the tutor of the treasure-discoverer [Namcho Mingyur Dorje](#namcho-mingyur-dorje).

## karma family
*las kyi rigs*, Skt. *karmakula*, One of the five buddha families, it is presided over by the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi.

## Karma Kaṃtsang
Karma Kaṃtsang is another way to refer to the Karma Kagyü lineage that began with the first Karmapa, Düsum Khyenpa (1110–93).

## Karma Mipham Sönam Rapten
A king of Jangyul (d. 1647).

## Karma Pakṣi
Karma Pakṣi (1204–83) was second in the line of Karmapa incarnations. His recognition as the reincarnation of the first Karmapa, Dusum Khyenpa (1110–93), is regarded as the beginning of the tulku tradition in Tibet.

## Karma Paldrub
Born in the seventeenth century, he was a lineage holder of literary and grammatical teachings.

## Karmaśa
*ka ra ma sha*, Skt. *karmaśa*, An arhat.

## Karmadā
*las sbyin ma*, Skt. *karmadā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## karmadhāraya
Skt. *karmadhāraya*, Type of Sanskrit compound.

## Karmaḍākinī
*las kyi mkha’ ’gro ma*, Skt. *karmaḍākinī*, A deity in Vajraḍākinī’s maṇḍala.

## karmamudrā
*las kyi phyag rgya*, Skt. *karmamudrā*, See “action mudrā.”

## Karmapa
*kar ma pa*, name of a series of great [lama](#lama)s of the [Kagyupa](#kagyupa) school, whose lineage of reincarnations goes back to Dusum Khyenpa (1110 - 1193). The Karmapas were the first [tulkus](#tulku) recognized in Tibet.

## Karmapa Chödrak Gyatso
As the seventh Karmapa, Chödrak Gyatso (1454–1506) was the head of the Karma Kagyü school. He was an accomplished practitioner and a prolific scholar who spent much of his life in retreat. He was nevertheless very socially engaged and worked to put an end to military conflicts, finance bridge construction, instruct people to give up hunting and fishing, and restore Buddhist iconography, specifically the central Buddha statues at Bodhgaya and Tshurpu.

## Karmapa III, Rangjung Dorjé
*rang ’byung rdo rje*, Skt. *rang ’byung rdo rje*, (1284–1339). An important master in the Karma Kagyu lineage of Tibetan Buddhism (karma bka’ brgyud). He is considered the third master in the lineage to have the title of Karmapa.

## Karmaphalā
*las ’bras ma*, Skt. *karmaphalā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Karmaraṅga
*ka da raM tsa*, Skt. *karmaraṅga*, This seems to be the ancient name of Arakan, or what is now the Rakhine State in Myanmar.

## Karmarāja
Skt. *karmarāja*, Another name of the king Vṛtsudhāna.

## Karmavajra
*rdo rje las*, Skt. *karmavajra*, An alternative name for Īrṣyā Yamāri.

## karmic actions to be experienced in other lives
*lan grangs gzhan la myong bar ’gyur ba’i las*, Skt. *apara­paryāya­vedanīya*, One of the three types of karma whose results are experience neither in the present nor the next, but the subsequent lives. The other two types are the “karma that ripens in this life” (dṛṣṭa­dharma­vipāka or dṛṣṭa­dharma­vedanīya) and the “karma that is to be experienced in the immediately following life” (upapadya­vedanīya).

## karmic dispositions
*’du byed*, Skt. *saṃskāra*, One of the five aggregates; the very subtle karmic tendencies that give shape to an individual’s saṃsāric experience. In Abhidharma literature there are typically fifty-one saṃskāras.

## Karmic energy
*las kyi rlung*, [energy](#energy) determined by one's [karma](#karma), as opposed to *ye shes kyi rlung*, the [energy](#energy) connected with [wisdom](#wisdom).

## karmic fruition
The complex process of the ripening or maturation of karma, i.e., the development of the karmic result (Tib. las kyi ’bras bu) of karmically relevant actions committed with body, speech, and mind, by virtue of the power of the action as cause and supporting conditions.

## karmic imprint
*bag chags*, Skt. *vāsanā*, These are imprints left by actions in consciousness, which condition its future character and disposition.

## karmic influence
*zag pa*, Skt. *āsrava*, Literally “inflow.” These are karmic influences that prompt an individual to act in a certain way, leading to the accumulation of karma.

## karmic obscuration
*las kyi sgrib pa*, Skt. *karmāvaraṇa*, The emotional and cognitive veils that create impediments in one’s life and prevent one from seeing the nature of reality.

## karmic obscurations
The persistent physical, mental, or emotional obstacles to spiritual progress.

## Karmic obscurations (obscurations of past actions)
*las kyi sgrib pa*, Skt. *karmāvaraṇā*, [obscurations](#obscurations) created by [negative action](#negative-action)s. See [obscurations](#obscurations).

## karmic predispositions
*’du byed*, Skt. *saṃskāra*, This term denotes the deep-seated predispositions inherited from past actions and experiences, some of which function in association with mind, while others do not. Karmic predispositions are critical to the Buddhist understanding of the causal dynamics of karma and conditioning. It is the collection of such countless predispositions by afflicted mental states that constitutes the obscuration of misconceptions concerning the known range of phenomena, the total eradication of which occurs only when full awakening or buddhahood is achieved.

## karmic result
*las kyi ’bras bu*, Skt. *karmaphala*, Literally meaning the “fruit” of action(s), karmic result denotes rebirth and karmic punishment and reward as a consequence of, and in accordance with the moral character of, one’s actions.

## karmic ripening
*las kyi rnam par smin pa*, The complex process of the ripening of karma, i.e., the development of the karmic result (las kyi ’bras bu) of karmically relevant actions committed with body, speech, and mind by virtue of the power of the action as cause and supporting condition.

## karmic stains
*zag pa*, Skt. *āsrava*, Literally, “inflows,” these are negative karmic influences.

## Karmārapāṭaka
*las kyi brang*, Skt. *karmārapāṭaka*, One of the pīlavas.

## Karnāṭaka
*kar Na*, Skt. *karnāṭa*, A country corresponding to modern Karnataka State in India.

## karnikara
*kar ni*, Skt. *karṇikāra*, Pterospermum acerifolium. Other names include bayur, muchakunda, muchalinda, and dinner-plate tree.

## Karoṭapāṇi
*lag na gzhong thogs*, Skt. *karoṭapāṇi*, One of the three classes of yakṣas at the base of Sumeru, below the paradises of the mahārājas, as part of the lowest class of paradises in the desire realm. Their name means “those who have basins in their hands.” They are said to be at the very base of Sumeru, and worry that the rising ocean is going to flood them. Because they are continually bailing out water with the basins, they are unable to follow the path to enlightenment.

## karoṭapāṇi yakṣa
A class of yakṣa whose name means “having bowls in their hands.”

## karṣāpaṇa
A coin that varied in value according as to whether it was made of gold, silver, or copper.

## karpūra
*ha la sa*, Skt. *karpūra*, Possibly corresponds to the Borneo camphor tree. See Ludvik 2007, p. 315.

## Karpāsī forest
*ras bal can gyi tshal*, Skt. *karpāsīvana*, Where [Buddha](#buddha) converted a noble band of sixty youths.

## Śūkarāsyā
*phag gi gdong*, Skt. *śūkarāsyā*, One of the goddesses in the retinue of Heruka.

## Karīti
The name of a people in ancient India. The Tibetan rendering means “theatre performers.”

## kartri knife
*gri gug*, Skt. *kartri*, A ritual knife meant for flaying skin.

## Karuṇā
*snying rje*, Skt. *karuṇā*, One of the vidyārājñīs attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Karuṇa
*snying rje ldan*, Skt. *karuṇa*, One of the kinnara kings.

## Karuṇa­puṇḍarīka
*snying rje can dang pad+ma dkar po*, Skt. *karuṇa­puṇḍarīka*, It is not clear whose name this is.

## Karuṇatejas
*thugs rje’i ’od*, Skt. *karuṇatejas*, A buddha in the distant past.

## karuli
An unidentified substance.

## Karuṇāmati
*snying rje’i blo*, Skt. *karuṇāmati*, Youngest son of the universal monarch Nimiṃdhara.

## Karuṇāvicintin
*rtag tu snying rje sems*, Skt. *karuṇāvicintin*, The name of King Mahā­karuṇā­cintin as given in verse.

## Kṛṣṇa’s Offering
*gling bu can*, Skt. *gling bu can*, A Licchavi youth present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Kasadizé
*tshong ’dus ka sa di ze*, Skt. *tshong ’dus ka sa di ze*, A market in Virtuous Castle.

## Kashmir
*kha che*, Skt. *kaśmīra*, The area known today as the Kashmir Valley, situated between the Himalayas and the Pir Panjal Range. In this chapter, it is identified as the region in which the dwelling place of bodhisattvas called Sudarśaka is located.

## ākāśaspharaṇa
*nam mkha’ khyab par byed pa*, Skt. *ākāśaspharaṇa*, Lit. “pervading space.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Kathendra
*gsung dbang*, Skt. *kathendra*, The 793rd buddha in the first list, 792nd in the second list, and 782nd in the third list.

## Kathok Dorjeden
Katok monastery was founded by Katok Dampa Deshek in Horpo, Kham, in 1159. It is the oldest of the six mother Nyingma monasteries and is one of the twenty-four sacred sites of Kham.

## Kathokpa Dampa
Kathokpa Dampa Deshek (1122–92) was the founder of Kathok monastery. His elder brother was Pakmodrupa Dorjé Gyalpo. He is one of the “three men from Kham” (khams pa mi gsum), three famous students of Gampopa from eastern Tibet.

## Kṣatriya
*rgyal rigs*, one of the four classes of the ancient Indian social system, the class of kings and warriors.

## Katyāyanī
*ka tya’i bu*, Skt. *katyāyanī*, A god.

## Kauśala
The name of a country in the north of the Indian subcontinent, it covered the area north of the city of Ayodhya in the present-day state of Uttar Pradesh. Also spelled Kośala.

## Kauśalyā
*ko sa la*, Skt. *kauśalyā*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Kauberī
*lus ngan gyi chung ma*, Skt. *kauberī*, A great mātṛkā.

## Kauṣṭhila
One of the foremost disciples of the Buddha, known for his skill in analytical reasoning. Also called Mahākauṣṭhila.

## Kau­śika
*kau shi ka*, Skt. *kau­śika*, An epithet of Indra.

## Kauśika
*kau shi ka*, Skt. *kauśika*, The name by which the Buddha (and other interlocutors) address Śakra (q.v.). Kauśika is a Brahmanical clan name, and its use as a personal name for Śakra is said to be a reference to his identity in his previous human rebirth. For more details of Śakra’s role in this text, see .

## Kauśikama
*kau shi ka ma*, Skt. *kauśikama*, A river on Excellence of Exquisite Intelligence.

## Kauṇḍinya
*kauN+Di n+ya*, Skt. *kauṇḍinya*, One of the five excellent companions, with whom Siddhārtha Gautama practiced asceticism near the Nairañjanā River and who later heard the [Buddha](#buddha) first teach the Four Noble Truths at the Deer [Park](#park) in Sarnath. Kauṇḍinya immediately realized its import and entered the stream, shortly thereafter [becoming](#becoming) an [arhat](#arhat).

## Kauṇḍinyagotra
*kauN+Di n+yas rigs*, Skt. *kauṇḍinyagotra*, Name of a past buddha. The Sanskrit literally means “one belonging to Kauṇḍinya’s lineage/family/clan.”

## Kauṇḍinyāyanīya
The name of a family lineage.

## Kauṇḍiṇyārcis
*kauN+Di n+ya ’od ’phro ba*, Skt. *kauṇḍiṇyārcis*, One of the tathāgatas.

*glang chen ma*, Skt. *kauñjarā*, A great rākṣasī.

## Kaṭuka
*ka Tu ka*, Skt. *kaṭuka*, A land to the north of Jambudvīpa.

## Kaulita
*pang nas skyes*, Skt. *kaulita*, Another name of Maudgalyāyana.

## Kauśāmbī
*kau shAm bI*, Skt. *kauśāmbī*, Home to a group of troublesome monks who quarreled with monks from Vaiśālī.

## Kauśāmbi
An ancient city that was the capital of Vatsa, a region down the Ganges River from Rājagṛha.

## Kaumārī
*gzhon nu ma*, Skt. *kaumārī*, One of the great mātṛs.

## Kaumārapaurikā
*gzhon nu’i grong khyer*, Skt. *kaumārapaurikā*, One of the two auxiliary pīlavas.

## Kaunḍinya
*kauN+Di n+ya*, Skt. *kaunḍinya*, A buddha.

## kaupīna
*dkris ma’i gos bzang*, Skt. *kaupīna*, A small piece of cloth covering just the genitals.

## Kaurava
*ko’u ra pa*, Skt. *kaurava*, The hundred sons of King Dhṛtarāśtra, who were the enemies of their cousins, the Pāṇḍava brothers. Their family name means they are the descendants of the ancient King Kur (as were the Pāṇḍava brothers). Their battle is the central theme of the Mahābhārata, India’s greatest epic.

## Kauravya
*kau rab bya*, Skt. *kauravya*, (1) The king of the country of Kuru. (2) A king in the past.

## Kautūhalika
*ltad mo can*, Skt. *kautūhalika*, A bodhisattva in the retinue of the Buddha.

## Kauthubha
A sublineage of the Sāmavedins.

## Kauthuma
One of the lineages within the Sāmaveda branch of the brahmanical tradition and one of the sublineages connected with the Gautama lineage.

## Kautsa
The brahmin lineage that descends from the sage Kutsa.

## Kauverī
*lus ngan phyogs*, Skt. *kauverī*, The term is used as a reference to the northern direction, which is governed by the deity Kubera.

## Kauverdu
*ke’u wer du*, Skt. *kauverdu*, A bodhisattva of the past.

## Kṛṣṇavajra
*nag po rdo rje*, Skt. *kṛṣṇavajra*, An Eleventh or Twelfth century Buddhist commentator. Wrote Recollection: a commentary on the Mahāmāyā Tantra.

## Ākāśavat
*nam mkha’ bzhin*, Skt. *ākāśavat*, A bodhisattva. (Toh 555: bsam pa nam mkha’ ci bzhin)

## Ākāśa­viśuddha­prajña
*nam mkha’ rnam dag shes rab*, Skt. *ākāśa­viśuddha­prajña*, A deva. (Toh 555: nam mkha’i blo gros rnam par dag pa)

## Kawa Paltsek
*ska ba dpal brtsegs*, An important early Tibetan translator and editor who was also one of the twenty-five principal disciples of Guru Padmasambhava.

## Kaya
*ka ya*, Skt. *kaya*, A member of the Śākya clan.

## Kṣaya
Skt. *kṣaya*, One of the grahas.

## Kaṣāyadhvajā
*ngur smrig gi rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *kaṣāyadhvajā*, Kaṣāyadhvajā (Saffron-Colored Banners) is a buddhafield inhabited by the Buddha Vajra­sāra­pramardin.

## Kaṣāyadhvaja
*ngur smrig gi rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *kaṣāyadhvaja*, The eastern realm in which Vāyuviṣṇu, the eldest of the thousand Veda-reciting pupils of Samudrareṇu, will become the Buddha Śalendrarāja.

## Kaśyapa
*’od srung*, Skt. *kaśyapa*, An Indian sage, also known as Pūraṇa Kaśyapa, who maintained the doctrine of non-action (akriyāvāda). Not to be confused with one of the Buddha’s foremost disciples, who had the same name.

## kṣayāpagata
*zad pa dang bral ba*, Skt. *kṣayāpagata*, Lit. “free from exhaustion.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Kāberi
*kA be ri*, Skt. *kāberi*, A river in the south of Jambudvīpa.

## Kābīra
*kA bI ra*, Skt. *kābīra*, A forest in Promotion.

## Kāñcī
*’ching bu*, Skt. *kāñcī*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## kācalindika
*ka tsa lin di ka*, Skt. *kācalindika*, A frequent simile for softness, thought to refer either (1) to the down of the kācilindika or kācalindika bird (see Lamotte, Etienne, La Concentration de la Marche Héroïque, Bruxelles: Peeters 1975, p. 261, n321), or (2) to a tropical tree bearing silken pods, similar to kapok, from which garments were made, and identified (Monier Williams p. 266) with Abrus precatorius.

## Kāñcana
The name of a country.

## Kāñcanadhvaja
*gser gyi rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *kāñcanadhvaja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Kāñcanamālā
“She Who Has a Golden Garland.” The daughter of King Kṛkin of Vārāṇasī in the distant past.

## Kāñcanamālikā
*gser phreng can*, Skt. *kāñcanamālikā*, The name of a female Buddhist deity, meaning “Garlanded with Gold,” here used as an epithet of Sitātapatrā.

## Kāñcanaparvata
*gser gyi ri bo*, Skt. *kāñcanaparvata*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Kāñcanaprabha
*gser gyi ’od*, Skt. *kāñcanaprabha*, The 614th buddha in the first list, 613th in the second list, and 607th in the third list.

## Kāñcanavarṇa
*dri med dag pa’i gser gyi mdog can*, Skt. *kāñcanavarṇa*, One of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Kācarā
*mi bzad ma*, Skt. *kācarā*, A great rākṣasī.

## kācilindika
*ka tsa lin di ka*, Skt. *kācilindika*, An epithet for softness, usually applied to cloth, and probably in reference, directly or metaphorically, to the down of the kācilindika bird. See Lamotte, Etienne. La Concentration de la Marche Héroïque. Bruxelles: Peeters (1975), p. 261, n. 321. The Mahāvyutpatti includes the term using the variant spelling kācalindika.

## kācilindika cloth
*gos ka tsa lin di ka*, Skt. *kācilindika*, A very soft substance. The Tibetan translators added “cloth” (gos) to the term.

## Kṛṣṇācārya
*nag po spyod pa*, one of the eighty-four [Mahāsiddhas](#mahāsiddha) of India.

## Keśa
*skra can*, Skt. *keśa*, One of the asuras.

## Keśaranandin
*ze ba dga’ ba*, Skt. *keśaranandin*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Keśarin
*ral pa can*, Skt. *keśarin*, A king, one of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Keśavā
*skra ldan ma*, Skt. *keśavā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Keśava
*skra ’dra*, Skt. *keśava*, One of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Keen Intelligence
*blo gros sems pa*, Skt. *blo gros sems pa*, Attendant of the second buddha Kusuma.

## keep it in mind
*zung shig*, Skt. *dhāraya*, (cf. Sanskrit text in Matsuda 2013, p. 940 ad Lamotte VIII.41). Dhāraya is a causative imperative of dhṛ-.

## keeper of the seals
*dam bzhag pa, phyag rgya pa*, Skt. *mudrāvāra*, The terms phyag rgya pa and dam bzhag pa are synonyms refering to one of several official administrative or managerial positions at a monastery.

## keeping it in mind
*gzungs*, Skt. *dhāraṇī*, Also rendered here as “dhāraṇī,” “formula.”

## Keśin
*rngog ldan*, Skt. *keśin*, A supernatural horse (bodhisattva), also known as Valāhassa, who saved shipwrecked persons from the island of man-eating rākṣasīs. See Rouse 1895, p. 127.

## Keśinī
*skra ldan ma*, Skt. *keśinī*, Young woman appointed by King Śākya Suprabuddha to look after the hair of his daughters Mahā­māyā and Māyā (the Buddha’s mother and aunt, respectively).

## Kekaya
The name of a people in northern India who were located around the Jhelum River in the Punjab.

## Kekāpino
*ke kA pi no*, Skt. *kekāpino*, A land to the west of Jambudvīpa.

## Kelikilī
*ki lI ki lI*, Skt. *kelikilī*, One of the goddesses associated with Amoghapāśa. Kelikilī appears to be a variant of the name Kelikilā, identified by multiple lexicographers as Rati, the wife of Kāmadeva.

## Kelikila
*ki lI kI la*, Skt. *kelīkila*, A yakṣa appearing in some of the paintings of Amoghapāśa. Also described as “great vajravināyaka” and “great king.” Kelikila is also associated with Śiva and referred to by the name Mahākelikila.

## Kelin
Skt. *kelin*, A yakṣa appearing in some of the paintings of Amoghapāśa.

## Kelīkīla
The name of a yakṣa.

## Kṣemā
*bde ba*, Skt. *kṣemā*, Lit. “Security.” Name of four lotus ponds, each located in one of the four gardens of the residence of the bodhisattva great being Dharmodgata, in the city of Gandhavatī.

## Kṣema
*dge ba*, Skt. *kṣema*, The 553rd buddha in the first list, 553rd in the second list, and 546th in the third list.

## Kṣemacitri
*bde bkra*, Skt. *kṣemacitri*, One of the kings of the asuras.

## Kṣemadā
*bde sbyin ma*, Skt. *kṣemadā*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Kṣemadatta
*bde bas byin*, Skt. *kṣemadatta*, A bodhisattva in the distant past.

## Kṣemaṅkarā
*bde byed ma*, Skt. *kṣemaṅkarā*, Princess of Vārāṇasī, child of King Brahmadatta (present), elder sibling of Prince Kṣemaṅkara.

## Kṣemaṃkara
*bde mdzad*, Skt. *kṣemaṃkara*, A buddha in the past. Note that there appear to be three distinct buddhas with the name Kṣemaṃkara as is listed at . See also .

## Kṣemaṅkara
*bde byed*, Skt. *kṣemaṅkara*, The son of King Brahmadatta (present) of Vārāṇasī and the younger brother of Princess Kṣemaṅkarā.

## Kṣemapriya
*dge dgyes*, Skt. *kṣemapriya*, The 937th buddha in the first list, 936th in the second list, and 927th in the third list.

## Kṣemarāja
*bde ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *kṣemarāja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Kṣemavatī
*bye ba ldan*, Skt. *kṣemavatī*, The mother of Suvarṇottamaprabhāsā, who was married to King Bimbisāra. She is likely to be the same person as Khemā in the Pali Canon, one of Bimbisāra’s consorts who became an arhat and bhikṣuṇī. See also .

## Kśemottamā
*bde ldan*, Skt. *kṣemottamā*, Lit. “Most Secure.” Name of four lotus ponds, each located in one of the four gardens of the residence of the bodhisattva great being Dharmodgata, in the city of Gandhavatī.

## Kṣemottamarāja
*dge mchog rgyal po*, Skt. *kṣemottamarāja*, The 375th buddha in the first list, 374th in the second list, and 369th in the third list.

## Kṣemāvatī
*bde ba yod pa*, Skt. *kṣemāvatī*, A four-continent world in the distant past.

## Keśāntā
*skra mthar byed ma*, Skt. *keśāntā*, One of the great yakṣiṇīs.

## Keśānta
*skra mthar byed*, Skt. *keśānta*, One of the vidyārājas dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Kṣepa
*’phen pa*, Skt. *kṣepa*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## kesara
*ke sa ra*, Skt. *keśara*, Kesara can be the name of several species of plants.

## Kesarin
*ral pa can*, Skt. *kesarin*, One of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Ketacīvara­saṃbhṛta­rāja
*gnas kyi gos bstsags rgyal po*, Skt. *ketacīvara­saṃbhṛta­rāja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Ketaka
*ke ta ka*, Skt. *ketaka*, An island in the vicinity of Jambudvīpa.

## Ketaka Fragrance
*ke ta ka’i dris bsgos pa*, Skt. *ketaka*, A river on Saṅkāśa.

## Ketako
*ke ta ko*, Skt. *ketako*, A land in the south of Jambudvīpa.

## Ketapuri
*gnas pa’i grong khyer*, Skt. *ketapuri*, The personal name of the Brahmā in the world and era of the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

## kṣetra
*zhing*, Skt. *kṣetra*, A type of power place where yogins and yoginīs congregate.

## Kṣetrālaṃkṛta
A bodhisattva in the audience of this sūtra, whose name is attested in the Vimalakīrti­nirdeśa.

## Ketu
“The Tail.” The celestial body personified as a serpent demon’s tail, which, according to ancient Indian astronomical conceptions, was responsible for lunar eclipses.

## Ketudhvaja
*tog gi rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *ketudhvaja*, The 823rd buddha in the first list, 822nd in the second list, and 812th in the third list.

## Ketumat
*dpal can*, Skt. *ketumat*, An unidentified mountain only mentioned in this sūtra. Possibly an alternative name for one of the seven golden mountain ranges encircling Sumeru.

## Ketuprabhā
*dpal gyi ’od*, Skt. *ketuprabhā*, An upāsikā in Dhanyākara.

## Ketuprabha
*tog ’od*, Skt. *ketuprabha*, The 552nd buddha in the first list, 552nd in the second list, and 545th in the third list.

## Ketuśrī
*dpal gyi dpal*, Skt. *ketuśrī*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Keturājñī
*tog gi rgyal po*, Skt. *keturājñī*, A wife of the ancient king Prajñāsārathi.

## Keturāja
*tog gi rgyal po*, Skt. *keturāja*, A buddha.

## Keturāṣṭra
*yul ’khor tog*, Skt. *keturāṣṭra*, The 674th buddha in the first list, 673rd in the second list, and 665th in the third list.

## Ketusvara
*tog gi sgra*, Skt. *ketusvara*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Ketuvatī
*tog ldan ma*, Skt. *ketuvatī*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Kevalaka
*dag pa*, Skt. *kevalaka*, A region in Magadha.

## key
*lde mig kyog po*, Skt. *kuñcikā*, Forms part of a pair with “lock” (Tib. lde mig).

## key lever
*dbyug gu skam ka*, Skt. *ajapadaka­daṇḍakā*, Used for opening windows.

## Keyūrā
*dpung rgyan ma*, Skt. *keyūrā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Keyūrabala
*dpung rgyan stobs*, Skt. *keyūrabala*, One of the sixteen gods guarding the seat of awakening.

## Keyūravatī
*dpung rgyan ldan ma*, Skt. *keyūravatī*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## kūṭāgāra
*pho brang brtsegs pa*, Skt. *kūṭāgāra*, Distinctive Indian assembly hall or temple with one ground-floor room and a high ornamental roof, sometimes a barrel shape with apses but more usually a tapering roof, tower, or spire, it contains at least one additional upper room within the structure. Kūṭāgāra literally means “upper chamber” and is short for kūṭāgāraśala, “hall with an upper chamber or chambers.” The Mahābodhi temple in Bodhgaya is an example of a kūṭāgāra.

## kūṭāgāra hall
*khang pa brtsegs pa*, Skt. *kūṭāgāra*, Distinctive Indian assembly hall or temple with one ground-floor room and a high ornamental roof, either a barrel shape with apses or, more usually, a tapering roof as a tower dome or spire, containing at least one additional upper room within the structure. Kūṭāgāra literally means “upper chamber” and is short for kūṭāgāraśala (“hall with an upper chamber or chambers”). The Mahābodhi Temple in Bodhgaya is an example of a kūṭāgāra.

## Kūṭāgāraśālā
An important early monastery outside Vaiśālī. Many texts specify, as in this sūtra, that it was located on the banks of the Monkey Pond (q.v.), while others (several Mahāyāna sūtras and the Theravādin literature) place it in the Mahāvana (“Great Forest”), also on the outskirts of Vaiśālī. The name Kūṭāgāraśālā means “hall with an upper chamber” or “gabled hall.” It refers to a temple with one ground-floor room and at least one additional upper room within the structure.

## kāṣṭhā
A measure of time defined as consisting of eight lavas. Sixteen kāṣṭhās make one kalā, which means that the duration of one kāṣṭhā is three seconds.

## Khaṇḍā
See “Khaṇḍaruhī.”

## Khāśa
*nam mkha’ srung*, Skt. *khāśa*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Khaśa
*kha sha*, Skt. *khaśa*, The Central Asian city-state more commonly known in Tibetan as li yul and in English as Khotan. Here mentioned as the region in which the dwelling place of bodhisattvas called Gośṛṇga is located.

## Khaṇḍa
*dum bu*, Skt. *khaṇḍa*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Khaṣa
*kha sha*, Skt. *khaṣa*, An alternative name for the ancient kingdom of Khotan which was located on the southern branch of the Silk Road that passed through the Tarim Basin. The kingdom, which was an important oasis and center for trade, existed during the first millennium ᴄᴇ.

## Khaṇḍadravja
*khaN Da dra ba bya*, Skt. *khaṇḍadravja*, One of the members of a group of four monks described in the Vinaya as followers of Devadatta that attempted to create a schism in the Buddhist saṅgha.

## Khaṇḍadravya
*khan da drab bya*, Skt. *khaṇḍadravya*, One of four cronies of Devadatta.

## Khaṣadroṇi
*lang ba*, Skt. *khaṣadroṇi*, Unidentified; the Tibetan translation could suggest the island of Langkawi. The Sanskrit text may be corrupt.

## Khaṇḍaka
*dum bu pa*, Skt. *khaṇḍaka*, A yakṣa general.

## Ākhaṇḍala
*mi phyed pa*, Skt. *ākhaṇḍala*, (Indra)

## Khaṇḍarohā
*dum skyes ma*, Skt. *khaṇḍaroha*, One of the seven types of ḍākinīs.

## Khaṇḍaruhī
One of the eight yoginīs in the Mahākāla maṇḍala described in Mahākāla’s Sovereign Tantra.

## Khadira
*seng ldeng pa*, Skt. *khadira*, A yakṣa who is a “Dharma brother” of Vaiśravaṇa.

## Khadiraka
*seng ldeng can*, Skt. *khadiraka*, One of the seven golden mountains.

## Khadiravaṇika
*seng ldeng nags pa*, Skt. *khadiravaṇika*, One of the monks attending this teaching in Śrāvastī, at Jeta’s Grove.

## Khadiravanika
*seng ldeng nags pa*, Skt. *khadiravanika*, A monk (bhikṣu) and disciple of the Buddha.

## Khadyota
*srin bu me khyer*, Skt. *khadyota*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Khaḍga
*ral gri*, Skt. *khaḍga*, One of the rāśis.

## Khagamati
*nam mkha’i blo gros*, Skt. *khagamati*, A nobleman in the retinue of the Buddha.

## Khaḍgapaṭṭiśā
*ral gri ma dang paT+Ti sa*, Skt. *khaḍgapaṭṭiśā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Khaḍgapāṇi
*ral gri gshin rje’i gshed*, Skt. *khadgapāṇi*, “Sword Yamāri.” An attendant figure/ deity in the maṇḍala of Black Yamāri.

## Khaḍgasoma
*ral gri zla ba*, Skt. *khaḍgasoma*, One of the māras.

## Khaḍgavajra
*rdo rje ral gri*, Skt. *khaḍgavajra*, Another name for Khaḍgapāṇi.

## Khaja
*’theng po*, Skt. *khaja*, One of the grahas.

## Śṛṅkhalā
*lu gu rgyud ma*, Skt. *śṛṅkhalā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Khalatika
*kha la ti ka*, Skt. *khalatika*, Name of a mountain in present day Bihar, possibly at Barabar. The mention of it in this sūtra, as its setting, is the only mention at all in the Kangyur.

## Khalvavāhana
One of the sublineages connected with the Māṇḍavya lineage of the brahmanical tradition.

## Kham
Located in eastern Tibet, Kham is today considered one of the three main provinces (chol kha gsum) of Tibet. Referred to in some earlier sources as “Lower Dokham” (mdo khams smad).

## Khampa Lotsāwa Bari Chödrak
*khams pa lo tsA wa ba ri chos grags*, Skt. *khams pa lo tsA wa ba ri chos grags*, 1040–11; the Tibetan translator and second throne-holding Sakya heirarch, also known as Bari Lotsāwa or Rinchen Drak (rin chen grags) who, along with this and many other texts, also translated ninety-three sādhanas that are grouped together under his name in the Tengyur.

## Khampa Lungpa
*khams pa lung pa (sgang sha'kya yon tan) (1025 - 1115), a [Kadampa](#kadampa) [lama](#lama), one of [Drom Tönpa's](#drom-tönpa) principal [disciple](#disciple)s.

## Kharak Gomchung, (Geshe)
*kha rag sgom chung*, an 11th century [Kadampa](#kadampa) [lama](#lama), [disciple](#disciple) of [Geshe](#geshe) Potowa. His name [means](#means) "Little Meditator of Kharak," and he was famous for his perseverance and strict application of the teachings. It is said that he received the teachings of the [Great Perfection](#great-perfection) and achieved the rainbow body.

## Kharakarṇa
*rna rtsub*, Skt. *kharakarṇa*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Kharaskandha
*rab sim byed*, Skt. *kharaskandha*, An asura king. (Toh 555: bong bu dpung; Toh 556, Degé: rab tshim byed; Toh 557, Yunglo and Peking: rab sil byed)

## Kharjūrikā
*’bra go can*, Skt. *kharjūrikā*, A village.

## Kharopoṣta
*bong srung sel*, Skt. *kharopoṣta*, A yakṣa general.

## Khasa
*kha sha*, Skt. *khasa*, A tribe of people from the northwest of India and central Asia who were significant in ancient India and are described in the Mahābhārata as having taken part in the Kurukṣetra war on the side of the Kurus against the Paṇḍavas. The Purāṇic literature generally describes them in a negative light, as barbarians. They are often mentioned in Buddhist literature and presently maintain Khasa culture in Himachal Pradesh.

## Khasarpāṇi
The name of a country.

## khaskhas grass
*u shi ra*, Skt. *uśīra*, Vetiveris zizanioides.

## Kāṣṭhavāṭa
*shing thags can*, Skt. *kāṣṭhavāṭa*, [Maudgalyāyana](#maudgalyāyana)'s birthplace.

## Khāṇḍava Forest
*khan da ba yi tshal*, Skt. *khāṇḍavavana*, A forest that is burned to the ground by Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna in the conclusion to the first book (ādiparvan) of the Mahā­bhārata.

## Khaṭvāṅga
a trident with many symbolic ornaments.

## khaṭvāṅga staff
A staff with a skull on top, it is said to resemble the foot of a bedstead (khaṭu). It is carried to indicate that one stands outside of society.

## khecarī
*mkha’ spyod*, Skt. *khecarī*, A type of ḍākinī (literally, “sky traveller”).

## Khedrub Jé
1385–1438. A famous Tibetan scholar trained in the Sakya school and the Kadampa lineage. He later became one of the foremost disciples of Tsongkhapa (tsong kha pa; 1357–1419). He became the third throne holder of Ganden monastery after Tsongkhapa, and posthumously was declared the first Paṇchen Lama (paN chen bla ma).

## Khedrup Jé
*mkhas grub rje*, Skt. *mkhas grub rje*, One of the principal pupils of Tsongkhapa, the founder of the Gelug tradition. Also retrospectively know as the first Panchen Lama (b. 1385−d. 1438).

## Khenchen Chim
See “Chim Chenpo Namkha Drak.”

## khichri
*zan dron*, Skt. *kulmāṣa*, A nourishing porridge that is made by boiling rice and lentils together.

## Khön Nāgendra Rakṣita
A Tibetan translator during the imperial period.

## khoṭī
The seeds of this plant are used to prepare pills and a collyrium that grant the ability to see subterranean chambers. Possibly identified as Boswellia thurifera.

## Khotan
*li yul*, Skt. *li yul*, An ancient kingdom, located on the southern branch of the Silk Route that passed through the Tarim Basin. The kingdom, which was an important oasis and center for trade, existed during the first millennium ce.

## Khotika
The name of a sage.

## Khārā
*khA rA*, Skt. *khārā*, A land to the north of Jambudvīpa.

## khārī
*khal*, Skt. *khārī*, A measure of capacity for commodities, especially barley, etc. (1 khal = 20 bre). See .

## Khu, Ngok and Drom
the three main [disciple](#disciple)s of [Atīśa](#atīśa). Their full names are Khuton Tsondru Yungdrung, Ngok Lekpai Sherab, and Drom Gyalwai Jungne ([Drom Tönpa](#drom-tönpa)).

## kāṇṭāhāvīkaja
An unidentified ritual ingredient.

## Ākhyadivya
*grags bzang*, Skt. *ākhyadivya*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Śāṅkhāyanīya
The name of a family lineage.

## Khyātikarī
*grags byed ma*, Skt. *khyātikarī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Khyungpo Yudri
There is little biographical information about Khyungpo Yudri but he seems to have been a scholar and scribe from the imperial period (eighth–ninth century) who was responsible for developing many of the common Tibetan scripts. He is said to have continued the calligraphic tradition of the famous translator Kawa Paltsek.

## Kāśi
*kA shi*, Skt. *kāśi*, Country whose capital was Vārāṇasī, in the Buddha’s time it had been absorbed into Kośala. Its monarch was Brahmadatta (past).

## Kiśaṭṭa
The name of a people in ancient India, possibly the same people as the Kisaṣṭas or Kisadyas mentioned in the Vāyupurāṇa (XLV 110).

## Kiṃbhīra
*ci ’jigs*, Skt. *kiṃbhīra*, One of the twelve great yakṣa generals who protect and serve those who bear, read, recite, copy, or commission a copy of the Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha­rāja­sūtra.

## Kiñcaka
*cung zad pa*, Skt. *kiñcaka*, A nāga king.

## Ākiñcanya
*ci yang med pa*, Skt. *ākiñcanya*, One of the gods’ realms; also used as the name of the gods living there.

## Kiñcinī
*cung zad can*, Skt. *kiñcinī*, A nāga king.

## kidney bean
*sran ma*, Skt. *māṣa*, Phaseolus mungo, Vigna mungo.

## kiṃkarī
Skt. *kiṃkarī*, Female kiṃkara.

## Kiṃkara
*mngag gzhug pa*, Skt. *kiṃkara*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## kiṅkara
*mngag gzhug*, Skt. *kiṅkara*, A class of supernatural beings who are utilized in service of the practitioner.

## Kiṃkarottama
*mngag gzhug mchog*, Skt. *kiṃkarottama*, ‟Best Servant,” one of the eight bhūta kings.

## Kila
*phur ba*, wrathful [deity](#deity), the activity aspect of all the [Buddhas](#buddha), a manifestation of [Vajrasattva](#vajrasattva). Practice related to this [deity](#deity) is based on the four aspects of [Kila](#kila), those of the ritual object, compassion, bodhicitta and awareness-wisdom.

## Killer of Haughty Obstructers
*dgra rig dregs ’joms gsod*, Skt. *dgra rig dregs ’joms gsod*, A kinnara king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## killing
*gsad pa*, Skt. *māraṇā*, A ritual activity for eliminating enemies, both human and non-human; also, one of the four main categories of ritual activity.

## killing and extracting
*gsad pa dang dgug pa*, The name of a meditative absorption.

## killing maṇḍala
*gsad pa’i dkyil ’khor*, A maṇḍala that is used to perform the ritual action of killing.

## killing mantra
*bsad pa’i gsang sngags*, A mantra that is used to perform the ritual action of killing.

## killing of living creatures
*srog gcod pa*, Skt. *prāṇātighāta*, First of the ten non-virtuous actions.

## killing rite
A particular class of tantric ritual.

## Kimbhīra
A yakṣa of Rājagṛha who interacts with the Buddha in chapter 2 of the Bodhisatva­piṭaka.

## Kimi
*ci smra*, Skt. *kimi*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## kimpaka
*bran pa*, Skt. *kimpaka*, A class of malevolent spirits.

## kimpala
*kim pa la*, Skt. *kimpala*, A musical instrument of an unidentified kind, though sometimes translated as “cymbals.”

## Kimphala
*kib pa la*, Skt. *kimphala*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Kimpilā
*kim pi la*, Skt. *kimpilā*, (1) A village. (2) A forest near the village of Kimpilā.

## Kimpila
*kim pi la*, Skt. *kimpila*, A disciple of the Buddha.

## kimpāka
*kim pa ka*, Skt. *kimpāka*, A fruit that looks appealing and has a delicious taste, but is poisonous when eaten. According to Chandra Das, it is the cucurbitaceous plant Trichosanthes palmata; also possibly Cucumis colocynthis.

## Kimīśvarabīja
*ci’i dbang phyug sa bon*, Skt. *kimīśvarabīja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Ḍākinī
*mkha' 'gro ma*, lit. moving through space. The feminine principle associated with [wisdom](#wisdom). This term has several [levels](#levels) of meaning. There are or ordinary ḍākinīs who are beings with a certain degree of spiritual power, and [wisdom](#wisdom) ḍākinīs who are fully realized. See [three roots](#three-roots).

*rnam par dag pa’i dkyil ’khor rgyal po*, Skt. *rnam par dag pa’i dkyil ’khor rgyal po*, A buddha.

## King of the Qualities of Liberation
*thar pa’i yon tan rgyal po*, Skt. *thar pa’i yon tan rgyal po*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Guṇadharma.

## King of the Roar of the Grounds
*sa’i nga ro rgyal po*, Skt. *sa’i nga ro rgyal po*, A great bodhisattva.

## King of the Seven
*bdun pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *saptirāja*, An epithet of the deity Paramāśva.

## King of the Sāla Abiding in the Precious Lotus
*rin po che’i pad ma la rab tu gnas pa sA la’i rgyal po*, Skt. *rin po che’i pad ma la rab tu gnas pa sA la’i rgyal po*, A buddha who resides in the eastern buddha realm called Pleasant Melodious Sound.

## King of the Solar Lamp
*nyi ma’i sgron ma’i rgyal po*, Skt. *nyi ma’i sgron ma’i rgyal po*, The name of bodhisattva Cloud Voice when he becomes a buddha.

## King of the Source of Yogic Discipline
*brtul zhugs ’byung ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *brtul zhugs ’byung ba’i rgyal po*, Son of the buddha Vijita.

## King of the Splendid Light of Deep Accumulations of Gold
*gser stug po bsags pa’i ’od gzi brjid kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *gser stug po bsags pa’i ’od gzi brjid kyi rgyal po*, A bodhisattva present in the circle around Śākyamuni.

## King of the Splendid Light of Excellent Gold
*gser bzangs nges ’od gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *gser bzangs nges ’od gzi brjid rgyal po*, Father of the buddha Akṣobhyavarṇa.

## King of the Splendor of Excellent Body
*lus bzangs gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *lus bzangs gzi brjid rgyal po*, Attendant of the buddha Brahmagāmin.

## King of the Splendor of Liberated Abandonment
*rnam par grol bas spong ba’i gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *rnam par grol bas spong ba’i gzi brjid rgyal po*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Cāritratīrtha.

## King of the Splendor of the Stainless Moon
*zla ba dri ma med pa’i gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *zla ba dri ma med pa’i gzi brjid rgyal po*, A buddha.

## King of the Stainless Heap
*sgrib pa med par brtsegs pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sgrib pa med par brtsegs pa’i rgyal po*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Hitaiṣin.

## King of the Star Mound Adorned with Signs
*mtshan gyis brgyan pa skar ma brtsegs pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *mtshan gyis brgyan pa skar ma brtsegs pa’i rgyal po*, A bodhisattva from King of All Śāla Trees’ buddha realm.

## King of the Summit of Power of the Victory Banner
*dbang po’i tog gi rgyal mtshan gyi rgyal po*, Skt. *dbang po’i tog gi rgyal mtshan gyi rgyal po*, A buddha who resides in the eastern buddha realm called Exquisitely Joyful.

## King of the Superknowledge of the Flower of Wisdom
*ye shes me tog mngon par shes pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *ye shes me tog mngon par shes pa’i rgyal po*, Attendant of the buddha Uttīrṇapaṅka.

## King of the Supreme Refuge
*skyabs mchog rgyal po*, Skt. *skyabs mchog rgyal po*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Jīvaka.

## King of the Tip of the Flash of Lightning
*glog ’od tog gi rgyal*, Skt. *glog ’od tog gi rgyal*, Name of the thus-gone one of the world system Flash of Lightning. Likely an alternate name for the thus-gone one King of the Tip of the Lamp of Lightning.

## King of the Tip of the Lamp of Lightning
*glog gi sgron ma tog gi rgyal po*, Skt. *glog gi sgron ma tog gi rgyal po*, Name of the thus-gone one of the world system Flash of Lightning.

## King of the Well-Settled Treasury of Peace
*gter legs par gnas pa zhi ba rgyal po*, Skt. *gter legs par gnas pa zhi ba rgyal po*, Name of the thus-gone one of the world system Victorious.

## King of the World
*’jig rten dbang phyug rgyal po*, Skt. *’jig rten dbang phyug rgyal po*, A buddha.

## King of Thunderous Voice
*’brug sgra’i dbyangs kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *’brug sgra’i dbyangs kyi rgyal po*, A buddha from the past.

## King of Timely Knowledge
*dus mkhyen rgyal po*, Skt. *dus mkhyen rgyal po*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Anupamavādin (675 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## King of Trees
*ljon pa’i dbang po*, Skt. *ljon pa’i dbang po*, Father of the buddha Atyuccagāmin.

## King of Truth
*bden pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *bden pa’i rgyal po*, Attendant of the buddha Avabhāsadarśin.

## king of vidyās
*rig pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vidyārāja*, This epithet can refer to individual mantras (vidyā) as well as deities—typically those attending upon Vajrapāṇi; most of the time the mantra and the deity are one and the same, but, in some contexts, the focus may be on either one or the other. If the focus is on the mantra or its corresponding deity, the term has been translated as king of vidyās, and if it is on the class of deities and is used in the plural, it has been translated as vidyārāja . Vidyārāja can also be a deity name.

## King of Virtue
*dge ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *dge ba’i rgyal po*, Birthplace of the buddha Dharmacchattra.

## King of Wealth
*’byor pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *’byor pa’i rgyal po*, Father of the buddha Samṛddha.

## King of Wisdom
*ye shes rgyal po*, Skt. *ye shes rgyal po*, Attendant of the buddha Śaśin.

## King of Wisdom Light
*ye shes ’od zer rgyal po*, Skt. *ye shes ’od zer rgyal po*, King of Wisdom Light is a buddha who inhabits a buddhafield.

## King Pile of Courage
*spobs brtsegs rgyal po*, Skt. *gandhavara*, A buddha.

## King Precious Moonlight of Pure Virtue
*dge ba dri ma med pa rnam dag rin chen zla ’od rgyal po*, Skt. *dge ba dri ma med pa rnam dag rin chen zla ’od rgyal po*, One of the bodhisattva great beings.

## King Resplendent Untarnished Jewel of Striking Color Who Has Perfect Conduct
One of the Seven Thus-Gone Ones.

## King Rhythm of a Lion’s Roar
*seng ge’i nga ro rnga sgra’i rgyal po*, Skt. *seng ge’i nga ro rnga sgra’i rgyal po*, A buddha of a past eon.

## King Roaring Sea of Renown in the Dharma
One of the Seven Thus-Gone Ones.

## King Roaring Splendor of Mastery Who Is Adorned with Lotuses, the Moon, and Jewels
One of the Seven Thus-Gone Ones.

## King Senalek
*sad na legs*, Skt. *sad na legs*, Also commonly known by the names Senalek Jingyön (sad na legs mjing yon) and Mutik Tenpo (mu tig bstan po), he was a Tibetan king who reigned ca 800/804–15. He was the youngest son of King Trisong Detsen (khri srong lde btsan, r. 742–98).

## King, Subject and Friend
*rje 'bangs grogs gsum*, King [Trisong Detsen](#trisong-detsen), the great translator [Vairotṣana](#vairotṣana) and the [ḍākinī](#ḍākinī) [Yeshe Tsogyal](#yeshe-tsogyal).

## King Śuddhodana
*rgyal po zas gtsang ma*, Skt. *śuddhodana*, The father of the Buddha.

## King Victory Banner at the Pinnacle of Goodness
*bzang po’i tog gi rgyal mtshan rgyal po*, Skt. *bzang po’i tog gi rgyal mtshan rgyal po*, Name of the thus-gone one of the world system Supreme Goodness. Likely the same as the thus-gone one Victory Banner at the Pinnacle of Goodness.

## King Who Holds the Peak of Great Mount Meru
The name of a bodhisattva.

## King Who Is Ornamented by the Arrangement of Prayers
*smon lam gyi bkod pas brgyan pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *praṇidhāna­vyūhālaṃkāra­rāja*, The name prophesied for the bhikṣus who will attain buddhahood in the eon Difficult to Conquer King of Radiance, in the realm called Vimalaprabhā.

## King Who Is Superior Due to Freedom from Fear and Timidity in Any Activity Since First Generating the Mind of Awakening
*dang po bskyed pa yid la mdzad pa rnam grangs bsnyengs pa dang bag tsha ba dang bral bas mngon par ’phags pa’i rgyal po*, A buddha in the southern direction in the present.

## King Who Rules the Peak of Meru
*lhun po’i rtse mo rdob pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *lhun po’i rtse mo rdob pa’i rgyal po*, A bodhisattva.

## King Who Transcends His Boundless Domain
*spyod yul dpag tu med pa las yang dag par ’das pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *spyod yul dpag tu med pa las yang dag par ’das pa’i rgyal po*, A buddha from the past.

## King Who Transcends the Light of Mount Meru
*ri rab kyi ’od las yang dag par ’das pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *ri rab kyi ’od las yang dag par ’das pa’i rgyal po*, A buddha from the past.

## King Yola
*rgyal po yo la*, Skt. *rgyal po yo la*, A king in Khotan. Identified by Thomas (1935, p. 25) as Yehu-la.

## king’s counselor
*sngags pa*, Skt. *mantrin*, See “mantrin.”

## Ḍākinījālasaṃvara
*mkha’ ’gro ma’i dra ba’i sdom pa*, Skt. *ḍākinījālasaṃvara*, An elaborate name of the deity Saṃvara; its meaning varies according to different interpretations.

## Kinkikirāta
*kin+ki ki rA tA*, Skt. *kinkikirāta*, A barbaric people in Jambudvīpa.

## kinnarī
*mi’am ci mo*, Skt. *kinnarī*, A class of semidivine beings, whose male counterpart is the kinnara. They resemble humans to the degree that their very name—which means “Is that a man?”—suggests some confusion as to their divine status.

## kinnara
*mi’am ci*, Skt. *kinnara*, A class of semidivine beings that resemble humans to the degree that their very name—which means “Is that a man?”—suggests some confusion as to their divine status. Kinnaras are mythological beings found in both Buddhist and Hindu literature, where they are portrayed as creatures half human and half animal (horse or bird). They are also usually depicted as highly skilled celestial musicians.

## Kinnara Melody
*mi’am ci’i dbyangs*, Skt. *mi’am ci’i dbyangs*, Mother of the buddha Mayūra.

## Kintu
*kin du*, Skt. *kintu*, A brahmin mentioned in connection with what is likely a story of a past life of the Buddha.

## Kṣiprakarī
*myur du byed ma*, Skt. *kṣiprakarī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## kiṃpuruṣa
*skyes bu ’am ci*, Skt. *kiṃpuruṣa*, A race of beings said to live in the Himalayas who have bodies of lions and human heads.

## kiraṇa
*g.yengs byed*, Skt. *kiraṇa*, A class of spirits related to kākhordas.

## Kirāta
*tsi ra ta*, Skt. *kirāta*, The name of an indigenous community attested in Sanskrit literature going back into the Vedic period.

## Kāśisundarī
*kA shi mdzes ldan ma*, Skt. *kāśisundarī*, “Beauty of Kāśi.” Princess of Vārāṇasī, child of Brahmadatta (present), who was extraordinarily beautiful and desired by six royal suitors. When her father announced she would choose her own spouse, she “chose” the Buddha, went forth, and manifested arhatship.

## Kṣiteśvara
Skt. *kṣiteśvara*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Kṣiti
Skt. *kṣiti*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Kṣitigarbha
*sa’i snying po*, Skt. *kṣitigarbha*, “Essence of Earth,” one of the “eight close sons of the Buddha,” and one of the most popular bodhisattvas in East Asia. In China he has been venerated in particular for his ability to rescue beings reborn in the hells, and in Japan as a protector of children and travelers.

## Kṣiti­garbha
*sa’i snying po*, Skt. *kṣiti­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Kṣitipāṇi
*sa’i phyag*, Skt. *kṣitipāṇi*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Kṣititoya
*sa chu*, Skt. *kṣititoya*, One of the māras.

## kiṃśuka
*king shu ka*, Skt. *kiṃśuka*, Butea frondosa, also known as flame of the forest; a tree with bright red flowers.

## Kiulang
*ki’u lang*, Skt. *ki’u lang*, An image of the Buddha.

## kiṇva
A fermenting agent used in producing liquor.

## Kūjaka Jalapatha
*lam chu sgra can*, Skt. *kūjaka jalapatha*, A mountain.

## kāñjika
*rang skyur*, Skt. *kāñjika*, The name for a number of plants and substances such as a fermented rice gruel, a medicinal plant, an edible legume, or a kind of creeping plant.

## Kākī
*bya rog ma*, Skt. *kākī*, A great piśācī.

## Kṛkī
*kr-i kI*, Skt. *kṛkī*, Monarch who covered Buddha Kāśyapa’s reliquary stūpa and the surrounding area with four kinds of jewels to the distance of one mile.

## Kākaṭi
*kha la byin*, Skt. *kākaṭi*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Kākanāda
*gser ngad can*, Skt. *kākanāda*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## kākhorda
A term used in hostile magical rites that can alternatively refer a class of nonhuman being or type of magical device employed against the target of the rite. They are often mentioned together with kṛtyās, who serve a similar function.

## Kūṭākhya
*brtsegs pa’i mtshan*, Skt. *kūṭākhya*, One of the pratyeka­buddhas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Kṛkin
A king of a Vārāṇasī in the distant past, during the time of the Buddha Kāśyapa.

## kāṅkṣocchedana
*nem nur gcod pa*, Skt. *kāṅkṣocchedana*, Lit. “that cuts off doubt.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## kākodumbarikā
*khwa dang ’dra ba’i shing u dum bA ra*, Skt. *kākodumbarikā*, Ficus oppositifolia.

## Kālī
A fearsome, wrathful goddess venerated in both non-Buddhist and Buddhist traditions. Here an epithet for Śrīdevī Mahākālī.

## Kāla
*nag po*, Skt. *kāla*, The Kāla Mountains of Bhāratvarṣa (i.e., India) are listed in the Mahābhārata as the mountain ranges Vindhya (separating the Deccan from north India), Mahendra (the eastern Ghats), Malaya (southern half of the Western Ghats), Sahya (the northern half of the Western Ghats), Rakṣavat (northeast extension of the Vindhya), Pāripātra, and the Sūktimat (or Śuktimat), which is presumably another name for the one remaining significant mountain range, the Arbuda in the northwest.

## Kāla Mṛgāraputra
*ri dags ’dzin gyi bu nag po*, Skt. *kāla mṛgāraputra*, A disciple of the Buddha.

## Kālacakra
One of the most important tantric cycles practiced in Tibet, it contains a unique and influential description of the cosmology of the universe.

## Kālagata
*dus las ’das*, Skt. *kālagata*, A world system.

## Kālaka
*nag po*, Skt. *kālaka*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## kālakūṭa
*kA la ku Ta*, Skt. *kālakūṭa*, A deadly poison that originated when the gods and asuras churned the oceans to create the nectar of immortality.

## kālakūṭa poison
*nag po brtsegs pa’i dug*, Skt. *kālakūṭa*, A type of vegetable poison typically listed among poisonous substances in Āyurvedic literature. The terms is also used as synonym for the halāhala poison.

## Kālaka’s Grove
*nag po’i kun dga’ ra ba*, Skt. *kālakārāma*, Grove offered to the Buddha by Kālaka, a wealthy man of Sāketa.

## Kālapāśā
*dus kyi zhags pa can ma*, Skt. *kālapāśā*, Literally, “the noose of time,” the term generally refers to the noose wielded by Yama, the lord of death. Because this term is in the feminine, it is likely meant to refer to the personification of that noose as a rākṣasī.

## Kālaparvata
Literally “black mountain.” According to traditional Buddhist cosmology, the Nine Black Mountains are found on the northern edge of the continent of Jambudvīpa. There are three sets of three peaks, and behind them lies the great snow mountain that is the source of the Ganges River. A description of this cosmology can be found in chapter three of the Abhidharma­kośabhāṣya of Vasubandhu.

## Kālarūpa
*kA la rU pa*, Skt. *kālarūpa*, “Black Form.” This seems to be an epithet of Mūrdhaṭaka, one of the wrathful emanations of Mañjuśrī.

## Kālarātrī
*dus kyi mtshan mo*, Skt. *kālarātrī*, The seventh of the nine forms of Durgā, also worshiped in tantric Buddhism.

## Kālasūtra
*thig nag po*, Skt. *kālasūtra*, The second of the traditional Buddhist list of eight hot hells—the “black cord” hell. Explanations vary as to whether these cords or wires cut through a person, burn them, or mark them for cutting up.

## Kālava
Skt. *kālava*, When used in the plural, this is the name of an ancient country.

## kleśa
*nyon mongs pa*, Skt. *kleśa*, In Classical Sanskrit, kleśa means “pain,” “torment,” or “affliction.” As a technical term in Buddhist Sanskrit the word takes on the specialized meanings “impurity” or “depravity” which refers to a number of negative qualities of the mind that contribute to sentient beings’ continued existence in saṃsāra. The basic three kleśas are ignorance, attachment, and aversion.

## Kāleya-Maitrāyaṇīya
The name of a Vedic school.

## Kāliñjara
*ka lany+dzi*, Skt. *kāliñjara*, Name of a country; inhabitant of this country.

## Kālikā
One of the eight yoginīs in the Mahākāla maṇḍala described in Mahākāla’s Sovereign Tantra.

## Kālika
*nag po*, Skt. *kālika*, The [nāga](#nāga) king who lauded Siddhārtha after he gave up his austerities and prepared to sit under the bodhi tree.

## Kālikasūtra
*nag po yod pa’i mdo*, Skt. *kālikasūtra*, No Sanskrit sūtra with this title is known. The title may correspond with the name Kālaka or Kokālika, a partisan of Devadatta (see AN X.87); see Kudo 2004, p. 229, n. 2.

## Kīlikīla
*kI li kI la*, Skt. *kīlikīla*, An esoteric deity, often included in the class of wrathful (krodha) deities.

## Kālodāyin
*nag po ’char ldan*, Skt. *kālodāyin*, According to the Pāli tradition, he was the the son of King Śuddhodana’s family priest or minister (purohita) and was a playmate of the young Siddhārtha in their early childhood. As a counselor to Śuddhodana, he was sent by the Buddha’s father to invite the recently enlightened son to pay a visit to his former home.

## Kāmā
*kA mA*, Skt. *kA mA*, One of the sixteen great kingdoms of ancient India.

## kūṣmāṇḍa
*grul bum*, Skt. *kūṣmāṇḍa*, A disease-causing demon, with an etymology of “little warm egg,” also used for benevolent deities. However, the Tibetan term used in the Kāraṇḍavyūha is more commonly used (as in the Mahavyutpatti concordance) to translate kumbhanda, a humanoid being with an animal’s head that dwells in the sea.

## Kāmadevī
*’dod pa’i lha mo*, Skt. *kāmadevī*, A deity in Vajrānaṅga’s maṇḍala.

## Kāmadeva
*’dod lha*, Skt. *kāmadeva*, God of love; the name of a vetāla.

## Kūṣmala
*kum b+ha la*, Skt. *kūṣmala*, Name of a yakṣa.

## Kāmaśreṣṭha
*’dod pa’i gtso bo*, Skt. *kāmaśreṣṭha*, A yakṣa who is a “Dharma brother” of Vaiśravaṇa.

## Kāmarūpī
*’dod pa’i gzugs can ma*, Skt. *kāmarūpī*, The name of a yakṣiṇī.

## Kāmarūpa
*kA ma rU pa*, Skt. *kāmarūpa*, One of the two kṣetras.

## Kāmarūpin
*’dod dgur sgyur ba’i gzugs can*, Skt. *kāmarūpin*, A mountain.

## Kāmaśāstra
*’dod pa’i bstan bcos*, Skt. *kāmaśāstra*, A treatise on love.

## Kāmavajriṇī
*’dod pa’i rdo rje dang ldan ma*, Skt. *kāmavajriṇī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Kāmbojī
*kam po dzi*, Skt. *kāmbojī*, A great rākṣasī.

## Kāmeśvarī
*’dod pa’i dbang phyug ma*, Skt. *kāmeśvarī*, ‟Goddess of Desire,” one of the eight great bhūtinīs as well as one of the eight great yakṣinīs.

## Kāmeśvara
*’dod pa’i dbang phyug*, Skt. *kāmeśvara*, Literally, “Lord of Desire.” Name of Kubera/Vaiśravaṇa.

## Kṛmi
*srin bu*, Skt. *kṛmi*, A nāga king.

## Kṛmiśa
*srin bu gnas*, Skt. *kṛmiśa*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Kṛmila
*srin bu can*, Skt. *kṛmila*, A mountain king.

## Kāminī
*’dod ldan ma*, Skt. *kāminī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Kāmpisiṃha
A king.

## Kṛṣnagotamaka
*gau ta ma ni nag po*, Skt. *kṛṣnagotamaka*, A nāga king.

## Ākāśānantya
*nam mkha’ mtha’ yas*, Skt. *ākāśānantya*, One of the gods’ realms; also used as the name of the gods living there.

## kneecaps are elegant
*pus mo’i lha nga dag mdzes par gyur pa*, Skt. *cāru­niṣpanna­jānu­maṇḍala­tā*, Third of the eighty minor marks.

## Künga Gyatso
Künga Gyatso was one of the sons of the sixth Degé king, Pönchen Könchok Lhunthup. He ordained and became a renowned practitioner.

## Künga Rinchen
The fifth Degé king, Künga Rinchen (b. late sixteenth century; d. early seventeenth century) was the head of the house of Degé in its thirty-fifth generation. He was the first of the Degé kings to have monastic vows. For more on his life see his entry at The Treasury of Lives.

## Künga Sangpo
Ngorchen Künga Sangpo (1382–1456) is a central figure in the Sakya school of Tibetan Buddhism. He founded Ngor Ewaṃ Chöden monastery, and the Sakya Ngor tradition with which Lhundrup Teng was affiliated.

## Knot of Joy
*be’u dga’*, Skt. *be’u dga’*, Son of the buddha Anilavegagāmin.

## Knower of Existence
*srid pa shes pa rtogs pa*, Skt. *srid pa shes pa rtogs pa*, A king and sage; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Knower of the Gathering
*bsdu ba mkhyen pa*, Skt. *bsdu ba mkhyen pa*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Vratatapas (448 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Knower of the Meaning
*don ni dgongs pa*, Skt. *don ni dgongs pa*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Vidyutketu (509 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Knower of the Origin as Related to Knowledge of the Past
*sngon kyi mtha’ shes pa kun ’byung ba shes pa yongs su rtogs pa*, Skt. *sngon kyi mtha’ shes pa kun ’byung ba shes pa yongs su rtogs pa*, A king; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Knower of the Past
*sngon kyi mtha’ shes pa yongs su rtogs pa*, Skt. *sngon kyi mtha’ shes pa yongs su rtogs pa*, A king; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Knower of the Vedas
*rig byed shes pa*, Skt. *rig byed shes pa*, A sage; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## knower of the world
Skt. *lokavid*, An epithet of a buddha. Here it is the sixth epithet through which the Buddha Śākyamuni is to be recollected when experiencing fear, trepidation, or terror.

## Knowing neither Increase nor Decrease
*spar ’chums ma yin*, Skt. *spar ’chums ma yin*, A great bodhisattva.

## knowledge
*shes rab*, Skt. *prajñā*, In this text shes rab seems to mean primarily knowledge (defined as insight and understanding one has gained through studying and experience), specifically knowledge of the teachings of the Buddha in general, and of karmic cause and effect in particular (Cf. Edgerton, BHSD, s.v. prajñā: “(Skt., and Pāli paññā), knowledge: three kinds, śrutamayī, cintāmayī, and bhāvanāmayī”, i.e., knowledge consisting in listening to the teachings, reflecting on them, and meditation (cultivating or internalizing the teachings). Also translated here as “knowledge of the Dharma.” See also .

## knowledge and seeing of liberation
Both knowing and directly accessing liberated knowing; the fifth of the five undefiled aggregates that are characteristic of noble ones.

## knowledge and vision of liberation
Both fully knowing and directly accessing the knowledge of liberation; the fifth of five qualities of the Saṅgha (the others being discipline, samādhi, wisdom, and liberation) that are also described in other texts as the five undefiled (or beyond-worldly) aggregates (skandha) characteristic of noble ones.

*smon nas shes pa*, Skt. *praṇidhijñāna*, See also .

## knowledge in accord with sound
*sgra ji bzhin shes pa*, Skt. *yathāruta­jñāna*, Eleventh of the eleven knowledges.

## knowledge incantation
*rig sngags*, Skt. *vidyā*, A type of incantation or spell used to accomplish a ritual goal. This can be associated with either ordinary attainments or those whose goal is awakening.

## Knowledge Joy
*shes dga’*, Skt. *shes dga’*, Son of the buddha Sujñāna.

## knowledge mantra
*rig sngags*, Skt. *vidyā*, A type of incantation used in meditative and ritual contexts.

## knowledge of a knower of path aspects
*lam gyi rnam pa shes pa nyid kyi shes pa*, Skt. *mārgākāra­jñatā­jñāna*, Also referred to as “knowledge of paths,” it is the knowledge of a bodhisattva.

## knowledge of all aspects
*rnam pa thams cad mkhyen pa nyid*, Skt. *sarvākāra­jñatā*, See “three types of omniscience.”

## knowledge of all the dharmas
*thams cad shes pa*, Skt. *sarvajñatā*, Literally “knowledge of all” or “all-knowing,” but here rendered “knowledge of all the dharmas” rather than “omniscience.” In the Prajñāpāramitā literature, this is a technical term that refers to the full extent of knowledge realized by arhats and pratyekabuddhas, comprising particularly their understanding of the absence of a self in the aggregates, sense fields, and sensory elements. The term might intertextually refer to a discourse found in the Saṁyutta Nikāya/Saṁyuktāgama (SN 35:23/SĀ 319) in which the Buddha describes “the all” as the twelve sense fields. It is the third of the eight main topics or “clear realizations” of The Ornament of Clear Realization.

## knowledge of dharma
*chos shes pa*, Skt. *dharmajñāna*, See also .

## Knowledge of Gathering
*bsdu ba’i blo mnga*, Skt. *bsdu ba’i blo mnga*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Vighuṣṭarāja (532 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

*’dris pa shes pa*, Skt. *paricayajñāna*, Tenth of the eleven knowledges.

## knowledge of paths
*lam gyi rnam pa shes pa nyid*, Skt. *mārgajñatā*, See “three types of omniscience.” Also referred to as the “knowledge of a knower of path aspects,” it is the knowledge of a bodhisattva.

*chos shes pa*, Skt. *dharmajñāna*, Seventh of the eleven aspects of knowledge.

## knowledge of phenomena that is subsequently realized

## knowledge of relative appearances
*kun rdzob shes pa*, Skt. *saṃ­vṛti­jñāna*, Fourth of the eleven aspects of knowledge.

## knowledge of suffering
*sdug bsngal shes pa*, Skt. *duḥkhajñāna*, First of the eleven aspects of knowledge.

## knowledge of the aspects of the path
*lam gyi rnam pa shes pa nyid*, Skt. *mārgākāra­jñatā*, A key term in the Prajñā­pāramitā texts denoting the form of omniscience (‘knowing all’) that bodhisattvas progressively attain, the knowledge of all paths, including knowledge not only of their own path but also of the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. However, note that although this term is used with this meaning (and can be glossed as the second of the eight topics elucidated in the Abhisamayālaṃkāra), in the original formulation of the eight topics in the Abhisamayālaṃkāra the term used is simply mārgājñāta (lam shes pa nyid), “knowledge of the paths.”

## knowledge of the cessation
*’gog pa shes pa*, Skt. *nirodhajñāna*, Third of the eleven knowledges.

## knowledge of the cessation of suffering
*’gog pa shes pa*, Skt. *ni­rodha­jñāna*, Seventh of the eleven aspects of knowledge.

## knowledge of the conventional
*kun rdzob shes pa*, Skt. *saṃvṛtijñāna*, Ninth of the eleven knowledges.

## knowledge of the Dharma
*shes rab*, Skt. *prajñā*, See entry “knowledge” and also .

## knowledge of the extinction of contaminants
*zad par shes pa*, Skt. *kṣayajñāna*, Fifth of the eleven aspects of knowledge.

## knowledge of the origin
*kun ’byung ba shes pa*, Skt. *samudayajñāna*, Second of the eleven knowledges.

## knowledge of the origin of suffering
*kun ’byung ba shes pa*, Skt. *samudayajñāna*, Second of the eleven aspects of knowledge.

## knowledge of the path
*lam gyi rnam pa shes pa nyid*, Skt. *mārgākāra­jñatā*, A key term in the Prajñā­pāramitā texts denoting the (incomplete) equivalent of omniscience that bodhisattvas progressively attain, including knowledge not only of their own path but also of the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. It is the second of the eight main topics or “clear realizations” of The Ornament of Clear Realization. In this text it is explained clearly in chapter 58 at -.

*kun rdzob shes pa*, Skt. *saṃvṛtijñāna*, Ninth of the eleven aspects of knowledge.

*brtul zhugs shes*, Skt. *brtul zhugs shes*, Father of the buddha Amitalocana.

## knowledge that engages in subtlety
*phra ba la ’jug pa’i mkhyen pa*, Skt. *sūkṣma­praveśa­jñāna*, The various aspects of the knowledge that engages in subtlety of conduct, etc. include the knowledge that engages with subtle transmigration at the time of death, the knowledge that engages with subtle processes of rebirth, and the knowledge that engages with subtle buddha activities—emanation, renunciation, manifestly perfect enlightenment, turning the wheel of the sacred doctrine, consecrating the lifespan, passing into final nirvāṇa, and so forth. (See also .)

## koṭampa cloth
*ko tam pa'i ras*, Skt. *koṭambaka*, An acceptable form of cloth for a monk, as identified in the [Four Supports](#four-supports) [section](#section) of the ordination ritual. A low-grade cloth made from kotampa fibers or kausheyam [silk](#silk) and [linen](#linen) or cotton weave.

## Koṣṭhila
*stod rings*, Skt. *koṣṭhila*, Maternal uncle of [Śāriputra](#śāriputra) and son of [Māṭhara](#māṭhara). He went south to [study](#study) Lokāyata philosophy with [Tiṣya](#tiṣya). He later returned to [study](#study) Lokāyata philosophy with an order of wandering [ascetic](#ascetic)s, pledged not to cut his nails so long as he upheld Lokāyata philosophy and became known as [Dīrghanakha](#dīrghanakha), "He Who Has Long Fingernails."

*mdzad pa*, Skt. *kriyā*, A mere ritual performance (in contradistinction to karman, which is the same performance aiming at a particular outcome). The term is also used to denote a class of tantras, the Kriyā tantras.

## Kriyā (yoga)
*bya ba*, the first of the three outer [tantras](#tantra), the fourth of the nine [vehicle](#vehicle)s. In this type of practice the stress is mainly put on correct external behavior and cleanliness.

## Kriyātantra
*bya ba’i rgyud*, Skt. *kriyātantra*, A class of tantric scripture that generally features elaborate rites directed toward both mundane goals‍—such as health, prosperity, and protection‍—and to the ultimate goal of liberation. In this class of tantra, the practitioners do not identify themselves with the deity as in other classes of tantra, but rather seek their power, assistance, and intervention in pursuit of their goals. The Mañjuśrī­mūla­kalpa and Amoghapāśa­kalpa­rāja exemplify this class of tantra.

## kārākāra
*bya ba byed pa*, Skt. *kārākāra*, Lit. “does what needs to be done.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

*ru sbal*, Skt. *kūrma*, One of the avatars of Viṣṇu.

*rnam pa dor ba med pa*, Skt. *ākārānavakāra*, Lit. “not forsaking any aspect.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## krośa
A measure of distance defined as being equal to one thousand bows, presumably about 1.8 kilometers. It is considered to be the distance a voice can reach in “calling” (krośa). In the Abhidharmakośa (III 87), Vasubandhu defines a krośa as consisting of five hundreds bows, and he comments that it is the minimum distance at which a hermitage should be situated from the nearest village.

## Krodharāja
*khro bo’i rgyal po*, Skt. *krodharāja*, “Lord of Wrath,” usually an epithet of Vajrapāṇi but also applied to other wrathful deities, such as the wrathful lords of the four families—tathāgata, lotus, jewel, and vajra. In the AP it is mainly used to refer to the wrathful aspect of Amoghapāśa; in this sense he is called, on at least one occasion, Amogha­krodha­rāja.

*khro bo’i rgyal po lcags kyu*, Skt. *krodha­rājāṅkuśa*, Seems to be an elaboration of the name Krodhāṅkuśa.

## Krodhāṅkuśa

*grags pa’i dbang phyug rgyal po*, Skt. *kīrtīśvararāja*, A buddha in an eastern buddha realm.

## Kāruṇika
*snying rje can*, Skt. *kāruṇika*, This name refers to two people in this text: (1) A captain; a former incarnation of the Buddha while he was a practicing bodhisattva. (2) A prince; a former incarnation of the buddha while he was a practicing bodhisattva.

## Kāruṇya
*snying rje*, Skt. *kāruṇya*, One of the two pīlavas.

## kāsa

## ākāśāsaṃga­vimukti­nirupalepa
*nam mkha’ ltar chags pa med pas rnam par grol zhing gos pa med pa*, Skt. *ākāśāsaṃga­vimukti­nirupalepa*, Lit. “unattached, liberated, and uncovered like space.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Kṛtajña
*drin gzo*, Skt. *kṛtajña*, Known in the Avadāna literature as a previous life of the Buddha, his name is translated there as byas shes. In that tale, his brother (a previous life of Devadatta) gouges out his eyes. Nonetheless, a princess chooses him for a husband and is banished by her father, the king. When she speaks the words of truth of her love for him, one of Kṛtajña’s eyes is restored. When he speaks the words of truth that he has no hate for his brother, his other eye is restored, and he is enthroned by the king as his successor. YJ’s translation is slightly different and does not feature Kṛtajña as a personage but rather as an adjective (報恩語 bao’en yu “words of repaying kindness”).

## Kṛtavarman
*go bgos*, Skt. *kṛtavarman*, The 383rd buddha in the first list, 382nd in the second list, and 376th in the third list.
