## radish
*la phug*, Skt. *mūlaka*, The Tantra of Great Gaṇapati specifies that this is a type of mustard root (yungs ma) and describes it as “the most supreme of all foods,” that is said to contain the eight supreme flavors (bitter; sour; astringent; sweet; spicy; salty; juicy; and savory) that act as antidotes to eight classes of diseases. It is also used as one of the primary bali offerings (gtor ma, bali) that is offered to Gaṇapati.

## Śāradvatīputra
*sha ra dwa ti’i bu*, Skt. *śāradvatīputra*, Also known as Śāriputra. Along with Maudgalyāyana, he was one of the Buddha Śākyamuni’s two main bhikṣu disciples, renowned for his wisdom and pure observance of discipline. His father, Tiṣya, named him Śāriputra (Śārikā’s Son) to honor Śāriputra’s mother Śārikā.

## Śāradvatī­putra
*sha ra dwa ti’i bu*, Skt. *śāradvatī­putra*, More widely known as Śāriputra—the contracted version of his name—he was one of the Buddha’s foremost hearer disciples. Renowned for unparalleled knowledge of the teachings.

## Raṇemin
*g.yul gyi mu khyud*, Skt. *raṇemin*, One of the thousand sons of King Araṇemin.

## rag
*ras*, Skt. *karpaṭa*, This can refer to any worn out or soiled cloth, often derived from an impure source. It can serve as the surface on which a diagram or image is drawn, a mantra is written, or it can be a material ingredient for a specified rite.

## śūraṅgama
*dpa’ bar ’gro ba*, Skt. *śūraṅgama*, Lit. “heroic march.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## śūraṃgama absorption
*brgyan pa’i ting nge ’dzin*, Skt. *śūraṃgama­samādhi*, The Tibetan here, which could be translated “the ornamented absorption,” is tentatively assumed to represent the same absorption as the Chinese, usually used for the śūraṃgama absorption, a meditative state that enables one to overcome obstacles, with widespread mentions in the canonical texts but in Tibetan usually rendered dpa’ bar ’gro ba’i ting nge ’dzin.

## raging fever
*rims drag po*, Skt. *prajvara*, symptom that may be evidence of an illness considered an impediment to ordination.

## Rahagarjita
*gsang bsgrags*, Skt. *rahagarjita*, A bodhisattva sent by the Buddha Vimalateja­guṇa­rāja to pay homage to Śākyamuni.

## Rahuśa
*ra hu sha*, Skt. *ra hu sha*, Son of the buddha Dharmakīrti.

## railing
*kha khyer*, Skt. *vedikā*, The Blessed One ordered railings be built on the second story of meditation halls to prevent monks from falling to the ground. This word can also mean “balcony.”

## Rain Cloud
*char sprin gyi sprin*, Skt. *char sprin gyi sprin*, A tathāgata.

## Rain of Burning Stones
*rdo me ’bar ba char ltar ’bab pa*, Skt. *rdo me ’bar ba char ltar ’bab pa*, One of sixteen realms that surround the Howling Hell.

## Rain of Jambu Gold
*’dzam bu na da char ’bebs*, Skt. *’dzam bu na da char ’bebs*, A forest in Born in a Lap.

## Rain of the Sacred Dharma
*dam pa’i chos kyi char phab*, Skt. *dam pa’i chos kyi char phab*, A stūpa.

## Rain of Tossed Lotuses
*pad ma rab tu gtor ba’i char pa*, Skt. *pad ma rab tu gtor ba’i char pa*, A great bodhisattva.

## Rain of Weapons
*mtshon ’bab pa*, Skt. *śastrasāmpāti*, One of sixteen realms that surround the Reviving Hell.

## Rain River
*char dang char gyi rjes su ’byung ba’i chu klung*, Skt. *char dang char gyi rjes su ’byung ba’i chu klung*, A river on Saṅkāśa.

## Rainfall
*char ’bebs*, Skt. *char ’bebs*, Rainfall (the fall of rain, or the amount that falls), also the name of a virtuous nāga king.

## Rainfall from the Clouds of Dharma
*chos kyi sprin gyi char rab tu ’babs pa*, Skt. *chos kyi sprin gyi char rab tu ’babs pa*, A buddha.

## raised uṣṇīṣa
*gtsug tor ’phags pa*, Skt. *uṣṇīṣonnata*, The uṣṇīṣa, described in this text as “raised” (Skt. unnata) is one of the most prominent of the thirty-two signs of a great being and is often placed first or last in the list. In its simplest form it is an elevated shape of the head, like a turban (the Sanskrit term uṣṇīṣa in fact means “turban”), or more elaborately a dome-shaped extension. The extension is described as having various magical attributes such as emitting and absorbing rays of light or reaching such an immense height that the gods are incapable of flying over it.

## Raivata
*nam gru*, Skt. *raivata*, A sagely priest who hosts Prince Siddhārtha after he leaves his home.

## Raja
*rdul*, Skt. *raja*, One of the rāśis.

## Rajaniṃdhara
*mtshan mo ’dzin*, Skt. *rajaniṃdhara*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## rajas
*rdul*, Skt. *rajas*, One of the three principles or forces of nature, as known in the Sāṃkhya philosophy, characterized by energy and movement.

## rajobhuva
*rdul tshon sa*, Skt. *rajobhuva*, A particular part of the maṇḍala (?); the Tibetan reads “sand-colored ground”.

## rajopagata
*rdul dang bral ba*, Skt. *rajopagata*, Lit. “dust free.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Rajovimala­tejaḥśrī
*gzi brjid rdul gyi dri ma myed pa*, Skt. *rajovimala­tejaḥśrī*, A world realm in the distant past.

## Rakṣaka
*srung ba po*, Skt. *rakṣaka*, One of the thousand sons of King Araṇemin.

## Ārakṣapati Megheśvaradīpa
*kun tu srung ba’i bdag po sprin gyi dbang phyug mar me*, Skt. *kun tu srung ba’i bdag po sprin gyi dbang phyug mar me*, A buddha.

## Rakṣitikā
*srung ba mo*, Skt. *rakṣitikā*, A great piśācī.

## Raktamāli
*dmar phreng can*, Skt. *raktamāli*, A nāga king.

## Raktāṅga
*lus dmar po*, Skt. *raktāṅga*, An esoteric deity, sometimes counted as a king of vidyās (vidyārāja).

## Ralpachen
*khri ral pa can*, Skt. *khri ral pa can*, Considered to be the third great Dharma king of Tibet, he was the grandson of Trisong Detsen and reigned from 815 to 838 or 841. His reign saw the expansion of Tibet’s political dominion to its greatest extent, and a significant continuation of the “early period” of imperially sponsored text translation, the end of which is traditionally marked by the end of his reign.

## Ralpachen’s Six Volume Hundred Thousand
A manuscript translation of The Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred Thousand Lines that appears to have been named after Ralpachen, the forty-first king of Tibet.

## Ram
A clan or tribe in Tibet. According to the Catalog, one of the eighteen tribes of Nguchen Gyalmo, belonging to the divine lineage of Go.

## Raśmī
*’od can ma*, Skt. *raśmī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## śramaṇa
*dge sbyong*, Skt. *śramaṇa*, The word śramaṇa refers to ascetics/religious practitioners who are often distinguished from brāhmaṇa (brahmins). It seems that a common characteristic of śramaṇas was to have “gone forth” (pravrajita), i.e., to not be householders, or at least this is how the Buddhist commentarial tradition understands the term. At some point, the term also became an established way to distinguish non-Vedic ascetics from those who followed the Vedas; renunciates, not just Buddhists, could be called śramaṇa if they were not within the Vedic/brahminical fold. Thus, the term has several layers of meaning, and it was such a key term in Buddhist texts that the result of practice came also to be known as “the fruit of being a śramaṇa” (Skt. śrāmaṇyaphala, Pāli sāmaññaphala); the Buddha himself is epitomized as “the great śramaṇa” (mahāśramaṇa) in one of the most famous Buddhist verses (the ye dharmā stanza, found in colophons and epigraphy throughout the Buddhist world). The term śramaṇa is formed from the root śram, most likely in the sense of “to exert oneself” (tapasi). This is reflected in the second element of its Tibetan translation (sbyong, which is sometimes used as a translation of abhyāsa); thus, śramaṇas are—as per the Tibetan rendering—those who exert themselves (sbyong) toward virtue (dge). The reference to virtue may be connected to an etymology found in the Sanskrit Udānavarga and Pāli Dhammapada, according to which one is a śramaṇa if one has pacified sins (śamitatvāt tu pāpānāṁ śramaṇo hi nirucyate, Udānavarga 11.14, Berhard 1965, p. 190; sdig pa zhi ba de dag ni/ dge sbyong nyid ces brjod par bya, Udānavarga Tib. 11.15; Zongtse 1990, p. 127; samitattā hi pāpānaṃ samaṇo ti pavuccati | Dhammapada verse 265). Commentarial literature occasionally distinguishes between this as the higher sense of śramaṇa vs. the more ordinary sense of being a śramaṇa/samaṇa “only due to having gone forth” (pabbajjāmattasamaṇo); this distinction appears in contexts where the word is together with “brahmins,” as it often happens in sūtras/suttas (yaṃ no payirupāsato cittaṃ pasīdeyyāti vuttattā samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vāti ettha paramatthasamaṇo ca paramatthabrāhmaṇo ca adhippeto na pabbajjāmattasamaṇo na jātimattabrāhmaṇo cāti āha samitapāpatāya samaṇaṃ | bāhitapāpatāya brāhmaṇanti | Ṭīkā on the Sāmaññaphalasutta, Sīlakkhandavagga, Dīghanikāya). The Kāśyapa­parivarta­sūtra lists four types of śramaṇa: one who is so only in outer appearance (varṇa­rūpa­liṅga­saṃsthāna­śramaṇa), one who is hypocritical and hides their real conduct (ācāra­gupti­kuhaka­śramaṇa), one who does everything for the sake of fame (kīrti­śabda­śloka­śramaṇa), and one who practices genuinely (bhūta­pratipatti­śramaṇa). (See Vorobyova-Desyatovskaya 2002, pp. 41–44).

## śramaṇa attendant
A junior monk who is an attendant or disciple of an elder monk, literally one who follows behind.

## Śramaṇa Gautama
*dge sbyong gau ta ma*, Skt. *śramaṇa gautama*, “The renunciant Gautama,” the name by which the Buddha might have been referred to prior to his enlightenment or by those who were not his followers.

## Śramaṇa King
*dge sbyong rgyal po*, Skt. *dge sbyong rgyal po*, A buddha.

## Śramaṇa­maṇḍala
*dge sbyong gi dkyil ’khor*, Skt. *śramaṇa­maṇḍala*, A land in South India.

## śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas
*dge sbyong ngam bram ze*, Skt. *śramaṇa­brāhmaṇa*, A common two-member compound (dvandva) found as a stock phrase in Buddhist literature to refer broadly to two distinct systems of spiritual orientation and practice in early India. The term “śramaṇa” (Tib. dge sbyong) refers to those who took vows in non-brahmanical spiritual systems that focused on asceticism, renunciation, and monasticism. The term “brāhmaṇa” (Tib. bram ze) refers in this context not so much to brahmans in terms of caste identity alone but rather to those who actively participated in the Vedic tradition of learning and the ritual worship of brahmanical deities, mostly within the context of a householder lifestyle.

## Ramaṭha
The name of a people in the northwest of the Indian subcontinent, who were located on the banks of the lower Indus.

## Ramatha
*dga’ dang ldan*, Skt. *ramatha*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Ramayo
*ra ma yo*, Skt. *ramayo*, A sea to the west of Jambudvīpa.

## ārambanacchedaḥ
*dmigs pa gcod pa*, Skt. *ārambanacchedaḥ*, Lit. “objective support cut off.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Rambhā
*rtsom ma ma*, Skt. *rambhā*, An asparas; one of the eight goddesses of offerings in the Bhūtaḍāmara maṇḍala.

## Raśmi
*’od zer*, Skt. *raśmi*, The 93rd buddha in the first list, 93rd in the second list, and 94th in the third list.

## Raśmi­śata­sahasra­paripūrṇa­dhvaja
*’od zer brgya stong yongs su rdzogs pa’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *raśmi­śata­sahasra­paripūrṇa­dhvaja*, The name of Yaśodharā when she becomes a buddha in the future.

## Raśmi­candrorṇa­megha
*’od gzer zla ba mdzod spu’i sprin*, Skt. *raśmi­candrorṇa­megha*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Raśmidhvajā
Name of a buddha domain to the west of our world and presided over by the Buddha Raśmirāja. The name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Raśmi­guṇa­makuṭa­jñāna­prajñā­prabha
*’od gzer yon tan gyi cod pan ye shes dang shes rab kyi ’od*, Skt. *raśmi­guṇa­makuṭa­jñāna­prajñā­prabha*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Raśmijāla
*’od zer dra ba*, Skt. *raśmijāla*, The 697th buddha in the first list, 696th in the second list, and 687th in the third list.

## Raśmikūṭa
*’od zer brtsegs*, Skt. *raśmikūṭa*, A buddha.

## Raśmiketu
Skt. *raśmiketu*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Raśmi­maṇḍala­śikhara­rāja
*’od gzer gyi dkyil ’khor spo’i rgyal po*, Skt. *raśmi­maṇḍala­śikhara­rāja*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Raśmimaṇḍala­jyotiprabhāsa­rāja
*’od zer gyi dkyil ’khor snang ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *raśmimaṇḍala­jyotiprabhāsa­rāja*, One of ten names of a thousand buddhas prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha, with presumably a hundred buddhas having this name.

## Raśmi­mukha
*’od zer gyi zhal*, Skt. *raśmi­mukha*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Raśmi­netra­pratibhāsa­prabha­candra
*’od gzer gyi tshul rab tu snang ba’i ’od kyi zla ba*, Skt. *raśmi­netra­pratibhāsa­prabha­candra*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## raśminirhāra
*’od zer sgrub pa*, Skt. *raśminirhāra*, Lit. “light-ray producer.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Raśmi­parvata­vidyotita­megha
*’od gzer gyi ri bo rnam par snang ba’i sprin*, Skt. *raśmi­parvata­vidyotita­megha*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Raśmiprabhāsa
*’od zer rab tu snang ba*, Skt. *raśmiprabhāsa*, The name Kāśyapa will have when he becomes a buddha in the distant future.

## raśmipramukha
*’od zer rab tu ’gyed pa*, Skt. *raśmipramukha*, Lit. “diffusion of light rays.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Raśmirāja
The buddha in the buddha domain Raśmidhvajā, attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Raśmi­saṃkusumita­pradīpa
*’od gzer gyi me tog kun tu rgyas pa’i sgron ma*, Skt. *raśmi­saṃkusumita­pradīpa*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Raśmivyūha
*’od zer gyi bkod pa*, Skt. *raśmivyūha*, “Array of Light Rays.” Name by which Vimalaśraddhā will be known upon her attainment of buddhahood.

## Ramoché
One of the oldest and most important Buddhist temples in Tibet. Located in Lhasa, it was founded in the seventh century by King Songtsen Gampo (srong btsan sgam po) and houses the Jowo Mikyö Dorjé (jo bo mi bskyod rdo rje) and contains the statue of the buddha Akṣobhya that tradition tells us was brought to Tibet as a gift by Songtsen Gampo’s Nepalese wife Bhṛkuṭī.

## rare
*brgya la las*, Skt. *brgya la las*, brgya la las is literally “one in a hundred.” Also rendered here as “rarely,” “should it be the case that,” and “should it happen that.”

## Ūrṇa­śrī­prabhāsa­mati
*mdzod spu’i dpal gyi ’od kyi blo gros*, Skt. *ūrṇa­śrī­prabhāsa­mati*, A buddha in the distant past.

## rasa
*ra sa*, Skt. *rasa*, Guggulu or Commiphora mukul (McHugh 2008, p 180 n28).

## Rasalandhi
The name of a city.

## rasanā
*ro ma*, Skt. *rasanā*, The prāṇa channel on the right side of the body.

## Rasana
A king.

## Śūrasena
*dpa’ sde*, Skt. *śūrasena*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Rasātala
*sa’i ’og*, Skt. *rasātala*, One of the seven subterranean semiparadises, the abode of dānavas.

## rasāyana
*sman bcud kyis len*, Skt. *rasāyana*, The extraction of the elixir of life from herbs or minerals.

## Ūrṇatejas
*mdzod spu gzi brjid*, Skt. *ūrṇatejas*, A buddha in the past.

## Rathasyā
Skt. *rathasyā*, A river queen.

## Rathavatī
*shing rta ldan ma*, Skt. *rathavatī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Rati
*gsha’ zhing ’os*, Skt. *rati*, According to Monier-Williams: “amorous enjoyment, often personified as one of the two wives of Kāmadeva, together with Prīti.”

## Ratibala
*dga’ stobs*, Skt. *ratibala*, The 918th buddha in the first list, 917th in the second list, and 908th in the third list.

## ratijaha
*dga’ ba spong ba*, Skt. *ratijaha*, Lit. “enjoyment forsaking” (other versions have ’khrug pa spong pa: “upset forsaking”). Name of a meditative stabilization.

## ratikara
*dga’ ba byed pa*, Skt. *ratikara*, Lit. “causing delight.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Ratilola
*dga’ ba chags pa*, Skt. *ratilola*, One of the sons of Māra present on the eve of Siddhārtha’s awakening.

## Ratimegha
*dga’ sprin*, Skt. *ratimegha*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Ratiprabhā
*dga’ ba’i ’od*, Skt. *ratiprabhā*, A goddess in another world in the distant past who informs a courtesan’s daughter of the presence of a buddha.

## Ratipradhāna
*grong khyer dga’ mchog brgyan*, Skt. *ratipradhāna*, Name of a city built for Puṇyaraśmi’s enjoyment by his father, King Arciṣmān.

## Ratiprapūrṇa
*dga’ bas gang ba*, Skt. *ratiprapūrṇa*, “Filled with Joy.” The name of a future eon in which Mahā­maudgalyāyana will become a buddha.

## Ratipriyā
*dga’ ma dang yid ’ong ma*, Skt. *ratipriyā*, In the Tibetan, divided into two characters, “Rati” and “Priyā.”

## Rativyūhā
*dga’ bas brgyan pa*, Skt. *rativyūhā*, A royal capital in another world realm in the distant past.

## Rativyūha
*dga’ ba bkod*, Skt. *rativyūha*, The 317th buddha in the first list, 316th in the second list, and 311th in the third list.

## Ratnā
*rin chen ma*, Skt. *ratnā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Ratna
*rin po che*, Skt. *ratna*, The 380th buddha in the first list, 379th in the second list, and 374th in the third list.

## Ratnaśaila
*rin chen ri bo*, Skt. *ratnaśaila*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the eleventh) when he becomes a buddha.

## Ratnabhūṣaṇī
*rin chen rgyan can ma*, Skt. *ratnabhūṣaṇī*, ‟Jewel Goddess,” one of the eight goddesses of offerings in the Bhūtaḍāmara maṇḍala.

## Ratnabāhu
*lag bzang*, Skt. *ratnabāhu*, Synonym for Subāhu, translated as if it was Subāhu into Tibetan.

## Ratnabuddhi
*rin po che’i blo*, Skt. *ratnabuddhi*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Ratnacūḍa
*gtsug na rin po che*, Skt. *ratnacūḍa*, The 297th buddha in the first list, 296th in the second list, and 296th in the third list.

## Ratna­cūḍa
*gtsug na rin po che*, Skt. *ratna­cūḍa*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnacandra
*dkon mchog zla ba*, Skt. *ratnacandra*, One of the buddhas who assembled at Vimalakīrti’s house to teach the Tathāgata­guhyaka, according to the goddess.

## Ratna­candra­dhvaja
*rin chen zla ba’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *ratna­candra­dhvaja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Ratna­candra­prabha
*rin chen zla ’od*, Skt. *ratna­candra­prabha*, A tathāgata mentioned here as one of the thirty-five buddhas of confession.

## Ratna­candra­pradīpa­prabhā
*rin chen zla ba sgron ma’i ’od*, Skt. *ratna­candra­pradīpa­prabhā*, A four-continent world in the distant past.

## Ratnacchatra
*rin chen gdugs*, Skt. *ratnacchatra*, Lit. “Jewel Parasol.” Name of a buddha of the past.

## Ratnacchatraśrī
*rin chen gdugs kyi dpal*, Skt. *ratnacchatra­śrī*, One of the tathāgatas.

## Ratna­cchatrābhyudgata­raśmi
*rin po che chen po’i gdugs mngon par ’phags pa’i ’od zer*, Skt. *ratna­cchatrābhyudgata­raśmi*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagharba prophesies that Radiant Bull, one of the thirty million pupils of Samudrareṇu, will have at buddhahood.

## Ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsa
*rin po che’i gdugs mngon par ’phags pa snang ba*, Skt. *ratnacchatrābhyudgatāvabhāsa*, A thus-gone one.

## Ratna­cchatrābhyudgatāva­bhāsa
*rin po che’i snying po*, Skt. *ratna­cchatrābhyudgatāva­bhāsa*, A buddha in the distant past in whose presence many beings, including the Buddha Jyotīrasa, developed the aspiration to become a buddha during a kaliyuga. Note that the Tibetan translation of the name differs from the Sanskrit form found in the available Sanskrit manuscripts.

## Ratnacchattra
*rin chen gdugs*, Skt. *ratnacchattra*, Wheel-turning king said by the Buddha to be a former incarnation of the Buddha Ratnārcis.

## Ratnacchattra­kūṭa­saṃdarśana
*rin po che’i gdugs brtsegs pa kun tu ston pa*, Skt. *ratnacchattra­kūṭa­saṃdarśana*, A bodhisattva who resides in the world Ratnavyūhā of the Thus-Gone One Ratnārcis’ buddha realm, and comes to venerate the Buddha.

## Ratnacinta
*rin chen sems pa*, Skt. *ratnacinta*, “Mind of Jewels.” One of the bodhisattvas in the entourage of the Buddha Śākyamuni when he taught the girl Vimalaśraddhā.

## Ratnadatta
*rin chen byin*, Skt. *ratnadatta*, A three-year-old boy who plays the role of interlocutor in Teaching the Practice of a Bodhisattva.

## Ratnadeva
*rin chen lha*, Skt. *ratnadeva*, The 190th buddha in the first list, 189th in the second list, and 189th in the third list.

## Ratnadhara
*rin chen mnga’*, Skt. *ratnadhara*, The 828th buddha in the first list, 827th in the second list, and 817th in the third list.

## Ratnadhvaja
*rin po che’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *ratnadhvaja*, “Jeweled Victory Banner.” One of the bodhisattvas in the entourage of the Buddha Śākyamuni when he taught the girl Vimalaśraddhā.

## Ratna­dhvaja
*rin chen rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *ratna­dhvaja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Ratna­dhvajāgra­mati
*rin chen rgyal mtshan blo gros mchog*, Skt. *ratna­dhvajāgra­mati*, A realm in the distant past. BHS verse: Ratana­dhvajāgra­mati.

## Ratnadānaśri
*rin chen sbyin*, Skt. *ratnadānaśri*, The ninety-second buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. BHS verse: Ratanadānaśiri.

## Ratnadīpa
*rin chen sgron ma*, Skt. *ratnadīpa*, A bodhisattva.

## Ratnadvīpa
*rin po che’i gling*, Skt. *ratnadvīpa*, The Kāraṇḍavyūha in the Vaidya edition references a group of islands, the distinction between singular and plural being lost in the Tibetan. Ratnadvīpa was one of the ancient names of Laṅka, as it was a rich source of jewels. In this same passage, however, Laṅka is identified as the land of the rākṣasīs. The theme of an ocean island rich in jewels appears frequently in Buddhist narratives.

## Ratnagarbha
*rin po che’i snying po*, Skt. *ratnagarbha*, One of the eighty-one sons of Samudrareṇu, the chief court priest of King Araṇemin. The Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies the buddhahood of Samudrareṇu’s thirty million pupils.

## Ratna­garbha
*rin po che’i snying po*, Skt. *ratna­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Ratnagiri
*rin chen ri bo*, Skt. *ratnagiri*, A buddha in a western buddha realm.

## Ratna­gātra­śrī
*rin chen lus kyi dpal*, Skt. *ratna­gātra­śrī*, The seventy-ninth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. BHS verse: Ratana­gātra­śirī.

## Ratnaguṇa
*rin chen yon tan*, Skt. *ratnaguṇa*, “Precious Qualities.” One of the bodhisattvas in the entourage of the Buddha Śākyamuni when he taught the girl Vimalaśraddhā.

## Ratna­guṇa­saṃnicaya
*yon tan rin chen yang dag bstsags*, Skt. *ratna­guṇa­saṃnicaya*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Ratna­guṇa­vijṛmbhita­saṃcaya
*yon tan bsgyings pa yang dag bsags*, Skt. *ratna­guṇa­vijṛmbhitasaṃcaya*, A buddha in a southern buddha realm.

## Ratnahastin
*rin chen phyag*, Skt. *ratnahastin*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Ratna­śikhara
*rin po che’i rtse mo*, Skt. *ratna­śikhara*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnaśikhara
*rin po che’i rtse mo*, Skt. *ratnaśikhara*, A world system.

## Ratna­śikhara­kūṭāgāra­dharaṇiṃdharā
*rin po che’i rtse mo’i khang pa brtsegs pa’i gzungs ’dzin ma*, Skt. *ratna­śikhara­kūṭāgāra­dharaṇiṃdharā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Ratna­śikharārciḥ­parvata­pradīpa
*rin chen ri bo’i spo’i ’od zer sgron ma*, Skt. *ratna­śikharārciḥ­parvata­pradīpa*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Ratnaśikhin
*rin chen gtsug tor can*, Skt. *ratnaśikhin*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the thirty-second) when he becomes a buddha.

## ratnajahā
*rin po che spong ba*, Skt. *ratnajahā*, Lit. “jewel forsaking.” Other versions read raṇaṃjaha, nyon mongs ba med pa: “defilement forsaking.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Ratnajāla
*rin chen dra ba*, Skt. *ratnajāla*, A bodhisattva.

## Ratnajālin
*rin chen dra ba can*, Skt. *ratnajālin*, One of the bodhisattva great beings.

## Ratnakūṭa
*dkon brtsegs*, Skt. *ratnakūṭa*, The Ratnakūṭa section of the Kangyur (Toh 45–93) is a distinct collection, also found in the Chinese Tripiṭaka (Taishō 310), of forty-nine selected sūtras on a range of themes. In some titles and colophons the collection is presented as a single sūtra with its component texts as chapters.

## Ratna­kūṭa
*rin po che brtsegs pa*, Skt. *ratna­kūṭa*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnakeśa
*rin chen skra*, Skt. *ratnakeśa*, A yakṣa king. (Toh 555: rin chen gtsug phud)

## Ratnaketu
*rin po che tog*, Skt. *ratnaketu*, It occurs as the main title of the Ratnaketudhāraṇī and also as the name of the main dhāraṇī of the Ratnaketudhāraṇī. It is also used in Buddhist texts to designate a special meditative absorption, a tathāgata, and a bodhisattva. Generally, the term refers to something precious and illuminating, i.e., a guiding light.

## Ratna­ketu
*rin po che tog*, Skt. *ratna­ketu*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Ratnaketurāja
*rin po che’i tog gi rgyal po*, Skt. *ratnaketurāja*, The name of two thousand pupils of the Buddha when they become buddhas.

## Ratnaḍākinī
*rin chen mkha’ ’gro*, Skt. *ratnaḍākinī*, A deity in Vajraḍākinī’s maṇḍala.

## ratnakoṭi
*rin chen mtha’*, Skt. *ratna-koṭi*, Lit. “jewel limit.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Ratnakrama
*rin po che yi stabs*, Skt. *ratnakrama*, The 836th buddha in the first list, 835th in the second list, and 825th in the third list.

## Ratnakīrti
A bodhisattva in this sūtra who is a prince predicted to become the buddha Samantāloka and whose name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Ratnakuṇḍala
*rin po che’i rna cha*, Skt. *ratnakuṇḍala*, A pore on Avalokiteśvara’s body.

## Ratnakuṇḍalin
*thab sbyor dmar po can*, Skt. *ratnakuṇḍalin*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi. The variant Raktakuṇḍalin is found in the manuscript B (and confirmed in the Tib. thab sbyor dmar po can).

## Ratnakusuma
*rin chen me tog*, Skt. *ratnakusuma*, According to the commentary, an alternative name for Ratnapāṇi

## Ratna­kusuma­guṇa­sāgara­vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­suvarṇa­kāñcana­prabhāsa­śrī
*rin chen me tog yon tan rgya mtsho bai DUr+ya dang gser gyi ri kha dog bzang po gser du snang ba’i dpal*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­guṇa­sāgara­vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­suvarṇa­kāñcana­prabhāsa­śrī*, A buddha, teacher of the goddess Śrī. (Toh 555: bai DUr+ya dang gser gyi ri bo rin po che’i me tog snang ba spal gyi yon tan rgya mtsho; )

## Ratna­kusuma­guṇa­sāgara­vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­suvarṇa­kāñcana­prabhāsaśrī
*rin chen me tog yon tan rgya mtsho bai DUr+ya dang gser gyi ri kha dog bzang po gser du snang ba’i dpal*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­guṇa­sāgara­vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­suvarṇa­kāñcana­prabhāsaśrī*, (Toh 555: Vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­ratna­kusuma­prabhā­śrīguṇa­sāgara; bai DUr+ya dang gser gyi ri bo rin po che’i me tog snang ba spal gyi yon tan rgya mtsho)

## Ratna­kusuma­guṇa­sāgara­vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­suvarṇa­kāṃcana­prabhāsa­śrī
*rin po che’i me tog yon tan gyi rgya mtsho baidUrya dang gser gyi ri bo mdog mdzes gser ’od dpal*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­guṇa­sāgara­vaidūrya­kanaka­giri­suvarṇa­kāṃcana­prabhāsa­śrī*, A tathāgata in the past, in a world system called Ratna­saṃbhavā.

## Ratna­kusuma­megha
*rin po che’i me tog gi sprin*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­megha*, A bodhimaṇḍa in another world in the distant past.

## Ratna­kusuma­prabha
*rin po che’i me tog gi ’od*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­prabha*, A buddha of the present time in a world realm in the eastern directions, who had been King Dhanapati in the distant past.

## Ratna­kusuma­pradīpā
*rin chen me tog sgron ma*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­pradīpā*, A capital city in the distant past.

## Ratna­kusuma­pradīpa­dhvajā
*rin chen me tog sgron ma’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­pradīpa­dhvajā*, A four-continent world in the distant past.

## Ratna­kusuma­sampuṣpita
*rin chen me tog shin tu rgyas pa*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­sampuṣpita*, A world system.

## Ratna­kusuma­saṃpuṣpita­gotra
*rin chen me tog shin tu rgyas pa’i rigs*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­saṃpuṣpita­gotra*, Name of a tathāgata.

## Ratna­kusuma­vidyuddharma­nigarjita­megha­ghoṣa
*rin po che’i me tog dang glog dang chos kyi ’brug sgra’i sprin gyi dbyangs*, Skt. *ratna­kusuma­vidyuddharma­nigarjita­megha­ghoṣa*, “The Voice of Clouds of Precious Flowers, Lightning, and Dharma Thunder.” A lake in the distant past.

## Ratna­lakṣaṇa­vibhūṣita­meru
*mtshan rin po ches rnam par brgyan pa’i ri bo*, Skt. *ratna­lakṣaṇa­vibhūṣita­meru*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Ratnamaṇḍala
*rin po che’i dkyil ’khor*, Skt. *ratnamaṇḍala*, A buddha realm.

## Ratnamati
*rin chen blo gros*, Skt. *ratnamati*, “Precious Intelligence.” One of the bodhisattvas in the entourage of the Buddha Śākyamuni when he taught the girl Vimalaśraddhā.

## Ratnameru
*rin chen ri*, Skt. *ratnameru*, A buddha in the distant past. BHS: Ratanameru.

## Ratnamālā
*rin chen phreng ba ma*, Skt. *ratnamālā*, The name of an apsaras.

## ratnamudra
*rin chen phyag rgya*, Skt. *ratna-mudra*, Lit. “jewel seal.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Ratnamudrāhasta
A bodhisattva in the audience of this sūtra, whose name is attested in the Vimalakīrti­nirdeśa.

## Ratna­mudrā­hasta
*lag na phyag rgya rin po che*, Skt. *ratna­mudrā­hasta*, A bodhisattva great being present in the audience of this sūtra.

## Ratnamukuṭa
*rin chen cod pan*, Skt. *ratnamukuṭa*, One of the bodhisattva great beings.

## Ratna­mu­kuṭa
*rin po che’i cod pan*, Skt. *ratna­mu­kuṭa*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnamuni
*rin chen thub pa*, Skt. *ratnamuni*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnanetrā
*rin chen mig*, Skt. *ratnanetrā*, The goddess of Kapilavastu.

## Ratnanetra
*rin chen mig*, Skt. *ratnanetra*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Ratnanetra (the bodhisattva)
*rin po che’i myig*, Skt. *ratnanetra*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Ratnanetra (the buddha)
*rin chen spyan*, Skt. *ratnanetra*, The name of a buddha in the distant past. BHS in verse: Ratananetra.

## Ratna­padma­candra­viśuddhābhyud­gata­rāja
*rin po che’i pad ma’i zla ba rnam par dag pa mngon par ’phags pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *ratna­padma­candra­viśuddhābhyud­gata­rāja*, A buddha countless eons in the past.

## Ratna­padma­praphullita­gātra
*sku rin po che’i pad mo shin tu rgyas pa*, Skt. *ratna­padma­praphullita­gātra*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Ratna­padma­supratiṣṭhita­śailendra­rāja
*rin po che’i pad ma la rab tu bzhugs pa ri dbang gi rgyal po*, Skt. *ratna­padma­supratiṣṭhita­śailendra­rāja*, A tathāgata mentioned here as one of the thirty-five buddhas of confession.

## Ratna­padma­vikrāmin
*rin chen pad mas rnam par gnon pa*, Skt. *ratna­padma­vikramin*, A tathāgata mentioned here as one of the thirty-five buddhas of confession.

## Ratnapadmābha
*’od snang rin chen pad mo*, Skt. *ratnapadmābha*, A buddha.

## Ratna­padmāvabhāsa­garbha
*rin chen pad+mo snang ba’i snying po*, Skt. *ratna­padmāvabhāsa­garbha*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Ratnaparvata
*rin po che’i ri*, Skt. *ratnaparvata*, A mountain.

## Ratnapāṇi
*lag na rin po che*, Skt. *ratnapāṇi*, In the Kāraṇḍavyūha he is, as well as being listed as present at Buddha Śākyamuni’s teachings, the one who is described in Śākyamuni’s memories as the bodhisattva who questions Buddha Vipaśyin. He is the principal bodhisattva being addressed by Śākyamuni in chapter 35 of the Avatamsaka Sūtra. In the early tantras he is one of the sixteen bodhisattvas in the dharmadhātu maṇḍala. In the higher tantras he is associated with the ratna family of Buddha Ratnasambhava.

## Ratna­pāṇi
*lag na rin po che*, Skt. *ratna­pāṇi*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnaprabhā
*rin po che’i ’od*, Skt. *ratnaprabhā*, A world realm in the distant past. Also the name of a world realm in the distant future in which five hundred buddhas will appear.

## Ratnaprabha
*rin po che’i ’od*, Skt. *ratnaprabha*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī (translated as rin po che’i ’od), and also the name of the forty-second buddha in a kalpa in the distant past (translated as rin chen ’od).

## Ratnaprabhāsa
*rin chen ’od*, Skt. *ratnaprabhāsa*, The 891st buddha in the first list, 890th in the second list, and 881st in the third list.

## Ratnapradatta
*rin chen rab sbyin*, Skt. *ratnapradatta*, The 781st buddha in the first list, 780th in the second list, and 769th in the third list.

## Ratnapriya
*rin chen dgyes*, Skt. *ratnapriya*, The 876th buddha in the first list, 875th in the second list, and 866th in the third list.

## Ratnapuṣpa
*rin chen me tog*, Skt. *ratnapuṣpa*, A buddha realm.

## Ratna­śrī
*rin po che’i dpal*, Skt. *ratna­śrī*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnaśrī
*dkon mchog dpal*, Skt. *ratnaśrī*, One of the buddhas who appear in the house of Vimalakīrti on esoteric occasions; the Sanskrit name, but with a different rendering in Tibetan, also refers to a bodhisattva.

## Ratnaraśi
*rin chen brtsegs pa*, Skt. *ratnaraśi*, A buddha in the distant past. BHS verse: Ratanarāśi.

## Ratnarakṣita
Skt. *ratnarakṣita*, Eighth- to ninth-century Tibetan monk, preceptor, and translator (not to be confused with the thirteenth-century mahāpaṇḍita of the same name). See also .

## Ratna­raśmi­pradīpa­dhvaja­rāja
*rin po che’i ’od gzer sgron ma’i rgyal mtshan rgyal po*, Skt. *ratna­raśmi­pradīpa­dhvaja­rāja*, A buddha in a world in the eastern direction in the past.

## Ratna­śrī­haṃsa­citrā
*rin chen dpal gyi dad pas brgyan pa*, Skt. *ratna­śrī­haṃsa­citrā*, The realm of a buddha named Vairocana. See .

## Ratna­śrī­śikhara­megha­pradīpa
*rin chen dpal gyi rtse mo’i sprin rab tu snang ba*, Skt. *ratna­śrī­śikhara­megha­pradīpa*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Ratnarājaśri
*rin chen rgyal po dpal*, Skt. *ratnarājaśri*, The sixtieth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. BHS verse: Ratanarājaśiri.

## Ratna­śrī­pradīpa­guṇa­ketu
*rin chen dpal sgron yon tan dpal*, Skt. *ratna­śrī­pradīpa­guṇa­ketu*, A buddha in the distant past. BHS verse: Ratana­śirī­pradīpa­guṇa­ketu.

## Ratna­śrī­saṃbhava
*rin chen dpal ’byung*, Skt. *ratna­śrī­saṃbhava*, “The Source of Glorious Jewels.” The name of a world realm in the distant past.

## Ratna­rucira­śrī­rāja
*rin po che yid du ’ong ba’i dpal gyi rgyal po*, Skt. *ratna­rucira­śrī­rāja*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Ratnaruta
*rin chen dbyangs*, Skt. *ratnaruta*, The 473rd buddha in the first list, 472nd in the second list, and 466th in the third list.

## Ratna­saṃbhavā
*nor bu rin po che las byung ba*, Skt. *ratna­saṃbhavā*, The world system of the tathāgata Ratna­kusuma­guṇa­sāgara­vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­suvarṇa­kāṃcana­prabhāsa­śrī.

## Ratnasaṃbhava
*rin po che ’byung ba*, Skt. *ratnasaṃbhava*, The realm in which Subhūti will achieve buddhahood.

## Ratnasambhavā
*rin chen ’byung ba*, Skt. *ratnasambhavā*, The name of an eon.

## Ratnasambhava
*rin chen 'byung gnas*, the [Buddha](#buddha) of the Jewel Family. See [five families](#five-families).

## Ratnasaṃpad
*dkon mchog ’byung ba*, Skt. *ratnasaṃpad*, The name of a future eon.

## Ratnasiṃha
A bodhisattva in the Buddha’s retinue.

## Ratna­siṃhāvabhāsa­jvalanā
*rin po che’i seng ge snang zhing ’bar ba*, Skt. *ratna­siṃhāvabhāsa­jvalanā*, A buddha realm in the downward direction.

## Ratnaskandha
*rin chen phung po*, Skt. *ratnaskandha*, The 307th buddha in the first list, 306th in the second list, and 301st in the third list.

## Ratna­sāla­vyūha­megha­pradīpā
*rin po che’i sa las rnam par brgyan pa sprin gyi sgron ma*, Skt. *ratna­sāla­vyūha­megha­pradīpā*, A royal capital in another world realm in the distant past. Its short form in verse is Sāla­vyūha­megha.

## Ratna­svara­ghoṣa
*rin chen nga ro’i dbyangs*, Skt. *ratna­svara­ghoṣa*, The 974th buddha in the first list, 973rd in the second list, and 964th in the third list.

## Ratnatalanāgendra
*klu dbang rin chen ngos*, Skt. *ratna­talanāgendra*, A buddha in a southern buddha realm.

## Ratnatejas
*rin chen gzi brjid*, Skt. *ratnatejas*, The 314th buddha in the first list, 313th in the second list, and 308th in the third list.

## Ratna­tejobhyudgata­rāja
*dkon mchog gzi brjid mngon ’phags rgyal po*, Skt. *ratna­tejobhyudgata­rāja*, A buddha in the eastern direction.

## Ratnavṛṣabha
*rin chen khyu mchog*, Skt. *ratnavṛṣabha*, A buddha.

## Ratnavairocana
*rin po che rnam par snang byed*, Skt. *ratnavairocana*, The bodhisattva who asks the Buddha to teach about Buddha Padmottara.

## Ratnavali
*rin po che’i phreng ba*, Skt. *ratnavali*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnavara
*rin chen mchog*, Skt. *ratnavara*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Ratna­vastrāvabhāsa­dhvajā
*rin po che’i gos yongs su snang ba*, Skt. *ratna­vastrāvabhāsa­dhvajā*, A buddha realm in the northern direction.

## Ratnavatī
*rin chen yod pa*, Skt. *ratnavatī*, Name of a world system in the eastern direction, where the buddha Ratnākara teaches the perfection of wisdom to bodhisattva great beings.

## Ratnavicayā
*rin po che bstsags pa*, Skt. *ratnavicayā*, The eastern realm of the Buddha Ratnacandra during the lifetime of the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

## Ratnavisabha
*rin chen khyu mchog*, Skt. *ratnavisabha*, A southern buddha realm that the Buddha Śākyamuni sees.

## Ratnaviśuddhā
*rin po che rnam par dag pa*, Skt. *ratnaviśuddhā*, A distant realm to the east, where Buddha Prabhūtaratna had lived.

## Ratnavyūhā
*rin chen bkod pa*, Skt. *ratnavyūha*, The buddha field of the Buddha Ratnaketu in the present, during the time of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Ratnavyūha
*dkon mchog dkod pa*, Skt. *ratnavyūha*, Lit. “Jewel-Array.” Name of one of the bodhisattvas in the original assembly (rendered in Tibetan as rin chen bkod pa); also the name (with several renderings in Tibetan) of a buddha who presides in the universe called Ananta­guṇa­ratna­vyūha, yet who comes to Vimalakīrti’s house at the latter’s supplication, to participate in the esoteric teachings. He can be identified with the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava, one of the five major buddhas of the Guhya­samāja­tantra.

## Ratnayaśas
*rin chen grags pa*, Skt. *ratnayaśas*, The 403rd buddha in the first list, 402nd in the second list, and 396th in the third list.

## Ratnayaṣṭi
*rin chen srog zhing*, Skt. *ratnayaṣṭi*, A bodhisattva in the southern buddhafield Buddha Courage.

## Ratnayaṣti
*rin chen srog shing*, Skt. *ratnayaṣti*, A thus-gone one.

## Ratnābha
*’od snang rin chen*, Skt. *ratnābha*, A buddha.

## Ratnābhacandra
*rin chen zla ’od*, Skt. *ratnābhacandra*, The 742nd buddha in the first list, 741st in the second list, and 731st in the third list.

## Ratnendraśīla
Eighth- to ninth-century Tibetan translator.

## Ratneśvara
*rin chen dbang phyug*, Skt. *ratneśvara*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Ratneśvaraghoṣa
*rin chen dbang phyug dbyangs*, Skt. *ratneśvaraghoṣa*, The name of a buddha.

## Ratnāṅga
A buddha in the distant past.

## Ratnāgni
*rin po che yi me*, Skt. *ratnāgni*, The 392nd buddha in the first list, 391st in the second list, and 385th in the third list.

## Ratnāgrakeyūrā
*rin chen mchog gi dpung rgyan ma*, Skt. *ratnāgrakeyūrā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Ratnāgra­prabha­tejas
*rin chen mchog gi ’od kyi gzi brjid*, Skt. *ratnāgra­prabha­tejas*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Ratnākara
A realized one whose name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra and the name of a bodhisattva in the audience for this discourse.

## Ratnā­kara
*dkon mchog ’byung gnas*, Skt. *ratnā­kara*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Ratnākaraśānti
*rin chen ’byung gnas zhi ba*, Skt. *ratnākaraśānti*, An important eleventh-century Buddhist monastic scholar who wrote prolifically on a number on both Mahāyāna and Mantrayāna works.

## Ratnāloka
*rin chen snang*, Skt. *ratnāloka*, A great bodhisattva.

## Ratnāmbuda
*rin chen chu sbyin*, Skt. *ratnāmbuda*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Ratnoccaya
*rin chen sogs pa*, Skt. *ratnoccaya*, A dharmabhāṇaka in the distant past who eventually became the Buddha Akṣobhya. (Yongle, Lithang, Peking, Narthang, and Choné: rin chen sogs, rin chen sogs pa. Toh 555: rin chen brtsegs pa)

## Ratnodgata
*rin chen ’phags*, Skt. *ratnodgata*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Ratnotpalaśrī
*rin chen ud pa la’i dpal*, Skt. *ratnotpalaśrī*, Name of a tathāgata.

## Ratnottama
*dmar po’i mchog*, Skt. *ratnottama*, This Buddha who sends the previous life of Śākyamuni to Buddha Padmottama. However, the Tibetan had dmar po’i mchog, “supreme red,” which would have been a translation of Raktottama, evidently a mistake for Ratnottama, which would have been translated as nor bu’i mchog or rin chen mchog.

## Ratnārcī
*rin chen ’od ’phro*, Skt. *ratnārcī*, A goddess who later becomes the bodhisattva Cittaratnārcī.

## Ratnārci
*rin chen ’od zer*, Skt. *ratnārci*, The 361st buddha in the first list, 360th in the second list, and 355th in the third list.

## Ratnārci­netra­prabha
*rin po che ’od ’phro ba’i mig gi ’od*, Skt. *ratnārci­netra­prabha*, A king in the distant past.

## Ratnārciḥ­parvata
*rin po che ’od ’phro ba’i ri bo*, Skt. *ratnārciḥ­parvata*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Ratnārci­parvata­śrī
*rin chen ’od ’phro ri dpal*, Skt. *ratnārci­parvata­śrī*, The thirty-first buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. BHS verse: Ratnārci­parvata­śirī.

## Ratnārciḥparvata­śrī
*rin chen ’od ’phro ri bo’i dpal*, Skt. *ratnārciḥparvata­śrī*, A tathāgata.

## Ratnārciḥ­parvata­śrī­tejorāja
*rin chen ’od ’phro ba’i ri bo dpal gyi gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *ratnārciḥ­parvata­śrī­tejorāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Ratnārcis
*dkon mchog ’od ’phro*, Skt. *ratnārcis*, One of the buddhas who appear in the house of Vimalakīrti on esoteric occasions. According to the Prajñā­pāramitā, he is the Buddha of the universe Upaśānta, in the western direction (see Lamotte, p. 384, n. 27).

## Ratnāvabhāsa
*rin chen snang ba*, Skt. *ratnāvabhāsa*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Ratnāvatī
*rin chen can*, Skt. *ratnāvatī*, Lit. “Bejeweled.” A world system in the eastern direction, where the buddha Ratnākara now dwells.

## rattan
*sba*, Skt. *vetra*, Calamus ratang.

## rattleweed
Crotalaria retusa.

## Ratīśvara
*dga’ ba’i dbang phyug*, Skt. *ratīśvara*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the seventieth) when he becomes a buddha.

## Ratīśvara­ghoṣa­jyoti
*dga’ ba’i dbang phyug sgra dbyangs ’od zer*, Skt. *ratīśvara­ghoṣa­jyoti*, A buddha in an eastern buddha realm.

## Raudrā
*drag mo*, Skt. *raudrā*, A great rākṣasī.

## Raudrī
*rdo rje drag mo*, Skt. *vajraraudrī*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## Raudra
The fifty-fourth in the sixty-year cycle of Vedic astrology. The name literally translates as “fierce” or “wrathful.”

## Raudraka
*drag po’i bu*, Skt. *raudraka*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Raudra­kātyāyanī
*drag mo ka ta ya na*, Skt. *raudra­kātyāyanī*, ‟Wild Kātyāyanī,” one of the eight kātyāyanī spirits.

## Raudrapiśācī
*sha za mo drag mo*, Skt. *raudrapiśācī*, One of the great piśācīs.

## Raudrākṣa
*mi bzang mig can*, Skt. *raudrākṣa*, An evil brahmin.

## Raurava
*’o dod ’bod pa*, Skt. *raurava*, The fourth of the eight hot hells. In later translations it is ngu ’bod, which also means “wailing” as a compound of the words for “weep” and “shout.”

## Rauruka
*’o dod can*, Skt. *rauruka*, According to Pāli sources (DN 19: Mahāgovindasutta), Roruka was the capital of Sovīra, reigned over by King Bharata, who was the Bodhisatta in a former birth.

## Śravaṇā
*gro bzhin*, Skt. *śravaṇā*, The name of a lunar asterism. Its chief star is known as Alpha Aquilae in the occidental tradition.

## Śravaṇa
*gro bzhin*, Skt. *śravaṇa*, A constellation in the west, personified as a semidivine being. Here called upon for protection.

## Raven Mouths
*bya rog kha*, Skt. *kākāsyaka*, One of sixteen realms that surround the Hell of Ultimate Torment.

## Raven’s Belly
*bya rog lto*, Skt. *bya rog lto*, One of sixteen realms that surround the Hell of Ultimate Torment. Also called Black Belly.

## Ravens’ Peak
*khwa spungs*, Skt. *vāyasakūṭa*, A mountain in the hell called Wailer.

## Ravens with Vajra-Like Beaks
*khwa’i chu rdo rje lta bu*, Skt. *vajra­vāyasa­tuṇḍa*, One of sixteen realms that surround the Great Howling Hell.

## Ravishing
*yid ’phrog ma*, Skt. *yid ’phrog ma*, Ravishing (extremely beautiful or delightful), also the name of the mother of the buddha Vikrīḍitāvin.

## Ravishing Women’s Minds
*bud med sems ’phrog*, Skt. *bud med sems ’phrog*, A kinnara king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## raw silk
*mon dar*, Skt. *kauśeyaka*, an acceptable form of cloth for a monk, as identified in the [Four Supports](#four-supports) [section](#section) of the ordination ritual.

## Āraṇyaka
*dgon pa pa*, Skt. *āraṇyaka*, “Forest Dweller,” the name of the son of householders in Śrāvastī, he preferred seclusion, eventually attaining arhatship.

## Razor
*spu gri ba*, Skt. *spu gri ba*, Razor (a sharp-bladed instrument for shaving), also the name of a vulture king.

## Śrībhadrā
*dpal bzang mo*, Skt. *śrībhadrā*, An upāsikā in Dhanyākara; also an eminent daughter in Dhanyākara.

## Śrībhadra
*dpal bzang*, Skt. *śrībhadra*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Śūrdatta
*dpas byin*, Skt. *śūrdatta*, A great bodhisattva.

## Śrāddhā
*dad ma*, Skt. *śrāddhā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## śrāddha
The ritual offering of food (bali) to nourish and support the spirit of one’s deceased parent during the afterlife.

## Śrīdevī Kālī
A fearsome, wrathful goddess who in the Buddhist tradition is a protector of the teachings. In Tibet, she is widely propitiated and takes on many forms, many of which are known through the Tibetan name Palden Lhamo (dpal ldan lha mo), which translates the Sanskrit śrīdevī. She is most often portrayed riding on a donkey and adorned with various wrathful ornaments and hand implements.

## Śrīdevī Mahākālī
*dpal lha mo nag mo chen mo*, Skt. *śrīdevī mahākālī*, A wrathful Dharma protector who is often portrayed together with her servant Rematī. At times she is conflated with Rematī, so that the two appear to be identical. In the Tibetan tradition, she is better known under her Tibetan name, Palden Lhamo (dpal ldan lha mo). She is most often portrayed riding on a donkey and adorned with various wrathful ornaments and hand implements.

## Śrīdeva
*lha yi dpal*, Skt. *śrīdeva*, The 37th buddha in the first list, 37th in the second list, and 38th in the third list.

## Śrīdevamati
*dpal gyi blo gros lha*, Skt. *śrīdevamati*, The twenty-fourth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. BHS verse: Śiridevamati.

## Rādhā
*dga’ mo*, Skt. *rādhā*, An incarnation of a goddess as a milkmaid, who became Kṛṣṇa’s lover. (Toh 556 Degé: rgan’ mo.)

## Rādhaka
*sgrub byed*, Skt. *rādhaka*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Ūrdhvaga
*steng ’gro*, Skt. *ūrdhvaga*, One of the rāśis.

## Ūrdhvajaṭā
*ral pa ’greng*, Skt. *ūrdhvajaṭā*, A great rākṣasī.

## Śārdūla
Skt. *śārdūla*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa. See .

## Śārdūlakarṇa
“Tiger Ear.” The son of the outcaste king Triśaṅku.

## Ārdrā
*lag*, Skt. *ārdrā*, The name of a lunar asterism. Its chief star is known as Alpha Orionis in the occidental tradition.

## Ārdrabalaka
*rlan stobs can*, Skt. *ārdrabalaka*, A nāga king.

## Reaching Awakening
*byang chub reg*, Skt. *byang chub reg*, Attendant of the buddha Durjaya.

## Reaching Liberation
*thar pa ’byor*, Skt. *thar pa ’byor*, Birthplace of the buddha Arthasiddhi.

## Reaching One’s Goal
*yul la phebs pa*, A world system in the western direction in the present. Realm of the buddha named Subjugator of Resentment and Conceit.

## Reaching the Far Shore of Definitive Meaning to Fulfill Beings’ Aspirations
*sems can gyi bsam pa nges pa’i don gyi pha rol tu bgrod par dong ba*, Skt. *sems can gyi bsam pa nges pa’i don gyi pha rol tu bgrod par dong ba*, The name of a bodhisattva in the Buddha’s audience.

## Reaching the Meaningful Stage
*don yod go ’phang gnon*, Skt. *don yod go ’phang gnon*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Praśāntagāmin.

## ready
*go bskon*, Skt. *saṃ√nah*, To call up reserves or members of a standing army.

## ready confidence
*spobs pa*, Skt. *pratibhāna*, Also rendered here as “confident readiness.”

## Reṇaja
*glang po ’thob*, Skt. *reṇaja*, One of the thousand sons of King Araṇemin.

## real basis
*dngos po*, Skt. *vastu*, Also rendered as “existent thing,” “real thing,” and “something that exists.”

## real endpoint
*yang dag pa’i mtha’*, Skt. *bhūtakoṭi*, A synonym for ultimate truth, and a way of describing the attainment of perfection as the culmination of the spiritual path.

## Real meaning
*nges don*, Skt. *nītārtha*, direct expression of truth from the point of [view](#view) of realized beings. See also [expedient meaning](#expedient-meaning).

## real nature
*de bzhin nyid*, Skt. *tathatā*, Literally, “thusness” or “suchness.” The ultimate nature of things, or the way things are beyond all concepts and duality, as opposed to the way they appear to unawakened beings.

## real thing
*dngos po*, Skt. *bhāva*, Also rendered as “existent thing,” “something that exists,” and “real basis.”

## realgar
*ni ldong ros*, Skt. *manaḥśilā*, Arsenic sulphide, which consists of bright orange-red soft crystals. It is also called “ruby sulphur” and “ruby of arsenic.” A number of Sanskrit synonyms include yavāgraja, pākya, mansil, manoguptā, nāgajihivikā, golā, śilā, kunṭī, and naipālī.

## reality
*chos nyid*, Skt. *dharmatā*, The quality or condition of things as they really are, which cannot be conveyed in conceptual, dualistic terms. Throughout Buddhist discourse this term is used both in regard to the specific relative characteristics of phenomena, such as the heat of fire and the moisture of water, and in terms of their common ultimate characteristic, emptiness.

## reality-limit
*yang dag pa’i mtha’*, Skt. *bhūtakoṭi*, A synonym of the ultimate reality. In the Mahāyāna sūtras, it has a somewhat negative flavor, connoting the Hinayāna concept of a static nirvāṇa. Sthiramati glosses the term as follows: “ ‘Reality’ means undistorted truth. ‘Limit’ means the extreme beyond which there is nothing to be known by anyone” (bhūtaṃ satyam aviparītamityarthaḥ / koṭiḥ paryanto yataḥ pareṇa-anyajjñeyaṃ nāsti…/).

## Realization
*mngon rtogs*, Skt. *mngon rtogs*, Realization (the act of becoming fully aware or of achieving something), also the name of a buddha.

## Realization and Relinquishment
*rtogs pa spong ba*, Skt. *rtogs pa spong ba*, Birthplace of the buddha Śuddhasāgara.

## Realization of the Meaning
*don legs par dgongs*, Skt. *don legs par dgongs*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Nakṣatrarāja (528 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Realized by All Beings
*kun gyi rtogs pa*, Skt. *kun gyi rtogs pa*, Name of a gandharva, a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## realized one
A common epithet of the buddhas, translated into Tibetan as “the one gone thus,” from which one gets the translation “thus-gone one.” The term has a sense of literal movement, of having “gone” or “come” somewhere, but it also carries the sense of having “realized” something, in both senses of having understood it and made it real. In some traditional explanations of the term, the adverb tathā (“thus” or “in that way”) is therefore connected to tathatā (“the way things are”).

## Realizer
*rtogs byed*, Skt. *rtogs byed*, Realizer (one who realizes or comprehends), also the name of a wandering mendicant (parivrājaka).

## Realizer of Existence
*srid pa rig pa*, Skt. *srid pa rig pa*, A sage.

## Realizer of Qualities
*yon tan rtogs byed*, Skt. *yon tan rtogs byed*, Mother of the buddha Puṣpaprabha.

## Realizing the Heard
*thos pa rtogs*, Skt. *thos pa rtogs*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Atiyaśas.

## Realm
see [six realms](#six-realms-of-existence).

## Realm of Brahmā
*tshangs pa’i ’jig rten*, Skt. *brahmaloka*, The realm (loka) or heaven of Brahmā, usually located just above the desire realm (kāmadhātu) as one of the first levels of the form realm (rūpadhātu) and equated with the state that one achieves in the first concentration (dhyāna).

## realm of desire
*’dod pa’i khams*, Skt. *kāmadhātu*, This realm is composed of the six classes of existence: hell beings, pretas, animals, humans, asuras, and devas. These are all existences where a being is reborn through karma. In the two higher realms beings are reborn there through the power of their meditation.

## realm of ghosts
A synonym for pretaloka, it is the realm of the dead or the ghosts, where Yama, the Lord of Death, rules and judges the dead. Yama is also said to rule over the hells. This is also the name of the Vedic afterlife inhabited by the ancestors (Skt. pitṛ). The Pali commentarial tradition, and possibly other early Buddhist schools, identified Yama’s domain (Pali yamavisaya) with the realm of the ghosts (Pali petaloka). The commentary on the Kuṇālajātaka (Jātaka no. 536), the Kuṇālajātakavaṇṇanā, divides the realm of ghosts into the abode of ghosts and the abode of the asuras called Kālakañcika (Petarājavisayanti petavisayañca kālakañcikaasuravisayañca).

## realm of gods atop Mount Meru
*ri rab kyi steng lha’i gnas*, Skt. *ri rab kyi steng lha’i gnas*, Likely refers to the Heaven of the Thirty-Three (Trāyastriṃśa, sum cu rtsa gsum), the second heaven of the desire realm situated on the summit of Mount Meru and presided over by thirty-three gods, of whom Śakra is the chief.

## Realm of Lotuses
*padma can*, Skt. *padmāvatī*, A buddhafield in the east.

## realm of phenomena
*chos kyi dbyings*, Skt. *dharmadhātu*, Interpreted variously‍—given the many connotations of both dharma and dhātu‍—as the realm, element, or nature, of phenomena, reality, or truth, but generally taken to denote the entirety of phenomena and particularly their nature as a synonym of other terms designating the ultimate. In Tibetan, instances of the Sanskrit dharmadhātu with this range of meanings (rendered chos kyi dbyings) are distinguished from instances of the same Sanskrit term with its rather different meaning related to mental perception in the context of the twelve sense sources and eighteen elements (rendered chos kyi khams).

## realm of reality
An expression that seems to refer to the entirety of the world, the container (dhātu) of all things.

## realm of sentient beings
*sems can gyi khams*, Skt. *sattvadhātu*, The world as it is perceived by ordinary beings.

## realm of the asuras
*a su ra’i ’jig rten*, Skt. *asuraloka*, Sanskrit and Pāli asura literally means “non-gods”; often translated as “demigods, titans.” A class of beings that rank between devas and humans. The asuras were expelled from their original home in the god realm because of their chronic jealousy; now they wage constant war with the devas in the hope of regaining their old home. According to Transformation of Karma, this class of beings is counted among the unfortunate (or lower) realms of rebirth.

## realm of the Four Great Kings
*rgyal chen bzhi’i ris*, Skt. *cāturmahā­rājakāyika*, One of the heavens of Buddhist cosmology, lowest among the six heavens of the desire realm. Dwelling place of the Four Great Kings, traditionally located on a terrace of Mount Meru.

## realm of the inconceivable
*bsam gyis myi khyab pa’i dbyings*, Skt. *acintyadhātu*, A synonym of ultimate reality.

## Realm of the Lord of Death
*gshin rje’i ’jig rten*, Skt. *yamaloka*, The realm of the Lord of Death is another name for the realm of hungry ghosts or pretas. This term is also the name of the Vedic afterlife inhabited by the ancestors (pitṛ).

## realm of the pretas
*yi dags ’jig rten*, Skt. *pretaloka*, The realm of the dead or the ghosts, where Yama, the Lord of Death, is the ruler and judges the dead. Yama is also said to rule over the hells. This term is also the name of the Vedic afterlife inhabited by the ancestors (Skt. pitṛ). The Pāli commentarial tradition, and possibly other early Buddhist schools, identified Yama’s domain (Pāli yamavisaya) with the realm of the pretas (Pāli petaloka).

## Realm of the Pure Abode
*gnas gtsang ma*, Skt. *śuddhāvāsa*, The highest division of the realm of form, comprising its five highest heavens; also used as the name of the gods living there. The name is rendered elsewhere in this translation as “Śuddhāvāsa.”

## realm of the Thirty-Three
*sum cu rtsa gsum*, Skt. *tṛdaśa*, One of the gods’ realms; also used as the name of the gods living there.

## realm of the yāma gods
See “Yāma Heaven.”

## realm of Yama
*gshin rje’i ’jig rten*, Skt. *yamaloka*, Another name for the hungry ghost realm.

## Realms of the High Priests of Brahmā
*tshangs pa’i mdun na ’don*, Skt. *brahma­purohita*, The second god realm of form, this is the second of the three heavens that make up the first dhyāna heaven in the form realm. Also called Brahmā’s Entourage (Brahmā­pariṣadya).

## Reasoning Mind
*yid ’thad*, Skt. *yid ’thad*, Attendant of the buddha Garjitasvara.

## rebirth
The eleventh link of the twelve links of dependent origination.

## rebirth process
*srid pa*, Skt. *bhava*, Tenth of the twelve links of dependent origination; third of the four torrents. Also translated here as “phenomenal existence.”

## rebirth, rebirth process
*srid pa*, Skt. *bhava*, Tenth of the twelve links of dependent origination; third of the four torrents. Also translated here as “phenomenal existence.”

## recaka
*re tsa ka*, Skt. *recaka*, Exhalation (one of the four stages during a single breath).

## receive alms
*bsod snyoms*, Skt. *piṇḍapāta*, To receive food that is offered in a bowl to mendicants in order to accumulate merit. The Tibetan term can be literally understood as “merit equalizing.”

## receiver of alms
*bsod snyoms pa*, Skt. *piṇḍapātika*, A spiritual practitioner living from alms as described in the Vinaya.

## Receiver of Goodness
The daughter of a wealthy brahmin in the city Gone to Bliss during the time of the Buddha Dīpaṅkara. She aids the bodhisattva Megha, the future Buddha Śākyamuni, in offering flowers to the newly awakened Dīpaṅkara. A past life of Śākyamuni’s wife Gopā, when he was still Prince Siddhārtha, although in some accounts said to become his wife Yaśodharā.

## Receiver of the Worship of the Worthy
*dgra bcom mchod gnas*, Skt. *dgra bcom mchod gnas*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Ratnadhara (817 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Receiver of True Blessings
*yang dag par byin pa’i bslab blangs*, Skt. *yang dag par byin pa’i bslab blangs*, A great bodhisattva.

## receiving the seal
*phyag rgya yongs su ’dzin pa*, Skt. *dhāraṇīmudrā*, The 20th meditative stability in chapters 6 and 8. The Sanskrit from Dutt would suggest, rather, “Dhāraṇī seal,” as in the Ten Thousand (gzungs kyi phyag rgya).

## receptacle
*za ma tog*, Skt. *karaṇḍa*, A basket, box, or other kind of receptacle with a lid.

## receptive to
*bzod pa*, Skt. *kṣānti*, See “patience.” Also translated here as “endure” and “acceptance.”

## receptive to the unborn nature of phenomena
*chos la bzod pa*, Skt. *dharmakṣāṇti*, The term dharmakṣāṇti can refer either to a set of ways one becomes “receptive” to key points of the Dharma, or it can be an abbreviation of anutpattikadharmakṣāṇti, “receptivity to the unborn nature of phenomena.”

## receptivity
*bzod pa*, Skt. *kṣānti*, See Patience.

## Rechungpa
*ras chung pa*, Skt. *ras chung pa*, (1083–1161). A close disciple of Milarepa, who traveled to India and brought back some of the teaching cycles that Marpa had not transmitted, as well as the Amitāyus tradition he received from the yoginī Siddharājñī.

## Recipient of Divine Worship
*lha yi mchod gnas*, Skt. *lha yi mchod gnas*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Samṛddha (750 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Recipient of the World’s Worship
*’jig rten mchod gnas*, Skt. *’jig rten mchod gnas*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Satyadeva.

## recission
*dbyung ba*, Skt. *āvarhaṇa*, A probation is a remedial act imposed on a monk for having committed a saṅgha remnant. A “penance” (Tib. spo ba; Skt. parivāsa) is imposed, in addition to the probation, if the offense is concealed. The offending monk must ask the saṅgha to give him a penance and/or probation, during which the monk loses five privileges and must perform five menial chores. After completing the penance and/or probation, the saṅgha may rescind the punishment, lit. give a “recission” (Tib. dbyungs ba; Skt. āvarhaṇa), thus restoring the monk’s privileges.

## recitation
A genre of Buddhist literature, and listed as one of both the nine or twelve types. It seems to refer to any text in which verses are mixed with prose, but literally the word means “to be sung,” and could have been used to refer to texts commonly used for recitation.

## recitation instructor
*klog gi slob dpon*, Skt. *pāṭhācārya*, a monk who teaches another to recite even a single verse. One of five types of [instructor](#instructor)s named by the [Buddha](#buddha) when asked to elaborate on the role of an [instructor](#instructor).

## recitation mālā
*bzlas pa’i phreng ba*, Skt. *jāpamālā*, The string of beads used to count mantra recitations. It can be made of a variety of substances depending on the deity or purpose of the recitation.

## Reciter
*bsnyen pa*, Skt. *bsnyen pa*, Reciter (one who recites, especially aloud), also the name of the one foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Krakucchanda.

## Recognizer of Unafflicted Realization
*nyon mongs pa med pa rtogs par khong du chud pa*, Skt. *nyon mongs pa med pa rtogs par khong du chud pa*, A bodhisattva.

## recollecting the Buddha
*sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *buddhānusmṛti*, The practice of recollecting the Buddha is common in all Buddhist traditions and involves taking a buddha such as Śākyamuni or Amitābha as one’s meditative object. The practice typically involves recollecting the qualities of a buddha, reciting their epithets, recalling their image, and so forth.

## Recollecting the Words
*tshig len*, Skt. *tshig len*, Son of the buddha Deveśvara.

## recollection
*dran pa*, Skt. *smṛti*, This is the faculty that enables the mind to maintain its attention on a referent object, counteracting the arising of forgetfulness, which is a great obstacle to meditative stability. Together with alertness, recollection is one of the two indispensable factors for the development of calm abiding (Skt. śamatha). Also translated here as “mindfulness.”

## recollection of breathing
*dbugs phyi nang du rgyu ba rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *praśvāsānusmṛti*, Eighth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of death
*’chi ba rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *mṛtyanusmṛti*, Ninth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of disillusionment
*skyo ba rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *udvegānusmṛti*, Seventh of the ten recollections. In some texts (see ) this item of the ten is replaced by the recollection of quiescence (vyupaśamānusmṛti, nye bar zhi ba rjes su dran pa).

## recollection of ethical discipline
*tshul khrims rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *śīlānusmṛti*, Fourth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of giving away
*gtong ba rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *tyāgānusmṛti*, Fifth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of physicality
*lus su gtogs pa rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *kāya­gatānu­smṛti*, Ninth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of quiescence
*nye bar zhi ba rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *vyupa­śamānu­smṛti*, Seventh of the ten recollections.

## recollection of renunciation
*gtong ba rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *tyāgānu­smṛti*, Fifth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of respiration
*dbugs ’byung ba dang rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *pra­śvāsānu­smṛti*, Eighth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of the body
*lus kyi rnam pa rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *kāya­gatānusmṛti*, Tenth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of the Buddha
*sangs rgyas rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *buddhānusmṛti*, The Sanskrit term buddhānusmṛti (Pali buddhānussati), meaning “mindfulness or recollection of the Buddha,” is a common practice in all Buddhist traditions that involves taking a buddha such as the Buddha Śākyamuni or Amitābha as one’s meditative object.

## recollection of the Dharma
*chos rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *dharmānusmṛti*, Second of the ten recollections.

*lha rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *devānusmṛti*, Sixth of the ten recollections.

## recollection of the Saṅgha
*dge ’dun rjes su dran pa*, Skt. *saṅghānusmṛti*, Third of the ten recollections.

## Red

*dung dang mu tig dmar po*, Skt. *dung dang mu tig dmar po*, An island in the vicinity of Jambudvīpa.

## red lotus
*pad mo*, Skt. *nalinī*, Nelumbo nucifera. The true lotus that has a central pericarp, while the “night lotus” and the “blue lotus” are actually lilies. Padma or nalinī refers to the red variety of the lotus, while the white lotus is called puṇḍarīka.

## refuge instructor
*gnas kyi slob dpon*, newly ordained monks are not allowed to [live independently](#live-independently) until they have passed ten years as a monk and possess one of twenty-one sets of five qualities described in “The Chapter on Going Forth.” Until that time, they are obliged to live as [apprentice](#apprentice)s or journeymen to a [refuge](#refuge) so that they may learn and become established in the conduct expected of a Buddhist renunciate.

“Grasping at the unreal,” creating concepts about an object’s status as real beyond it being a dependently arising phenomenon.

## relativity
*rten cing ’brel bar ’byung ba*, Skt. *pratītya­samutpāda*, In most contexts, this term is properly translated by “dependent origination.” But in the Mādhyamika context, wherein the concept of the ultimate nonorigination of all things is emphasized, “relativity” better serves to convey the message that things exist only in relation to verbal designation and that nothing exists as an independent, self-sufficient entity, even on the superficial level.

## reliance
In the Dharmasaṃgraha, there are said to be four types or sources of reliance, namely reliance on the meaning, reliance on knowledge, reliance on the definitive meaning (or sūtras taken to contain definitive meaning), and reliance on the true nature of reality. This list is also found in the The Teaching of Vimalakīrti (Vimalakīrti­nirdeśa), .

## relic
*ring bsrel*, Skt. *dhātu*, The physical remains or personal objects of a previous tathāgata, arhat, or other realized person that are venerated for their perpetual spiritual potency. They are often enshrined in stūpas and other public monuments so that the Buddhist community at large can benefit from their blessings and power.

## Remaju
The name of a goddess who is said to be Mahākālī’s body emanation.

## Rematī
*re ma ti*, Skt. *re ma ti*, A wrathful Dharma protector who is often portrayed together with her mistress Śrīdevī Mahākālī. At times she is conflated with Śrīdevī Mahākālī, so that the two appear to be identical. She is most often portrayed riding on a donkey and adorned with various wrathful ornaments and hand implements. Rematī is also known for her ability to inflict disease on others and retract it at will. In Kangyur literature Rematī is at times linked to the Indian goddess Revatī and also to the rākṣasī demoness Revatī. This link appears to have been made by the editors of the Kangyur.

## Remati
The name of a goddess who accompanies Mahākālī. At times, the two goddesses appear to be conflated into one, but at other times they are clearly two distinct goddesses. In this text Remati is also said to be Mahākālī’s speech emanation.

## renunciant
*rab byung*, the Sanskrit pravrajyā literally [means](#means) “going forth,” with the sense of leaving the life of a householder and embracing the life of a renunciant. When the term is applied more technically, it refers to the [act](#act) of [becoming](#becoming) a male [novice](#novice) (śrāmaṇera; dge tshul) or female [novice](#novice) (śrāmaṇerikā; dge tshul ma), this being a first stage leading to full ordination.

*dga’ ba spong ba*, Skt. *ratijaha*, The 63rd meditative stability in chapters 6 and 8.

Two factors that are essential for progressing on the path and reaching awakening: the requisite of merit and the requisite of wisdom.

## rescission
*dbyung ba*, Skt. *āvarhaṇa*, The process by which the saṅgha restores a monk’s status. Following the completion of a probation (a remedial act imposed on a monk for having committed a saṅgha remnant) and/or a penance (imposed in addition to the probation if the offense was concealed), the saṅgha may rescind the punishment, lit. “give a rescission,” thus restoring the monk’s privileges.

*pad ma chen po lta bu*, Skt. *kumuda*, One of the sixteen realms that surround the Hell of Heat.

*zla ba’i gnas ltar nya ba*, Skt. *zla ba’i gnas ltar nya ba*, A realm in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three. Also called Moving Like the Moon.

*dong ka’i shing dang sa ha ka ra dang me tog ’byung ba’i ka dam pa lta bu*, Skt. *dong ka’i shing dang sa ha ka ra dang me tog ’byung ba’i ka dam pa lta bu*, One of the bodhisattva great beings.

## resentment
*’chab pa*, Skt. *mrakṣa*, One of twenty or twenty-four so-called secondary mental defilements/afflictions, it is the jealous disparagement of others’ qualities.

## residence
*gnas mal*, Skt. *śayanāsana*, The compound term Tib. gnas mal; Skt. śayanāsana comprises the words “dwelling” or “bed” (see Tib. gnas and mal cha; Skt. śayana) and “seating” (Tib. stan; Skt. āsana). In Vinaya usage, it refers to a monastic residence and its furnishings. The “residence caretaker” (Tib. gnas mal bstabs pa; Skt. śayanāsana­parihāra) is in charge of distributing keys for the individual “dwellings” (Tib. gnas khang; Skt. layana) on site. The term “dwelling/residence” (Tib. gnas mal; Skt. śayana) also appears in terms like bas mtha’ gnas mal, Skt. prāntaśayana (“remote residence”) and Tib. dben pa’i gnas mal (“isolated residence”).

## resident monk
*gnyug mar gnas pa*, Skt. *naivāsiko bhikṣuḥ*, In The Chapter on Lifting Restrictions, a distinction is drawn between “boarding and resident monks” (Tib. gnas pa dang gnyug mar gnas pa’i dge slong rnams). The former, also rendered as “visiting” monks, are short-term occupants who are not familiar with the inner or outer workings of the community. The latter, “resident monks,” are long-term occupants who are familiar with the inner and outer workings of the community. See Kalyāṇamitra (Toh 4113, F.313.b): gnas pa zhes bya ba ni dus thung ngur gnas pa phyi nang gi rgyus mi shes pa’o/ /gnyug mar gnas pa zhes bya ba ni dus yun ring du gnas pa phyi nang gi rgyus shes pa’o.

A bodhisattva in the Meghavatī world of the realized one Melodious King of Clouds. The Sanskrit could be something like Svaraghoṣanirghoṣa.

*sprin las byung ba snang bar byed pa’i dkyil ’khor phyogs bcu mtho ’gebs rnga’i sgra dbyangs shin tu rab sgrogs*, Skt. *sprin las byung ba snang bar byed pa’i dkyil ’khor phyogs bcu mtho ’gebs rnga’i sgra dbyangs shin tu rab sgrogs*, A tathāgata.

The bodhisattva who will be prophesied to become the Buddha All Pervasive Lord. This prophecy will be given to him by the future buddha Vikurvāṇarāja in the world system called Great Array.

## Resting in the Branches of Awakening
*byang chub yan lag gnas*, Skt. *sambodhyaṅ­gastha*, A buddha to the north, from whose buddha field which the bodhisattva child Flower of Clairvoyance comes. The branches of awakening (Skt. bodhyaṅga, Tib. byang chub yan lag) are normally counted as seven: mindfulness, discrimination, diligence, joy, pliability, absorption, and equanimity.

## resting place
*gnas*, Skt. *layana*, Also translated here as “sanctuary,” and “abode.”

## restoration
*gso sbyong*, Skt. *poṣadha*, a twice monthly ceremony performed by monks, nuns, and [novice](#novice)s in which the ordained confess and remedy offenses against their vows, thereby purifying and restoring the vows.

## restoration and purification of vows
*gso sbyin*, Skt. *poṣadha*, Also rendered as “poṣadha.”

## restoration and purification rites
*gso sbyong*, Skt. *poṣadha*, The fortnightly ceremony during which ordained monks and nuns gather to recite the prātimokṣa vows and confess faults and breaches. The term is also sometimes used in reference to the taking of eight vows by a layperson for just one day, a full-moon or new-moon day.

## restoration rite
*gso sbyong*, Skt. *poṣadha*, A bi-weekly ritual performed on the upavasatha holiday, from which the term poṣadha derives. Monastics are expected to confess most types of offenses without delay and so confessions are generally done prior to the start of the restoration rite. During the rite, monastics affirm that they have confessed and amended for offenses, thereby affirming their “purity,” and thus that of the saṅgha as a whole.

## restoration rite site
*gso sbyong gi gnas*, Skt. *poṣadhāmukha*, The Sanskrit compound poṣadha-āmukham (lit. “restoration commencement”) was translated into Tibetan as gso sbyong gi gnas (lit. “restoration rite site”). Kalyāṇamitra’s gloss of poṣadhāmukhaṃ clarifies the Tibetan translation gso sbyong gi gnas: “ ‘should agree on a restoration rite site’; that site where the restoration rite will commence is called the ‘restoration rite site.’ The saṅgha should, through a twofold act and motion, agree to hold the restoration rite at that site.” Toh 4113, (F.312.b): gso sbyong gi gnas la blo mthun par bya’o zhes bya ba ni gnas gang du gso sbyong mngon du byed pa’i gnas de ni gso sbyong gi gnas zhes bya ste/ gnas der gso sbyong bya bar dge ’dun gyis gsol ba dang gnyis kyi las kyis blo mthun par bya ba’o.

## Restrained Faculties
*dbang po bsdams pa*, Skt. *dbang po bsdams pa*, A sage; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## result of non-returners
The third of the four levels of attainment of the vehicle of the śrāvakas, at which one will no longer be reborn in the desire realm.

## result of once-returners
One who has achieved the second of the four levels of attainment on the śrāvaka path and who will thus only be reborn in saṃsāra once more.

## result of stream entry
The first of four levels of attainment on the śrāvaka path, the point from which one is then continuously approaching nirvāṇa.

*phyir mi ’ong ba’i ’bras bu*, Skt. *phyir mi ’ong ba’i ’bras bu*, The state achieved by a non-returner.

*lan cig phyir ’ong ba’i ’bras bu*, Skt. *lan cig phyir ’ong ba’i ’bras bu*, The state achieved by a once-returner.

## retainer
*phyi ’khor*, Skt. *amātya*, blon po is the usual Tibetan translation of amātya.

## retention
*gzungs*, Skt. *dhāraṇī*, The ability to remember all Dharma teachings that are heard. In other contexts, a dhāraṇi is a powerful recitation that is a precursor of mantras and is usually in the form of intelligible sentences or phrases that preserve or retain the essence of a teaching. There are two sets of “four retentions” in relation to this text. (A) As explained in the sūtra itself in chapter 24 (): the retention, respectively, of teachings on composites, on sounds, on kleśas, and on purifications. (B) As explained in the commentary to the opening of the sūtra (1.2, see ): the recited dhāraṇī sentences and phrases themselves, the retention of the memory of the words of all teachings given, the retention of the memory of the meaning of these teachings, and the retention of the realization gained through meditation on that meaning.

## Retentive Intelligence
*gzungs kyi blo gros*, Skt. *dhāraṇī­mati*, Name of the ninety-fifth meditative stability.

## Retinue
*’khor*, Skt. *’khor*, Retinue (a group of attendants accompanying an important person), also the name of a realm of the triple-lute-bearer gods.

## retinue of the Four Great Kings
*rgyal chen bzhi’i ris*, Skt. *cāturmahā­rājika*, The realm of the Four Great Kings and their retinue constitutes the first and lowest heaven of the form realm on the slopes of Mount Meru. The Four Great Kings are Dhṛtarāṣṭra in the east, Virūḍhaka in the south, Virūpākṣa in the west, and Vaiśravaṇa in the north.

## Retuka
*re tu ka*, Skt. *re tu ka*, A village or town. See also .

## Reṇu
*rdul*, Skt. *reṇu*, A son of King Diśāṃpati of Pāṁśula who lived before the time of Buddha Śākyamuni. He became king after the death of his father. In The Hundred Deeds, he is said to have been a previous incarnation of King Bimbisāra.

## Reṇukā
The wife of the sage Jamadagni and the mother of Paraśurāma (“Rāma with an Axe”), the sixth avatāra of Viṣṇu.

## Revatī
*re ba ti*, Skt. *revatī*, This name can refer to various non-Buddhist goddesses (such as Durgā), who often have a wrathful and protective nature. Revatī is also the name of a rākṣasī associated with the illness and mortality of children. Revatī is also one of the constellations in the heavens, personified as a goddess. The Tibetan rendering of this name can also refer to a group of local female deities and even a male monastic disciple of the Buddha Śākyamuni (in which case nam gru translates the Sanskrit name Revata). In Kangyur literature Revatī (both the goddess and the rākṣasī) is at times linked to the Dharma protector Rematī. This link appears to have been made by the editors of the Kangyur.

## Revatī Who Extends One Hand
A grahī. This seems to be another name for the grahī otherwise called Great Revatī Who Extends One Hand (nam gru chen mo lag gcig nyab pa).

## Revata
*nam grus*, Skt. *revata*, A śrāvaka monk among the foremost disciples of the Buddha. His principal quality, according to The Episode of Dṛḍhādhyāśaya, is concentration.

*nam gru som nyi can*, Skt. *kāṅkṣārevata*, An nickname of Revata, a disciple of the Buddha.

*na ma gru ma*, Skt. *revatikā*, One of the great yakṣiṇīs.

## revised terminology
*skad gsar chad*, The ninth century revision and codification of translational equivalents and procedure in Tibet. It was undertaken during the reigns of Senalek (sad na legs, d. 815 ce) and Ralpachen (ral pa can, r. 815–838) and resulted in the Mahāvyutpatti and Drajor Bampo Nyipa (sgra sbyor bam po gnyis pa), the very influential manuals of translation from Sanskrit to Tibetan.

*dbyugs ’byin pa stsol ba*, Skt. *dbyugs ’byin pa stsol ba*, Revitalizer (one who or that which restores vitality), also the name of a buddha.

## Reviving
*yang sos*, Skt. *saṃjīva*, Reviving (bringing back to life or consciousness), also the name of one of the eight hot hells.

## Reviving Hell
*yang sos*, Skt. *sañjīva*, First (and lightest) of the eight hot hells of Buddhist cosmology. Born frightened of one another, the inhabitants of the Reviving Hell fight with each other using sharp weapons, die, and are instantly revived over and over to continue fighting.
