*rnam grangs sems*, Skt. *rnam grangs sems*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Ratna.

## Śreṇya Bimbisāra
*bzo sbyangs gzugs can snying po*, Skt. *śreṇya bimbisāra*, The king of Magadha and a great patron of the Buddha. In other sources he is simply called “King Bimbisāra.” There are several accounts of King Śreṇya Bimbisāra’s first meeting with the Buddha, early on when the latter was the wandering mendicant known as Gautama. Impressed by his conduct, Bimbisāra offered to take Gautama into his court, but Gautama refused, and Bimbisāra wished him success in in his quest for enlightenment and asked him to visit his palace after he had achieved his goal. One account of this episode can be found in the sixteenth chapter of The Play in Full (Toh 95, Lalitavistara). There are other accounts where the two meet earlier on in childhood. Later, after the Buddha’s enlightenment, Bimbisāra became one of his most famous patrons and donated to his saṅgha the Kalandakanivāpa Bamboo Grove, which is the setting of the Bhava­saṅkrānti­sūtra and many other teachings.

*dpal ldan ma*, Skt. *śreyasī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi; one of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK; the name of a nakṣatra.

*dpal stug po*, Skt. *śrīghana*, A tathāgata.

## Śrīgupta

Chief protagonist of the Śrīgupta Sūtra, he sets multiple traps to kill the Buddha on the instruction of his teacher, which the Buddha foresees and skillfully avoids. Feeling remorse for his actions, he takes refuge in the Buddha.

*glang po che’i dpal*, Skt. *śrīhasti*, A great bodhisattva.

*shing pa ta skye ba*, Skt. *rūḍhavaḍa*, A name of Jambudvīpa in an earlier eon.

## Rāhu Holder
*sgra gcan ’dzin*, Skt. *sgra gcan ’dzin*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Brahmadeva.

*sgra gcan stobs med*, Skt. *rāhubala*, One of the thousand sons of King Araṇemin.

## Rāhula
*sgra gcan zin*, Skt. *rāhula*, Rāhula is the name of Śākyamuni Buddha’s physical son. Edgerton reports from different sources that he miraculously descended from Tuṣita heaven into his mother’s womb, and insisted on becoming a monk when he found out that the Buddha was his father. He was ordained by Śāriputra.

## Rāhulabhadra
*sgra can zin bzang po*, Skt. *rāhulabhadra*, son of Siddhārtha Gautama.

## Rāhu­sūrya­garbha
*sgra gcan nyi ma’i snying*, Skt. *rāhu­sūrya­garbha*, The 801st buddha in the first list, 800th in the second list, and 790th in the third list.

## rhythmic-consecutive person
*zla ba phyed pa'i ma ning*, Skt. *pakṣapaṇḍaka*, someone who is female for half of the month and then becomes male for the other half; someone who is stricken with female desires for half of the month and male desires for the other half; or a person who has a sexual disability for half of the month. One of the five types of [person labeled a paṇḍaka](#person-labeled-a-paṇḍaka), all of whom are barred from joining the renunciate order.

## rāśi
*khyim*, Skt. *rāśi*, Literally “heap,” it also means a zodiac sign; in the MMK the meaning extends to cover other categories grouped together with the zodiac constellations.

## rṣi Guṃjika’s abode
*drang srong sgra sgrogs kyi gnas*, Skt. *guṃjikāvasatha*, A place near Nādikā, a village in the country of Vṛji.

## Riṣṭa
*’dod pa*, Skt. *riṣṭa*, One of the pratyeka­buddhas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Rib Roaster
*rtsib ma sreg*, Skt. *rtsib ma sreg*, A rākṣasa king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Ribbon of Joy
*be’u dga’*, Skt. *be’u dga’*, Father of the buddha Vimatijaha.

## rice
*'bras zan*, Skt. *bhakta*, an acceptable form of food for a monk, as identified in the [Four Supports](#four-supports) [section](#section) of the ordination ritual.

## rice leaf
A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## rice porridge
A sweet dish that consists of rice boiled in milk.

## Rice-Milk Mud
*’o thug gi ’dam*, Skt. *’o thug gi ’dam*, A river on Saṅkāśa.

## Rich and Dark Shade
*grib ma snum zhing nag pa*, Skt. *grib ma snum zhing nag pa*, A forest in Continuous Movement.

## Rich Array of Excellence
*bkod pa sna tshogs bzang po*, Skt. *bkod pa sna tshogs bzang po*, Birthplace of the buddha Dharmakūṭa.

## Rich Connections
*sna tshogs rjes su ’brel ba*, Skt. *sna tshogs rjes su ’brel ba*, Birthplace of the buddha Girīndrakalpa.

## Rich Mind
*’byor pa’i blo*, Skt. *’byor pa’i blo*, Attendant of the buddha Mahādatta.

## Rich Treasury
*’byor pa’i mdzod*, Skt. *’byor pa’i mdzod*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Nala.

## Rich with All Wishes
*’dod pa thams cad ’byor pa*, Skt. *’dod pa thams cad ’byor pa*, The name of a yakṣa.

## Riches
*dbyig*, Riches (wealth; abundant possessions), also the name of a member of the Malla clan who worships the Buddha at his parinirvāṇa.

## Ārṣṭiṣeṇa
One of the sublineages connected with the Gautama lineage of the brahmanical tradition. A sublineage of the Sāmavedins.

## right action
*yang dag pa’i las kyi mtha’*, Skt. *saṃyakkarmānta*, Also called “right conduct,” it is convincing others that your activities conform with the doctrine and are harmonious with pure ethics (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.”

## right cognition
*yang dag par shes spa*, Skt. *yang dag par shes spa*, Possibly a reference to yang dag par shes pa’i ye shes bzhi, the “four right cognitions [of the mode of being of phenomena]” (Rangjung Yeshe).

## right effort
*yang dag pa’i rtsol ba*, Skt. *saṃyagvyāyāma*, To meditate repeatedly on the meaning of reality that has already been seen or experienced; an antidote to the objects to be abandoned on the path of seeing (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.”

## right efforts
*yang dag par spong ba*, Skt. *samyakprahāṇa*, A list of four actions that refers to the act of eliminating unwholesome states that have arisen and making sure they do not arise, as well as causing wholesome states to arise and developing them once they have arisen.

## right exertions
*yang dag par spong ba*, Skt. *samyakprahāṇa (bhs)*, These are four: preventing the arising of evil that has not arisen, eliminating the evil that has arisen, generating good qualities that have not arisen, and maintaining good qualities that have arisen.

## right livelihood
*yang dag pa’i ’tsho ba*, Skt. *saṃyagājīva*, To convince others that your livelihood is free from wrong means, such as wheedling behavior, flattery, and so forth (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.”

## right meditation
*yang dag pa’i ting nge ’dzin*, Skt. *saṃyaksamādhi*, Also called “right concentration,” it is to establish meditative concentration free from the faults of laxity and excitement; an antidote to hindrances (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.” Also rendered here as “right meditative concentration.”

## right meditative concentration
*yang dag pa’i ting nge ’dzin*, Skt. *saṃyaksamādhi*, See “right meditation.”

## right mindfulness
*yang dag pa’i dran pa*, Skt. *saṃyaksmṛti*, To retain the object of calm abiding and insight meditation without forgetting it; an antidote to forgetfulness (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.”

## right speech
*yang dag pa’i ngag*, Skt. *saṃyagvāk*, To show others—by means of teaching, debate, and writing—the nature of reality free from conceptual elaborations (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.”

## right understanding
*yang dag pa’i rtog pa*, Skt. *saṃyaksaṃkalpa*, Also called “right determination,” “right thought,” it is to examine how the profound meaning understood through the study of texts complies with the teachings of the Buddha (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.”

## right view
*yang dag pa’i lta*, Skt. *saṃyakdṛṣṭi*, To discern through analytical means the reality of the four noble truths and other phenomena (Rigzin 377). See also “noble eightfold path,” “thirty-seven wings of enlightenment.”

## righteousness
*chos*, Skt. *dharma*, Also translated as “phenomena” and “Dharma” (see entry for “Dharma and Vinaya”).

## rightful recipient of the offerings
In general, a term for a pure monk or ascetic (or the saṅgha as a whole) who may be considered a worthy field of merit (Skt. puṇyakṣetra).

## Śārikā
*shA ri, shA ri kA*, Skt. *śārikā*, [Māṭhara](#māṭhara)’s daughter and mother of [Upatiṣya](#upatiṣya) (aka [Śāriputra](#śāriputra)).

## Rāśika
*tshogs can*, Skt. *rāśika*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Rikpai Raldri
See also “Chom Ralpa.”

## Rikzin Gödemchen
Rikzin Gödemchen Ngödrub Gyaltsen (1337–1409) was the first in the incarnation line of Dorjé Drak Rikzin. His name comes from the fact that three feather-like growths sprouted from his head, so he was given the name “the one with (chen) the feathers (dem) of a vulture (rgod).”

## Rāśina
Skt. *rāśina*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Rinchen Dé
*rin chen sde*, Skt. *rin chen sde*, Eighth-century Tibetan translator of Toh 21.

## Rinchen Drup
*rin chen grub*, Skt. *rin chen grub*, One of the two Tibetan translators of this scripture.

## Rinchen Sangpo
A famous translator and editor of canonical texts during the second spread of Indian Buddhism into Tibet. He lived from 958 to 1055 ᴄᴇ and was mainly active in western Tibet, especially at Tholing monastery.

## Rinchen Tso
*rin chen ’tsho*, Skt. *rin chen ’tsho*, A Tibetan translator active sometime during the late eighth and early ninth centuries.

## Rinchen Zangpo
*rin chen bzang po* (958 - 1055), the most famous translator of the second propagation of Buddhism in Tibet, when the [New Tradition](#new-tradition) began.

## ringing staff
*khar sil*, Skt. *khakkhara*, A rather ornate staff carried by Buddhist monks. The metal rings that hang from the top ornament jingle when the monk plants the staff on the ground as he walks. See The Sūtra on the Ringing Staff (Toh 335), where the Buddha allows the carrying of the ringing staff and describes its characteristics, and The Rite for the Protocols Associated with Carrying the Ringing Staff (Toh 336), where the Buddha prescribes the rite of taking up a ringing staff and explains its use.

## Rṣipatana
*drang srong lhung ba*, Skt. *rṣipatana*, The site near Vārāṇasī where the Buddha first turned the wheel of Dharma.

## Ripe Vessel
*smin pa’i snod*, Skt. *smin pa’i snod*, A town in Videha.

## ripening
In the theory of karma (action) and its effects, ripening refers to the manifestation of the effects of a past action, often in a time and a place far removed from the action itself.

## ripening of karma
*las kyi rnam par smin pa*, Skt. *karmavipāka*, The maturation of past actions (karman) and the manifestation of their effects.

## Ripping of All Vital Points
*gnad dang gnad gcod pa*, Skt. *marma­marma­nikṛntana*, One of sixteen realms that surround the Crushing Hell.

## Śāriputra
*sha ri'i bu*, one of the two foremost [Śrāvaka](#śrāvaka) [disciple](#disciple)s of [Buddha](#buddha) [Śākyamuni](#śākyamuni)

## Śāriputra Upatiṣya
*shA ri’i bu nye rgyal*, Skt. *śāriputra upatiṣya*, See “Śāriputra.”

## Śrisamudra
*dpal gyi rgya mtsho*, Skt. *śrisamudra*, A buddha in the distant past. BHS: Śirisamudra.

## rishi
*drang srong*, Skt. *ṛṣi*, Sage. An ancient Indian spiritual title especially for divinely inspired individuals credited with creating the foundations for all Indian culture.

## Rising
*shar ba*, Skt. *shar ba*, Rising (moving upward; ascending), also the name of a mountain in the eastern sea beyond Jambudvīpa.

## Rising Above All
*phyogs kyi lhun po*, Skt. *phyogs kyi lhun po*, A great bodhisattva.

## Rising like a Mountain
*ri ltar brtsegs*, Skt. *ri ltar brtsegs*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Ratnāgni.

## Rising Mountain
*ri bo brtsegs pa*, Skt. *ri bo brtsegs pa*, Birthplace of the buddha Meruprabha.

## Rising Sun
*nyi ma’i ’char ka*, Skt. *nyi ma’i ’char ka*, One of the bodhisattva great beings.

## Śārisuta
*shA ri’i bu*, Skt. *śārisuta*, Alternative name for Śāriputra.

## Āśritā
*gnas ma*, Skt. *āśritā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## rite
*las*, Skt. *karman*, A rite that is meant to accomplish an activity (such as pacifying, nourishing, etc.). This term is also translated in other instances as “activity,” “karma,” “karman,” or “karmic accumulation.” In the latter three cases the term refers to karmic accumulation, positive or negative, that will produce results in the future, unless it is purified.

## rite to make it hail
*ser ba dbab pa’i las*, A ritual that is performed to bring hail down on an enemy’s lands or country.

## ritual
*cho ga*, Skt. *kalpa*, A ritual or a rite; in our presentation it is translated as “ritual” when it refers to a group or a cycle of rites, and as “rite” when it refers to an individual rite (the distinction, however, is blurred). The term can also refer to a text that is a collection of rites, such as the AP, in the sense of a manual of rites.

## ritual activity
A term that denotes a range of ritual activities that fall under the four broad categories of pacification (śānti; zhi ba), enriching (pauṣṭika; rgyas pa), enthralling (vaśya; dbang byed), and assault (abhicāra; mngon spyod).

## ritual fire pūjā
*me’i sbyin sreg*, Skt. *agnihotra*, Traditional ritual worship involving a sacrificial fire into which oblations are offered.

## Ritual of Peace
*zhi ba’i cho ga*, Skt. *zhi ba’i cho ga*, A world system.

## ritual vase
*ril ba spyi blugs*, Skt. *kamaṇḍalu*, A vase commonly used in brahminical rituals; a vase used to store drinking water.

## Riu
*ri’u*, Skt. *riu*, A scriptural exegete from the south during the Buddha’s time, who Princess She Who Gathers of Takṣaśīla let defeat her in debate, in order to marry him. Their child was Kātyāyana.

## rival communities
*mu stegs can*, Skt. *tīrthika*, A generic term for the followers of the non-Buddhist religious systems that rivaled Buddhism in India, especially during its foundational period.

## rival tīrthika
*pha rol mu stegs can*, Skt. *paratīrthya*, Non-Buddhist sectarians.

## rivalry
*’gran zla*, Enmity or rivalry among wives of the same husband.

## river Ganges
*gang gA’i klung*, Skt. *gaṅgānadī*, The major river in North India and, according to Buddhist cosmology, one of the four sacred rivers that flow through the southernmost continent of Jambudvīpa.

## River Holder
*klung ’dzin*, A nāga king. (Toh 555: chu’i rgyu ’dzin)

## River of a Thousand Flows
*chu bo stong ’bab*, Skt. *chu bo stong ’bab*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Carelessness
*bag med pa’i chu*, Skt. *bag med pa’i chu*, A river in Garlands of Flowers.

## River of Enjoyments
*chu bo dga’ bcas*, Skt. *chu bo dga’ bcas*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Free Flow
*chu bo gar dgar ’bab*, Skt. *chu bo gar dgar ’bab*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Great Enjoyments
*chu bo dga’ bcas che*, Skt. *chu bo dga’ bcas che*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Layered Flows
*chu bo brtsegs ’bab*, Skt. *chu bo brtsegs ’bab*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Purity
*chu bo rnam dag*, Skt. *chu bo rnam dag*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Caraṇabhrāja (930 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## River of Strong Current
*chu bo shugs chen ’bab*, Skt. *chu bo shugs chen ’bab*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Strong Garlands
*chu bo shugs phreng*, Skt. *chu bo shugs phreng*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Sweet Taste
*chu bo ro zhim*, Skt. *chu bo ro zhim*, A river in Dwelling in the Lofty.

## River of Wine
*chang ’bab chu bo*, Skt. *chang ’bab chu bo*, A river in Enjoyment of Scents.

## Rivers and Flatlands
*chu bo sman ljong*, Skt. *chu bo sman ljong*, A peak upon Mount Sumeru.

## Śriyā
*dpal byed ma*, Skt. *śriyā*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Śriyāmatī
*dpal ldan ma*, Skt. *śriyāmatī*, One of the eight goddesses in the south, called upon to grant protection.

## Rājadhāna
*rgyal por gnas*, Skt. *rājadhāna*, One of the thousand sons of King Araṇemin.

## Rājagṛha
*rgyal po’i khab*, Now known as Rajgir and located in the modern Indian state of Bihar, Rājagṛha was the capital of the kingdom of [Magadha](#magadha) during the [Buddha](#buddha)’s lifetime.

## Rāja­gṛha
*rgyal po’i khab*, Skt. *rāja­gṛha*, Modern Rajgir.

## Rājaka
*’od ldan*, Skt. *rājaka*, A person who hosts Prince Siddhārtha after he leaves his home.

## rājamudra
*rgyal po’i phyag rgya*, Skt. *rājamudra*, Lit. “Seal of the king.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Rājan
*rgyal po*, Skt. *rājan*, The 595th buddha in the first list, 594th in the second list, and 588th in the third list.

## Rājanina
*rA dza ni na*, Skt. *rājanina*, A lake in Living by Rājanina.

## rājarṣi
*rgyal po’i drang srong*, Skt. *rājarṣi*, A class of beings.

## Rājendra
*dbang po’i rgyal po*, Skt. *rājendra*, One of the eight tathāgatas.

## Rājgṛha
*rgyal po’i khab*, Skt. *rājgṛha*, Town close to Nālānda in the modern state of Bihar.

## Rājgir
*rgyal po’i khab*, Skt. *rājagṛha*, “King’s House;” name of a town in modern-day Bihar, North India.

## Śrījñānākara
*ye shes ’byung gnas dpal*, Skt. *śrījñānākara*, A buddha.

## Rājyavardhana
*rgyal srid ’phel*, Skt. *rājyavardhana*, An elephant. See also .

## Rājya­vardhana
Skt. *rājya­vardhana*, A seventh-century king who ruled over a part of Madhyadeśa.

## Ārka
The name of a king.

## Śrīkūṭa
A bodhisattva in the audience of this sūtra.

## Śrīkaṇṭha
*dpal mgrin*, Skt. *śrīkaṇṭha*, The district around Sthāṇvīśvara.

## Śrīkūṭa­jñāna­buddhi
*ye shes dpal brtsegs blo*, Skt. *śrīkūṭa­jñāna­buddhi*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## rākṣasī
*srin mo*, Skt. *rākṣasī*, A female rākṣasa. Supernatural beings with a yearning for human flesh but who can also be converted into being protectors of the Dharma.

## Rākṣasa
*srin po*, a kind of malignant spirit that eats human flesh.

## rākṣasa/rākṣasī
*srin po*, Skt. *rākṣasa*, A flesh-eating demon that haunts frightening places.

## rākṣasīs who flash like lightning
*nam mkha’i glog ma srin*, A class of demonic female beings.

## Śrīkūṭavināśaka
*dpal brtsegs rnam par ’joms pa*, Skt. *śrī­kūṭa­vināśaka*, A buddha.

## Śrīkānti
*dpal mdzes pa*, Skt. *śrīkānti*, Another name of Lakṣmī.

## Rāmā
*rA ma*, Skt. *rāmā*, A rākṣasī living on Ardhamaru.

## Rāma
The name of a sage who was born to the sage Jamadagni and his kṣatriya wife Reṇukā. Also referred to as Rāma Bhārgava or Paraśurāma (“Rāma with an Axe”), he is the sixth avatāra of Viṣṇu, not to be confused with Viṣṇu’s seventh incarnation as King Rāma, the protagonist of the Rāmāyaṇa.

## Śrāmaṇa
*dge tshul*, Skt. *śrāmaṇa*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Rāmadeva
*rA ma de ba*, Skt. *rāmadeva*, The name of a vetāla.

## rāmadūtī
*rA ma du ti*, Skt. *rāmadūtī*, This has not been identified.

## śrāmaṇerī
Within the Buddhist tradition, it means a novice nun who, in the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda monastic tradition, takes thirty-six vows.

## śrāmaṇera
A renunciant who lives his life as a mendicant. More specifically, within the monastic tradition, it can also mean a novice monk who, in the Tibetan Mūlasarvāstivāda monastic tradition, takes thirty-six vows.

## Śrāmaṇeraka
*dge tshul*, Skt. *śrāmaṇeraka*, A nāga king.

## Śrī­mahā­ratna­pratimaṇḍitā
*dpal rin po ches brgyan pa*, Skt. *śrī­mahā­ratna­pratimaṇḍitā*, The world system of the buddha Śrī­maṇi­ratna­sambhava.

## Śrīmahāviraja
*nga rgyal dpal dang rdul bral*, Skt. *śrīmahāviraja*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the fifty-ninth) when he becomes a buddha.

## Śrī­maṇi­ratna­sambhava
*dpal nor bu rin po che las byung ba*, Skt. *śrī­maṇi­ratna­sambhava*, A buddha in the world system called Śrī­mahā­ratna­pratimaṇḍitā.

## Rāmakāṅkṣi
*dga’ ba’i tshang tshing*, Skt. *rāmakāṅkṣi*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Śrīmanta
*dpal ldan*, Skt. *śrīmanta*, A mountain king.

## Rāmapāla
*ne bai pA la*, Skt. *rāmapāla*, (1) A king of the Pāla dynasty who ruled from 1077–1120 ce (rA ma phA la). (2) The alternate spelling, ne bai pA la, is tentatively identified to be the very same king of the Pāla dynasty. See .

## Śrīmat
*dpal ldan*, Skt. *śrīmat*, A nāga king.

## Śrīmatī
A woman of the brahmin caste from Vārāṇasī.

## Śrīmati
*dpal gyi lha mo*, Skt. *śrīmati*, A goddess; a yakṣiṇī in the Mahā­māyūrī­vidyārājñī (Toh 559).

## Śrāmaṇyaphala­sūtra
*dge sbyong gi ’bras bu’i mdo*, Skt. *śrāmaṇyaphala­sūtra*, No complete Sanskrit version of this sūtra is known (see Kudo 2004, p. 250, n. 22, for a summary of extant versions of this sūtra and further readings).

## Rāmeśvara
*dga’ ba’i dbang phyug*, Skt. *rāmeśvara*, One of the four auxiliary pīṭhas.

## Śrīmitra
Skt. *śrīmitra*, Śrīmitra (d. 343), a prince from Kucha (龜茲, Qiuci, in the Tarim Basin on the Silk Road, present-day Kuqa in Xinjiang), who lived one generation before the other famous Kuchean translator, Kumārajīva. Kucha at the time was a culturally Indic, Tocharian-speaking kingdom. Śrīmitra abdicated the throne in favor of his younger brother and became a monk and translator, traveling to China. He spent 307–312 in Luoyang (洛陽) where he translated Taishō 1331 mentioned here, later moving to Jiankang (建康). He was responsible for introducing a number of other Buddhist texts and dhāraṇīs to China.

## Rāmāvarānta
*mi mo gya nom mchog*, Skt. *rāmāvarānta*, A land in South India.

## Rāndhava
*nor bdag*, Skt. *rāndhava*, One of the thousand sons of King Araṇemin.

## Śroṇa
*gro zhin*, Skt. *śroṇa*, A śrāvaka disciple of the Buddha.

## Śroṇa (Śroṇajāt)
*gro byin skyes*, a [vīṇā](#vīṇā) player who became a [disciple](#disciple) of the [Buddha](#buddha) and gained the ability to visit other [realm](#realm)s, notably those of the [pretas](#preta).

## Roadless
*lam med pa*, Skt. *lam med pa*, Roadless (having no roads), also the name of an island in the vicinity of Jambudvīpa.

## Śroṇakoṭīkarṇa
*gro bzhin skyes rna ba bye ba ri*, Skt. *śroṇakoṭīkarṇa*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa
*gro zhin skyes bye ba nyi shu pa*, Skt. *śroṇakoṭīviṃśa*, A disciple of the Buddha, known in Pāli as Soṇa Koḷivisa.

## roamers
*rab tu rgyug pa*, Skt. *rab tu rgyug pa*, A class of asuras.

## roaming
*gnas med par spyod pa*, Skt. *aniketacārī*, The 73rd meditative stability in chapters 6 and 8.

## Roaming Sumeru
*ri rab tu rgyu ba*, Skt. *ri rab tu rgyu ba*, A land in Godānīya.

## roaming the cimiśa cave
*tsi mi sha’i phug na rgyu ba*, Skt. *tsi mi sha’i phug na rgyu ba*, A class of vidyādharas.

## Śroṇaparāntaka
*rgyun gyi pha rol mthar byed*, Skt. *śroṇaparāntaka*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Roar Adorned with a Hundred Thousand Virtues
*dge ba brgya stong gis rab tu brgyan pa’i nga ro*, Skt. *dge ba brgya stong gis rab tu brgyan pa’i nga ro*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Mayūra.

## Roar Adorned with the Splendor of the Sun
*nyi ma’i gzi brjid kyis rab tu brgyan pa’i nga ro*, Skt. *nyi ma’i gzi brjid kyis rab tu brgyan pa’i nga ro*, Attendant of the buddha Jñānin.

## Roar Attainment
*nga ro thob*, Skt. *nga ro thob*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Mahendra.

## Roar Beyond Marks

## Roca
*snang ba*, Skt. *roca*, The last buddha of the Bhadra kalpa, which according to The White Lotus of Compassion Sūtra (Toh 111, Mahā­karuṇā­puṇḍarīka­sūtra, where it was translated as gsal mdzad) is the thousand-and-fifth buddha. The Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesied that the youngest of the thousand Vedapāṭhaka pupils of Brahmin Samudrarenu would be the Buddha Roca. In present times it is most commonly translated as mos pa.

## rocanā
*smig bcud*, Skt. *rocanā*, In the Cakra­saṃvara-tantra, rocanā is a medical concretion or bezoar stone found within the organs of certain animals (Gray, 2007, p 207 n3). Alternatively, Monier-Williams identifies it as “a particular yellow pigment,” or even a plant. It is unclear to us what the term refers to in this particular context.

## Rongpo
There is very little biographical information on Rongpo, but he appears to have come a generation after Khyungpo Yudri. He is responsible for having made amendments to the scripts of Khyungpo Yudri’s tradition and is the author of an important handwriting manual, yig ge’i thig ris gsal ba’i rin chen sgrom bu.

## Rongtönpa
*rong ston shes bya kun rig shA kya rgal mtshan*, A great Sakya scholar (1367–1449), very influential for the tradition of Perfection of Wisdom studies in Tibet.

## rooftop shed

## root downfall
*ltung ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *mūlāpatti*, The most severe of the five types of offenses a monastic can incur. A monastic who violates one of the four principal vows and thereby incurs a defeat is expelled from the saṅgha community. They are no longer entitled to participate in communal activities, nor are they entitled to enjoy its perquisites, such as food and lodging. The four are sexual intercourse, theft, murder, and claiming greater realization than one has. See also “pārājika.”

## root downfalls
*ltung ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *mūlāpatti*, Downfalls are actions of body, speech, and mind that cause one to fall from the path of awakening and, in the cases of root downfalls, to fall into the lower realms of existence.

## root mantra
*rtsa ba’i sngags*, Skt. *mūlamantra*, A term for the most important and often the most simplified spell associated with a particular buddha, bodhisattva, or other being.

## root of madness
*myos pa’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *myos pa’i rtsa ba*, A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## root of virtue
*dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *kuśalamūla*, A virtuous action or state of mind that will “ripen” into happiness later in this life, the next, or at some point in the unknown future.

## Root teacher
*rtsa ba'i bla ma*,
1. the principal, or first, spiritual teacher from whom one has received [empowerment](#empowerment)s, commentaries and pith instructions.
2. the teacher who has introduced one to the nature of the mind.

## roots of demerit
*mi dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *akuśalamūla*, See “roots of nonvirtue.”

## roots of merit
*dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *kuśalamūla*, See “roots of virtue.”

## roots of nonvirtue
*mi dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *akuśalamūla*, The opposite of the “roots of virtue.”

## roots of unwholesome states
*mi dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *akuśalamūla*, See “roots of wholesome states.”

## roots of virtue
*dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *kuśalamūla*, In most contexts designates the three roots of good, i.e., virtuous, states of mind: the opposites of the three mental “poisons” of greed (lobha), hatred (dveṣa), and confusion (moha). Edgerton (BHSD, s.v. “kuśalamūla”) translates kuśalamūla as “the root(s) of merit.” See . For a different list of three roots of virtue, see Dharmasaṃgraha (Müller and Wenzel 1885, no. 15).

## roots of wholesome states
*dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *kuśalamūla*, According to most lists (specifically those of the Pāli and some Abhidharma traditions), the (three) roots of virtue or the roots of the good or wholesome states (of mind) are what makes a mental state good or bad; they are identified as the opposites of the three mental “poisons” of greed, hatred, and delusion. Actions based on the roots of virtue will eventually lead to future happiness. The Dharmasaṃgraha, however, lists the three roots of virtue as (1) the mind of enlightenment, (2) purity of thought, and (3) freedom from egotism (Skt. trīṇi kuśala­mūlāni | bodhi­cittotpādaḥ, āśayaviśuddhiḥ, ahaṃkāramama­kāraparityāgaśceti|).

*dpal gyi gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *śrītejorāja*, A buddha.

## Śrī­tejo­vimala­gātra
*gzi brjid dri ma med pa’i lus*, Skt. *śrī­tejo­vimala­gātra*, A bodhisattva present in the Buddha’s assembly.

## Ārti
*nyam thag pa*, Skt. *ārti*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Rātri
*mtshan mo*, Skt. *rātri*, The goddess of the night.

## Āruṇā
*skya rengs*, Skt. *āruṇā*, One of the eight goddesses in the west, called upon to grant protection.

## Ru Tsam
*ru ’tshams*, A place and monastery at the border of Ü and Tsang, between Tsurphu and Nyemo, figuring in the history of the early Sakya masters.

## Ruby Forest
*pad ma rA ga’i nags*, Skt. *pad ma rA ga’i nags*, A forest in Moving in Mixed Environments.

## Rucira­bhadra­yaśas
*grags pa yid du ’ong bas bzang ba*, Skt. *rucira­bhadra­yaśas*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Rucira­brahmā
*tshangs pa yid du ’ong ba*, Skt. *rucira­brahmā*, Literally “Attractive Brahmā,” an epithet for Brahmā, one of the epithets that in the non-Buddhist tradition designated him as the primordial creator.

## Rucira­dhvaja
*mdzes pa’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *rucira­dhvaja*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Ruciraketu
*mdzes pa’i tog*, Skt. *ruciraketu*, The name of a bodhisattva, central to the narrative of this sūtra, who has a dream in which a prayer of confession emanates from a shining golden drum. (In chapter 12, this is also the name a king in the distant past.)

## Ruciramati
*mdzes pa’i blo gros*, Skt. *ruciramati*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Rucira­śrī­garbha
*dpal yid du ’ong ba’i snying po*, Skt. *rucira­śrī­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Rudanī
*ngud mo*, Skt. *rudanī*, A river.

## Rudhirāhāriṇī
*khrag za ma*, Skt. *rudhirāhāriṇī*, A great rākṣasī.

## rudrā
A female rudra. The term rudra here seems to be applied to a class of nonhuman beings who, as their name indicates, are specifically wrathful or hostile.

## Rudra
A brahmanical deity, the wrathful form of Śiva.

## Rudradatta
*drag pos ’od byin*, Skt. *rudradatta*, A character from literature (it is not clear which one).

## Rudraka
*lhag spyod*, Skt. *rudraka*, A meditation teacher who was one of the Buddha’s teachers before he attained awakening. Although the spelling Rudraka is attested in the Sanskrit of this sūtra, in most other texts his name is Udraka, or Udraka Rāmaputra (“Udraka the son of Rāma”).

## Rudrakātyāyanī
*ka ta ya na dregs ma*, Skt. *rudrakātyāyanī*, ‟Violent Kātyāyanī,” one of the eight kātyāyanī spirits.

## rudrākṣa
*ru drAk+Sha*, Skt. *rudrākṣa*, Seeds of Elaeocarpus ganitrus with rough surface. The larger ones are used for counting the mantras of wrathful deities.

## Śrughnā
*yul srug na*, Skt. *śrughnā*, A country.

## Śrughna
*’gro ’joms*, Skt. *śrughna*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Āruṇika
One of the lineages within the Sāmaveda branch of the brahmanical tradition.

## rule
*khrims su bca’ ba*, Skt. *kriyākāra*, A rule devised to meet specific or local conditions. Tibetan monasteries are governed by a “constitution” (bca’ yig), which is a document that compiles the “rules” (Tib. bca’ khrims) specific to that monastery.

## rule of training
*bslab pa’i gzhi*, Skt. *sikṣāpada*, The prātimokṣa rules for monks and nuns, ten rules for novices, six rules for female probationers, and five rules for laypeople.

## Ruler
*dbang po*, Skt. *dbang po*, Ruler (one who governs or reigns), also the name of a son of the buddha Indra.

## Ruler Gift
*dbang pos byin*, Skt. *dbang pos byin*, Attendant of the buddha Jagatpūjita.

## Ruler of Demigods
*lha ma yin gyi bdag mo*, Skt. *lha ma yin gyi bdag mo*, Mother of the buddha Rāhudeva.

## Ruler of Gods
*lha yi dbang phyug*, Skt. *lha yi dbang phyug*, Mother of the buddha Ratnapradatta.

## Ruler of Humanity
*mi yi dbang phyug ma*, Skt. *mi yi dbang phyug ma*, Mother of the buddha Uccaratna.

## Ruler of Humans
*skye ba’i dbang po*, Skt. *skye ba’i dbang po*, Father of the buddha Pūrṇacandra.

## Ruler of Men
*skye dbang*, Skt. *skye dbang*, Attendant of the buddha Anunnata.

## Ruler of Victors
*rgyal ba’i dbang po*, Skt. *rgyal ba’i dbang po*, Father of the buddha Drumendra.

## Ruler Qualities
*yon tan dbang po*, Skt. *yon tan dbang po*, Father of the buddha Viraja.

## Ruler Radiance
*dbang po’i ’od zer*, Skt. *dbang po’i ’od zer*, Son of the buddha Jagatpūjita.

## rules adopted
*khrims su bca’ ba*, Skt. *kriyākāra*, The “rules adopted” at a monastic site are unique regulations devised to meet specific or local conditions. Yijing renders this term as both 立制 (Taishō 1445) and 所有制法 (Taishō 1446).

## rules of customary conduct
*kun tu spyod pa’i chos*, Skt. *āsamudācāriko dharmaḥ*, This term is frequently used in the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya to define the rights and responsibilities of positions within the administration of monasteries. It is also used, as here, to stipulate monastics’ regular obligations, from hygiene to training. This word appears in several variants throughout the Kangyur and Tengyur, including rig pa spyod pa can.

## Ruling Banner
*rgyal mtshan dbang po*, Skt. *rgyal mtshan dbang po*, Father of the buddha Indra.

## Ruling Light
*dbang po ’od*, Skt. *dbang po ’od*, Mother of the buddha Druma.

## Rumbling Like Drums
*rnga bo che dang cang te’u yi sgra ltar dir dir*, Skt. *rnga bo che dang cang te’u yi sgra ltar dir dir*, A garuḍa king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Runglung Shödrok
A monastery associated with the early production of vinaya texts.

## runners
*kun tu rgyug pa*, Skt. *kun tu rgyug pa*, A class of asuras.

## Rurubha
*ri dags can*, Skt. *rurubha*, A mountain king.

## Rutaprabhāsa
*sgra snang*, Skt. *rutaprabhāsa*, The name of the eon in which, according to the prophecy of the Buddha Ratnagarbha, the young brahmin Radiant Bull will become the Buddha Ratna­cchatrābhyudgata­raśmi in the realm Rutasañcaya.

## Rutasañcaya
*sgra yang dag par bstsags pa*, Skt. *rutasañcaya*, The realm in which the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies Samudrareṇu’s pupil Radiant Bull will become the Buddha Ratna­cchatrābhyudgata­raśmi.

## Rutasvara
*skad kyi sgra*, Skt. *rutasvara*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Rāvaṇī
*sgra sgrogs pa*, Skt. *rāvaṇī*, Name of a rākṣasī and Dharma protector.

## Rāvaṇa
Skt. *rāvaṇa*, King of the Rākṣasas in Laṅka. He features prominently in the Ramāyāna where he kidnaps Rāma’s wife Sīta.

## Śrāvaṇa
*dbyar zla tha chung*, Skt. *śrāvaṇa*, The month of Śrāvaṇa generally falls in July or August, and on its fifteenth day begins the “later rains” retreat.

## śrāvakā
*nyan thos*, Skt. *śrāvakā*, See “disciple.”

## Śrāvaka
*nyan thos*, a follower of the root [vehicle](#vehicle) of Buddhism whose goal is to attain [liberation](#liberation) from the sufferings of [saṃsāra](#saṃsāra) as an [Arhat](#arhat). Unlike the followers of the [Great Vehicle](#great-vehicle), the Śrāvakas do not aspire to full [enlightenment](#enlightenment) for the sake of all beings.

## Śrāvaka Vehicle
The vehicle comprising the teaching of the śrāvakas, those disciples of the Buddha who aspire to attain the state of an arhat by seeking self-liberation. The śrāvakas are typically defined as “those who hear the teaching from the Buddha and make it heard by others.”

## Śrāvakayāna
*nyan thos kyi theg pa*, the [vehicle](#vehicle) of the [Śrāvakas](#śrāvaka).

## Śrāvaka­yāna
*nyan thos kyi theg pa*, Skt. *śrāvaka­yāna*, The vehicle comprising the teaching of the śrāvakas.

## Śrīvardhana
*dpal ’phel*, Skt. *śrīvardhana*, A nāga king.

## Śrāvastī
*mnyan yod*, During the life of the [Buddha](#buddha), Śrāvastī was a major city in the kingdom of Kosala, in present day Uttar Pradesh.

## Śrāvasti
*mnyan yod*, Skt. *śrāvasti*, The capital of the ancient Kosala kingdom in India.

## Ūrṇāvat
*mdzod spu ldan*, Skt. *ūrṇāvat*, The 280th buddha in the first list, 279th in the second list, and 279th in the third list.

## śrīvatsa
*dpal gyi be’u*, Skt. *śrīvatsa*, An auspicious design on the Buddha’s body, mentioned in this text at his heart (in the form of a curl of hair in that shape) as well as on his hands and feet (in the form of lines in the skin). It is often depicted in Tibetan Buddhist tradition as the “eternal knot” symbol, but takes different forms as a motif shared by other traditions of Indian origin. It is said, for example, to be an auspicious mark on Viṣṇu’s chest that represents the insignia of his consort Lakṣmī in the form of an inverted triangle or the shape of a four-petaled flower.

## śrīvatsa mark
*dpal be’u*, Skt. *śrīvatsa*, A swirl of chest hair that in the Buddhist tradition is counted as one of the eighty minor marks of a great being. It is also a regular iconographic feature of the Brahmanical deity Viṣṇu. The srīvatsa can be stylistically depicted as an endless knot, and is thus included among the eight auspicious symbols in Buddhism.

## śrīvatsa motif
*dpal gyi be’u*, Skt. *śrī­vatsa*, An auspicious symbol, taking the form of an endless knot, indicative of eternity.

## āryā
*’phags ma*, Skt. *āryā*, Generally has the common meaning of a noble female, one of a higher class or caste. In Dharma terms it means a female who has gained the realization of the path and is superior for that reason.

## Īrṣyā Yamāri
*phrag dog gshin rje’i gshed*, Skt. *īrṣyāyamāri*, “Jealousy Yamāri,” a deity in the maṇḍala of Black Yamāri. Also known as Īrṣyāvajra Yamāri Īrṣyāvajra

## ārya
*’phags pa*, Skt. *ārya*, Generally has the common meaning of a noble male, one of a higher class or caste. In Dharma terms it means a male who has gained the realization of the path and is superior for that reason.

## Āryadeva
*'phags pa lha* (2nd century), the most famous [disciple](#disciple) of [Nāgārjuna](#nāgārjuna), whose teaching he commented upon in several treatises on [Mādhyamika](#mādhyamika) philosophy. See [Middle way](#middle-way).

## Āryapriya
*’phags pa dgyes pa*, Skt. *āryapriya*, The 755th buddha in the first list, 754th in the second list, and 744th in the third list.

## āryas’ level
*’phags pa’i sa*, Skt. *āryabhūmi*, Levels of bodhisattvas on the paths of seeing, meditation, and no more learning.

## Āryastuta
*’phags pas bstod*, Skt. *āryastuta*, The 884th buddha in the first list, 883rd in the second list, and 874th in the third list.

## Āryavimuktisena
*rnam grol sde*, Skt. *vimuktisena*, Indian commentator on the Abhisamayālaṃkāra (fl. early sixth century).

## Āryāsaṅga
*’phags pa thogs med*, Skt. *āryāsaṅga*, This great Indian philosopher lived in the fourth century and was the founder of the Vijñānavāda, or “Consciousness-Only,” school of Mahāyāna Buddhism.

## Īrṣyāvajra
*phrag dog rdo rje*, Skt. *īṛṣyāvajra*, “Vajra Jealousy,” a deity in the maṇḍala of Black Yamāri. Also known as Īrṣyā Yamāri and Yamāri Īrṣyāvajra.

## Saṃbhavā
*’byung ba*, Skt. *saṃbhavā*, A realm in the distant past.

## Saṃbhava
*yang dag ’byung*, Skt. *saṃbhava*, The second of the brahmin Samudrareṇu’s eighty sons. The Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies that he will become the Buddha Vairocanakusuma.

## Saṃbhavagiri
*yang dag ’byung ba’i mchog*, Skt. *saṃbhavagiri*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Saṃbhavapuṣpa
*yang dag ’byung dang me tog*, Skt. *saṃbhavapuṣpa*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the sixty-sixth) when he becomes a buddha.

## Saṃbhogakāya
*longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku*, Body of Perfect Enjoyment, the spontaneously luminous aspect of Buddhahood, only perceptible to highly realized beings.

## Saṃbhāra
*tshogs*, Skt. *saṃbhāra*, A buddha realm.

## Sabzang Mati Paṇchen
*sa bzang ma ti paN chen blo gros rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *sa bzang ma ti paN chen blo gros rgyal mtshan*, A great fourteenth century (1294–1376) Jonangpa scholar and translator, student of Dolpopa, who had earlier studied at Nyetang, Ralung, Sakya, and Zhalu. He is best known for his revised translations, made with Jonang Lotsāwa Lodrö Pal, of the Kālacakra­tantra and Vimala­prabhā.

## Sacintyārtha­garbha
Skt. *sacintyārtha­garbha*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Saṃcālitā
*shin tu sbyangs*, Skt. *saṃcālitā*, The daughter of a courtesan in another world in the distant past. A previous life of Gopā. The name as given in verse. In prose she is called Sucalita­rati­prabhāsa­śrī.

## Sañcodaka
*yang dag skul pa*, Skt. *sañcodaka*, A god.

## sacramental substances
*dam tshig gyi rdzas*, Skt. *samayadravya*, Sacramental substances ingested as part of tantric ritual; frequently composed of bodily fluids or illicit meats.

## Sacred
*dam pa*, Skt. *dam pa*, See “Sacred Goddess Who Upholds the Teachings and Delights in the Great Vehicle.”

## Sacred Dharma
*dam chos*, Skt. *dam chos*, Attendant of the buddha Brahmā.

## sacred doctrine
*chos*, Skt. *dharma*, The term dharma (chos) conveys ten different meanings, according to Vasubandhu’s Vyākhyā­yukti. In the context‌ of the present work, it may mean “sacred doctrine” (also rendered “Dharma” in this translation), the “attributes” which buddhas and bodhisattvas acquire, “phenomena” or “things” in general, and, more specifically, “mental phenomena” which are the object of the mental faculty (manas, yid).

## Sacred Goddess
*dam pa lha mo*, Skt. *dam pa lha mo*, See “Sacred Goddess Who Upholds the Teachings and Delights in the Great Vehicle.”

## Sacred Goddess Who Upholds the Teachings and Delights in the Great Vehicle
*dam pa lha mo theg pa chen po la rab tu dga’ bar sems pa bstan pa ’dzin pa*, Skt. *dam pa lha mo theg pa chen po la rab tu dga’ bar sems pa bstan pa ’dzin pa*, A queen of the Dharma king Great Diligent Nāga.

## sacred thread
The sacred thread worn by a member of the so-called “twice-born” higher castes in India.

## sacrifice
Any Vedic ritual in which offerings are made, typically by means of a sacrificial fire.

## Sacrifice Gift
*mchod sbyin byin*, Skt. *mchod sbyin byin*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Brahmarāja (897 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Sacrifice of the Strong Accomplishment of Power
*mthu rtsal stobs grub mchod sbyin*, Skt. *mthu rtsal stobs grub mchod sbyin*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Arajas.

## sacrifice tree
Ficus indica.

## sacrificial post
*mchod sdong*, Skt. *yūpa*, A post set up as a marker to which offerings may be presented. Described in the Maitreyāvadāna (“The Story of Maitreya”), which in the Kangyur is found within the Bhaiṣajya­vastu (in Vinayavastu, Toh 1, Degé Kangyur vol. kha, folios 29a-32b), see Yao (2021), 3.139 (the term is translated as “divine pillar”); a matching passage from the Divyāvadāna is translated in Rotman (2008), pp. 121–24.

## sacrificial rite
A type of ritual.

## sad destinies
*ngan ’gro*, Skt. *durgati*, See “evil destinies.”

## Saddharma­ghoṣāmbara­dīpa­rāja
*dam chos dbyangs mchog sgron ma’i rgyal po*, Skt. *saddharma­ghoṣāmbara­dīpa­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past, as rendered in verse. In prose he is called Dharma­cakra­nirghoṣa­gagana­pradīpa­rāja.

## saddle horse
*pa ha na*, Skt. *pa ha na*, A type of worm (srin bu) that lives in and feeds on the body.

## Sadgaṇin
*legs tshogs can*, Skt. *sadgaṇin*, The 345th buddha in the first list, 344th in the second list, and 339th in the third list.

## Saṃdhi­nirmocana­sūtra
*dgongs pa nges ’grel pa’i mdo*, Skt. *saṃdhi­nirmocana­sūtra*, The Saṃdhi­nirmocana­sūtra ( Unraveling the Intent , Toh 106) is one of the most important Mahāyāna sūtras, especially for the Yogācāra school. As an authoritative source for Mahāyāna Buddhist hermeneutics, it is perhaps best known for its delineation of the three turnings of the wheel of the dharma (dharmacakrapravartana), which became a highly influential schema for classifying the teachings of the Buddha according to their various intended meanings and target audiences.

## Saṃdhāna
*’dum byed*, Skt. *saṃdhāna*, A householder who was the Buddha in a former life.

## Sadāmatta
*rtag tu myos*, Skt. *sadāmatta*, One of the three classes of yakṣas at the base of Meru, below the paradises of the mahārājas, as part of the lowest class of paradises in the desire realm. Their name means “constantly intoxicated or insane” and because of their condition they are unable to follow the path to enlightenment.

## Sadāparibhūta
*rtag tu brnyas pa*, Skt. *sadāparibhūta*, A bodhisattva in the distant past, whose name has been translated to mean “Constantly Ridiculed” (sadā-pari­bhūta) in Tibetan and by Burnouf from the Sanskrit. The Chinese translation and Kern from the Sanskrit translate it as “Never Ridiculed” (sadā-apari­bhūta). The difference results from how the compound is broken apart. It is the Chinese and Kern version that better fits the context.

## Sadprarudita
*rtag tu ngu*, a [Bodhisattva](#bodhisattva) whose name [means](#means) "Ever Weeping", on account of the numerous tears he [shed](#shed) in his quest to receive the teachings on transcendent [wisdom](#wisdom).

## Sadāprarudita
*rtag par rab tu ngu ba*, Skt. *sadāprarudita*, Sadāprarudita (literally, “He Who Was Always Weeping”) is the bodhisattva whose exemplary search for the Perfection of Wisdom and devotion to his teacher Dharmodgata are narrated in the final chapters (73–76) of this text.

## Sadā­vatāra­prekṣin
*rtag tu glags tshol ba la rjes su lta ba*, Skt. *sadā­vatāra­prekṣin*, A māra (lit. “He Who Always Looks for a Weak Point”).

## safflower
*le brgan rtsi*, Skt. *kusumbha*, Carthamus tinctorius.

## saffron
*gur kum*, Skt. *kuṅkuma*, Although YJ’s transliteration 茶矩麼 chajumo corresponds to kuṅkuma or saffron, his translation, 鬱金 yujin instead refers to turmeric or Curcuma longa.

## Saffron Color
*kha dog ngur smrig*, Skt. *kha dog ngur smrig*, A bodhisattva who seeks a prophecy from Śākyamuni.

## Saffron Summit
*gur kum gyi rtse mo*, Skt. *gur kum gyi rtse mo*, A holy site blessed by the presence of sages.

## Saga
*sa ga*, Skt. *sa ga*, Father of the buddha Jayanandin.

## Sagacious
*blo ldan*, Skt. *matimān*, Sagacious (having or showing keen discernment; wise), also another name of Citraketu.

## Sagara
*dug chen mtsho*, Skt. *sagara*, A legendary king before the time of the Buddha.

## sage
*thub pa*, Skt. *muni*, An ancient title given to ascetics, monks, hermits, and saints, namely, someone who has attained the realization of a truth through their own contemplation and not by divine revelation. Here also used as a specific epithet of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Sage Faith
*drang srong dad pa*, Skt. *drang srong dad pa*, Birthplace of the buddha Arthakīrti.

## Sage Friend
*drang srong bshes gnyen*, Skt. *drang srong bshes gnyen*, Father of the buddha Ṛṣideva.

## Sage Gift
*drang srong byin*, Skt. *drang srong byin*, Son of the buddha Guṇakīrti.

## Sage Intelligence
*drang srong blo*, Skt. *drang srong blo*, Father of the buddha Hutārci.

## Sage Joy
*drang srong dga’*, Skt. *drang srong dga’*, Mother of the buddha Sugandha.

## Sage Landing
The hermitage for ascetics at the Deer Park where the Buddha is said to have delivered his first sermon and subsequently other teachings. This translation derives from the story that the place got its name from the fact that sages would fly down and land there.

## Sage Leader
*drang srong gtso*, Skt. *drang srong gtso*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Vigatabhaya.

## Sage Mind
*drang srong blo*, Skt. *drang srong blo*, Attendant of the buddha Susthita.

## Sage of Clear Mind
*drang srong sems gsal*, Skt. *drang srong sems gsal*, Father of the buddha Hitaiṣin.

## Sage of Mount Kailāśa
*ti se’i gangs thub*, Skt. *ti se’i gangs thub*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Sage of the Śākyas
*shAkya thub pa*, Skt. *śākyamuni*, The name of the historical Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama, who was a sage (muni) from the Śākya clan.

## Sage Realization
*drang srong rtogs*, Skt. *drang srong rtogs*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Chedana.

## Sagely Joy
*drang srong dga’ ba*, Skt. *drang srong dga’ ba*, A river on Flocking Peacocks.

## saṅghāṭī
*snam sbyar*, Skt. *saṅghāṭī*, One of the three robes of a monk. This robe is a shawl with thirty-two patches, allowed for fully ordained monks.

## Saṅgha
*dge 'dun*. In its broad meaning it refers to all the practitioners of the [Buddha's](#buddha) teaching. It can have a more restricted meaning according to the context, referring to ordained monks, [Arhat](#arhat)s, [Bodhisattva](#bodhisattva)s, etc.

## saṅgha of hearers
*nyan thos kyi dge ’dun*, Skt. *śrāvakasaṅgha*, A term for the original disciples of the Buddha, those who received teachings directly from the historical Buddha himself.

## saṅgha remnant
*dge 'dun lhag ma*, Skt. *saṅghāvaśeṣa*, one of five types of offense a monk can incur. Second only to a [defeat](#defeat) in severity, there are thirteen such offenses. After a monastic incurs one of these offenses, a “remnant” (Tib. lhag ma; Skt. śeṣa) of the [prātimokṣa](#prātimokṣa) vow must be restored through the serving of a [probation](#probation) or, if the offense is concealed, a [penance](#penance) followed by [probation](#probation), during which the offending monk loses certain privileges and must perform [menial tasks](#menial-tasks). Upon completion of this period of [probation](#probation) and [penance](#penance), the [saṅgha](#saṅgha) may then reinstate the monk with full honors and privileges.

## Saṃghaṭṭa
Skt. *saṃghaṭṭa*, One of the kings of the rākṣasas.

## Saṃghaṭṭaśabda
*’khrug sgra*, Skt. *saṃghaṭṭaśabda*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Saṅgharakṣita
*dge 'dun 'tsho*, Skt. *saṅgharakṣita*, a [disciple](#disciple) of [Śāriputra](#śāriputra) who was abducted by [nāga](#nāga)s and taken back to their land under the sea where he helped three young [nāga](#nāga)s memorize the Four [Āgama](#āgama)s, thereby establishing the [sūtra](#sūtra)s in the land of the [nāga](#nāga)s.

## Saṃghāta
*ris gzhom pa*, Skt. *saṃghāta*, The third of the “hot hells.” Here, beings are perpetually crushed between rocks the size of mountains.

## Saṅgila
*sang ghila*, Skt. *sang ghila*, Attendant of the buddha Merudhvaja.

## Sagittarius
*gzhu*, Skt. *dhanus*, See “Dhanus.”

## Saṃgīti
*glu dbyangs*, Skt. *saṃgīti*, The 959th buddha in the first list, 958th in the second list, and 949th in the third list.

## Saṃgupta
*kun tu sbas pa*, Skt. *saṃgupta*, Name of a past buddha.

## Sahā
A name for the “world” or perhaps “galaxy” or “world system,” more literally, “the container of worlds” (lokadhātu), that forms the extent of the Buddha Śākyamuni’s domain. Its name suggests that it is a world in which beings experience suffering. It could also be described as the extent of the world over which Great Brahmā is said to be the lord and sovereign god (Sahāṃpati). Opinions vary over the precise extent of Sahā, and its expanse seems to have extended over time. For the purposes of this sūtra, it is sometimes equated with “the cosmos of a billion worlds.” More generally, it can also be conceived as the world in which the implied target audience of the sūtra can locate themselves, the place where we are located.

## Sahā universe
*mi mjed*, Skt. *sahā*, This term usually refers to the trichiliocosm, the world system that is the universe of ordinary beings, but sometimes only to our own world with four continents around Mount Meru. It means “Endurance,” as beings there have to endure suffering.

## Sahā world
*mi mjed*, Skt. *sahālokadhātu*, This universe of ours, or the trichiliocosm (but sometimes referring to just this world system of four continents), presided over by Brahmā. The term is variously interpreted as meaning the world of suffering, of endurance, of fearlessness, or of concomitance (of karmic cause and effect).

## Sahā world system
*’jig rten gyi khams mi mjed*, Skt. *sahālokadhātu*, The world system presided over by the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Saha­cittotpāda­dharma­cakra­pravartin
*sems bskyed ma thag tu chos kyi ’khor lo bskor ba*, Skt. *saha­cittotpāda­dharma­cakra­pravartin*, A great bodhisattva.

## Sahadeva
*lhar bcas*, Skt. *sahadeva*, Son of Siddhārtha Gautama’s maternal grandfather King Suprabuddha of Videha.

## Sahadevakaivartaputra
A king.

## Sahajā
Sahajā is a goddess who presides over the Tibetan lands as described in the eighteenth chapter of the Vajraḍāka Tantra.

## Sahasraśrī

## Sahasraśīrṣa

## Sahasraraśmi
*’od zer stong ldan*, Skt. *sahasraraśmi*, One of the vidyārājas dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Sahasrayajña
*mchod sbyin stong ldan*, Skt. *sahasrayajña*, A king, one of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Sahasrāvartā
*stong ’khyil ma*, Skt. *sahasrāvartā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Saṃhatana
Skt. *saṃhatana*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Sahetu­kṛṣṇa­vidhvaṃsana­rāja
*nag po rnam par ’joms pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sahetu­kṛṣṇa­vidhvaṃsana­rāja*, The name of the bodhisattva Sārakusumita on becoming a buddha.

## Sahetusaṃskarṣana
*rgyu bcas yang dag ’dren*, Skt. *sahetusaṃskarṣana*, The northern realm in which the bodhisattva Sārakusumita became the Buddha Sahetu­kṛṣṇa­vidhvaṃsana­rāja.

## Saṇṭhila
*gnas bcas*, Skt. *saṇṭhila*, One of the twelve great yakṣa generals who protect and serve those who bear, read, recite, copy, or commission a copy of the Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha­rāja­sūtra.

## Sahita
*phan bcas*, Skt. *sahita*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the thirtieth) when he becomes a buddha.

## Sahitaraśmi
*’od zer ldan pa*, Skt. *sahitaraśmi*, The 364th buddha in the first list, 363rd in the second list, and 358th in the third list.

## Sahākhya
*kun nas grags pa*, Skt. *sahākhya*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sahāṃpati
*mi mjed kyi bdag po*, Skt. *sahāṃpati*, Epithet of Brahmā, head god of the Brahma heavens.

## Sahāṃpati Brahmā
*mi mjed kyi bdag po tshangs pa*, Skt. *sahāṃpati brahmā*, An epithet of Brahmā meaning “Lord of the Sahā World.”

## Saṃhāra
*tshogs*, Skt. *saṃhāra*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Sahāsrakārṇa
The name of a king.

## Sahya
*sa ha*, Skt. *sahya*, A mountain range in the Deccan.

## Saikata
*bye ma skyes*, Skt. *saikata*, This monk is the central protagonist in the narrative that introduces the exemption on the grounds of being of unsound mind.

## Saindhava
*sen da pa*, Skt. *saindhava*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## saṃjñā
*’du shes*, Skt. *saṃjñā*, Perception, the third of the five skandhas.

## Saṃjayī Vairaṭṭīputra
*smra ’dod kyi bu mo’i bu yang dag rgyal ba can*, Skt. *saṃjayī vairaṭṭīputra*, One of the six teachers at the time of the Buddha.

## Sañjaya
*yang dag shes*, Skt. *sañjaya*, The son of Kubera, about whom very little is known. His name is often rendered as yang dag shes in Tibetan translation, reflecting a frequent variant in the Sanskrit, Sañjñeya.

## Saṃjaya
*kun rgyal*, Skt. *saṃjaya*, The 316th buddha in the first list, 315th in the second list, and 310th in the third list.

## Sañjayi Vairattīputra
*kun rgyal ’be’i ra ti’i bu*, Skt. *sañjayi vairattīputra*, A proponent of the doctrine of scepticism (vikṣepavāda).

## Sañjayin
*sdom can*, Skt. *sañjayin*, The 48th buddha in the first list, 48th in the second list, and 49th in the third list.

## Sañjayin, the teacher
*ston pa yang dag rgyal*, Skt. *śāstā sañjayin*, [Śāriputra](#śāriputra) and [Maudgalyāyana](#maudgalyāyana) joined his order after rejecting the six [tīrthika](#tīrthika) teachers.

## Saṃjayin Vairaṭīputra
*smra ’dod kyi bu mo’i bu*, Skt. *vairaṭīputra*, One of the six philosophical extremists who lived during the time of Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Sañjñeya
*yang dag shes*, Skt. *sañjñeya*, Name of a yakṣa general.

## Saṃjñeya
*yang dag shes*, Skt. *saṃjñeya*, A yakṣa general.

## Saṃjñika
*yang dag shes*, Skt. *saṃjñika*, One of the five yakṣa generals.

## saṃjñāparyanta
*’du shes mu med pa*, Skt. *saṃjñāparyanta*, Lit. “limitless perception.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sañjīva
*yang sos*, Skt. *sañjīva*, “Reviving,” one of the hells.

## Saṃjīvana
*yang dag ’tsho*, Skt. *saṃjīvana*, An ājīvika ascetic who asks King Ambara, a previous life of Śākyamuni, for his genitalia. Also the name of an eastern buddha realm. The Sanskrit is also the name for one of the hells, which in Tibetan is rendered yang sos. In the traditional Buddhist list of eight hot hells, this is the “reviving” hell where beings are repeatedly killed.

## Saṃjñāvikaraṇa­bhīṣma
*mi ’gyur ’jigs byed*, Skt. *saṃjñāvikaraṇa­bhīṣma*, An ājīvika ascetic who prays to beg for everything from Samudrareṇu in his future lives and be his disciple when he is the Śākyamuni Buddha.

## Saṃjāyin Vairāṭī­putra
*smra ’dod kyi bu mo’i bu yang dag rgyal ba can*, Skt. *saṃjāyin vairāṭī­putra*, One of the six outsider teachers.

## Saṅkāśa
*sang kA sha kA*, Skt. *saṅkāśa*, A mountain in Kuru.

## Saṅkalā
*lcags sgrog ma*, Skt. *saṅkalā*, One of the goddesses.

## Saṃkaramardārci
*dres spong ’od zer*, Skt. *saṃkaramardārci*, The name of the bodhisattva Dharaṇidatta when he became a buddha.

## Saṃkarṣana
*yang dag ’dren*, Skt. *saṃkarṣana*, A realm to the south of the Buddha Ratnagarbha’s realm into which the Buddha Śākyamuni in his previous lives was repeatedly reborn as a caṇḍāla who becomes a cakravartin and gives away his body or parts of his body.

## Saṃkaśya
*nai ka sha*, Skt. *saṃkaśya*, The country where Śākyamuni descended to the earth after preaching to his deceased mother in Indra’s heaven.

## saṃkrānti
*’pho ba*, Skt. *saṃkrānti*, Unit of time related to the counting of breath.

## Saṃkusuma
*yang dag pa’i me tog*, Skt. *saṃkusuma*, One of the tathāgatas.

## Saṃkusumitā
*me tog kun tu rgyas pa*, Skt. *saṃkusumitā*, A realm above the Buddha Ratnagarbha’s realm in which resides the Buddha Prasphulitakusuma­vairocana.

## Saṃkusumita
*me tog dang ldan pa*, Skt. *saṃkusumita*, “Fully Manifested,” or “Filled with Blossoms,” a buddhafield which contains the world sphere Kusumāvatī.

## Saṃkusumita Rājendra
*me tog kun tu skyes pa’i rgyal po’i dbang po*, Skt. *saṃkusumita­rājendra*, The tathāgata who orders, in the MMK, the bodhisattva Mañjuśrī to go and receive teachings from Lord Śākyamuni; one of the eight tathāgatas; a bodhisattva.

## Saṃkusumita­gandhottama Rāja
*me tog kun nas skyes pa’i dri mchog rgyal po*, Skt. *saṃkusumita­gandhottama rāja*, One of the tathāgatas.

## Sakya
One of the four main schools of Tibetan Buddhism, taking its name from Sakya monastery in southern central Tibet.

## Sakya Paṇḍita
Sakya Paṇḍita Künga Gyaltsen (1182–1251) was one of the five Sakya patriarchs and a highly influential scholar whose ideal of scholasticism became deeply embedded in Buddhist learning in Tibet.

## Sakyapa
*sa skya pa*, one of the schools of the [New Tradition](#new-tradition), founded by Khön Könchok Gyalpo (1034 - 1102).

## Sakyapa Chenpo
Sachen Kunga Nyingpo (1092–1158), the founder of Sakya as a distinctive school of Tibetan Buddhism. His father founded the first physical center at Sakya, but it was Sachen who was innovative in terms of its practices and doctrines.

## Sakyong Dampa Jampa
See “Jampa Phuntsok.”

## sal
*sA la*, Skt. *śāla*, Shorea robusta. This is the dominant tree in the forests where it occurs. Also known as the sakhua or shala tree. It is the tree under which the Buddha was born.

## sal tree
*shing sA la*, Skt. *śāla*, A hardwood tree, Shorea robusta, widespread on the Indian subcontinent.

## Saṃlākṣa
*ma lus spyan*, Skt. *saṃlākṣa*, One of the pratyeka­buddhas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Salīla
One of the sublineages connected with the Vātsya lineage of the brahmanical tradition.

## Salīlagajagāmin
*ngom bag glang po’i ’dros*, Skt. *salīlagajagāmin*, A buddha in the past.

## Saltong Shogom
Saltong Shogom (twelfth century) was a student of Gampopa who founded a minor sect that has since disappeared. He is one of the “three men from Kham” (khams pa mi gsum), three famous students of Gampopa from eastern Tibet.

## salty
*lan tshwa*, Skt. *lavaṇa*, One of the eight supreme flavors. Also, one of the six tastes of the Āyurveda and Tibetan medical traditions.

## Salty Gift
*tshwa rgo byin*, Skt. *tshwa rgo byin*, Attendant of the buddha Gaṇimuktirāja.

## Saluted by Jambu
*’dzam bu ’dud pa*, Skt. *’dzam bu ’dud pa*, Name of a past buddha.

## Samaśarīra
*zhi ba’i sku yi ’od*, Skt. *samaśarīra*, The seventy-fifth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. The equivalent of ’od (“light”) is not in the Sanskrit.

## Samacitta
The name of the merchant Naradatta when he attains buddhahood in the distant future.

## Samadhyāyin
*bsam gtan snyoms*, Skt. *samadhyāyin*, The 786th buddha in the first list, 785th in the second list, and 775th in the third list.

*ldan ma*, Skt. *samaṅginī*, One of the eight goddesses dwelling in the Bodhi tree.

## Samaṅgira
*ngag mnyam*, Skt. *samaṅgira*, A great ṛṣi.

## samaṭiraṇa
An unidentified ritual ingredient.

## Samaṃkara
*zhi byed*, Skt. *samaṃkara*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Samanantarāśi
*kun nas phung po*, Skt. *samanantarāśi*, One of the uṣṇīṣa kings attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Samanta
*kun tu yod*, Skt. *samanta*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Samantabhadra
*kun tu bzang po*,
1. the original [Buddha](#buddha) (Adibuddha), he who has never fallen into delusion, the [Dharmakāya](#dharmakāya) [Buddha](#buddha) represented as a naked figure, deep blue like the sky, in union with Samantabhadrī, as a symbol of awareness-emptiness, the pure, absolute nature ever present and unobstructed. The source of the lineage of the [tantra](#tantra) transmissions of the [Nyingma](#nyingmapa) school.
2. [Bodhisattva](#bodhisattva) Samantabhadra, one of the [Eight Great Close Sons](#eight-great-close-sons), renowned for the way in which, through the power of his [concentration](#concentration), he miraculously multiplied the offerings he made.

## Samanta­bhadra
*kun tu bzang po*, Skt. *samanta­bhadra*, Presently classed as one of the eight principal bodhisattvas, he is distinct from the primordial buddha with the same name in the Tibetan Nyingma tradition. He is prominent in the Gaṇḍa­vyūha, and also in The White Lotus of the Good Dharma (Toh 113, Saddharma­puṇḍarīka) and The White Lotus of Compassion Sūtra (Toh 111, Mahā­karuṇā­puṇḍarīka­sūtra).

## Sa­manta­bhadra
*kun tu bzang po*, Skt. *sa­manta­bhadra*, A great bodhisattva.

## Samanta­bhadra­caryā­praṇidhāna
*kun tu bzang po’i spyod pa’i smon lam*, Skt. *samanta­bhadra­caryā­praṇidhāna*, The Samanta­bhadra­caryā­praṇidhāna appears in the final part of the Gaṇḍa­vyūha­sūtra, which itself forms part of the Buddhāvataṃsaka­sūtra. It is well-known in Tibet, where it has been the subject of numerous commentaries. It continues to be recited daily in some monastic traditions in Tibet and China. The work also goes under the Sanskrit titles Bhadracari(-ī), and Bhadra­caryā­praṇidhāna. See Skilling and Saerji 2013, 198 n. 30.

## Samantabuddhi
*kun tu blo*, Skt. *samantabuddhi*, A bodhisattva.

## Samantacakṣu
*kun du mig*, Skt. *samantacakṣu*, A king and sage; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Samanta­cakṣu

## Sa­manta­cāri­tra­mati
*kun tu spyod pa’i blo gros*, Skt. *sa­manta­cāri­tra­mati*, A great bodhisattva.

*kun nas lta ba’i myig*, Skt. *samanta­darśana­netra*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Samantadarśin
*kun gzigs*, Skt. *samantadarśin*, The 427th buddha in the first list, 426th in the second list, and 420th in the third list. The translation is tentative; kun gzigs found in list three corresponds to Samantadarśin, but kun du gzi brjid found in list one and two would expect *Samantatejas.

*chos kyi dbyings nam mkha’ kun nas snang ba’i cod pan*, Skt. *samanta­dharma­dhātu­gagana­pratibhāsa­mukuṭa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

*spos kun tu rnam par yangs pa*, Skt. *samanta­gandha­vitāna*, A buddha in a southern realm.

*kun du snying po*, Skt. *samantagarbha*, A buddha in a western buddha realm.

## Samanta­guṇa­megha

## Samantaguptasāgara­rāja
*kun sbed rgya mtsho’i rgyal po*, Skt. *samantaguptasāgara­rāja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Samantahastin
*kun nas phyag*, Skt. *samantahastin*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

*kun nas ral pa ma*, Skt. *samantajaṭā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Samanta­jñāna­bhadra­maṇḍala
*ye shes kun tu bzang po’i dkyil ’khor*, Skt. *samanta­jñāna­bhadra­maṇḍala*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

*ye shes kyi dkyil ’khor kun tu snang ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *samanta­jñāna­maṇḍala­pratibhāsa­nirghoṣa*, A buddha in a realm in the upward direction.

## Samanta­jñāna­prabha­rāja
*ye shes kun snang rgyal po*, Skt. *samanta­jñāna­prabha­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Samanta­jñāna­prabhā­meru
*ye shes kun tu snang ba’i ri bo*, Skt. *samanta­jñāna­prabhā­meru*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Samanta­jñāna­prabhāsa
*ye shes kyi ’od kun tu snang ba*, Skt. *samanta­jñāna­prabhāsa*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Samanta­jñāna­ratnārci­śrī­guṇa­ketu­rāja
*ye shes rin po che’i ’od kun tu ’phro ba’i dpal yon tan dpal gyi rgyal po*, Skt. *samanta­jñāna­ratnārci­śrī­guṇa­ketu­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past. See .

## Samanta­jñānābha­pravara
*ye shes kun tu snang ba’i dam pa*, Skt. *samanta­jñānābha­pravara*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Samanta­jñānāloka­vikrama­siṃha
*ye shes snang bas rnam par gnon pa’i seng ge*, Skt. *samanta­jñānāloka­vikrama­siṃha*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Samanta­jñānārci­padma­bhadrābhirāma­netra­śrī­candrā
*ye shes kyi ’od kun tu ’phro ba pad+mo bzang mo mig yid du ’ong ba’i dpal gyi zla ba*, Skt. *samanta­jñānārci­padma­bhadrābhirāma­netra­śrī­candrā*, A cakravartin’s princess in the distant past. Also called Padma­bhadrābhirāma­netra­śrī­candrā and Padma­bhadrābhirāma­netra­śrī.

*kun nas rna ba*, Skt. *samantakarṇa*, One of the kings of the rākṣasas.

## Samanta­mukha­jñāna­bhadra­meru
*sgo kun nas mkhyen pa’i ri bzang po*, Skt. *samanta­mukha­jñāna­bhadra­meru*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

*sgo kun nas ye shes rnam par snang ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *samanta­mukha­jñāna­virocana­ghoṣa*, A buddha in a southwestern realm.

*kun tu mig*, Skt. *samantanetra*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Samanta­netra
*kun tu lta ba*, Skt. *samanta­netra*, A perfume seller, the kalyāṇamitra of chapter 19.

## Sa­manta­netra
*kun nas mig*, Skt. *sa­manta­netra*, A great bodhisattva.

## Samanta­nirmathana
Skt. *samanta­nirmathana*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Samantanātha
*kun nas mgon po*, Skt. *samantanātha*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

The name of the buddha realm of the future buddha Vajravikrāmin, as attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra. The name means something like “wholly pure”.

## Samantaprabha
*kun tu ’od*, Skt. *samantaprabha*, The name of a buddha in the eastern direction. Also the name of thirty-two thousand gods when they attain buddhahood in the future, as prophesied by the Buddha.

*kun nas ’od dpal gzi brjid*, Skt. *samanta­prabha­śrī­tejas*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Samantaprabhāsa
*kun tu snang ba*, Skt. *samanta­prabhāsa*, The name of the nāga king Attainment of Perpetual Faith when, as the bodhisattva Lofty Aspiration, he attains buddhahood in the future, as prophesied by the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Samanta­prabhāsa
*kun tu snang ba*, Skt. *samanta­prabhāsa*, Kauṇḍinya’s name when he becomes a buddha in the distant future. It will also be the name of five hundred of Śākyamuni’s arhats when they attain buddhahood. Also called “Samanta­prabhāsa” and “Samanta­prabha.”

*gzugs brnyan kun tu snang ba’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *samanta­pratibhāsa­cūḍa*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

A king.

## Samaya
*dam tshig*, lit. promise. Sacred links between teacher and [disciple](#disciple), and also between [disciple](#disciple)s, in the [Vajrayāna](#vajrayāna). The Sanskrit word samaya can mean: agreement, engagement, convention, precept, [boundary](#boundary),e tc. Although there are many detailed obligations, the most essential samaya is to consider the teacher's body, speech and mind as pure.

## samaya holder
A general term for beings that are bound to a particular deity maṇḍala and bound by contractual agreement to protect, support, and commune with practitioners who provide them with the requisite offerings.

## Samaya object or substance
*dam tshig gi rdzas*, object or ingredient which is necessary for or enhances the practices of the [Vajrayāna](#vajrayāna).

## samaya substances
*dam rdzas*, A term for the substances that are offered to a deity as part of the propitiator’s fulfillment of the samaya vow.

## samayagola
The precise identification of this flower is not clear, but it may refer to either Vangueria spinosa (Skt. golā) or the jujube (Skt. kolā).

## samayasattva
*dam tshig sems dpa*, Skt. *samayasattva*, The form of the deity generated and visualized by the practitioner.

## Samayoṣṇīṣa
*spyi gtsug*, Skt. *samayoṣṇīṣa*, One of the mantra deities.

## sambhoga cakra
*longs spyod ’khor lo*, Skt. *sambhogacakra*, The name of the energy center (cakra) in the throat.

## sambhogakāya
*longs spyod rdzogs pa’i sku*, Skt. *sambhogakāya*, The “enjoyment body,” one of the three bodies of a buddha, refers to the way a buddha manifests for realized beings; this may be represented by different iconographic forms of deity figures.

## Sambuka
The name of a city.

## Samṛddha
*’byor par ldan*, Skt. *samṛddha*, The 220th buddha in the first list, 219th in the second list, and 219th in the third list.

## Samṛddhajñāna
*ye shes ’byor ldan*, Skt. *samṛddhajñāna*, The 680th buddha in the first list, 679th in the second list, and 671st in the third list.

## Samṛddhapakṣa
A bodhisattva who is a prince predicted to be the buddha Abhyupagatagāmin and whose name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Samṛddhayaśas
*’byor ldan grags pa*, Skt. *samṛddhayaśas*, The 840th buddha in the first list, 839th in the second list, and 829th in the third list.

## Samṛddhi
*’byor pa ma*, Skt. *samṛddhi*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## samādhi
*ting nge ’dzin*, Skt. *samādhi*, Some readers may be familiar with the term samadhi, written without diacritics as it would appear in English dictionaries, where it is usually explained as referring to meditation or meditative states. In a more restricted sense, and when understood as a mental state, samādhi is defined as the one-pointedness of the mind (cittaikāgratā), the ability to remain on the same object over long periods of time. In Vaibhāṣika abhidharma, samādhi is a mental state that accompanies each and every moment of mind; the practice of meditation and the like is for the purpose of making samādhi more powerful (samādhiś cittasyaikagrateti | agram ālambanam ity eko 'rthaḥ | yadyogāc cittaṃ prabandhena ekatrālambane vartate | sa samādhiḥ | yadi samādhiḥ sarva­cetasi bhavati | kim arthaṃ dhyāneṣu yatnaḥ kriyate | balavatsamādhiniṣpādanārthaṃ, Abhidharma­kośa­vyākhyā 2.24, Wogihara 1989, p. 128). Some forms of abhidharma (Yogācāra, for example) do not consider samādhi as a mental factor that accompanies every moment of mind. In a slightly less technical sense, samādhi can describe a number of different meditative states, including the highest such as the “samādhi that is like a diamond” (vajropamasamādhi). If we understand the term samādhi as derived from sam + ā + dhā, the sense is something like to “place together” or “collect.” In the Tibetan rendering of this term, the ’dzin represents, we think, the root dhā and matches one of the senses of this root, “to hold” (dhāraṇa). The possible etymology of ting nge is debated and possibly a complex matter; if we accept the hypothesis that ting nge is related to gting, then the sense is probably akin to “profound” or “deep,” which may indicate taking sam + ā more or less as intensifiers. The sgra sbyor bam po gnyis pa commentary on the Mahāvyutpatti explains the term samādhi as referring to the instrument through which mind and mental states “get collected,” i.e., it is by the force of samādhi that the continuum of mind and mental states becomes collected on a single point of reference without getting distracted (samādhi zhes pa samādhiyante anena zhes bya ste | ting nge ’dzin gyi mthus sems dang sems las byung ba’i rgyud dmigs pa gcig la sdud cing mi g.yo bar ting nge ’dzin ’jog pas na ting nge ’dzin zhes bya).

## samādhi of valiant progress
The name of a samādhi that is considered one of the main samādhis of a bodhisattva. This samādhi is described in The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Valiant Progress (Toh 132; forthcoming).

## Samādhi­garbha
*ting nge ’dzin gyi snying po*, Skt. *samādhi­garbha*, A great bodhisattva.

## Samādhihastyuttaraśrī
