## Samādhi­hastyuttara­śrī
*ting nge ’dzin gyi glang po dam pa’i dpal*, Skt. *samādhi­hastyuttara­śrī*, Lit. “Glorious Supreme Elephant of Meditative Stabilization.” A buddha in a world system called Samādhyalaṃkṛtā in the intermediate northeast direction.

## Samādhi­mervabhyudgata­jñāna
*ting nge ’dzin gyi ri rab mngon par ’phags pa’i ye shes*, Skt. *samādhi­mervabhyudgata­jñāna*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Samādhi­mudrā­vipula­makuṭa­prajñā­prabha
*ting nge ’dzin gyi phyag rgya shin tu yangs pa’i cod pan shes rab kyi ’od*, Skt. *samādhi­mudrā­vipula­makuṭa­prajñā­prabha*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## samādhirāja
*ting nge ’dzin gyi rgyal po*, Skt. *samādhirāja*, Lit. “king of meditative stabilizations.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## samādhi­rāja­su­pratiṣṭhita
*ting nge ’dzin la rgyal po ltar rab tu gnas pa*, Skt. *samādhi­rāja­su­pratiṣṭhita*, Lit. “good standing like a king in meditative stabilization.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## samādhisamata
*ting nge ’dzin mnyam pa nyid*, Skt. *samādhisamata*, Lit. “sameness meditative stabilization.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Samādhyalaṃkṛtā
*ting nge ’dzin gyis brgyan pa*, Skt. *samādhyalaṃkṛtā*, Lit. “Adorned with Meditative Stabilizations.” A world system in the intermediate northeast direction, where the buddha Samādhi­hastyuttara­śrī now dwells.

## Samādhyalaṅkṛta
*ting nge ’dzin gyis brgyan pa*, Skt. *samādhyalaṅkṛta*, Name of a world system in the northeastern direction, where the buddha Samādhi­hastyuttara­śrī teaches the perfection of wisdom to bodhisattva great beings.

## same
*gcig pa nyid*, Skt. *gcig pa nyid*, Also translated here as “single” in the context of the ten continuities of Dharma.

## Same Image
*bzhin ’dra*, Skt. *bzhin ’dra*, Son of the buddha Vairocana.

## sameness
Refers here to the awakened realization of the sameness or equality of all phenomena, since all phenomena share the ultimate nature in emptiness.

## sameness of all phenomena
*chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­samatā*, A meditative stability. As well as its more general meaning, this is the name of the sixty-second meditative stability, and the first of twenty-four aspects of the perfection of wisdom taught by Dharmodgata, and realized as meditative stabilities by Sadāprarudita, in chapter 75.

## sameness of all things
*chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­sama­tā*, As well as its more general meaning, this is the name of the fifty-seventh meditative stability.

## sameness of meditative stability
*ting nge ’dzin mnyam pa nyid*, Skt. *samādhisamatā*, The 111th meditative stability in chapters 6 and 8.

## (sameness of the) irreducibility of all phenomena
*chos thams cad rnam par ’jig pa mnyam pa nyid*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāvibhāvanāsamatā*, The twentieth of twenty-four aspects of the perfection of wisdom taught by Dharmodgata, and the twenty-second of the meditative stabilities realized by Sadāprarudita, in chapter 75. The Sanskrit term vibhāvana has a complex range of meanings and the English rendering here is a tentative attempt to reconcile the Sanskrit and Tibetan. See also breaking down of the cultivation.

## Saṃmūḍhasmṛti
A māra who appears to the brothers Samvara and Samvarasthita.

## Samāhitātman
*mnyam gzhag bdag nyid*, Skt. *samāhitātman*, The 660th buddha in the first list, 659th in the second list, and 651st in the third list.

## samāhitāvasthā­pratiṣṭhāna
*mnyam par gzhag pa’i gnas la gnas pa*, Skt. *samāhitāvasthā­pratiṣṭhāna*, Lit. “stationed in the absorption stage.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sami
*zhi ldan*, Skt. *sami*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## samikā
*kun tu phreng bar byed pa*, Skt. *samikā*, A class of supernatural beings.

## Samitāyus
*skye bcil ba*, Skt. *samitāyus*, The sixth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past.

## samākṣarāvakāra
*yi ge mnyam par ’god pa*, Skt. *samākṣarāvakāra*, Lit. “sets down all syllables the same.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Samālikā
*byis bcas mo*, Skt. *samālikā*, One of the seven types of ḍākinīs..

## samāna
*mnyam gnas*, Skt. *samāna*, One of the five vital airs, centered in the navel area.

## Samori
The name of a city.

## Sampadā
*phun sum tshogs ma*, Skt. *sampadā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Samāpadyata
*mnyam par gzhag pa*, Skt. *samāpadyata*, A kalpa in the distant past.

## samāpatti
*snyoms par ’jug pa*, Skt. *samāpatti*, One of the synonyms for the meditative state, in tems of both the state itself and the various meditative states that serve as attainments along the path. The Tibetan translation interprets it as sama-āpatti, which brings in the idea of “equal,” or “level;” however, it can also be parsed as sam-āpatti, in which case it would have the sense of “concentration,” or “absorption,” much like “samādhi,” but with the added sense of “completion.”

## Sampūjita
*yang dag mchod*, Skt. *sampūjita*, A buddha in the past.

## Sampūrṇa
*gang ba bzang*, Skt. *sampūrṇa*, A brahmin devotee of Buddhism.

## sampuṭa
*yang dag par sbyor ba*, Skt. *sampuṭa*, Sexual union perceived as the union of wisdom and skillful means; space between two concave surfaces; the principle of sampuṭa personified; an epithet of Vajrasattva/Saṃvara. See also .

## Samāta
*mnyam pa*, Skt. *samāta*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## samudgata
*yang dag par ’phags pa*, Skt. *samudgata*, Lit. “truly noble.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Samudgataśrī
*kun tu ’phags pa’i dpal*, Skt. *samudgataśrī*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Samudgata­rāja
*rgyal po yang dag par ’phags pa*, Skt. *samudgata­rāja*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Samudrā
The name of a goddess who is said to be an emanation of Mahākālī’s body, speech, and mind.

## Samudra
*rgya mtsho*, Skt. *samudra*, The ocean personified; the Gupta emperor Samudragupta who ruled Gauḍa and Magadha in the third quarter of the fourth century.

## Samudradatta
*rgya mtshos byin*, Skt. *samudradatta*, One of the members of a group of four monks described in the Vinaya as followers of Devadatta that attempted to create a schism in the Buddhist saṅgha.

## Samudradeva
*rgya mtsho’i lha*, Skt. *samudradeva*, Name of a former incarnation of the Buddha while he was a practicing bodhisattva.

## Samudragarbha
*rgya mtsho’i snying po*, Skt. *samudragarbha*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the twelfth) when he becomes a buddha.

## Samudrakaccha
*rgya mtsho’i ’gram*, Skt. *samudrakaccha*, A province in South India.

## Samudra­pratiṣṭhāna
*rgya mtsho brten pa*, Skt. *samudra­pratiṣṭhāna*, A town in South India.

## Samudraputra
*rgya mtsho’i bu*, Skt. *samudraputra*, A nāga king.

## Samudrareṇu
*rgya mtsho’i rdul*, Skt. *samudrareṇu*, The past life of the Buddha Śākyamuni as a brahmin priest, who is the principal figure in The White Lotus of Compassion Sūtra. In this sūtra, he is the court priest of King Araṇemin and the father of the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

## Samudravetāḍī
*rgya mtsho rnam par rlob pa*, Skt. *samudravetāḍī*, An area in the south of India.

## Samudreśvarabhuvi
*rgya mtsho’i dbang phyug khyab bdag*, Skt. *samudreśvara­bhuvi*, The eldest of the brahmin Samudrareṇu’s eighty sons and the brother of the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

## samudrāparyanta
*rgya mtsho mu med pa*, Skt. *samudrāparyanta*, Lit. “limitless ocean.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Saṃmukha
“Facing.” The name of a muhūrta.

## Samutkhalī
*mu khu li*, Skt. *samutkhalī*, One of the four goddesses who attended and kept guard over Prince Siddhārtha while he was in the womb of his mother.

## Samvara
Lit. Disciplined; a son of the householder Suvicaya. See also “Samvarasthita.” These are the same words that were translated as “vows” (Samvara) and “keeping to vows” (Samvarasthita) above.

## Samvarasthita
Lit. Firm Discipline; a son of the householder Suvicaya. See also “Samvara.” These are the same words that were translated as “vows” (Samvara) and “keeping to vows” (Samvarasthita) above.

## Samveda
The name of a king.

## Samyé
*bsam yas*, Skt. *bsam yas*, The first monastery established in Tibet, built between 775 and 779 ce. It was the location of the decades-long program of translating Buddhist texts.

## Samyé Chimphu
Tibet’s first monastery and a center of Buddhist activity throughout the imperial period.

## samyaksaṃbuddha
*yang dag par rdzogs pa’i sangs rgyas*, Skt. *samyaksaṃbuddha*, “Perfectly realized one.” A buddha who teaches the Dharma, as opposed to a pratyekabuddha, who does not teach.

## samyak­saṃbuddha
*yang dag par rdzogs pa’i sangs rgyas*, Skt. *samyak­saṃbuddha*, “A perfect buddha.” A buddha who teaches the Dharma, as opposed to a pratyeka­buddha, who does not teach.

## samyaksam­buddha
*yang dag par rdzogs pa’i sangs rgyas*, Skt. *samyak­sambuddha*, A perfect buddha: a buddha who teaches the Dharma and brings it into a world, as opposed to a pratyekabuddha, who does not teach the Dharma or bring it into a world.

## samyak­sambuddha
*yang dag par rdzogs pa’i sangs rgyas*, Skt. *samyak­sambuddha*, A perfect buddha: a buddha who teaches the Dharma and brings it into a world, as opposed to a pratyekabuddha, who does not teach the Dharma or bring it into a world.

## samyaktva­mithyātva­sarva­saṃgrasana
*yang dag pa dang log pa thams cad yang dag par sel ba*, Skt. *samyaktva­mithyātva­sarva­saṃgrasana*, Lit. “eliminator of all right and wrong.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Samye
*bsam yas*, the first monastery in Tibet, in the Tsangpo valley south-east of Lhasa, built during the time of King [Trisong Detsen](#trisong-detsen). The name [means](#means) "inconceivable."

## Samye Chimpu
*bsam yas mchims phu*, name of a group of hermitages situated on the mountainside above [Samye](#samye) Monastery, where many great Buddhist masters have attained [accomplishment](#accomplishment).

## Śāsanadhara
*bstan pa ’dzin*, Skt. *śāsanadhara*, A mountain king.

## Sanat
*kun bged*, Skt. *sanat*, One of the grahas.

## Sanatkumāra
*sa nad ku mA ra*, Skt. *sanatkumāra*, The son of the god Brahmā.

## sanctified conduct
*tshangs par spyod pa*, Skt. *brahmacarya*, In Buddhism, a term denoting a religious life grounded in renunciation and chastity. In the brahmanical traditions, this refers specifically to the stage in one’s youth dedicated to focused study of religious scripture and practice.

## sanction
*byin gyis brlab pa*, Skt. *adhiṣṭhāna*, a monk’s robes are sanctioned at ordination. Furthermore, two types of offenses, [saṅgha remnant](#saṅgha-remnant) offense and [transgression](#transgression)s requiring forfeiture, must be formally sanctioned or excused in order to be completely expunged.

## sanctuary
*dri gtsang khang*, Skt. *gandhakuṭī*, a special room or [shrine](#shrine) dedicated to a [buddha](#buddha), intended as both residence and reliquary. A common feature especially in rock-cut [temple](#temple)s.

## sand
A term that often refers to dust or dirt but may also refer to sand.

## Sand Castle
*mkhar phye ma*, Skt. *mkhar phye ma*, An ancient settlement in the eastern part of Khotan.

## sandalwood
Santalum album. The white sandalwood tree.

## Sandalwood Dwelling
*tsan dan khyim*, Skt. *tsan dan khyim*, A tathāgata in the past eon Most Fragrant, of the world realm Fragrant.

## Sandalwood Essence
*tsan dan gyi snying po*, Skt. *tsan dan gyi snying po*, A brahmin.

## Sandalwood Fragrance
*tsan dan spos*, Skt. *tsan dan spos*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Laḍitakrama (797 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## Sandalwood Heir
*gtso bo’i bu tsan dan*, Skt. *gtso bo’i bu tsan dan*, Name of a former incarnation of the Buddha while he was a practicing bodhisattva.

## Sandalwood Incense
*tsan dan spos*, Skt. *tsan dan spos*, A buddha realm.

## Sandalwood Joy
*tsan dan dga’*, Skt. *tsan dan dga’*, Son of the buddha Sūkṣmabuddhi.

## Sandalwood Light
*tsan dan ’od*, Skt. *tsan dan ’od*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Anilavegagāmin.

## Sandalwood Mansion
*tsan dan khang pa*, Skt. *tsan dan khang pa*, A buddha.

## sandalwood paste
*tsan+dana a bar ta ka*, Skt. *candana āvartana*, Skt. candana is sandalwood, while āvartana means “turning around repeatedly” as in a churning or grinding motion (Monier-Williams).

## Sandalwood Retreat
*tsan dan phug*, Skt. *tsan dan phug*, A buddha realm.

## Sandy Stretch
*bye ma’i gnas skabs*, Skt. *bye ma’i gnas skabs*, An area between Godānīya and Videha.

## Sanema
*mu khyud can*, Skt. *sanema*, A Śakra deity who prays to be Samudrareṇu’s disciple with wisdom when he is the Buddha Śākyamuni, i.e., Śāriputra.

## Sanetya­jñāna­saṃbhava
*spyod bcas dang ye shes ’byung*, Skt. *sanetya­jñāna­saṃbhava*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the seventy-fifth) when he becomes a buddha. The Tibetan divides this into two names: Sanetya and Jñānasaṃbhava.

## Sangyé Menla
*sangs rgyas sman bla*, Skt. *sangs rgyas sman bla*, Tibetan short form of Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha, also known as the Medicine Buddha.

## Sangyé Tenpa
Sangyé Tenpa (ca. 1638–1710) was the son of the seventh Degé king and the third abbot of Lhundrup Teng. He was known for his religious ecumenicalism.

## āsanna­rūpa­rājas
*gzugs kyi rdul sel*, Skt. *āsanna­rūpa­rājas*, Lit. “eliminating material dirt.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sannimika
*mu khyud bzang po*, Skt. *sannimika*, One of the māras.

## Sanātana
*kun bged*, Skt. *sanātana*, An epithet of Viṣṇu. Sometimes also used as an epithet of Brahmā.

## Santata
“Continual.” The name of muhūrta.

## Santuṣita
*dga’ ldan*, Skt. *santuṣita*, The lord of the desire realm who resides in the Tuṣita heaven.

## sapakṣa
Skt. *sapakṣa*, Technical term in Buddhist logic.

## Saṃpannakīrti
*grags rdzogs*, Skt. *saṃpannakīrti*, The 134th buddha in the first list, 134th in the second list, and 134th in the third list.

## Saphala
*’bras bu dang bcas pa*, Skt. *saphala*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Saphalātreya
*rgyun shes kyi bu ’bras bu dang bcas pa*, Skt. *saphalātreya*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Saṃpūrṇa
*yongs su gang ba*, Skt. *saṃpūrṇa*, One of the śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## saṃpracchada
*yongs su ’gengs*, Skt. *saṃpracchada*, A magical tree, the name of which means “completely covering.”

## Saṃpūrṇa­śrīvakrā
*dpal gyi bzhin yongs su rgyas pa*, Skt. *saṃpūrṇa­śrīvakrā*, A cakravartin’s precious queen in the distant past.

## sapta
An unidentified ritual ingredient.

## Saptalakṣaṇa
A king.

## Saptaparṇā
*’dab bdun ma*, Skt. *saptaparṇā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## saptaparṇa
Alstonia scholaris. The scholar tree, also known as milkwood or devil’s tree.

## Saptaśīrṣa
*mgo bdun*, Skt. *saptaśīrṣa*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Sapta­ratna­padma­vikrānta­gāmin
*rin po che sna bdun gyi pad ma la gom pas ’gro ba*, Skt. *sapta­ratna­padma­vikrānta­gāmin*, The name of Rāhula when he becomes a buddha.

## Sapta­ratna­vicitrasan­darśana
*rin po che sna bdun rnam par bkra bar snang ba*, Skt. *sapta­ratna­vicitrasan­darśana*, A Bodhi tree, the name meaning “The Lovely Appearance of a Variety of the Seven Jewels.”

## Saptarājñī
*bdun pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *saptarājñī*, “Queen of the Seven,” a yoginī in Paramāśva’s maṇḍala.

## Saṃpuṣpita
*me tog kun tu rgyas pa*, Skt. *saṃpuṣpita*, The name of an eastern buddha realm.

## Saraṇa
*sa ra Na*, Skt. *saraṇa*, Son of King Udayana of Vatsa, he went forth by Venerable Kātyāyanaputra.

## Saracchighoṣa
*sgra bzang*, Skt. *saracchighoṣa*, A brahmin who asks King Ambara, a previous life of Śākyamuni, for his ears.

## Saraha
*sa ra ha*, Indian [mahāsiddha](#mahāsiddha), author of three cycles of [dohās](#dohā)

## Saṇṭīraka
Skt. *saṇṭīraka*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## sarala pine
*gdug pa’i shing*, gdug pa’i shing is an alternate spelling for the Tibetan bdug pa’i shing, which translates the Sanskrit dhūpavṛkṣa—one of many names for the sarala pine or Pinus roxburghii, but the literal meaning of this term (“a tree that gives off aromatic smoke”) might apply to a number of different trees such as juniper, which is commonly used in Tibetan smoke offering rites.

## Sarasvatī
*dbyangs can ma*, Skt. *sarasvatī*, The goddess of music and eloquence. The Sanskrit name means “she who has flow,” or “she who has a body of water.” She was originally the personification of the Punjab river of that name.

## Sarasvatī Grove
Skt. *sarasvatyārāma*, The name of a garden in Kauśāmbī.

## Sarasvati­saṃgīti
*glu snyan pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarasvati­saṃgīti*, A palace in another world in the distant past.

## Sarayū
*sar yu*, Skt. *sarayū*, A river.

## Saṃśrayasa
*legs bcas*, Skt. *saṃśrayasa*, A previous eon, during which Śākyamuni was a cakravartin named Ambara.

## Sarṣibhañjikā
The name of a town.

## Sarma
The name of a king.

## Saṃrocana
*legs dga’*, Skt. *saṃrocana*, A pupil of the Buddha Śākyamuni who is one of only eight bodhisattvas in the past or future who equal the Buddha Śākyamuni’s generosity in his previous lives.

## Saṃrocanabuddha
*sangs rgyas yang dag ’dod*, Skt. *saṃrocana­buddha*, A bodhisattva sent by the Buddha Vigata­saṃtāpodbhava­vaiśravaṇasāla­rāja to pay homage to Śākyamuni.

## Sarpadāsa
*sbrul kho*, Skt. *sarpadāsa*, A disciple of the Buddha. Note that this name rendered as sprul khol in the Degé Kangyur.

## Sarva­śaṅkita­sumardaka
*dogs pa thams cad legs par ’joms pa*, Skt. *sarva­śaṅkita­sumardaka*, A buddha.

## Sarvaśatrudamana
*dgra thams cad ’dul ba*, Skt. *sarva­śatru­damana*, A buddha.

## Sarva­bala­vegavatī
*stobs thams cad kyi shugs dang ldan pa*, Skt. *sarva­bala­vegavatī*, A southern realm.

## Sarvabhadra
*thams cad bzang*, Skt. *sarvabhadra*, A yakṣa general.

## Sarvabhayahara
*’jigs pa thams cad sel ba*, Skt. *sarvabhayahara*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of this teaching.

## Sarvabhūtaketu
*’byung po thams cad kyi tog ma*, Skt. *sarvabhūtaketu*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarva­bhūta­saṃkṣayaka
*’byung po thams cad yang dag par ’khrug par byed pa*, Skt. *sarva­bhūta­saṃkṣayaka*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Sarva­bhūta­vaśaṅkarī
*’byung po thams cad dbang du byed pa*, Skt. *sarva­bhūta­vaśaṅkarī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Sarva­bhūta­yakṣa­rākṣasa­preta­piśāca­kuṃbhāṇḍa­mahoraga­śrī
*byung bo thams cad dang gnod sbyin dang srin po dang yi dgas dang sha za dang grul bum dang lto ’phye chen po thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­bhūta­yakṣa­rākṣasa­preta­piśāca­kuṃbhāṇḍa­mahoraga­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarvabhūtika
*’byung po thams cad pa*, Skt. *sarvabhūtika*, One of the rāśis.

## Sarva­bhūtāvartā
*’byung po thams cad ’khyil ma*, Skt. *sarva­bhūtāvartā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarva­bodhisattva­śrī
*byangs chub sems pa thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­bodhisattva­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­buddha­kṣetra­pariśuddhi­nigarjita­pratibhāsa­vijñāpanā
*sangs rgyas kyi zhing thams cad yongs su dag par sgra ’byin pa’i gzugs brnyan rnam par dmigs pa*, Skt. *sarva­buddha­kṣetra­pariśuddhi­nigarjita­pratibhāsa­vijñāpanā*, “The Perception of the Speech Emitted by All the Pure Buddha Realms.” The name of a ray of light.

## Sarva­buddha­nirmāṇa­pratibhāsa­cūḍa
*sangs rgyas thams cad kyi sprul pa snang ba’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *sarva­buddha­nirmāṇa­pratibhāsa­cūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­buddha­saṃbhūta­garbha­maṇi­mukuṭa
*sangs rgyas thams cad yang dag par ’byung ba’i snying po*, Skt. *sarva­buddha­saṃbhūta­garbha­maṇi­mukuṭa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarvacaṇḍāla
*thams cad du gdol pa*, Skt. *sarvacaṇḍāla*, One of the sons of Māra present on the eve of Siddhārtha’s awakening.

## Sarva­caryātiśaya­jñāna­rāja
*spyod pa thams cad kyi yul shes pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­caryātiśaya­jñāna­rāja*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvadada
*kun sbyin*, Skt. *sarvadada*, One of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Sarvaṃdada
*thams cad sbyin pa*, Skt. *sarvaṃdada*, The name given by the devas to the cakravartin Ambara, a previous life of Śākyamuni, on account of his generosity. It means “The One Who Gives Away Everything.”

## Sarvadarśin
*kun mthong*, Skt. *sarvadarśin*, One of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Sarva­deva­gaṇa­mukha­śrī
*lha’i tshogs thams cad la mngon du phyogs pa’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­deva­gaṇa­mukha­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­deva­nāga­yakṣa­gandharvāsura­garuḍa­kinnara­mahoraga­śrī
*lha dang klu dang gnod sbyin dang dri za dang lha ma yin dang nam mkha’ lding dang mi ’am ci dang lto ’phye chen po thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­deva­nāga­yakṣa­gandharvāsura­garuḍa­kinnara­mahoraga­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­devatābhiṣiktā
*lha thams cad kyi dbang bskur ba*, Skt. *sarva­devatābhiṣiktā*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­devatābhimukha­śrī
*lha sogs pa thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­devatābhimukha­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­devatā­mātṛ
*lha thams cad kyi ma*, Skt. *sarva­devatā­mātṛ*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## sarvadhalī
Unidentified ritual ingredient.

## Sarva­dhana­dhānyākarṣaṇa­śrī
*nor dang ’bru thams cad sdud pa’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­dhana­dhānyākarṣaṇa­śrī*, A tathāgata.

## Sarva­dharma­bhāvanārambha­saṃbhava­tejas
*chos thams cad kyi gnas bsgrub pa yongs su ’grub pa’i gzi brjid*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­bhāvanārambha­saṃbhava­tejas*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Sarva­dharma­darśin
*chos thams cad gzigs*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­darśin*, A buddha.

## sarva­dharma­dhāraṇī­mukha­mudra
*chos thams cad kyi gzungs kyi sgo’i phyag rgya*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­dhāraṇī­mukha­mudra*, Lit. “seal of the dhāraṇī gateway for all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharma­dhātu­sāgara­nigarjita­ghoṣa
*chos rgya mtsho thams cad rab tu sgrog pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­dhātu­sāgara­nigarjita­ghoṣa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­dharma­dhātu­spharaṇa­ghoṣa
*chos kyi dbyings kun tu rgyas pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­dhātu­spharaṇa­ghoṣa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­dharma­dhātu­tala­bheda­ketu­rāja
*chos kyi dbyings kyi gzhi tha dad pa’i dpal gyi rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­dhātu­tala­bheda­ketu­rāja*, A bodhisattva in a southeastern realm.

## sarva­dharmaikarasa
*chos thams cad ro gcig pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmaikarasa*, Lit. “the one taste of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­jñānādhivāsana­praveśa
*chos thams cad shes pa’i bzod pa la ’jug pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­jñānādhivāsana­praveśa*, Lit. “entry into knowledge forbearance for all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­mudra
*chos thams cad kyi phyag rgya*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­mudra*, Lit. “seal of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­mudrāgata
*chos thams cad kyi phyag rgyar gyur pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­mudrāgata*, Lit. “become exalted among all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­niśceṣṭa
*chos thams cad byed pa med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­niśceṣṭa*, Lit. “where all dharmas are motionless.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharma­nigarjita­rāja
*chos thams cad rab tu sgrog pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nigarjita­rāja*, This is a buddha in the distant past in chapter 34, where the name is translated as chos thams cad rab tu sgrog pa’i rgyal po, and a buddha in the distant past in chapter 41, where the name is translated as chos thams cad kyi ’brug sgra bsgrags pa’i rgyal po.

## sarva­dharma­nimittāpagata
*chos thams cad mtshan ma dang bral ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nimittāpagata*, Lit. “separated from all causal signs.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharma­nirnādacchatra­maṇḍala­nirghoṣa
*chos thams cad kyi nga ro’i gdugs kyi dkyil ’khor rab tu sgrog pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nirnādacchatra­maṇḍala­nirghoṣa*, A cakravartin king in another world realm in the distant past.

## sarva­dharma­nirnānātva
*chos thams cad tha dad pa med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nirnānātva*, Lit. “where all dharmas are in a state without difference.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­nirukti­niyata­praveśa
*chos thams cad kyi nges pa’i tshig la gdon mi za bar ’jug pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nirukti­niyata­praveśa*, Lit. “entry into certainty about the etymologies of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­nirvedhaka
*chos thams cad la nges par ’bigs pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nirvedhaka*, Lit. “piercer of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­nirviśeṣa­darśin
*chos thams cad bye brag med par lta ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nirviśeṣa­darśin*, Lit. “that sees all dharmas without particularizing them.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­nirvikāra­darśin
*chos thams cad ’gyur ba med par mthong ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nirvikāra­darśin*, Lit. “seeing all dharmas as unchanging.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharma­nityadarśana­dhīmat
*chos thams cad la rtag tu lta ba’i blo ldan*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­nityadarśana­dhīmat*, The name of a bodhisattva. “Intelligence That Always Sees All Phenomena.”

## sarva­dharma­pada­prabheda
*chos thams cad kyi tshig rab tu ’byed pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­pada­prabheda*, Lit. “sorts out the words for all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharma­prabha­rāja
*chos ’od rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­prabha­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Sarva­dharma­prabhāsa­vyūha­śrī
*chos kyi snang ba thams cad bkod pa’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­prabhāsa­vyūha­śrī*, A tathāgata.

## sarva­dharma­praveśa­mudra
*chos thams cad la ’jug pa’i phyag rgya*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­praveśa­mudra*, Lit. “seal of entry into all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­praveśa­mukha
*chos thams cad la ’jug pa’i sgo*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­praveśa­mukha*, Lit. “gateway of the entry into all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­samatā
*chos thams cad mnyam pa nyid*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­samatā*, Lit. “sameness of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­samavasaraṇa­samudra
*chos thams cad yang dag par ’du ba rgya mtsho*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­samavasaraṇa­samudra*, Lit. “ocean in which all dharmas are united.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­samavasaraṇa­sāgara­mudra
*chos thams cad yang dag par ’du ba rgya mtsho’i phyag rgya*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­samavasaraṇa­sāgara­mudrā*, Lit. “ocean seal in which all dharmas are united.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­samavasaraṇākāra­mudra
*chos thams cad yang dag par ’du ba’i rnam pa’i phyag rgya*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­samavasaraṇākāra­mudra*, Lit. “seal in a form in which all dharmas are united.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharma­samādhi­prabha­ghoṣa
*chos thams cad ting nge ’dzin gyi ’od kyi dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­samādhi­prabha­ghoṣa*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Sarva­dharma­samudrābhyudgata­vega­rāja
*chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyis mngon par ’phags pa’i shugs kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­samudrābhyudgata­vega­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Sarva­dharma­sāgara­nirghoṣa­prabha­rāja
*chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi dbyangs ’od kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­sāgara­nirghoṣa­prabha­rāja*, A buddha in another world in the distant past, the first of countless buddhas in that kalpa. In verse he is called Dharma­samudra­prabha­garjita­rāja.

## Sarva­dharma­sāgara­nirghoṣa­rāja
*chos rgya mtsho thams cad kyi gsung gi rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­sāgara­nirghoṣa­rāja*, A buddha in a world in the eastern direction in the past.

## sarva­dharma­svabhāva­vyavalokana
*chos thams cad kyi ngo bo nyid la rnam par lta ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­svabhāva­vyavalokana*, Lit. “looking at the intrinsic nature of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­svabhāvānupalabdhi
*chos thams cad kyi ngo bo nyid mi dmigs pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­svabhāvānupalabdhi*, Lit. “where the intrinsic nature of all dharmas cannot be found.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­tamopagata
*chos thams cad mun pa dang bral ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­tamopagata*, Lit. “where all dharmas are free from darkness.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­vibhava­samudra
*chos thams cad kyi ’byor pa rgya mtsho*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­vibhava­samudra*, Lit. “ocean of the wealth of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­vipaśyana
*chos thams cad la rnam par lta ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­vipaśyana*, Lit. “giving insight into all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharma­vivikta
*chos thams cad dben*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­vivikta*, Lit. “isolation of all dharmas.”Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharma­vīrya­vega­dhvaja
*chos thams cad kyi brtson ’grus drag po’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­vīrya­vega­dhvaja*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## sarva­dharmābhyudgata
*chos thams cad las mngon par ’phags pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmābhyudgata*, Lit. “that has risen above all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmācalana
*chos thams cad g.yo ba med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmācalana*, Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmācintya
*chos thams cad bsam gyis mi khyab*, Skt. *sarva­dharmācintya*, Lit. “inconceivability of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharmeśvara­vaśa­vikrānta­gāmin
*chos thams cad la dbang phyug gi dbang gi rtsal gyis spyod pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmeśvara­vaśa­vikrānta­gāmin*, A bodhisattva present in the Buddha’s assembly.

## sarva­dharmājñāna­vidhvaṃsana
*chos thams cad mi shes pa sel ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharmājñāna­vidhvaṃsana*, Lit. “shattering ignorance of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmājñānāpagata
*chos thams cad mi shes pa dang bral ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharmājñānāpagata*, Lit. “separated from not knowing all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmāmanana
*chos thams cad rlom sems med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāmanana*, Lit. “without conceit for any dharma.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmānirodha
*chos thams cad ’gag pa med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmānirodha*, Lit. “where all dharmas are in a state without cessation.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmānupalabdhi
*chos thams cad mi dmigs pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmānupalabdhi*, Lit. “all dharmas are not found.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmānutpāda
*chos thams cad skye ba med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmānutpāda*, Lit. “nonproduction of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmānāvaraṇa­koṭi
*chos thams cad la sgrib pa med pa’i mtha’*, Skt. *sarva­dharmānāvaraṇa­koṭi*, Lit. “unobstructed limit of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmodgata
*chos thams cad las shin tu ’phags*, Skt. *sarva­dharmodgata*, Lit. “superior to all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharmopaccheda
*chos ma yin pa gcod par byed pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmopaccheda*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK. The Tibetan term would translate *Sarvādharmopaccheda.

## sarva­dharmāparigṛhīta
*chos thams cad yongs su ma bzung ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāparigṛhīta*, Lit. “not grasping at any phenomena at all.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmāparyanta
*chos thams cad mu med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāparyanta*, Lit. “the limitlessness of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmāsaṃbheda
*chos thams cad ma ’dres pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāsaṃbheda*, Lit. “unadulterated nature of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmāsaṃpramoṣa
*chos thams cad brjed pa med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāsaṃpramoṣa*, Lit. “does not forget all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmāstambhita
*chos thams cad khengs pa med pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāstambhita*, Lit. “without arrogance toward any dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmātikramaṇa
*chos thams cad las ’da’ ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharmātikramaṇa*, Lit. “gone beyond all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmātma­bhāvānabhinirhāra
*chos thams cad bdag gi dngos po mi sgrub pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmātma­bhāvānabhinirhāra*, Lit. “does not establish the essential nature in all phenomena.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­dharmāvabhāsa­kara
*chos thams cad snang bar byed pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāvabhāsa­kara*, Lit. “illuminator of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­dharmīśvara­rāja
*chos thams cad kyi dbang phyug gi rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­dharmīśvara­rāja*, One of the sixteen great bodhisattvas. The content of the list varies from text to text.

## sarva­dharmāvibhāvanāsamatā
*chos thams cad rnam par ’jig pa mnyam pa nyid*, Skt. *sarva­dharmāvibhāvanāsamatā*, Lit. “sameness of the destruction of all dharmas.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­diśa­pradīpa­prabha­rāja
*phyogs rnams kun tu sgron ma gsal ba’i bdag*, Skt. *sarva­diśa­pradīpa­prabha­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## sarva­dṛṣṭi­kṛta­gahana­vivarjita
*lta bar gyur pa thibs po thams cad rnam par spong ba*, Skt. *sarva­dṛṣṭi­kṛta­gahana­vivarjita*, Lit. “extricated from the thicket of all the distortions.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarvagamin
*thams cad du ’gro ba*, Skt. *sarvagamin*, A parivrājaka who is the kalyāṇamitra of chapter 23.

## Sarva­gandha­prabhāsa­vatī
*spos thams cad kyi ’od dang ldan pa*, Skt. *sarva­gandha­prabhāsa­vatī*, A western buddha realm.

## Sarva­gandha­sugandhā
*spos thams cad kyi dri mchog*, Skt. *sarva­gandha­sugandhā*, Universe of the Buddha Gandhottama­kūṭa; a universe wherein the Dharma is taught through the medium of scent. According to Lamotte, p. 319, n. 2, this universe is mentioned in the Śikṣāsamuccaya, the Laṇkāvatāra, and the Prasannapadā. However, In the Prasannapadā, this universe is said to be ruled by Samantabhadra, not Gandhottama­kūṭa (see Lamotte, p. 320, n. 3).

## Sarva­gandhārci­mukha
*zhal nas spos thams cad ’od du ’phro ba*, Skt. *sarva­gandhārci­mukha*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Sarvaghoṣa
*kun dbyangs*, Skt. *sarvaghoṣa*, The southern realm in which the bodhisattva Dharaṇidatta became the Buddha Saṃkaramardārci.

## sarva­giri­ghoṣākṣara­vimukta
*sgra dbyangs kyi yi ge thams cad dang bral ba*, Skt. *sarva­giri­ghoṣākṣara­vimukta*, Lit. “free from all sound and voiced syllables.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarvagrahaśrī
*zla thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarvagrahaśrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## sarva­guṇa­saṃcaya
*yon tan thams cad kyi tshogs su gyur pa*, Skt. *sarva­guṇa­saṃcaya*, Lit. “collection of all good qualities.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­guṇa­viśuddhi­garbha
*yon tan thams cad rnam par dag pa’i snying po*, Skt. *sarva­guṇa­viśuddhi­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Sarva­jagad­abhimukha­pradīpā
*’gro ba thams cad la mngon du gyur pa’i sgron ma*, Skt. *sarva­jagad­abhimukha­pradīpā*, “The Lamp of the Manifestation of All Beings.” The name of a ray of light.

## Sarva­jagadabhi­mukha­rūpa
*’gro ba thams cad mngon gzugs*, Skt. *sarva­jagadabhi­mukha­rūpa*, The seventy-third buddha in a kalpa in the distant past.

## Sarva­jagad­buddha­darśana­vipāka­kuśala­mūla­saṃbhavā
*’gro ba thams cad kyis sangs rgyas mthong ba rnam par smin pa’i dge ba’i rtsa ba las byung ba*, Skt. *sarva­jagad­buddha­darśana­vipāka­kuśala­mūla­saṃbhavā*, “The Vision of the Buddha by All Beings Arisen from Ripened Roots of Virtue.” The name of a ray of light.

## Sarva­jagad­dhita­praṇidhāna­candra
*’gro ba thams cad la phan pa’i smon lam zla ba*, Skt. *sarva­jagad­dhita­praṇidhāna­candra*, The second of five hundred buddhas in a kalpa in the distant future.

## Sarva­jagad­duḥkha­praśāntyāśvāsana­ghoṣa
*’gro ba thams cad sdug bsngal rab tu zhi bar bya ba’i dbugs ’byin pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­jagad­duḥkha­praśāntyāśvāsana­ghoṣa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­jagad­rakṣā­praṇidhāna­vīrya­prabhā
*’gro ba thams cad bsrung ba’i smon lam la brtson pa’i ’od*, Skt. *sarva­jagad­rakṣā­praṇidhāna­vīrya­prabhā*, A night goddess at the bodhimaṇḍa.

## Sarva­jagadvara­vyūha­garbha
*’gro ba thams cad na rgyan gyi dam pa phul*, Skt. *sarva­jagadvara­vyūha­garbha*, The palace of Mahābrahmā. The name could be translated as “The Essence of the Array of All Worlds.” Jagad can also mean “beings” and therefore is regularly translated as ’gro ba (“beings”) in this sūtra. Here garbha, usually meaning “essence,” is translated as phul (“perfection”).

## Sarvajñādeva
*sarba dz+nyA de ba*, Skt. *sarvajñādeva*, according to traditional accounts, the Kashmiri [preceptor](#preceptor) Sarvajñādeva was among the “one hundred” [paṇḍita](#paṇḍita)s invited by Trisong Deutsen (r. 755–797/800) to assist with the translation of the Buddhist scriptures into Tibetan. Sarvajñādeva assisted in the translation of more than twenty-three works, including numerous [sūtra](#sūtra)s and the first translations of [Śāntideva](#śāntideva)’s Bodhicaryāvatāra and Nāgarjuna’s Suhṛllekha. Much of this work was likely carried out in the first years of the ninth century and may have continued into the reign of Ralpachen, who ascended the throne in 815 and died in 838 or 841 ᴄᴇ. (See Dotson, 2007, for a summary of the imperial chronology between Trisong Deutsen’s abdication in 797 and Ralpachen’s ascension in 815).

## Sarvajit
The twenty-first in the sixty-year calendar of Vedic astrology, literally meaning “all-conquering.”

## Sarvajita
Skt. *sarvajita*, One of the rāśis.

## sarva­kausīdyāpagata
*le lo thams cad dang bral ba*, Skt. *sarva­kausīdyāpagata*, Lit. “separated from all laziness.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­kṣetrālaṅkāra­vyūhasandarśaka
*zhing thams cad kyi rgyan bkod pa kun tu ston pa*, Skt. *sarva­kṣetrālaṅkāra­vyūhasandarśaka*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva present in the Buddha’s assembly. His name means “Revealing the Ornamental Displays of All Buddhafields.”

## Sarva­kinnara­sarvāsuryottama­śrī
*dpal gyi mchog mi ’am ci mo thams cad dang lha ma yin mo thams cad kyi dpal gyi mchog*, Skt. *sarva­kinnara­sarvāsuryottama­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## sarva­kleśa­nirdahana
*nyon mongs pa thams cad nges par sreg pa*, Skt. *sarva­kleśa­nirdahana*, Lit. “burns all afflictive emotions.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarvakāmalatā
*’dod pa kun gyi ’khris ma*, Skt. *sarvakāmalatā*, A goddess in the maṇḍala of Heruka.

## Sarvakrodha
*khro bo thams cad*, Skt. *sarvakrodha*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Sarva­kuśala­mūla­saṃbhava­nirghoṣā
*dge ba’i rtsa ba thams cad yang dag par ’byung ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­kuśala­mūla­saṃbhava­nirghoṣā*, “The Voice That Causes the Emergence of All Roots of Merit.” The name of a ray of light.

## Sarvakuṇḍali
*’khyil bar bcas pa*, Skt. *sarvakuṇḍalin*, A deity in Heruka’s maṇḍala.

## Sarva­lakṣaṇa­pratimaṇḍita­viśuddhi­śrī­garbha
*mtshan thams cad kyis brgyan pas rnam par dag pa’i dpal gyi snying po*, Skt. *sarva­lakṣaṇa­pratimaṇḍita­viśuddhi­śrī­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Sarva­loka­bhayacchambhita­tva­vidhvaṃsana­rakara
*’jig rten thams cad kyi ’jigs pa dang pham pa dang bag tsha ba rnam par ’joms pa*, Skt. *sarva­loka­bhayacchambhita­tva­vidhvaṃsana­rakara*, A buddha in the northeastern direction.

## Sarva­loka­dhātūdgata­mukuṭa
*’jig rten thams cad las mngon par ’phags pa’i cod pan*, Skt. *sarva­loka­dhātūdgata­mukuṭa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­loka­dhātū­padra­vodvega­pratyuttīrṇa
*’jig rten gyi khams thams cad kyi gnod pa dang skyo ba las rab tu brgal ba*, Skt. *sarva­loka­dhātū­padra­vodvega­pratyuttīrṇa*, A buddha in the western direction.

## Sarva­loka­hitaiṣin
*’jig rten thams cad la phan par mdzad pa*, Skt. *sarva­loka­hitaiṣin*, The fourth of five hundred buddhas in a kalpa in the distant future.

## sarva­loka­prabhākara
*’jig rten thams cad du ’od byed pa*, Skt. *sarva­loka­prabhākara*, Lit. “illuminator of all worlds.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­maṅgala­dhāriṇī
*bkra shis thams cad ’dzin ma*, Skt. *sarva­maṅgala­dhāriṇī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­maṅgala­dhārin
*dga’ byed kyi bkra bshis thams cad ’dzin pa*, Skt. *sarva­maṅgala­dhārin*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of this teaching.

## Sarva­mahā­pṛthivī­rāja­maṇi­raśmi­jāla­pramuktā
*sa chen po thams cad du mdzes pa’i rin po che ’od zer gyi dra ba rab tu ’gyed pa*, Skt. *sarva­mahā­pṛthivī­rāja­maṇi­raśmi­jāla­pramuktā*, A buddha realm in the northeastern direction.

## Sarva­malā­pa­gata
*dri ma kun bral*, Skt. *sarva­malā­pa­gata*, A great bodhisattva.

## Sarva­māra­maṇḍala­pramardaṇa­ghoṣa
*bdud kyi dkyil ’khor thams cad rab tu ’dul ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­māra­maṇḍala­pramardaṇa­ghoṣa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­māra­maṇḍala­vikiraṇa­jñāna­dhvaja
*bdud kyi dkyil ’khor thams cad rnam par ’thor ba’i ye shes rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *sarva­māra­maṇḍala­vikiraṇa­jñāna­dhvaja*, A bodhisattva from a southwestern realm. Also known as Sarva­māra­maṇḍala­vikiraṇa­jñāna­dhvaja­rāja.

## Sarva­māra­maṇḍala­vikiraṇa­jñāna­dhvaja­rāja
*bdud kyi dkyil ’khor thams cad rnam par ’thor ba’i ye shes rgyal mtshan gyi rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­māra­maṇḍala­vikiraṇa­jñāna­dhvaja­rāja*, A bodhisattva from a southwestern realm. Also known as Sarva­māra­maṇḍala­vikiraṇa­jñāna­dhvaja.

## Sarva­māra­viśayasa­mati­krānta
*bdud thams cad kyi yul las ’das pa*, Skt. *sarva­māra­viśayasa­mati­krānta*, A buddha.

## Sarva­nadī­saricchrī
*chu klung dang mtsho thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­nadī­saricchrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­nagara­rakṣā­saṃbhava­tejaḥ­śrī
*grong khyer thams cad bsrung ba ’byung ba’i gzi brjid dpal*, Skt. *sarva­nagara­rakṣā­saṃbhava­tejaḥ­śrī*, A night goddess in Bodhgaya.

## Sarva­nivaraṇa­viṣkambhin
*sgrib pa thams cad rnam par sel*, Skt. *sarva­nivaraṇa­viṣkambhin*, One of the celestial bodhisattvas.

## Sarva­nīvaraṇa­viṣkaṃbhin
*sgrib pa thams cad rnam par sel ba*, Skt. *sarva­nīvaraṇa­viṣkaṃbhin*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of this teaching.

## Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin
*sgrib pa rnam sel*, one of the [Eight Great Close Sons](#eight-great-close-sons) of [Buddha](#buddha) [Śākyamuni](#śākyamuni).

## Sarva­nīvaraṇa­viṣkambhin
*sgrib pa thams cad rnam par sel ba*, Skt. *sarva­nīvaraṇavi­ṣkambhin*, One of the eight great bodhisattvas. In particular, he has an important role in the Lotus Sūtra, in which Buddha Śākyamuni sends him to Vārāṇasī to see Avalokiteśvara. This is paralleled in the Kāraṇḍavyūha, in which he is sent to Vārāṇasī to obtain Avalokitesvara’s mahāvidyā.

## Sarva­nīvaraṇa­viṣkam­bhin
*sgrib pa thams cad rnam par sel ba*, Skt. *sarva­nīvaraṇa­viṣkam­bhin*, A great bodhisattva, visitor from the distant buddhafield of Padmanetra, and the Buddha Śākyamuni’s main interlocutor in this text.

## Sarva­śokāndha­kārāpoha­mati
*mya ngan gyi mun pa thams cad sel ba’i blo gros*, Skt. *sarva­śokāndha­kārāpoha­mati*, The name of a bodhisattva. “Intelligence Dispelling All Darkness of Sorrow.”

## Sarva­śokāpagata
*mya ngan med pa*, Skt. *sarva­śokāpagata*, Name of a world system in the southern direction, where the buddha Aśokaśrī teaches the perfection of wisdom to bodhisattva great beings.

## Sarvaśokāpagata
*mya ngan med pa*, Skt. *sarva­śokāpagata*, Name of a world system in the southern direction, where the buddha Aśokaśrī teaches the perfection of wisdom to bodhisattva great beings.

## Sarva­pāpa­hantrī
*sdig pa thams cad ’phrog ma*, Skt. *sarva­pāpa­hantrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­praṇidhāna­sāgara­nirghoṣa­maṇi­rāja­cūḍa
*smon lam rgya mtsho thams cad rab tu sgrog pa’i rin chen rgyal po’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *sarva­praṇidhāna­sāgara­nirghoṣa­maṇi­rāja­cūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­pṛthivī­śrī
*sa thams cad dang rgyal po thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­pṛthivī­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­puṇya­lakṣaṇa­dhārin
*bsod nams kyi mtshan tham cad ’dzin pa*, Skt. *sarva­puṇya­lakṣaṇa­dhārin*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of this teaching.

## Sarva­puṇyākarṣaṇa­śrī
*bsod nams thams cad sdud pa’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­puṇyākarṣaṇa­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­puṇyopacitāṅgī
*bsod nams kyi phung po thams cad kyi lus can*, Skt. *sarva­puṇyopacitāṅgī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarvaśrī
*bkra shis thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarvaśrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarvarasa
The name of a muhūrta.

## Sarva­ratna­garbha­vicitrābha
*rin po che thams cad kyi snying po ’od sna tshogs can*, Skt. *sarva­ratna­garbha­vicitrābha*, A bodhimaṇḍa in a world realm in the eastern direction.

## Sarva­ratna­śikhara­dhvaja
*rin po che sna tshogs kyi rtse mo’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *sarva­ratna­śikhara­dhvaja*, A four-continent world in the distant past.

## Sarvaratnapāṇi
*thams cad phyag na rin po che*, Skt. *sarvaratnapāṇi*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarva­ratna­rucirā
*rin po che thams cad rab tu ’bar ba*, Skt. *sarva­ratna­rucirā*, A northeastern buddha realm.

## Sarva­ratna­saṃnicaya
*rin po che thams cad yang dag par bsags pa*, Skt. *sarva­ratna­saṃnicaya*, Literally “An Accumulation of All Jewels.” Prince Avalokiteśvara will attain complete enlightenment and become the Tathāgata Samantaraśmyabhyudgataśrīkūṭarāja in this realm.

## Sarva­ratna­varṇa­samanta­prabhāsa­śrī
*rin po che thams cad kyi mdog kun tu snang ba’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­ratna­varṇa­samanta­prabhāsa­śrī*, A world realm in the distant past.

## Sarva­ratna­vicitra­varṇa­maṇi­kuṇḍala
*rin po che’i dkyil ’khor rin po che thams cad kyis rnam par brgyan pa’i kha dog*, Skt. *sarva­ratna­vicitra­varṇa­maṇi­kuṇḍala*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Sarva­ratna­vimala­prabhā­vyūha
*rin po che thams cad kyi dri ma med pa’i ’od rnam par brgyan pa*, Skt. *sarva­ratna­vimala­prabhā­vyūha*, A universe of world realms far to the east.

## Sarvaratnābha
*rin chen thams cad ’od*, Skt. *sarvaratnābha*, A realm in the distant past. BHS: Sarvaratanābha.

## Sarva­rṣi­pavitra­śrī
*drang srong thams cad dag par byed pa’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­rṣi­pavitra­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## sarva­rodha­nirodha­saṃpraśamana
*’gal ba dang ’gog pa thams cad yang dag par zhi ba*, Skt. *sarva­rodha­nirodha­saṃpraśamana*, Lit. “pacifier of all obstruction and stopping.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­rūpa­saṃdarśanā
*gzugs thams cad shin tu ston pa*, Skt. *sarva­rūpa­saṃdarśanā*, A world realm in the distant past.

## Sarva­rūpa­saṃdarśana
*gzugs thams cad ston pa*, Skt. *sarva­rūpa­saṃdarśana*, This bodhisattva asks Vimalakīrti the whereabouts of his family, etc., thus prompting the latter’s extraordinary verses on the family and accoutrements of all bodhisattvas (Chap. 8).

## Sarvartha­siddha
*don thams cad grub pa*, Skt. *sarvartha­siddha*, A great bodhisattva.

## Sarvasa­ddharmā­vismaraṇasthita
*dam pa’i chos thams cad mi brjed par gnas pa*, Skt. *sarvasa­ddharmā­vismaraṇasthita*, The name of a bodhisattva. “Not-Forgetting All the Sacred Teachings”

## sarva­saṅga­vimukta
*chags pa thams cad las rnam par grol ba*, Skt. *sarva­saṅga­vimukta*, Lit. “free from all attachments.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­saṃketa­rūta­praveśa
*brda dang sgra thams cad la ’jug pa*, Skt. *sarva­saṃketa­rūta­praveśa*, Lit. “entry into all terms and sounds.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­samādhi­sāgarāvabhāsa­siṃha
*ting nge ’dzin rgya mtsho thams cad snang bar mdzad pa’i seng ge*, Skt. *sarva­samādhi­sāgarāvabhāsa­siṃha*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Sarva­sattva­karma­vipāka­nirghoṣa
*sems can thams cad kyi las rnam par smin pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­karma­vipāka­nirghoṣa*, “The Voice That Ripens the Karma of All Beings.” The name of a ray of light.

## Sarva­sattva­kuśala­mūla­nigarjita­svara
*sems can kun gyi dge ba’i rtsa ba rab tu sgrog pa’i sgra*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­kuśala­mūla­nigarjita­svara*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­sattva­praharṣa­prīti­prāmodya­samudaya­nirghoṣā
*sems can thams cad rab tu dga’ ba dang spro ba dang mos pa yongs su ’byung ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­praharṣa­prīti­prāmodya­samudaya­nirghoṣā*, “The Voice That Gives Rise to Joy, Delight, and Aspiration in All Beings.” The name of a ray of light.

## Sarva­sattva­priyadarśana
*’jig rten thams cad kyis mthong*, Skt. *sarvasattvapriyadarśana*, A Licchavī youth.

## Sarva­sattva­priya­darśana
*sems can thams cad kyis mthong na dga’ ba*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­priya­darśana*, The name of Mahāprajāpatī when she becomes a buddha in the future. Also the name of a bodhisattva.

## sarva­sattva­ruta­kauśalyānugata
*sems can thams cad kyi sgra la mkhas pa’i rjes su song ba*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­ruta­kauśalyānugata*, Lit. “following the knowledge of sounds of all beings.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­sattva­ruta­nirhāra
*sems can thams cad kyi sgra sgrub pa*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­ruta­nirhāra*, Lit. “that produces the sounds of all beings.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­sattva­trātā
*sems can thams cad skyob pa*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­trātā*, Name of a Mahābrahmā in the eastern direction.

## Sarva­sattva­virajaḥpradīpa
*sems can thams cad rdul dang ’byed pa’i sgron ma*, Skt. *sarva­sattva­virajaḥpradīpa*, “The Lamp That Removes the Dust from All Beings.” The name of a ray of light.

## sarva­sattvābhibhavana
*sems can thams cad zil gyis gnon pa*, Skt. *sarva­sattvābhibhavana*, Lit. “overcomes all beings.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­sattvābhimukhī
*sems can thams cad la mngon du phyogs ma’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­sattvābhimukhī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## sarva­sattvābhipramodana
*sems can thams cad mngon par dga’ ba*, Skt. *sarva­sattvābhipramodana*, Lit. “that delights all beings.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­sattvojohārī
*sems can thams cad kyi mdangs ’phrog*, Skt. *sarva­sattvojohārī*, A rākṣasī known only from this sūtra.

## Sarva­sattvāvabhāsa­tejas
*sems can thams cad tu snang ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­sattvāvabhāsa­tejas*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Sarvasiddhārtha
*don kun ’grub pa*, Skt. *sarvasiddhārtha*, A great bodhisattva.

## sarva­sārānugata
*snying po thams cad kyi rjes su song ba*, Skt. *sarva­sārānugata*, Lit. “following all essences.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarva­sukha­duḥkha­nirabhinandin
*bde ba dang sdug bsngal thams cad la mngon par dga’ ba med pa*, Skt. *sarva­sukha­duḥkha­nirabhinandin*, Lit. “not taking pleasure in any happiness or suffering.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarva­sukha­pratimaṇḍita
*bde ba thams cad kyis rab tu brgyan pa*, Skt. *sarva­sukha­pratimaṇḍita*, A universe, or buddhafield, where the bodhisattvas live in a constant state of bliss. The Skt. of the Potala MS has Sarva­sukha­pratimaṇḍita, that of the excerpt cited in the Śikṣāsamuccaya has Sarvasukhamaṇḍitā.

## Sarva­sumeru­parvata­rāja­śrī
*ri bo’i rgyal po ri rab thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­sumeru­parvata­rāja­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­svarāṅga­ruta­ghoṣa­śrī
*thams cad dbyangs kyi yan lag sgra skad dpal*, Skt. *sarva­svarāṅga­ruta­ghoṣa­śrī*, The hundred-and-fifth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. BHS verse: Sarva­svarāṅga­ruta­ghoṣa­śirī.

## Sarva­svarāṅga­ruta­nirghoṣa­śrī
*gsung gi yan lag thams cad kyi sgra dbyangs dpal*, Skt. *sarva­svarāṅga­ruta­nirghoṣa­śrī*, A tathāgata.

## Sarva­tamāndha­kāra­vidhamana­rāja
*mun nag thams cad ’joms pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­tamāndha­kāra­vidhamana­rāja*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarva­tathāgata­dharma­cakra­nirghoṣa­cūḍa
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi chos kyi ’khor lo sgrog pa’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­dharma­cakra­nirghoṣa­cūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­tathāgata­mātṛ
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yum*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­mātṛ*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­tathāgata­prabhā­maṇḍala­pramuñcana­maṇi­ratna­nigarjita­cūḍa
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi ’od kyi dkyil ’khor rab tu ’gyed pa’i nor bu rin chen ’brug sgra’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­prabhā­maṇḍala­pramuñcana­maṇi­ratna­nigarjita­cūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­tathāgata­prabhā­maṇḍala­vairocanā
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi ’od kyi dkyil ’khor rnam par snang ba*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­prabhā­maṇḍala­vairocanā*, A buddha realm in the downward direction.

## Sarva­tathāgata­prabhā­praṇidhi­nirghoṣa
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi ’od dang smon lam gyi dbyangs*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­prabhā­praṇidhi­nirghoṣa*, A group of world realms in the eastern direction.

## Sarva­tathāgata­śrī
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­tathāgata­siṃhāsana­saṃpratiṣṭhita­maṇi­mukuṭa
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi seng ge’i khri ’dzin pa’i cod pan*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­siṃhāsana­saṃpratiṣṭhita­maṇi­mukuṭa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­tathāgata­vaśavartinī
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad dbang sgyur ma*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­vaśavartinī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­tathāgata­viṣayāsaṃbheda­pradīpā
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul tha mi dad pa’i sgron ma*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­viṣayāsaṃbheda­pradīpā*, “The Lamp of the Different Ranges of All the Tathāgatas.” The name of a ray of light.

## Sarva­tathāgata­vikurvita­pratibhāsa­dhvaja­maṇi­rāja­jāla­saṃchādita­cūḍa
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad rnam par ’phrul pa snang ba’i rgyal mtshan dang rin po che’i rgyal po’i dra bas kun nas yog pa’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgata­vikurvita­pratibhāsa­dhvaja­maṇi­rāja­jāla­saṃchādita­cūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­tathāgatābhiṣiktā
*de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi dbang bskur ba*, Skt. *sarva­tathāgatābhiṣiktā*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarvatejas
*gzi byin thams cad pa*, Skt. *sarvatejas*, The 622nd buddha in the first list, 621st in the second list, and 614th in the third list.

## Sarva­toya­samudra­śrī
*chu thams cad kyi rgya mtsho’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­toya­samudra­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarvatīrthā
*mu tegs kyi sgo thams cad kyi bkra shis ma*, Skt. *sarvatīrthā*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­tīrtha­maṅgala­dhārin
*mu stegs kyi bkra bshis tham cad ’dzin pa*, Skt. *sarva­tīrtha­maṅgala­dhārin*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of this teaching.

## Sarva­tīrthābhimukha­śrī
*mu tegs thams cad du mngon du phyogs pa’i dpal*, Skt. *sarva­tīrthābhimukha­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­tryadhva­nāma­cakra­nirghoṣa­cūḍa
*dus gsum gyi mying thams cad rab tu sgrog pa’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *sarva­tryadhva­nāma­cakra­nirghoṣa­cūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Sarva­tryadhva­tathāgata­viṣaya­patra­saṃdhi­vidyotita­megha­vyūha
*lo ma’i mtshams nas dus gsum gyi de bzhin gshegs pa thams cad kyi yul rnam par ston pa’i ’od gzer gyi sprin gyi rgyan*, Skt. *sarva­tryadhva­tathāgata­viṣaya­patra­saṃdhi­vidyotita­megha­vyūha*, The name of a magical lotus in the distant past; the name means “An Array of the Clouds of the Light Rays from between the Petals That Reveal the Range of All the Tathāgatas of the Three Times.”

## Sarvauṣadhi­tṛṇa­vanaspati­dhana­dhānya­śrī
*sman dang rtsi tog dang shing dang nor dang ’bru thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarvauṣadhi­tṛṇa­vanaspati­dhana­dhānya­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­vaśita­kāya­pratibhāsa
*thams cad la dbang ba’i lus rab tu snang ba*, Skt. **sarva­vaśita­kāya­pratibhāsa*, A bodhimaṇḍa in a world realm in the eastern direction. The Sanskrit is a reconstruction from the Tibetan. The Chinese and Sanskrit each have a different version of the name. See .

## Sarva­vara­guṇa­prabha
*yon tan mchog ma kun gyi ’od*, Skt. *sarva­vara­guṇa­prabha*, The 705th buddha in the first list, 704th in the second list, and 694th in the third list.

## Sarva­viṣamadarśin
*mi mnyam pa thams cad ston pa*, Skt. *sarva­viṣamadarśin*, The name of a bodhisattva. “Unequaled Teacher of All.”

## Sarva­vidyā­dhara­rāja­śrī
*rig sngags ’chang gi rgyal po thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­vidyā­dhara­rāja­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­vidyā­dhara­vajra­pāṇi­vajra­dhara­śrī
*rig sngags ’chang dang lag na rdo rje dang rdo rje ’chang ba thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarva­vidyā­dhara­vajra­pāṇi­vajra­dhara­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarva­vidyāntaś­cara
*rig pa thams cad kyi nang spyod*, Skt. *sarva­vidyāntaś­cara*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Sarva­vikiraṇa­bodhi­vidhvaṃsana­rāja
*gnod pa thams cad rnam par ’jig pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sarva­vikiraṇa­bodhi­vidhvaṃsana­rāja*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvavit
*kun rig*, Skt. *sarvavit*, A sage, former incarnation of the Buddha Dīpaṃkara.

## Sarva­vṛkṣpraphullana­sukha­saṃvāsā
*shing thams cad kyi me tog rgyas par bde bar gnas pa*, Skt. *sarva­vṛkṣpraphullana­sukha­saṃvāsā*, A goddess of the night at the bodhimaṇḍa.

## Sarva­vyādhi­cikitsanī
*nad thams cad gso bar byed ma*, Skt. *sarva­vyādhi­cikitsanī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Sarva­vyūhālaṃkāra­pratibhāsa­saṃdarśana­garbha
*rgyan rnam par bkod pa thams cad rab tu snang bar ston pa’i snying po*, Skt. *sarva­vyūhālaṃkāra­pratibhāsa­saṃdarśana­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Sarvābhibhū
*thams cad zil gyis gnon*, Skt. *sarvābhibhū*, The second of eight named buddhas of the past (with the addition of Śākyamuni making nine) in The Four Boys’ Absorption.

## Sarvābhijñāmati­rāja
*mngon par shes pa thams cad blo gros ’od zer rgyal po*, Skt. *sarvābhijñāmati­rāja*, Sarvābhijñāmati­rāja (King with a Mind of All Supernatural Abilities) is a buddha who inhabits the buddhafield Vyūhā.

## Sarvābhijñā­mati­rāja
*mngon par shes pa’i blo gros thams cad kyi rgyal po*, Skt. *sarvābhijñā­mati­rāja*, “The King of All Clairvoyant Knowledge.” A buddha seen by the assembly of bodhisattvas when they are inside bodhisattva Vajra­garbha’s body. He does not appear anywhere else in the Kangyur .

## Sarvākāśa­talāsaṃbheda­vijñapti­maṇi­ratna­vibhūṣita­cūḍa
*nam mkha’i dbyings thams cad tha myi dad par rnam par dmyigs pa’i rin chen rgyal pos brgyan pa’i gtsug phud*, Skt. *sarvākāśa­talāsaṃbheda­vijñapti­maṇi­ratna­vibhūṣita­cūḍa*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## sarvākāra­prabhākara
*rnam pa thams cad du ’od byed pa*, Skt. *sarvākāra­prabhākara*, Lit. “total illuminator.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## sarvākāra­varopeta
*rnam pa thams cad kyi mchog dang ldan pa*, Skt. *sarvākāra­varopeta*, Lit. “furnished with the supreme of all aspects.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Sarvālakṣmī­nāśayitrī
*bkra mi shis pa thams cad med par byed pa*, Skt. *sarvālakṣmī­nāśayitrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarvālaṅkāra­vibhūṣita
*rgyan thams cad kyis brgyan pa*, Skt. *sarvālaṅkāra­vibhūṣita*, The buddha realm of the Buddha Sālendrarāja in the distant past. Maitreya was a disciple of that buddha.

## Sarvodbhava
*thams cad ’byung ba*, Skt. *sarvodbhava*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvodgata
*thams cad du ’phags pa*, Skt. *sarvodgata*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvārthadarśa
*mthong ba don yod*, Skt. *sarvārthadarśa*, Name of a tathāgata.

## Sarvārthadarśin
*don thams cad gzigs pa*, Skt. *sarvārthadarśin*, Name of a past buddha.

## Sarvārtha­darśin
*don rnams thams cad gzigs*, Skt. *sarvārtha­darśin*, The 218th buddha in the first list, 217th in the second list, and 217th in the third list.

## Sarvārtha­garbha
*don thams cad kyi snying po*, Skt. *sarvārtha­garbha*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvārthaṃkara
*don thams cad mdzad*, Skt. *sarvārthaṃkara*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvārthanāman
*don thams cad*, Skt. *sarvārthanāman*, A bodhisattva present at the sūtra’s teaching.

## Sarvārthaśrī
*don thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarvārthaśrī*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvārthasiddha
*don thams cad grub pa*, Skt. *sarvārthasiddha*, Name the buddha Śākyamuni in the Lalitavistara ( The Play in Full , Toh 95); he is the fourth Buddha of the Fortunate Eon or Bhadrakalpa and the seventh of the seven buddhas of antiquity (Skt. saptatathāgata).

## Sarvārtha­siddha
*don thams cad grub pa*, Skt. *sarvārtha­siddha*, One of the buddhas who appear in Vimalakīrti’s house to teach the Tathāgata­guhyaka, according to the goddess.

## Sarvārthasiddhi
*don kun grub pas byas pa*, Skt. *sarvārthasiddhi*, An unknown figure who is said to be one of three brothers, along with Jayakara and Madhukara. The more common form of his name is Siddhikara.

## Sarvārtha­siddhi
*don thams cad grub pa*, Skt. *sarvārtha­siddhi*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvārya­śrāvaka­pratyeka­buddha­śrī
*’phags pa nyan thos dang rang sangs ryas thams cad kyi dpal*, Skt. *sarvārya­śrāvaka­pratyeka­buddha­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Sarvāvaraṇa
Skt. *sarvāvaraṇa*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvāvaraṇa­viṣkambhin
Skt. *sarvāvaraṇa­viṣkambhin*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Sarvāvaraṇa­vikiraṇa­jñāna­vikrāmin
*bsgribs pa thams cad rnam par ’thor ba’i ye shes kyis rnam par non pa*, Skt. *sarvāvaraṇa­vikiraṇa­jñāna­vikrāmin*, A bodhisattva from a buddha realm in the downward direction. Also called Sarvāvaraṇa­vikiraṇa­jñāna­vikrānta­rāja.

## Sarvāvaraṇa­vikiraṇa­jñāna­vikrānta­rāja
*sgrib pa thams cad rnam par ’thor ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *sarvāvaraṇa­vikiraṇa­jñāna­vikrānta­rāja*, A bodhisattva from a buddha realm in the downward direction. Also called Sarvāvaraṇa­vikiraṇa­jñāna­vikrāmin.

## Sash Wearer
A bodhisattva in this sūtra said to be one of the sons of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra who will go on to become the Buddha Maitreya.

## saṃskāra

Nirgrantha Jñātiputra is often believed to have been associated with the Jain traditions.

## Saumya
A creature whom the śakra Sunetra, who was the Buddha Śākyamuni in a previous life, spontaneously generated to heal the people of Kuru during a period of great pestilence. The Tibetan term is attested elsewhere as a translation for the Sanskrit terms sūrata and sauratya (Mahāvyutpatti), peśala (Bodhisattva­bhūmi), and some other terms, and is attested as a translation equivalent for the name Surata in the title of Surata’s Questions (Toh 71). However, in the Sanskrit of the parallel telling of this story found in the Bodhisatvapiṭaka (Toh 56), the name is attested as Saumya. This Sanskrit name is derived from Soma, both the plant and the moon, and can have the meanings of gentleness and mildness as well as auspiciousness.

*bzhin mdzes ma*, Skt. *saumyamukhī*, ‟Gentle-Faced One/She with the Beautiful Face,” one of the eight demonesses who inhabit the eight great charnel grounds.

## scope of a buddha
The term buddhaviṣaya refers to the perceptual range of the awakened state. A buddha is beyond ordinary, dualistic perception and recognizes the sameness of all phenomena as emptiness. Therefore the perceptual range of buddha is boundless, and defies any description, categorization, or quantification. The term buddhaviṣaya is often closely related to the alternative term buddhagocara (Tib. sangs rgays kyi spyod yul). The term may also be used to refer to buddhafields. The term has been translated elsewhere as the “domain of a buddha” and the “sphere of a buddha.”

## seal
*phyag rgya*, Skt. *mudrā*, A polysemous term that indicates a “seal” in both the literal and metaphoric sense. It can refer to an emblem or symbol, a ritual hand gesture, or a consort in sexual practices. When paired with the term dhāraṇī it conveys the idea that a dhāraṇī seals or stamps the nature that it embodies upon the reciter or the targeted phenomenon.

## seat of awakening
*byang chub kyi snying po*, Skt. *bodhimaṇda*, The place where Śakyamuni Buddha achieved awakening and where countless other buddhas are said to have achieved awakening, and will do so in the future. This is understood to be located under the bodhi tree in present-day Bodhgaya, India. In some texts, the term is used to refer to a seat of awakening in other buddha realms.

## seat of enlightenment
*byang chub kyi snying po*, Skt. *bodhimaṇḍa*, Haribhadra defines it as “a place used as a seat, where the maṇḍa, here ‘essence,’ of enlightenment is present.” See Lamotte, p. 198, n. 105. The main “seat of enlightenment” is the spot under the bo tree at Buddha Gaya, where the Buddha sat and attained unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. It is not to be confused with bodhimaṇḍala, “circle of enlightenment.”

## seated practice
*’dug pa*, Skt. *niṣadyā*, According to Kalyāṇamitra, this refers to the practice of yoga while seated, i.e. the cultivation of samādhi (Toh 4113, F.308.b).

## secluded meditation
*nang du yang dag par ’jog pa*, Skt. *pratisaṃlayana*, Appearing in the Mahā­vyutpatti as a type of dhyāna, this term is used in The Hundred Deeds to signify a period of secluded meditation retreat.

## seclusion
*nang du yang dag 'jog*, Skt. *pratisaṃlayana*, this term can mean both physical seclusion and a meditative state of withdrawal.

## second-week embryo
*sko*, Skt. *arbuda*, The Gaṇḍa­vyūha uses the same terminology as the Jain text Tandulaveyāliyua and differs from other sūtras. In the Nanda­garbhāvakranti­nirdeśa­sūtra , arbuda is translated as mer mer po.

## secret
Derived from a verb that means to hide, conceal, or keep secret, the term means a secret, a mystery, as well as a hiding place or secret location, such as a place where one finds buried treasure. In this way, the term also has the sense that what is kept secret or hidden is something precious and mysterious. It is closely connected with the term guhyaka, the guardians of hidden treasures.

## secured from the king the liberty of a prince
*rgyal po las gzhon nu'i yongs su spang ba thob*, a stylized way to say that a person or group may govern itself and is not subject to the “law of the land.” The Buddhist [saṅgha](#saṅgha) enjoyed such autonomy. The analogy [means](#means) the king granted sovereignty to the [saṅgha](#saṅgha), which was then allowed to govern itself and was not subject to the law of the land. The legal exemption members of the [saṅgha](#saṅgha) enjoyed made it an attractive [sanctuary](#sanctuary) for those on the run from their masters, debt collectors, and the law, who would join the [saṅgha](#saṅgha) for legal rather than spiritual reasons. “From ancient times the legal tradition recognized the right of properly constituted groups to formulate their own laws” (Olivelle, 1993, 209).

## self
*bdag*, Skt. *ātma*, It is crucial to understand what is meant by “self,” before one is able to realize the all-important “absence of self.” Before we can discover an absence, we have to know what we are looking for. In Mahāyāna, there is a self of persons and a self of things, both presumed habitually by living beings and hence informative of their perceptions. Were these “selves” to exist as they appear because of our presumption, they should exist as substantial, self-subsistent entities within things, or as the intrinsic realities of things, or as the intrinsic identities of things, all permanent, unrelated and unrelative, etc. The nondiscovery of such “selves” within changing, relative, interdependent persons and things is the realization of ultimate reality, or absence of self.

They are sometimes called collectively “the six sense fields,” meaning six pairs of two (this set of six is the fifth of the twelve links of dependent origination), or the “twelve sense fields.”

The Abhidharma categorizes it as one of the eleven virtuous mental factors (Tib. sems byung dge ba; Skt. kuśalacaitta), a subgroup of the mental states or factors associated with the mind (Skt. caitasika, caitta).

## sense source
*skye mched*, Skt. *āyatana*, These can be listed as twelve or as six sense sources (sometimes also called sense fields, bases of cognition, or simply āyatanas). In context of epistemology, it is one way of describing experience and the world in terms of twelve sense sources, which can be divided into inner and outer sense sources, namely, (1–2) eye and form, (3–4) ear and sound, (5–6) nose and odor, (7–8) tongue and taste, (9–10) body and touch, (11–12) mind and mental phenomena. These are subsumed under the eighteen elements, where to the twelve sense sources the six consciousnesses are added. In the context of the twelve links of dependent origination, only six sense sources are mentioned—they are the inner sense sources (similar to the six faculties) of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

## sense sources
*skye mched*, Skt. *āyatana*, The six “inner” senses (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind), and their respective six “outer” objects of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, touch, and mental objects, are sometimes called collectively the “six sense sources,” but are also sometimes taken as two separate groups, making twelve.

## sense-media
*skye mched*, Skt. *āyatana*, The twelve sense-media are eye-medium (cakṣurāyatana), form-medium (rūpa-), ear-medium (śrotra-), sound-medium (śabda-), nose-medium (ghrāna-), scent-medium (gandha-), tongue-medium (jihvā-), taste-medium (rasa-), body-medium (kāya-), texture-medium (spraṣṭavya), mental-medium (mana-), and phenomena-medium (dharmāyatana). In some passages they are enumerated as six, the object-faculty pair being taken as one, and it is this set of six that is the fifth member of the twelve links of dependent origination. The word āyatana is usually translated as “base,” but the Skt., Tib., and Ch. all indicate “something through which the senses function” rather than a basis from which they function; hence “medium” is suggested.
