*pi wang*, Skt. *vīṇa*, Presently this refers to the “Indian lute,” made with two gourds, and has been translated into Tibetan as the piwang, the traditional Tibetan stringed instrument. The term has been used as a general term for many stringed instruments in India in the past.

## Vṛṣa
*kyu mchog*, Skt. *vṛṣa*, One of the kings of Nepal, possibly Vṛṣadeva of the seventh century.

## Vaḍa
*dga’ ba*, Skt. *vaḍa*, A name of a Jambudvīpa in an earlier eon.

## vaḍabāgni
*rgod ma’i me*, Skt. *vaḍabāgni*, “Mare’s fire,” a subterranean mythical fire.

## Vaḍabāmukha
*rgya mtsho’i glong*, Skt. *vaḍabāmukha*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vaśakarī
*dbang du byed ma*, Skt. *vaśakarī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Vaḍavā
*ba da biM*, Skt. *vaḍavā*, “Mare Faced,” a yoginī in Paramāśva’s maṇḍala.

## Vaśavartiguṇa
*dbang sgyur yon tan*, Skt. **vaśavartiguṇa*, Name of a tathāgata.

## Vaśavartin
*dbang sgyur*, Skt. *vaśavartin*, “Mastery.” The highest paradise in the desire realm, so named because the inhabitants have power over the emanations of others. Also called Para­nirmita­vaśa­vartin.

## Vaśa­vartin
*dbang byed*, Skt. *vaśa­vartin*, The chief god of the Heaven of Making Use of Others’ Emanations.

## Vaśavartirāja
*dbang sgyur rgyal po*, Skt. *vaśavartirāja*, The 784th buddha in the first list, 783rd in the second list, and 773rd in the third list.

## Vaśa­vartiyajñayaśayaṣṭi­mati
*dbang sgyur mchod sbyin grags pa’i mchod sdong blo*, Skt. *vaśa­vartiyajñayaśayaṣṭi­mati*, The hundred-and-sixth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past.

## Vaḍavāmukhā
*ba Da ba mu kha*, Skt. *vaḍavāmukhā*, “Mare-faced,” a yoginī; also found in the Śaiva Kaula tradition.

## Vaḍavāmukha
*rta rgod ma’i gdong*, Skt. *vaḍavāmukha*, A great submarine fire in the far south-east of the ocean, which is the fire that will ultimately burn up the world. Also regarded as the entrance to the hells.

## Vaṭavāsinī
*shing la mu la gnas ma*, Skt. *vaṭavāsinī*, One of the great yakṣiṇīs.

## Vṛṣabha
*khyu mchog*, Skt. *vṛṣabha*, The 468th buddha in the first list, 467th in the second list, and 461st in the third list.

## Vṛṣabhadatta
A son of a merchant in the city of Puṇḍravardhana, he marries Anāthapiṇḍada’s daughter Sumāgadhā in The Exemplary Tale of Sumāgadhā.

## Śvabhrapāda
Skt. *śvabhrapāda*, No information about this person could be found. He may be the protagonist of a (lost) avadāna? Alternate spelling: Śvabhrapada, Śvaprapada.

## Vaśībhūtā
*dbang du gyur pa*, Skt. *vaśībhūtā*, Name of a world system in the northwestern direction, where the buddha Ekacchatra teaches the perfection of wisdom to bodhisattva great beings.

## Vaśībhūta
*dbang du gyur pa*, Skt. *vaśībhūta*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## vacā
*shu dag*, Skt. *vacā*, Acorus calamus; sweet flag.

## Vacanaśrī
*nor gyi dpal*, Skt. *vacanaśrī*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vaccaḍa
*bab+ba Da*, Skt. *vaccaḍa*, A yakṣa general.

## Vaccaḍādhāna
*bab+ba da bskyed*, Skt. *vaccaḍādhāna*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Vadaha
The name of a city.

## Vadhūyakṣiṇī
*mna’ ma gnod sbyin mo*, Skt. *vadhūyakṣiṇī*, One of the seven yakṣiṇīs.

## Vadālī
*ba dA lI*, Skt. *vadālī*, An epithet of Mārīcī.

## Vadāli
*ba dA li*, Skt. *vadāli*, A goddess.

## vaṅga
*va dhU*, Skt. *vaṅga*, Can be a name of several plants and substances.

## Vahā
Skt. *vahā*, The name of a nakṣatra.

## Vahna
The name of a king.

## Vahura
The name of a mountain that is the home of numerous rākṣasas.

## Vaḍi
*ba Di*, Skt. *vaḍi*, A yakṣa who is a “Dharma brother” of Vaiśravaṇa.

## Vaiśakha
*dpyid zla ’bring po*, Skt. *dpyid zla ’bring po*, The month of Vaiśakha.

## Vaiśalī
*yangs pa can*, Skt. *vaiśalī*, The ancient capital of the Licchavi republican state, the Buddha visited this city several times during his lifetime. It is perhaps most famous as the location where, on different occasions, the Buddha cured a plague, admitted the first nuns into the Buddhist order, was offered a bowl of honey by monkeys, and announced his parinirvāṇa three months prior to his departure.

## Vaiśampāyana
*be’i sham bA ya*, Skt. *vaiśampāyana*, Ancient rishi, a pupil of Vyāsa and teacher of the Taittirīyasaṃhita.

## Vaiṣṇavī
*khyab ’jug ma*, Skt. *vaiṣṇavī*, One of the great mātṛs.

## Vaiṣṇava
Another name for the lunar asterism Śravaṇā. The Sanskrit vaiṣṇava is the adjectival form of viṣṇu, the name of one of the main gods in the brahmanical pantheon.

## Vaibhiḍiṅgī
*bai bhi Ting gi*, Skt. *vaibhiḍiṅgī*, A town.

## Vaibhāṣika
An early Buddhist philosophical school that was part of the Sarvāstivāda Vinaya lineage, they held the Abhidharma teachings to be definitive.

## Vaidehī
*lus ’phags ma*, Skt. *vaidehī*, The queen of King Bimbisāra of Magadha and the mother of his successor, King Ajātaśatru.

## Vaideha
*lus ’phags*, Skt. *vaideha*, A family in Magadha.

## Vaidehaka Mountain
*lus ’phags ri*, Skt. *vaidehakaparvat*, A mountain in Videha.

## Vaidika
*rig byed smra ba*, Skt. *vaidika*, The preachers of the Vedas.

## Vaidya
*sman pa*, Skt. *vaidya*, The 33rd buddha in the first list, 33rd in the second list, and 34th in the third list.

## Vaidyarāja
*sman pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vaidyarāja*, The 239th buddha in the first list, 238th in the second list, and 238th in the third list.

## Vaidyādhipa
*sman bdag*, Skt. *vaidyādhipa*, The 915th buddha in the first list, 914th in the second list, and 905th in the third list.

## Vaidyottama
*sman pa’i dam pa*, Skt. *vaidyottama*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vaiśeṣika
*bye brag pa*, Skt. *vaiśeṣika*, “Particularists,” a non-Buddhist philosophical school.

## Vaśiṣṭha
*gnas ’jog*, Skt. *vaśiṣṭha*, One of the seven great rishis of ancient India, said to have composed part of the Rigveda.

## Vaijayanta
Skt. *vaijayanta*, The name of Śakra’s crest insignia. The Tibetan term literally means “Brings Victory.”

## Vaijayanta Palace
*rnam rgyal khang*, Skt. *vaijayanta*, The palace of Śakra, an epithet for the god Indra, in the Heaven of the Thirty-Three.

## Vaiśākhā
*sa ga*, Skt. *vaiśākhā*, During the Buddha’s time, a certain lay vow holder in Śrāvastī. Elsewhere there is also the Viśākha who was the son of King Prasenajit’s minister.

## Vaiśākha
*sa ga zla ba*, the fourth month of the Tibetan lunar calendar. It is on the fifteenth of that month that the [Buddha](#buddha) was born, attained [enlightenment](#enlightenment) and passed into [nirvāṇa](#nirvāṇa).

## Vaiśākha Mind
*sa ga’i sems*, Skt. *sa ga’i sems*, Father of the buddha Samantadarśin.

## Vaikhānasa
One of the sublineages connected with the Gautama lineage of the brahmanical tradition.

## Vaiśālī
*yangs pa can*, Skt. *vaiśālī*, The ancient capital of the Licchavi republican state, the Buddha visited this city several times during his lifetime. It is perhaps most famous as the location where, on different occasions, Buddha cured a plague, admitted the first nuns into the Buddhist order, was offered a bowl of honey by monkeys, and announced his parinirvāṇa three months prior to his departure.

## Vainateya
*nam mkha’ lding*, Skt. *vainateya*, An epithet for the mythical, bird-like creature garuḍa.

## vaipulya
*shin tu rgyas pa*, Skt. *vaipulya*, One of the twelve branches of scripture. Literally meaning “vast” or “extensive,” it refers to a particular set of lengthy sūtras or collections of sūtras that each provide a comprehensive overview of Buddhist thought and practice. This category includes individual works such as the Lalitavistara and Saddharma­puṇḍarīka and collections such as the Mahā­sannipāta, Buddhāvataṃsaka, Ratnakūta, and Prajñāpāramitā.

## vaipulya sūtras of the Heap of Jewels
*shin tu rgyas pa’i sde kon mchog brtsegs pa’i mdo*, Skt. *ratna­kūṭa­vaipulya­sūtra*, This could refer to the Ratnakūṭa collection of sūtras as it is known in the Kangyur and Chinese canons; however, as the collection is not known to have existed, as such, in earlier times, this could also be either a general term covering Mahāyāna sūtras as a category, or a synonym for the Kāśyapa­parivarta.

## Vairā
*dgra can*, Skt. *vairā*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Vaira
*dpa’ bo*, Skt. *vaira*, A mariner who is the kalyāṇamitra of chapter 25.

## Vairāṭa
*dpa’ bo*, Skt. *vairāṭa*, A king contemporary with the Buddha.

## Vairaṭṭasiṃha
*smra ’dod kyi seng ge*, Skt. *vairaṭṭasiṃha*, A brahmin.

## Vaiśāradya­samavasaraṇa
*’jigs med yang dag gzhol*, Skt. *vaiśāradya­samavasaraṇa*, A bodhisattva present at the teaching of The White Lotus of Compassion Sūtra. The Buddha addresses him in particular at one point.

## Vaiśāradya­samuddhāraṇi
*’jigs med yang dag ’dren*, Skt. *vaiśāradya­samuddhāraṇi*, A bodhisattva who asks Śākyamuni for the title of The White Lotus of Compassion Sūtra. He appears nowhere else in the Kangyur.

## Vaiśāradya­vajra­nārāyaṇa­siṃha
*mi bsnyengs pa’i rdo rje seng ge mthu bo che*, Skt. *vaiśāradya­vajra­nārāyaṇa­siṃha*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Vairāṭaka
*dgras dogs pa*, Skt. *vairāṭaka*, A yakṣa general.

## Vaiśramaṇa
A past buddha whose name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Vairambha
*rtsom chen*, Skt. *vairambha*, One of the four winds.

## Vairambhaka
*rnam par ’thor rlung*, Skt. *vairambhaka*, A wind deity referred to as king of the wind.

## Vairambhya
*yul dgra mtha’*, Skt. *vairambhya*, A country.

## Vairaprabha
*khon sbyong ’od*, Skt. *vairaprabha*, The name of an eastern buddha realm.

## Vaiśravaṇa
*rnam thos sras*, one of the [Four Great Kings](#four-great-kings) (whose god [realm](#realm) is the first in the World of Desire), guardian of the North and god of wealth.

## Vairāmaka
*mtha’ ma*, Skt. *vairāmaka*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## vairocanā
*bai ro tsa na*, Skt. *vairocanā*, A substance used in tantric rituals. In at least one instance from The Emergence of Sampuṭa this refers to feces.

## Vairocana
*rnam par snang mdzad*, the [Buddha](#buddha) of the [Buddha](#buddha) family. See [five families](#five-families).

## Vairocanadharma
*chos rnam par snang mdzad*, Skt. *vairocana­dharma*, The name that the bodhisattva Prahasitabāhu will have when he becomes a buddha.

## Vairocana­dhvaja
*rnam par snang ba’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *vairocana­dhvaja*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Vairocana­dhvaja­pradīpa­śrī
*rnam snang rgyal mtshan sgron ma’i dpal*, Skt. *vairocana­dhvaja­pradīpa­śrī*, A realm in the distant past. This is the name given in verse, while the prose has Vairocana­tejaḥśrī. BHS has Vairocana­tejaḥ­śirī .

## Vairocanagarbha
*rnam par snang byed kyi snying po*, Skt. *vairocana­garbha*, A bodhisattva.

## Vairocana­garbha
*rnam par snang ba’i snying po*, Skt. *vairocana­garbha*, The name of a bodhisattva in the presence of the Buddha at Śrāvastī, and also the name of a bodhisattva seen by Muktaka in the buddha realm of the Buddha Tāreśvararāja in the east.

## Vairocana­garbha­mahā­megha
*rnam par snang mdzad snying po can gyi sprin chen po*, Skt. *vairocana­garbha­mahā­megha*, A tathāgata.

## Vairocanaketu
*rnam par snang mdzad dpal*, Skt. *vairocanaketu*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## vairocanakośa
*rnam par snang ba’i mdzod*, Skt. *vairocanakośa*, A magical tree. The name means “radiant treasure.”

## Vairocanakusuma
*rnam par snang mdzad me tog*, Skt. *vairocana­kusuma*, The buddha that Saṃbhava, the second of Samudrareṇu’s eighty sons, is prophesied to become.

## Vairocanamati
*rnam par snang byed blo gros*, Skt. *vairocanamati*, A bodhisattva present at the teaching of The White Lotus of Compassion Sūtra.

## Vairocana­prabha­śrī
*rnam par snang mdzad ’od dpal*, Skt. *vairocana­prabha­śrī*, The sixty-eighth buddha in the distant past. BHS verse: Vairocana­prabha­śirī .

## Vairocana­prabha­vyūha
*rnam par snang mdzad ’od kyi rgyan*, Skt. *vairocana­prabha­vyūha*, A buddha in the distant past. BHS verse: Vairocana­prabha­viyūha .

## Vairocana­praṇidhi­jñāna­ketu
*rnam par snang ba’i smon lam ye shes dpal*, Skt. *vairocana­praṇidhi­jñāna­ketu*, A bodhisattva from a northwestern buddha realm. Also known as Vairocana­praṇidhāna­ketu­dhvaja.

## Vairocana­praṇidhāna­ketu­dhvaja
*rnam par snang mdzad kyi smon lam dpal gyi rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *vairocana­praṇidhāna­ketu­dhvaja*, A bodhisattva from a northwestern realm. Also known as Vairocana­praṇidhi­jñāna­ketu.

## Vairocana­praṇidhāna­nābhi­raśmi­prabha
*rnam par snang ba’i smon lam gyi gtsug gi ’od zer snang ba*, Skt. *vairocana­praṇidhāna­nābhi­raśmi­prabha*, A bodhisattva from an eastern realm.

## Vairocana­śrī
*rnam par snang ba’i dpal*, Skt. *vairocana­śrī*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Vairocana­rakṣita
*bai ro tsa na rak+Shi ta*, Skt. *vairocana­rakṣita*, Eighth-century Tibetan master and translator, usually referred to simply as Vairocana or Bairotsana.

## Vairocana­raśmi­prati­maṇḍitā
*rnam par snang ba’i ’od zer gyis brgyan pa*, Skt. *vairocana­raśmi­prati­maṇḍitā*, A buddha realm a great distance in the eastern direction.

## Vairocana­raśmi­prati­maṇḍita­dhvaja­rāja
*rnam par snang ba’i ’od zer gyis brgyan pa’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *vairocana­raśmi­prati­maṇḍita­dhvaja­rāja*, A bodhisattva present at the sūtra’s teaching, who in the distant past had been Queen Vimaladatta. He is known only from this sūtra.

## Vairocana­ratna­padma­garbha­śrī­cūḍa
*rnam par snang ba rin chen pad mo dpal gyi gtsug phud snying po*, Skt. *vairocana­ratna­padma­garbha­śrī­cūḍa*, A cakravartin king in the distant past.

## Vairocana­śrī­garbha
*rnam par snang mdzad dpal gyi snying po*, Skt. *vairocana­śrī­garbha*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vairocana­śrī­garbha­rāja
*rnam par snang mdzad dpal gyi snying po’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vairocana­śrī­garbha­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vairocana­śrī­praṇidhi­garbhā
*rnam par snang mdzad kyi snying po*, Skt. *vairocana­śrī­praṇidhi­garbhā*, A buddha realm in the northwestern direction. See .

## Vairocana­śrī­sumeru
*rnam par snang mdzad dpal gyi ri rab*, Skt. **vairocana­śrī­sumeru*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa. Not present in available Sanskrit editions.

## Vairocana­śrī­tejorāja
*rnam par snang mdzad dpal gyi gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *vairocana­śrī­tejorāja*, A buddha in an eastern realm.

## Vairocana­tejaḥśrī
*rnam par snang mdzad gzi brjid dpal*, Skt. *vairocana­tejaḥśrī*, A realm in the distant past. In verse it is called Vairocana­dhvaja­pradīpa­śrī. Also called Vairocana­śrī in Sanskrit and rnam par snang ba (Vairocana) in Tibetan.

## Vairocana­vyūhālaṃkāra­garbha
*rnam par snang mdzad kyi rgyan gyis brgyan pa’i snying po*, Skt. *vairocana­vyūhālaṃkāra­garbha*, A kūṭāgāra in South India in which Maitreya resides.

## Vairocanottara­jñānin
*rnam par snang ba dam pa’i ye shes*, Skt. *vairocanottara­jñānin*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Vairotṣana
*bai ro tsa na*, Tibet's greatest translator and one of the first seven monks to be ordained in Tibet. He was one of the principal [disciple](#disciple)s of [Padmasambhava](#padmasambhava-of-oḍḍiyāna) and of [Śrī Siṃha](#śrī-siṃha).

## Vaiḍūrya Golden Mountain Precious Flower Glorious Appearance’s Ocean of Qualities
*bai DUr+ya dang gser gyi ri bo rin po che’i me tog snang ba dpal gyi yon tan rgya mtsho*, Skt. *vaiḍūrya­kanaka­giri­ratna­kusuma­prabha­śrī­guṇa­sāgara*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vaiḍūryagarbha
*bai dUr+ya snying*, Skt. *vaiḍūryagarbha*, The 699th buddha in the first list, 698th in the second list, and 688th in the third list.

## Vaiḍūrya­nirbhāsa
*bai DUr+ya ra snang ba*, Skt. *vaiḍūrya­nirbhāsa*, The buddhafield of the Thus-Gone Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha­rāja.

## Vaiḍūryaprabha
*bai dUr+ya’i ’od*, Skt. *vaiḍūryaprabha*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vaitaraṇī
*rab med*, Skt. *vaitaraṇī*, A river in hell.

## Vaitaraṇī River
A river said to separate the living from the dead. In Tibetan rab med means “without a ford,” i.e., uncrossable on foot. The river causes great suffering to anyone who attempts to cross it.

## Vaitarāṇi River
*chu bo be’i ta ra ni chen po*, Skt. *vaitarāṇi*, A river said to separate the living from the dead, like the River Styx. It causes great suffering to anyone who attempts to cross it.

## Vaivasvatī
*nyi ma’i bu mo*, Skt. *vaivasvatī*, One of the great mātṛs.

## Vaivasvata
*nyi ma’i bu*, Skt. *vaivasvata*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi; also a patronymic of Yama.

## Vaiśvānara­nirghoṣa
*thams cad sgrol ba’i dbyangs sgrol*, Skt. *vaiśvānara­nirghoṣa*, Name of a tathāgata.

## Vaiśvānaratejas
*gzi brjid me ’dra*, Skt. *vaiśvānaratejas*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## vaiśya
A member of the caste of “commoners,” those involved in agriculture and trade, the third category in the caste system as conceived by the brahmanical tradition.

## Vaiśyāyanīya
The name of a family lineage.

## Vajrā
*rdo rje*, Skt. *vajrā*, The name of a female Buddhist deity, here used as an epithet of Sitātapatrā.

## Vajra
*rdo rje*, AT: diamond, [adamantine](#adamantine) thunderbolt. Symbol of unchanging and indestructible [wisdom](#wisdom) capable of penetrating through everything. Ritual instrument symbolizing compassion, [skilful means](#skilful-means), [awareness](#awareness). Always associated with the [bell](#bell), *dril bu*, Skt. *ghaṇṭā*, the symbol of [wisdom](#wisdom), [emptiness](#emptiness). For the vajra's form see illustration of [Vajrasattva](#vajrasattva) who holds the vajra in his right hand and the [bell](#bell) in his left.

## Vajraśāṭī
Skt. *vajraśāṭī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## vajra and bell
*rdo rje dril bu*, Skt. *vajraghaṇṭā*, In the Tantra of Back Yamāri, the third in a series of four initiations.

## vajra banner
*rdo rje’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *rdo rje’i rgyal mtshan*, An absorption.

## vajra bell
*rdo rje dril bu*, Skt. *vajraghaṇṭā*, Bell with a handle in the shape of a vajra scepter.

## vajra body
*rdo rje’i lus*, Skt. *vajra­kāya­śarīra*, The body of the Buddha is like an indestructible vajra. While the term vajrakāya has specialized meaning in a tantric context, it is unlikely that such meaning is applicable here. In the Chinese, the term is translated as a “vajra-like, indestructible solid body” (jin gang bu huai jian gu zhi shen 金剛不壞堅固之身).

## Vajra Bow
*rdo rje gzhu*, The name of a bodhisattva.

## Vajra brothers and sisters
*rdo rje spun*, students of the same teacher, or with whom one has received [Vajrayāna](#vajrayāna) teachings. See [spiritual companions](#spiritual-companions).

## vajra clan
*rdo rje’i rigs*, Skt. *vajrakula*, One of the three, four, or five clans into which esoteric Buddhist deities are organized. In Kriyātantra literature, the head of this clan is Vajrapāṇi.

## vajra dwelling
A location for performing rites.

## vajra enclosure
A protective net of impenetrable, interlinking vajras that surrounds the outside of a maṇḍala in all directions and acts as its protective boundary.

## Vajra Eyes
*rdo rje’i mig*, Skt. *rdo rje’i mig*, A bodhisattva.

## Vajra family
*rdo rje’i rigs*, Skt. *vajra­kula*, In this context‌, the term vajrakula denotes the retinue of the wrathful bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajra Force
*rdo rje sde*, Skt. *rdo rje sde*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Sūryagarbha.

## Vajra Garland
*rdo rje phreng ldan*, Skt. *rdo rje phreng ldan*, A Licchavi youth present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vajra Gift
*rdo rje byin*, Skt. *rdo rje byin*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Pradyota.

## Vajra Golden Eyes
The name of a king of the garuḍas.

## Vajra Guard
*rdo rje skyong*, A Licchavī youth. (Toh 555: rdo rje skyabs)

## vajra holder
*rdo rje ’dzin*, Skt. *vajradhara*, Here used as an epithet of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajra Intelligence
*rdo rje’i blo gros*, Skt. *rdo rje’i blo gros*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Asaṅga.

## Vajra Light
The fourth of the twelve buddha grounds.

## vajra like
*rdo rje lta bu*, Skt. *vajropama*, An absorption.

## vajra maṇḍala
*rdo rje’i dkyil ’khor*, Skt. *vajramaṇḍala*, The 24th meditative stability in chapters 6 and 8.

## Vajra master
*rdo rje slob spon*, Skt. *vajrācārya*, "the spiritual master who introduces one to a [maṇḍala](#maṇḍala) of the [Secret Mantrayāna](#secret-mantrayāna) and gives the liberating instructions." DICT.

## vajra milk
The identity of this substance is uncertain.

## Vajra Mode
*rdo rje’i ’gros*, Skt. *rdo rje’i ’gros*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Vegajaha.

## Vajra Monastery
*rdo rje’i gtsug lag khang*, Skt. *rdo rje’i gtsug lag khang*, The name of a monastery

## Vajra Mountain, Site of Four Great Oceans
*rgya mtsho chen po bzhi’i gnas rdo rje’i ri*, Skt. *rgya mtsho chen po bzhi’i gnas rdo rje’i ri*, Dwelling place of the bodhisattva Dharmodgata.

## vajra navel
*rdo rje lte ba*, Skt. *rdo rje lte ba*, An absorption.

## Vajra of Joy
*dgyes pa rdo rje*, a name of [Garab Dorje](#garab-dorje).

## Vajra of Laughter
*bzhad pa rdo rje*, another name of [Garab Dorje](#garab-dorje).

## Vajra Ornament
*rdo rje rgyan*, The name of a bodhisattva.

## Vajra posture
*rdo rje dkyil krung*, Skt. *vajrāsana*, meditation posture with the legs crossed and the feet resting on the thighs.

## Vajra Power
*mthu rtsal rdo rje*, Skt. *mthu rtsal rdo rje*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Amṛtaprabha.

## Vajra realm
*rdo rje’i gnas*, Skt. *vajrabhavana*, This seems to be the name of the realm/abode of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajra recitation
*rdo rje bzlas pa*, recitation of [mantra](#mantra)s in concert with inhalation, holding and exhalation.

## Vajra Seat
*rdo rje gdan*, Skt. *Vajrāsana*, the place in India (the present name is Bodh Gayā) where all the [Buddha](#buddha)s of this [kalpa](#kalpa) are to attain [enlightenment](#enlightenment).

## Vajra song
*rdo rje mgur*, song (*mgur*) expressing the inner experiences of a [yogī](#yogī-or-yoginī), his realization of the ultimate indestructible ([vajra](#vajra)) nature.

## Vajra Source
*rdo rje ’byung*, Skt. *rdo rje ’byung*, A buddha realm.

## Vajra Sow-Faced One
*rdo rje phag gdong ma*, An epithet for Arcikarī, Gaṇapati’s consort.

## vajra stages
Mahākāla’s Sovereign Tantra uses this term to refer to the system for performing the sixth consecration.

## Vajra Subduer
*rdo rje rnam par gnon*, Skt. *rdo rje rnam par gnon*, A great bodhisattva.

## vajra that conquers all māras
*bdud thams cad rnam par ’joms pa’i rdo rje*, Skt. *sarvamāranikṛntanavajra*, Name of a meditative absorption.

## vajra that terrifies death
*rdo rje nag po ’jigs pa*, The name of a meditative absorption.

## vajra throne
*rdo rje’i gdan*, Skt. *vajrāsana*, The seat upon which a full realization of a buddha is attained. This attainment is one of the twelve great deeds of a tathāgata.

## vajra water
*rdo rje chu*, Skt. *vajrodaka*, Urine; it is referred to as “vajra water” when used in rituals.

## Vajra Wish
*rdo rje bzhed*, Skt. *rdo rje bzhed*, A buddha.

## vajra words
*rdo rje’i tshig*, Skt. *vajrapada*, One of ten different kinds of verbal phrase or statement (Skt. pada) mentioned in this text.

## Vajra Yama’s Destroyer
*gshin rje’i gshed rdo rje*, Skt. *yamamathana­vajra*, An epithet of Yamāri.

## Vajra Yoginī
*rdo rje rnal 'byor ma*, a female [saṃbhogakāya](#saṃbhogakāya) for of [Buddha](#buddha).

## Vajraśaṅkalī
*rdo rje lcags sgrog*, Skt. *vajraśaṅkalī*, One of the goddesses associated with Amoghapāśa, probably the same as Vajraśṛṅkhalā (“Vajra Chain”).

## Vajraśaṃkara
*rdo rje bde byed*, Skt. *vajraśaṃkara*, The Buddhist counterpart of Śiva.

## Vajraśara
*rdo rje mda’*, Skt. *vajraśara*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## vajra-being
*rdo rje sems dpa’*, Skt. *vajrasattva*, This term is primarily used in the present text as an epithet of Yamāri, but is also used to identify the deity Vajrasattva who is one of the principal deities of the esoteric Buddhist pantheon,

## Vajrabhairava
A wrathful Buddhist tantric deity with the head of a buffalo. He is the main deity of the Vajrabhairava cycle of tantras (Toh 468–472) and is considered an emanation of Mañjuśrī.

## Vajrabhṛkuṭī
*rdo rje khro gnyer ma*, Skt. *vajrabhṛkuṭī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrabhṛkuṭikā
*rdo rje khro gnyer can*, Skt. *vajrabhṛkuṭikā*, One of the goddesses associated with Amoghapāśa.

## Vajrabhrū
*rdo rje’i sbyin ma*, Skt. *vajrabhrū*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi. The attested Tibetan appears to in error, and should read rdo rje’i smin ma.

## Vajrabhūtinī
The name of a goddess.

## Vajrabāhu
*rdo rje dpung pa*, Skt. *vajrabāhu*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrabimbā
*rdo rje gzugs brnyan*, Skt. *vajraviśvā*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## Vajrabodhi
671–741. Indian monk and Buddhist missionary who was instrumental in the introduction of tantric Buddhist traditions to China. He translated a number of tantric works into Chinese, most famously the Vajra­śekhara­sūtra (related to the Sarva­tathāgata­saṃgraha).

## Vajracūṣaṇī
*badz+ra tsU ShI NI*, Skt. *vajracūṣaṇī*, One of the goddesses in the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## Vajracaṇḍa
*rdo rje gtum po*, Skt. *vajracaṇḍa*, The name of a bodhisattva.

## Vajracarcikā
*rdo rje tsar rtsi kA*, Skt. *vajracarcikā*, A deity in the maṇḍala of Black Yamāri.

## Vajraccheda­prajñā­vabhāsaśrī
*rdo rjes gcod pa shes rab snang ba’i dpal*, Skt. *vajraccheda­prajñāvabhāsaśrī*, The bodhisattva name given to Anaṅgaṇa, the fourth son of King Araṇemin.

## Vajradaṇḍa
*rdo rje dbyug pa*, Skt. *vajradaṇḍa*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajradaṃṣṭra
*rdo rje mche ba*, Skt. *vajradaṃṣṭra*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajradhanuḥ
*rdo rje gzhu*, Skt. *vajradhanuḥ*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajradharā
*rdo rje ’dzin ma*, Skt. *vajradharā*, The name of a female Buddhist deity, meaning “Vajra Bearer,” here used as an epithet of Sitātapatrā.

## Vajradhara
*rdo rje 'chang*, lit. [vajra](#vajra) holder. In the [New Tradition](#new-tradition), he is the primordial [Buddha](#buddha), source of all the [tantras](#tantra). In the [Ancient Tradition](#ancient-tradition), Vajradhara represents the principle of the Teacher as enlightened holder of the [Vajrayāna](#vajrayāna) teachings.

## Vajradhara Künga Sangpo
Also known as Ngorchen Künga Sangpo (ngor chen kun dga’ bzang po, 1382–1456), he was an important Sakya master and founder of the Ngor tradition. He also commissioned the production of a Kangyur catalog in Mustang written in gold lettering.

## Vajradharasāgaragarjin
*rdo rje ’dzin pa rgya mtsho ’joms pa*, Skt. *vajradhara­sāgaragarjin*, The name of a buddha.

## vajradhātu
*rdo rje dbyings*, Skt. *vajradhātu*, Intrinsically pure reality experienced through non-dual cognition.

## Vajradhātvīśvarī
*rdo rje dbyings 'phugs ma*, one of the [consorts](#consort) of the [Buddha](#buddha)s of the [Five Families](#five-families).

## Vajra­dhātvīśvarī
*rdo rje dbyings kyi dbang phyug ma*, Skt. *vajra­dhātvīśvarī*, Consort of Caṇḍa­mahā­roṣaṇa.

## Vajradhvaja
*rdo rje’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *vajradhvaja*, The name of countless buddhas, each in a realm named Vajraśrī, from which countless bodhisattvas come at the conclusion of the sūtra.

## Vajradīptatejā
*badz+ra dIp+ta he dze*, Skt. *vajradīptatejā*, One of the goddesses from the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## vajradūtī
*rdo rje’i pho nya mo*, Skt. *vajradūtī*, A type of female “messenger” deity. In The Great Amulet, they are said to number sixty-four.

## Vajraśekhara
*rdo rje rtse mo*, Skt. *vajraśekhara*, A deity.

## Vajragarbha
Name of a tantric bodhisattva. He is the interlocutor of the Blessed One in many tantras of the Unexcelled yoga class, most prominently in the Hevajra Tantra. He is also the bodhisattva who teaches The Ten Bhūmis .

## Vajra­garbha
*rdo rje’i snying po*, Skt. *vajra­garbha*, The bodhisattva who gives all the teachings of The Ten Bhūmis while in the Para­nirmita­vaśa­vartin paradise in the presence of a silent emanation of the Buddha Śākyamuni who has just attained buddhahood in Jambudvīpa. A bodhisattva of that name appears in passing in a few other sūtras and is the name of the principal interlocutor for the Hevajra Tantra, and the commentary to that tantra is also attributed to him.

## Vajra­garbha­pramardin
*rdo rje’i snying pos rab tu ’joms pa*, Skt. *vajra­garbha­pramardin*, A tathāgata mentioned here as one of the thirty-five buddhas of confession.

## Vajragarvā
*rdo rje snyems ma*, Skt. *vajragarvā*, One of the four retinue goddesses of Mahāsukhavajra.

## Vajragaurī
*rdo rje gau rI ma*, Skt. *vajragaurī*, A deity in the maṇḍala of Black Yamāri.

## Vajraghaṇṭā
*rdo rje dril bu ma*, Skt. *vajraghaṇṭā*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## Vajragiri
*rdo rje ri bo*, Skt. *vajragiri*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vajragrīva
*rdo rje mgrin pa*, Skt. *vajragrīva*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajragātra
*rdo rje’i lus*, Skt. *vajragātra*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Vajra­guhyakādhipati
*rdo rje gsang bdag*, Skt. *vajra­guhyakādhipati*, One of the names of Kubera, the god of wealth, meaning “Lightning Lord of the Guhyakas,” or “treasure guardian.” In the tantra tradition, Guhyapati, “Lord of Secrets,” became a title of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrahasta
*rdo rje lag pa*, Skt. *vajrahasta*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajraśikha
*A vidyārāja*, Skt. *vajraśikha*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajraśikhara
*rdo rje rtse mo*, Skt. *vajraśikhara*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrajambukā
*badz+ra dza bu ke*, Skt. *vajrajambukā*, One of the goddesses in the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## Vajrajihvā
*rdo rje lce ma*, Skt. *vajrajihvā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajra­jñāna­parvata
*ye shes rdo rje’i ri bo*, Skt. *vajra­jñāna­parvata*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vajrajvālā
Skt. *vajrajvālā*, “Vajra Blaze,” a female deity invoked to kill spirits.

## Vajraka
The name of a muhūrta.

## Vajrakūṭa
*rdo rje brtsegs pa*, Skt. *vajrakūṭa*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Vajraḍāka
*rdo rje mkha’ ’gro*, Skt. *vajraḍāka*, A wrathful deity.

## Vajrakambojā
*badz+ra kaM po dze*, Skt. *vajrakambojā*, One of the goddesses in the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## Vajrakapāla
*thod pa can*, Skt. *vajrakapāla*, A wrathful emanation of Hevajra(?).

## Vajrakaumārī
*rdo rje gzhon nu ma*, Skt. *vajrakaumārī*, The name of a female deity and class of female deities. The name means “Youthful Vajra.”

## Vajrakavaca
*rdo rje go cha*, Skt. *vajrakavaca*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrakelīkilā
*badz+ra kI li kI la*, Skt. *vajrakelīkilā*, One of the four retinue goddesses of Mahāsukhavajra.

## Vajraketu
*rdo rje’i tog*, Skt. *vajraketu*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Vajraśṛṅkhalā
*rdo rje lu gu rgyud*, Skt. *vajraśṛṅkhalā*, The name of a Buddhist deity who is typically male but here given in the feminine as an epithet of Sitātapatrā. The name means “Vajra Shackles.”

## Vajraḍākinī
*rdo rje mkha’ ’gro ma*, Skt. *vajraḍākinī*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva; one of the five ḍākinīs visualized on the five prongs of the vajra scepter.

## Vajrakāminī
*rdo rje ’dod ldan ma*, Skt. *vajrakāminī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrakrauñca
Skt. *vajrakrauñca*, One of the mantra deities.

## Vajrakrodha
*rdo rje khro bo*, Skt. *vajrakrodha*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrakīrti
*rdo rje grags pa*, Skt. *vajrakīrti*, A buddha in an eastern buddha realm.

## Vajrakukṣi
*rdo rje’i mngal*, Skt. *vajrakukṣi*, A cave inhabited by the asuras.

## Vajrakumāra
*rdo rje gzhon nu*, Skt. *vajrakumāra*, “The Youthful Vajra.” It is unclear who the referent of this name is in this text, but given the title of the work, it could perhaps be understood as an epithet of Vajrapāṇi, albeit not a common one. Vajrakumāra is also, at least in later Tibetan literature, quite commonly an epithet of Vajrakīlaya.

## Vajraśālavatī
*gnas dang ldan ma*, Skt. *vajraśālavatī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajralekhā
*rdo rje yi ge ma*, Skt. *vajralekhā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## vajra-like
*rdo rje lta bu*, Skt. *vajropama*, Applied to a particular meditative absorption that destroys all fetters and leads to the fifth path, that of “no more learning,” in Sarvāstivāda and Mahāyāna systems.

## Vajralocanā
*rdo rje’i spyan ma*, Skt. *vajralocanā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## vajramaṇḍala
*rdo rje’i dkyil ’khor*, Skt. *vajramaṇḍala*, Lit. “vajra circle.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vajra­maṇi­vicitra
*rdo rje rin po ches rnam par brgyan pa*, Skt. *vajra­maṇi­vicitra*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vajramati
A bodhisattva in the audience of this sūtra.

## Vajra­mati
*rdo rje’i blo gros*, Skt. *vajra­mati*, A great bodhisattva.

## Vajramatin
*rdo rje blo gros*, Skt. *vajramatin*, A bodhisattva great being present in the audience of this sūtra.

## Vajramālā
*rdo rje phreng*, Skt. *vajramālā*, The name of a female Buddhist deity, meaning “Vajra Garland,” here used as an epithet of Sitātapatrā.

## Vajramuṣṭī
*rdo rje khu tshur ma*, Skt. *vajramuṣṭī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajramukha
*rdo rje’i sgo*, Skt. *vajramukha*, A pore on Avalokiteśvara’s body.

## Vajra­māṇyabhedyadṛḍha­tejas
*rdo rje’i rang bzhin mi phyed gzi brjid brtan*, Skt. *vajra­māṇyabhedyadṛḍha­tejas*, A realm in the distant past.

## Vajranābhi
*rdo rje’i gtsug*, Skt. *vajranābhi*, The names of two buddhas in the past: one not long before Dīpaṅkara and another in the far distant past. BHS verse: Vajiranābhi.

## Vajranemin
*rdo rje’i mu khyud*, Skt. *vajranemin*, One of the thousand sons of King Araṇemin.

## Vajranetra
*rdo rje spyan*, Skt. *vajranetra*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajranārāca
*rdo rje lcags mda’*, Skt. *vajranārāca*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajranārāyaṇa
*rdo rje sred med kyi bu*, Skt. *vajranārāyaṇa*, The Buddhist counterpart of Viṣṇu.

## Vajra­nārāyaṇa­ketu
*rdo rje mthu bo che’i dpal*, Skt. *vajra­nārāyaṇa­ketu*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vajrapāśī
*rdo rje zhags pa ma*, Skt. *vajrapāśī*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## vajrapada
*rdo rje’i tshig*, Skt. *vajrapada*, Statements regarding the ultimate nature of phenomena.

## Vajra­pada­vikrāmin
*rdo rje’i gom pas rnam par gnon pa*, Skt. *vajra­pada­vikrāmin*, A bodhisattva in a northern realm.

## Vajra­padmottara
*rdo rje pad mo’i bla*, Skt. *vajra­padmottara*, A buddha in an analogy given by the bodhisattva Vajra­garbha.

## Vajrapañjara
*rdo rje dra ba*, Skt. *vajrapañjara*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrapatāka
*rdo rje ba dan*, Skt. *vajrapatāka*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrapāda
One of the sublineages connected with the Gautama lineage of the brahmanical tradition.

## Vajrapāṇi
*phyag na rdo rje*, one of the [Eight Great Close Sons](#eight-great-close-sons).

## Vajrapiṅgala
*rdo rje ping ga la*, Skt. *vajrapiṅgala*, The name could suggest a Buddhist counterpart of the Śaiva deity Piṅgala, an attendant of Śiva.

## Vajraprabhā
Skt. *vajraprabhā*, The name of a female Buddhist deity, meaning “Shines like a Vajra,” here used as an epithet of Sitātapatrā.

## Vajraprabha
*rdo rje’i ’od*, Skt. *vajraprabha*, The fifty-fourth buddha in the distant past. See .

## Vajraprabhāsa
*rdo rje’i ’od*, Skt. *vajraprabhāsa*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the seventy-second) when he becomes a buddha.

## Vajrapradīpa
*rdo rje’i sgron ma*, Skt. *vajrapradīpa*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vajra­pramardana
*rdo rje rab tu ’dul ba*, Skt. *vajra­pramardana*, A buddha in a northern realm.

## Vajrapramardin
*rdo rje rab tu ’joms pa*, Skt. *vajrapramardin*, Vajrapramardin (Vajra Vanquisher) is a buddha who inhabits a buddhafield. This buddhafield is specifically said to be Kaṣāyadhvajā in Toh 44-37 and Toh 104. In Toh 104 he is named Vajrasārapramardin (Vajra Essence Vanquisher).

## Vajraprākara
*rdo rje’i ’byung gnas*, Skt. *vajraprākara*, A mountain.

## Vajraprākāra
*rdo rje ra ba*, Skt. *vajraprākāra*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrapātāla
*rdo rje sa ’og*, Skt. *vajrapātāla*, A deity whose practice is taught in The Tantra of Black Yamāri.

## Vajrapura
*rdo rje’i grong khyer*, Skt. *vajrapura*, A town in the Draviḍa region in South India.

## Vajraśrī
*rdo rje’i dpal*, Skt. *vajraśrī*, The name of countless realms in the ten directions, in each of which is a buddha named Vajradhvaja.

## vajraratna
*rdo rje rin po che*, Skt. *vajraratna*, Lit. “vajra jewel.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vajra­ratna­giri­tejas
*rdo rje rin po che’i ri’i gzi brjid*, Skt. *vajra­ratna­giri­tejas*, “The Magnificence of a Mountain of Precious Diamonds.” The precious elephant of a cakravartin in the past.

## Vajraśravaṇā
*rdo rje rna ba ma*, Skt. *vajraśravaṇā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrarāśi
*rdo rje phung po*, Skt. *vajrarāśi*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Vajrarāja
*rdo rje rgyal*, Skt. *vajrarāja*, A sambhogakāya buddha personifying the true nature of the aggregate of mental formations.

## Vajrarājendrī
*badz+ra ra dzen+d+ri*, Skt. *vajrarājendrī*, One of the goddesses in the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## Vajraroman
*rdo rje ba spu*, Skt. *vajraroman*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrasaṃhata
*rdo rje mkhregs*, Skt. *vajrasaṃhata*, The 749th buddha in the first list, 748th in the second list, and 738th in the third list.

## Vajrasaṅkalā
*rdo rje’i lu gu rgyud*, Skt. *vajrasaṅkalā*, A member of the audience in this sūtra.

## Vajrasarasvatī
*rdo rje dbyangs can ma*, Skt. *vajrasarasvatī*, A deity in the maṇḍala of Black Yamāri.

## Vajrasattvī
The Indian female master credited with translating this Dhāraṇī along with the Tibetan translator Gar Sherap Jungne.

## Vajrasattva
*rdo rje sems dpa'*, the [Buddha](#buddha) who embodies the [Hundred Families](#hundred-families). The practice of [Vajrasattva](#vajrasattva) and recitation of his [mantra](#mantra) are particularly effective for purifying [negative action](#negative-action)s. In the lineage of the [Great Perfection](#great-perfection) he is the  [saṃbhogakāya](#saṃbhogakāya) [Buddha](#buddha).

## Vajrasaumyā
*rdo rje zhi ba ma*, Skt. *vajrasaumyā*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## Vajrasūcī
*rdo rje khab ma*, Skt. *vajrasūcī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrasenā
*rdo rje sde ma*, Skt. *vajrasenā*, One of the goddesses from Vajrapāṇī’s retinue in the maṇḍala of Mañjuśrī.

## Vajrasena
Vajrapāṇi’s eldest son in this sūtra, whose name is attested as that of a bodhisattva in the Kāraṇḍavyūha.

## Vajra­sāgara­dhvaja­megha
*rdo rje ltar brtan pa’i rgyal mtshan rgya mtsho’i sprin*, Skt. *vajra­sāgara­dhvaja­megha*, One of countless buddhas in a past kalpa.

## Vajra­sāgara­garbhā
*rdo rje rgyal mtshan gyi snying po*, Skt. *vajra­sāgara­garbhā*, A buddha realm in the southern direction.

## Vajrasiṃha
*rdo rje seng ge*, Skt. *vajrasiṃha*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vajrasiṃhinī
*badz+re siM hi ni*, Skt. *vajrasiṃhinī*, One of the goddesses in the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## Vajrasphoṭā
*rdo rje lcags sgrog ma*, Skt. *vajrasphoṭā*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## Vajrasphoṭa
*A vidyārāja*, Skt. *vajrasphoṭa*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajra­sāra­pramardin
*rdo rje snying pos rab tu ’dul ba*, Skt. *vajra­sāra­pramardin*, Vajra­sārapramardin (Vajra Essence Vanquisher) is a buddha who inhabits the buddhafield Kaṣāyadhvajā.

## Vajrasūrya
*rdo rje nyi ma*, Skt. *vajrasūrya*, A sambhogakāya buddha personifying the true nature of the aggregate of sensation.

## Vajrasundarī
*rdo rje mdzes ma nyid*, Skt. *vajrasundarī*, One of the goddesses associated with Amoghapāśa.

## Vajratejoṣṇīṣa
*gzi brjid gtsug tor*, Skt. *vajratejoṣṇīṣa*, One of the mantra deities.

## Vajratārā
*rdo rje sgrol ma*, Skt. *vajratārā*, A form of Tārā, the Buddhist goddess of compassion, commonly depicted as golden yellow in color, with four faces and eight arms.

## Vajratuṇḍī
*rdo rje’i mchu can*, Skt. *vajratuṇḍī*, The name of a female Buddhist deity, meaning “Vajra Beaked,” here used as an epithet of Sitātapatrā.

## Vajratuṇḍa
*rdo rje mchu*, Skt. *vajratuṇḍa*, The name of a great yakṣa in Gaṇapati’s maṇḍala. Vajratuṇḍa, which literally means “vajra-beaked,” is more commonly an epithet for Garuḍa.

## Vajraśuddha
*rdo rje dag pa*, Skt. *vajraśuddha*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vajra-ulūkāsyā
*badz+ra u lU kA s+ye*, Skt. *vajra•ulūkāsyā*, One of the goddesses from the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## Vajravakṣas
*rdo rje mthon ka*, Skt. *vajravakṣas*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajravidāraṇa
*rdo rje rnam ’joms*, Skt. *vajravidāraṇa*, A form of Vajrapāṇi widely employed in esoteric rites.

## Vajravikrāmin
The name by which Vajrapāṇi will be known when he becomes a perfect buddha, as attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra. It is also the name of a bodhisattva in a list of bodhisattvas given at the beginning of this sūtra, though the Sanskrit for that section of the text is no longer extant.

## Vajravikurvita
*rdo rje rnam par ’phrul pa*, Skt. *vajravikurvita*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## vajravināyaka
*rdo rje rnam par ’dren pa*, Skt. *vajravināyaka*, This seems to be a class of enlightened beings.

## Vajravārāhī
*rdo rje phag mo*, Skt. *vajravārāhī*, A Buddhist goddess related to Vajrayoginī with the face of a sow.

## Vajravyāghrī
*badz+ra byA g+h+ra*, Skt. *vajravyāghrī*, One of the goddesses from the retinue of Jñānaḍākinī.

## Vajrāśaya­giri­śrī
*dgongs pa rdo rje ri bo dpal*, Skt. *vajrāśaya­giri­śrī*, The eighty-second buddha in a kalpa in the distant past. BHS verse: Vajrāśaya­giri­śirī.

## Vajrayakṣī
*rdo rje gnod sbyin ma*, Skt. *vajrayakṣī*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## Vajrayāna
*rdo rje theg pa*, see [Secret Mantrayāna](#secret-mantrayāna).

## vajrayoga
*rdo rje’i rnal ’byor*, Skt. *vajrayoga*, (1) The four vajrayogas are the vajrayogas of purity (Skt. viśuddha), dharma, mantra, and form (Skt. saṃsthāna). (2) In this text, Vajrayoga is also the name of one of the six self-arisen supramundane beings, see .

## Vajrayoginī
*rdo rje rnal ’byor ma*, Skt. *vajrayoginī*, A Buddhist goddess.

## Vajrayudha
*rdo rje mtshon*, Skt. *vajrayudha*, A yakṣa general.

## Vajrābha
*’od snang rdo rje*, Skt. *vajrābha*, A buddha.

## vajrācārya
*rdo rje slob dpon*, Skt. *vajrācārya*, A person who has mastered the mantras, maṇḍalas, and other elements of a particular deity and their ritual practices, usually through being consecrated by and receiving direct instructions from another master of that tradition.

## Vajriṇī
*badz+ri NI*, Skt. *vajriṇī*, She is visualized as part of the Perfection of Wisdom practice.

## vajrin
*rdo rje can*, Skt. *vajrin*, “Possessor of vajra”; an epithet of male sambhogakāya deities embodying the adamantine non-duality; a follower of the Vajrayāna; an epithet for anyone abiding in non-duality.

## Vajrāṅka
*rdo rje sa mtshon pa*, Skt. *vajrāṅka*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrākara
*rdo rje byed pa*, Skt. *vajrākara*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vajrāṃkuśī
*rdo rje lcags kyu ma*, Skt. *vajrāṃkuśī*, One of the goddesses in the maṇḍala of Vajrasattva.

## Vajrāṅkuśī
*rdo rje lcags kyu*, Skt. *vajrāṅkuśī*, One of the eight goddesses visualized on the petals of a lotus in a ritual associated with the vajra scepter.

## Vajrāṅkuśa
*rdo rje lcags kyu*, Skt. *vajrāṅkuśa*, An esoteric Buddhist deity who can be employed in rites of subjugation.

## Vajrāmṛta
*badz+ra mR ta*, Skt. *vajrāmṛta*, In the Vajrāmṛta Tantra he is an emanation of Ratnasambhava; in the Sampuṭodbhava Tantra this name seems to be an epithet of Vajrasattva.

## Vajrānaṅga
*rdo rje lus med*, Skt. *vajrānaṅga*, The Buddhist form of Kāmadeva, the Indian god of love.

## Vajrānala­pramohanī­dhāraṇī

## Vararuci
*mchog srid*, Skt. *vararuci*, The colophon to this praise attributes its composition to a certain brahmin named Vararuci. However, in Toh 671, from which the praise was extracted, Vararuci utters not this praise but rather the subsequent tribute that follows in Toh 671 at . In Toh 842, a brahmin Vararuci, who is most like the same person who appears in this text, acts as the first Buddhist teacher for Śrīdevī Mahākālī and Rematī after their encounter with the Buddha and their conversion to Buddhism. It is unclear whether this brahmin Vararuci is thought within the literature to be identical with the historical person Vararuci, a well-known author of several treatises on grammar and astrology.

## Varuṇa
*chu’i lha*, Skt. *varuṇa*, The name of the deity of water, whose weapon is a noose. In the Vedas, Varuṇa is an important deity and in particular the deity of the sky, but in later Indian tradition he is the deity of the water and the underworld. The Tibetan does not attempt to translate his name but instead has “god of water.” The Sanskrit name has ancient pre-Sanskrit origins, and, as he was originally the god of the sky, is related to the root vṛ, meaning “enveloping” or “covering.” He has the same ancient origins as the ancient Greek sky deity Uranus and the Zoroastrian supreme deity Mazda.

*rig byed klog pa*, Skt. *vedapāṭhaka*, Brahmins who memorize and chant the Vedas, the authoritative scriptures of the Brahmanical tradition.

The vows of conduct that are taken up while engaged in learning the Vedas.

## Vegabhuja
*shugs kyis spyod*, Skt. *vegabhuja*, The fourth of the five young brahmin attendants of the brahmin Samudrareṇu. The Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies that he will be the Buddha Priyaprasanna, the 1,003rd of the 1,005 buddhas in the Bhadraka eon.

*shugs ’chang*, Skt. *vegadharin*, A māra; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Vegadhāra
*shugs ’chang*, Skt. *vegadhāra*, A buddha.

## Vegadhārin
A bodhisattva who visits the Buddha while he is turning the wheel of Dharma at Deer Park after his awakening. The name attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Vegajaha

*shugs ’od zhi gnas dbyangs kyi rgyal*, Skt. *vega­prabha­śamatha­ghoṣa*, The ninety-sixth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past.

## vegetables

*theg pa*, Skt. *yāna*, the [means](#means) for traveling the [path](#path) to [enlightenment](#enlightenment).

## vehicle of conditions

*byang chub sems dpa’i theg pa*, Skt. *bodhi­sattva­yāna*, This is equivalent to the Great Vehicle.

*nan khugs*, Skt. *veṣṭhila*, A householder, the kalyāṇamitra of chapter 29.

*dkris pa po*, Skt. *veṣṭitaka*, A yakṣa general.

A term for an exceedingly high number.

## Velāma
*dus dpog*, Skt. *velāma*, (1) A brahmin living in the country of King Piṇḍavaṃśa. (2) A brahmin who is the Buddha in a past life.

Mucuna pruriens.

*thags zangs*, Skt. *vemacitra*, The king of the asuras. Also translated as bzang ris. Degé Toh 556, Peking, Narthang and Lhasa: thag bzangs. Degé Toh 557: thag bzangs.

## Vema­citra
*thags bzang ris*, Skt. *vema­citra*, A ruler of the demigods.

*thags bzang ris*, Skt. *vemacitri*, One of the kings of the asuras.

*thag zangs ris*, Skt. *vemacitrin*, A lord of the asuras; a member of the Buddha’s retinue.

## Vemānika
*nga rgyal bral*, Skt. *vemānika*, A yakṣa general.

## venerable
*tshe dang ldan pa*, Skt. *āyuṣmān*, A monk or mendicant of seniority. Āyuṣmān (tshe dang ldan pa) is a title of respect directed toward a monk or wandering mendicant who is venerable and in a position of seniority, but not a fully realized buddha. (In the Lalitavistara, ch. 26, Śākyamuni famously rejects this title as a suitable term of address for himself. See, e.g., Dudjom Rinpoche 1991: p. 423). Āyuṣmān may imply one who has held monastic ordination for a significant number of years, and who has some level of realization, but is still “mortal” and tied to cyclic existence, in contrast to the buddhas, who are “immortal.” Even today Thai monks colloquially address each other, using ayusma for someone senior and avuso (“friend”) for someone junior.

## venerable monk
*btsun pa*, Skt. *bhadanta*, A term of respect used for Buddhist monks, akin to the modern address, bhante.

## venerable one
More literally, one who is worthy of offerings (dakṣiṇā).

## Venerated by All
*kun gyis bkur*, Skt. *kun gyis bkur*, Son of the buddha Sumati.

## Venerated by Gods

*mang pos mchod*, Skt. *mang pos mchod*, Mother of the buddha Lokasundara.

*mche ba’i dug*, Skt. *mche ba’i dug*, A nāga who visits Saṅkāśa Mountain.

## Venus
*pa ba bsangs*, Skt. *śukra*, In Indian astrology, the presence of Venus in the night sky is one of the indicators of future rains because it is considered to cancel out the influence of heavenly bodies that obstruct rainfall.

## veranda
*bsil khang*, Skt. *harmya*, an acceptable form of shelter for a monk, as identified in the [Four Supports](#four-supports) [section](#section) of the ordination ritual. Here, a covered area or overhang formed by crossbeams extending from a house rather than a harmyam [mansion](#mansion) with several rooms and an open courtyard.

## veranda above a gatehouse

## verbally communicate
*ngag gi rnam par rig byed kyis*, Skt. *vāgvijñapti*, If monastics are unable to attend an official act of the saṅgha, they must send their consent for the act and convey their purity (Tib. yongs su dag pa; Skt. pariśuddhi) through a proxy or intermediary. Such consents and professions may be conveyed either verbally or physically.

*mtshal*, Skt. *hiṅgulaka*, A red pigment made from mercury sulfide.

*daN+Da ut+pal*, Skt. *daṇḍotpala*, Vernonia cinerea.

## verse

## verse narrations
*dbyangs kyis bsnyad pa’i sde*, Skt. *geya*, One of the “twelve branches of excellent speech.”

## verse text
One of the genres of Buddhist literature included in the list of nine or twelve classifications. Seemingly refers to verse texts without any prose.

## verses
*tshigs su bcad pa*, Skt. *gāthā*, As one of the twelve aspects of the wheel of Dharma, it means those teachings given in verse.

## Verses of the Ṛṣi
*gtsug lag khang gi tshigs su bcad pa*, Skt. *ārṣā gāthā*, A series of verses that were supposed to prevent dangers.

## verses section

## very limit of reality

More generally, this term has three meanings: (1) the ultimate nature, (2) the experience of the ultimate nature, and (3) the quiescent state of an arhat to be avoided by bodhisattvas.

## very solid

The name of a karmic wind involved in the formation of an embryo in its twentieth week.

## Veṇuvana
*’od ma’i tshal*, Skt. *veṇuvana*, The famous bamboo grove near Rājagṛha where the Buddha regularly stayed and gave teachings. It was situated on land donated by King Bimbisāra of Magadha and, as such, was the first of several landholdings donated to the Buddhist community during the time of the Buddha.

## Veṇuvana Kalandaka­nivāsa

It was situated on land donated by King Śreṇya Bimbisāra of Magadha and, as such, was the first of several landholdings donated to the Buddhist community during the time of the Buddha. Kalandaka­nivāpa means “feeding place of the kalandakas,” where kalandaka could refer to a flying squirrel or bird, as explained by differing sources.

*sA la sna tshogs kyi rgyal mtshan gyi rgyan*, Skt. *vicitra­sāra­dhvaja­vyūha*, A forest to the east of Dhanyākara. The Sanskrit vicitrasāra means “various essences.” The Tibetan appears to preserve a version that read vicitrasāla, which means “various sal trees.” See .

## victor
*rgyal ba*, Skt. *jina*, A common epithet of the buddhas, and also used among the Jains, whose name is derived from the term jina.

## Victorious

*sA la’i sgra rgyal*, Skt. *sA la’i sgra rgyal*, Mother of the buddha Ratnadhara.

*rgyal ba’i dbang po*, Skt. *rgyal ba’i dbang po*, Father of the buddha Janendrakalpa.

## Victors
Skt. *jina*, An epithet for the buddhas, signifying their victory over the māras.

## victor's prize
*rgol ba'i longs spyod*, Skt. *vādibhoga*, a prize awarded by a king to the winner of a debate. In the Vinayavastu, the prize was title to a village and its taxes.

## victor’s prize
*rgol ba’i longs spyod*, Skt. *vādibhoga*, A prize awarded by a king to the winner of a debate. In the Vinayavastu, the prize was title to a village and its taxes.

## Victory

## victory banner

*gser gyi me tog ’od zer rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *suvarṇa­puṣpa­raśmidhvaja*, A buddha.

*mdzes pa’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *mdzes pa’i rgyal mtshan*, A bodhisattva.

## Videha

*rnam grags blo gros*, Skt. *vidhuṣṭhamati*, A bodhisattva.

*rnam ’jig dbang phyug*, Skt. *vidhvasteśvara*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

*rig pa ’dzin pa rtse dga’ bas gnas pa*, Skt. *rig pa ’dzin pa rtse dga’ bas gnas pa*, A stream on Saṅkāśa.

*rnam par ’ju byed*, Skt. *vidrāvaṇa*, One of the kings of the rākṣasas.

*mkhas ma*, Skt. *vidu*, One of the eight goddesses dwelling in the Bodhi tree.

Skt. *vidurā*, A great rākṣasī.

## Vidvagañja­karuṇāśraya
*mkhas mdzod snying rje rten*, Skt. *vidvagañja­karuṇāśraya*, The bodhisattva name given to Viśvagupta, the third of the thousand young Veda-reciting brahmin pupils of Samudrareṇu.

## vidyā
*rig pa*, Skt. *vidyā*, A term that at once refers to a type of mantra or dhāraṇī and to the deity it invokes, thereby reflecting their inseparability. A vidyā is typically applied to female deities, and is often, but not exclusively, used for worldly goals in esoteric ritual. In worldly contexts a vidyā is similar to a “spell.”

## vidyā goddess
*rig pa’i lha mo*, Skt. *vidyādevī*, A class of goddesses who are identified with the vidyā spells that bear their names.

## vidyā holder
*rig pa ’dzin pa*, Skt. *vidyādhara*, The term literally means “possessor of vidyā” and refers to practitioners of mantra. When the term is used in the sense of “vidyādhara” (a class of semidivine beings), it has been rendered in its Sanskrit form.

## vidyā king
*rig pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vidyārāja*, See “vidyārāja.”

## vidyā mantra
A mantra or sacred utterance for producing vidyā, which means “knowledge” or “insight.” The term vidyā has a wide range of meaning, but in this context, it may refer to a magic spell made for the purpose of attaining either worldly or transcendent benefits.

## Vidyādharā
*rig ’dzin ma*, Skt. *vidyādharā*, A great rākṣasī.

## vidyādharī
*rig ’dzin ma*, Skt. *vidyādharī*, A female vidyādhara (a class of semidivine beings).

## Vidyādhara
*rig 'dzin*, knowledge holder. "One who through profound [means](#means) holds the deities, [mantra](#mantra)s, and the [wisdom](#wisdom) of great bliss." DICT. In the [Nyingmapa](#nyingmapa) Tradition there are four [levels](#levels) of vidyādhara:
1. Totally matured (*rnam smin*)
2. Mastering the duration of his life (*tshe dbang*)
3. [Mahāmudrā](#mahāmudrā) (*phyag chen*)
4. Spontaneously accomplished (*lhun grub*)

## Vidyādhara Basket
*rig pa’i ’dzin pa’i sde snod*, Skt. *vidyā­dharapaṭala*, A term for the collection of writings preserving the spells and rites performed by vidyā holders. There is no known collection of this sort that is currently extant, and it may simply refer to a category or genre of texts instead of a physical collection.

## vidyādharas
Meaning those who wield (dhara) spells (vidyā), the term can be used to refer to both a class of supernatural beings who wield magical power and human practitioners of the magical arts. The later Buddhist tradition, playing on the dual valences of vidyā as “spell” and “knowledge,” began to apply this term more broadly to realized figures in the Buddhist pantheon.

## Vidyādhara’s Basket
*rig ’dzin sde snod*, Skt. *vidyādhara­piṭaka*, A compendium of esoteric ritual manuals, now lost. There may never have been a single text with this title, or the title may refer to a mythical source text from which extant ritual manuals were transmitted.

## Vidyākaraprabha
*bi dyA ka ra pra bha*, Skt. *vidyākaraprabha*, according to Nyangral Nyimai Özer's history, Ralpachen invited the Indian [preceptor](#preceptor) Vidyākaraprabha to Tibet along with Jinamitra, Surendrabodhi, and Dānaśīla in the first part of the ninth century (Martin, 2002, n. 13). Vidyākaraprabha was the author of the Madhyamakanayasārasamāsaprakaraṇa, a work in the Yogācāra-Madhyamaka school pioneered by [Śāntarakṣita](#śāntarakṣita) (Ruegg, 1981, 99, n. 311), translated into Tibetan with [Paltsek](#paltsek) under the name dbu ma'i lugs kyi snying po mdor bsdus pa'i rab tu byed pa (Toh 3893, Degé Tengyur, vol. HA, folios 43b.5–50a.6). He worked with [Paltsek](#paltsek) on numerous other translations on topics as diverse as the Sphuṭārthā commentary to the Abhisamayālaṅkāra, an extract from Buddhaghoṣa's Vimuktimārga, and the early [tantra](#tantra) Vidyottamamahātantra (see Martin, 2006).

## Vidyākarasiṃha
*bid+yA ka ra sing ha*, Skt. *vidyākarasiṃha*, An Indian preceptor (Tib. mkhan po) active in Tibet in the early ninth century.

## Vidyākara­siṁha
*bidyA ka ra sing ha*, Skt. *vidyākara­siṁha*, Indian translator of The Good Eon.

## vidyā-mantra
*rig sngags*, Skt. *vidyāmantra*, A sacred utterance or spell made for the purpose of attaining worldly or transcendent benefits.

## vidyāmantra
*rig pa’i gsang sngags*, Skt. *vidyāmantra*, More often vidyā (literally “knowledge”) is used to mean “a mantra” and is synonymous with that term, but it is usually translated into Tibetan as rig pa’i gsang sngags, which could be back-translated as vidyāmantra) to make it clear that it is a mantra and not “knowledge.”

*gsal*, Skt. *vidyota*, A king based in Ujjain, contemporary of the Buddha.

*snang byed ma*, Skt. *vidyotanī*, A great rākṣasī.

## Vidyotana
*glog ’byin*, Skt. *vidyotana*, A nāga king.

## Vidyottama
*rig pa mchog*, Skt. *vidyottama*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Vidyottama Tantra
*rig pa’i mchog*, Skt. *vidyottama*, The full title of this text as preserved in the Tibetan canon is the Vidyottamamahā­tantra (Toh 746), which can be translated as The Great Tantra: The Supreme Vidyā. This lengthy tantra of the Kriyā class appears to be a compendium of diverse rites arranged as a single collection.

## vidyārājñī
*rig sngags kyi rgyal mo*, Skt. *vidyārājñī*, A female vidyārāja—a powerful female mantra deity of the vidyārāja class.

*rig pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vidyārāja*, This seems to be the name of some of the amogha emanations of Avalokiteśvara, although the distinction between Vidyārāja (proper name) and “king of vidyās” (literal translation) is often blurred.

*glog ’byin*, Skt. *vidyuddatta*, The 341st buddha in the first list, 340th in the second list, and 335th in the third list.

*glog thob*, Skt. *vidyutprāpta*, A bodhisattva.

## Viśeṣacintin
*khyad par sems*, Skt. *viśeṣacintin*, Literally “Distinctive Thinker.” A great bodhisattva who is the main interlocutor in this discourse. Also referred to as Brahmaviśeṣacintin and Mahābrahmaviśeṣacintin in The Questions of Brahmaviśeṣacintin (Brahmaviśeṣacintiparipṛcchā, Toh 160).

## View
*lta ba*, Skt. *dṛṣṭi*
1. point of view, belief
2. the authentic point of view, the real knowledge of the [natural state](#natural-state) of all phenomena.

## View and Mind
*lta sems*, Skt. *lta sems*, Attendant of the buddha Jitaśatru.

## View and Worship
*lta mchod*, Skt. *lta mchod*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Damajyeṣṭha.

## view of belief in a self
*’jig tshogs la lta ba*, Skt. *satkāyadṛṣti*, The Tibetan is literally “the view of the perishable accumulation,” and the Sanskrit is “the view that the body is real.” This refers to the mistaken view that the transitory aggregates are a self.

## View of Equality
*mnyam lta*, Skt. *mnyam lta*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## View of Infinite Renown
*rnam par lta ba grags pa dpag med*, Skt. *rnam par lta ba grags pa dpag med*, Son of the buddha Puṣpadatta.

## View of Qualities
*yon tan lta*, Skt. *yon tan lta*, Mother of the buddha Vaidyādhipa.

## View of Splendid Qualities
*yon tan gzi brjid lta ba*, Skt. *yon tan gzi brjid lta ba*, Birthplace of the buddha Amṛtaprabha.

## view of the perishable collection
*’jig tshogs la lta ba*, Skt. *satkāyadṛṣṭi*, The Sanskrit term means “the view that the body is real,” and the Tibetan term can be translated as “the view of the perishing collection.” It refers to viewing the “perishing” collection of momentary, transitory aggregates‍—the body‍—as a self.

## view of the transitory collection
The view that perceives the transitory collection of the five aggregates as the basis for the self or that which belongs to a self. The Tibetan literally means “the view of the destructible accumulation,” and the Sanskrit means “seeing (dṛṣṭi) the body (kāya) as real (sat),” (i.e., the view that holds the body to be truly existent). Some sources classify twenty types of satkāyadṛṣṭī by delineating for each of the five aggregates the false notion that (1) the self is the same as the aggregates, (2) the self is contained in the aggregates, (3) the self is different from the aggregates, or (4) the self possesses the aggregates.

*kun tu lta ba*, Skt. *kun tu lta ba*, Viewing (the act of looking at or observing), also the name of a realm of the vessel-bearer gods.

## viewing the essential nature of all phenomena
*chos thams cad kyi ngo bo nyid rnam par lta ba*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­svabhāva­vyavalokano*, The first of the fifty-one meditative stabilities manifested to Sadāprarudita in chapter 73.

*’jig rten lta*, Skt. *’jig rten lta*, Birthplace of the buddha Mahādarśana.
