## Vigata­bhaya­kīrti­rāja
*’jigs bral grags pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vigata­bhaya­kīrti­rāja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vigata­bhaya­paryutthāna­ghoṣa
*kun nas ldang ba’i ’jigs pa dang bral ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *vigata­bhaya­paryutthāna­ghoṣa*, A buddha in a realm in the downward direction who sends bodhisattvas to make offerings to the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

## Vigatabhayasaṃtāpa
*’jigs pa’i gdung bral*, Skt. *vigatabhaya­saṃtāpa*, The youngest of the Buddha Ratnagarbha’s eighty brothers, whom he prophesies will become the Buddha Vigata­raja­samudgatābhyudgata­rāja.

## Vigatakāṅkṣa
*the tshom spangs pa*, Skt. *vigatakāṅkṣa*, The 181st buddha in the first list, 180th in the second list, and 180th in the third list.

## Vigatakrodha
*khro med*, Skt. *vigatakrodha*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vigatamala
*dri ma bral*, Skt. *vigatamala*, The 194th buddha in the first list, 193rd in the second list, and 193rd in the third list.

## Vigata­mohārtha­cintin
*don dgongs gti mug bral*, Skt. *vigata­mohārtha­cintin*, The 726th buddha in the first list, 725th in the second list, and 715th in the third list.

## Vigataśoka
*mya ngan bral*, Skt. *vigataśoka*, Son of King Lion Glory, who, together with his brother Aśoka, became a monk and a bodhisattva of the thus-gone King of Bliss. Finally, he became the buddha known as Supreme Accumulations.

## vigatarajas
*rdul med pa*, Skt. *vigatarajas*, Lit. “dustless.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vigatarajaḥsañcayā
*rdul gyi tshogs dang bral ba*, Skt. *vigata­rajaḥsañcayā*, Name of a world system in the southwestern direction, where the buddha Sūrya­maṇḍala­prabhāsottama­śrī teaches the perfection of wisdom to bodhisattva great beings.

## Vigata­rajasaṃcayā
*rdul gyi tshogs dang bral ba*, Skt. *vigata­rajasaṃcayā*, Lit. “Free of Dust Collections.” A world system in the intermediate southwest direction, where the buddha Sūrya­maṇḍala­prabhāsottara­śrī now dwells.

## Vigata­rajaḥsañcayā
*rdul gyi tshogs dang bral ba*, Skt. *vigata­rajaḥsañcayā*, Name of a world system in the southwestern direction, where the buddha Sūrya­maṇḍala­prabhāsottama­śrī teaches the perfection of wisdom to bodhisattva great beings.

## Vigata­raja­samudgatābhyudgata­rāja
*rdul bral yang dag ’phags mngon ’phags*, Skt. *vigata­raja­samudgatābhyudgata­rāja*, The last of the eighty buddhas in the Baliṣṭha realm during the Utpalasanīraṇa eon, as prophesied for Vigatabhyasaṃtāpa, the youngest of the Buddha Ratnagarbha’s brothers.

## Vigataraśmi
*’od zer bral*, Skt. *vigataraśmi*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vigataraśmighoṣa
*’od zer bral ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *vigataraśmighoṣa*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vigata­saṃtāpodbhava­vaiśravaṇasāla­rāja
*gdung bral mngon par ’phags pa rnam thos kyi bu sA la’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vigata­saṃtāpodbhava­vaiśravaṇasāla­rāja*, A buddha in a northeastern realm who sends bodhisattvas to pay homage to Śākyamuni.

## Vigatatamā
The mother of the future buddha Kāruṇika.

## Vigatatamas
*mun dang bral ba*, Skt. *vigatatamas*, The 112th buddha in the first list, 112th in the second list, and 113th in the third list.

## Vigatatamondhakārā
*gti mug mun bral*, Skt. *vigatatamondhakārā*, A realm below the Buddha Ratnagarbha’s realm in which resides the Buddha Vigata­bhaya­paryutthāna­ghoṣa.

## Vigatāśoka
*mya ngan med pa*, Skt. *vigatāśoka*, “Free from Sorrow.” A bodhisattva from a world system called Sarva­śokāpagata, in the southern direction, who comes to pay homage and listen to the Buddha.

## vighna
*bgegs*, Skt. *vighna*, Similar to vināyakas, the term vighna refers to a broad class of nonhuman beings that create obstacles and problems for spiritual practitioners specifically, and all people in general.

## Vighnapati
*bgegs med pa’i bdag po*, Skt. *vighnapati*, “Lord of obstacles,” although the Tibetan translates it as “lord of no obstacles.” One of the names of the elephant-headed deity that is the son of Śiva and Pārvatī, also known as Ganesh (Ganeśa or Gaṇapati; tshogs kyi bdag po).

## Vighuṣṭaśabda
*sgra grags*, Skt. *vighuṣṭaśabda*, The 511th buddha in the first list, 511th in the second list, and 504th in the third list.

## Vighuṣṭakīrti
*snyan pa rnam par grags pa*, Skt. *vighuṣṭakīrti*, A head merchant in the distant past.

## Vighuṣṭarāja
*rnam grags rgyal po*, Skt. *vighuṣṭarāja*, The 539th buddha in the first list, 539th in the second list, and 532nd in the third list.

## Vighuṣṭatejas
*gzi brjid rnam grags*, Skt. *vighuṣṭatejas*, The 927th buddha in the first list, 926th in the second list, and 917th in the third list.

## vigilance
*bag yod*, Skt. *apramāda*, Heedful attention to virtuous qualities.

## vigilant
A major aspect of mindfulness as broadly construed. Remaining attentive to nurturing virtuous activities of body, speech, and mind, and rejecting negative activities of body, speech, and mind. More fundamentally it means retaining awareness of the true nature.

## vigilant introspection
*shes bzhin*, Skt. *saṃprajāna*, Also called “mental alertness,” the faculty of mind that maintains a conscious watch for any inclination of the mind toward mental dullness or agitation, especially during meditation (Rigzin 423). Closely related to mindfulness.

## Vigopaśikhara
*’khrugs med rtse mo*, Skt. *vigopaśikhara*, A bodhisattva sent by the Buddha Vigata­saṃtāpodbhava­vaiśravaṇasāla­rāja to pay homage to Śākyamuni.

## vigor
*brtson ’grus*, Skt. *vīrya*, Also translated here as “diligence.”

## Viguṇamoharāja
*ti mug rnam bral yon tan rgyal po*, Skt. *viguṇamoharāja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vihasita
*rnam par rgod pa*, Skt. *vihasita*, One of the grahas.

## Viheṭhanā
*rnam par ’tshe*, Skt. *viheṭhanā*, A great rākṣasī.

## vihāra
*gtsug lag khang*, Skt. *vihāra*, Either a temple or monastery. In Buddhism it was originally a residence used during the monsoon for the otherwise wandering bhikṣus.

## Vihvalā
*ser po*, Skt. *vihvalā*, A deity in Mañjuvajra’s maṇḍala.

## Viśiṣṭa
*rnam par grags pa*, Skt. *viśiṣṭa*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Viśiṣṭacandra
*zla ba rnam par ’phags pa*, Skt. *viśiṣṭacandra*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vi­śiṣṭa­cāritra
*spyod pa khyad par can*, Skt. *vi­śiṣṭa­cāritra*, One of the four principal bodhisattvas who emerged from the ground at the time of the teaching of the Lotus Sūtra.

## Viśiṣṭagandha
*dri mchog*, Skt. *viśiṣṭagandha*, A southern buddha realm.

## Viśiṣṭa­svarāṅga
*dbyangs kyi yan lag khyad par ’phags*, Skt. *viśiṣṭa­svarāṅga*, The 727th buddha in the first list, 726th in the second list, and 716th in the third list.

## Viṣāṇin
*ru rings*, Skt. *viṣāṇin*, The 119th buddha in the first list, 119th in the second list, and 120th in the third list.

## Vijayā
*rnam par rgyal ma*, Skt. *vijayā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi; one of the great yakṣiṇīs; also a mantra goddess representing the power (śakti) of all the buddhas.

## Vijaya
*rnam par rgyal ba*, Skt. *vijaya*, Son of King Jaya. Not to be confused with the future buddha Vijaya.

## Vijayaśīla
*bi dza ya shI la*, Skt. *vijayaśīla*, A translator of canonical texts.

## Vijayantī
*rnam par rgyal ma*, Skt. *vijayantī*, One of the eight goddesses in the east, called upon to grant protection.

## Vijayarakṣa
*rnam par rgyal ba srung*, Skt. *vijayarakṣa*, The name of a child who requests the Buddha to allow him to go forth.

## Vijayasenā
*sde las rnam par rgyal*, Skt. *vijayasenā*, One of the ten girls who attended upon Prince Siddhārtha while he was practicing austerities.

## Vijayasena
*rnam par rgyal ba’i sde*, Skt. *vijayasena*, Name of Ajātaśatru in the state of a pratyekabuddha as prophesied by the Buddha.

## Vijayavatī
*rnam rgyal ldan ma*, Skt. *vijayavatī*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Vijayavikrāmin
*rnam par rgyal bas rnam par gnon pa*, Skt. *vijayavikrāmin*, “Conquest Suppressor.” A bodhisattva from a world system called Samādhyalaṃkṛtā, in the intermediate northeast direction, who comes to pay homage and listen to the Buddha.

## Vijayin
*rgyal ba dang ldan pa*, Skt. *vijayin*, A buddha.

## Vijayoṣṇīṣa
*rnam par rgyal ba’i gtsug tor*, Skt. *vijayoṣṇīṣa*, One of the uṣṇīṣa kings attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Vijita
*rnam bcom*, Skt. *vijita*, The 698th buddha in the first list, 697th in the second list, and not listed in the third list.

## Vijitadhvaja
The capital city of King Vijitāyus in the distant past, during the time of the Buddha Mahāskandha.

## Vijitaghoṣa
*rgyal sgra dbyangs*, Skt. *vijitaghoṣa*, A name of the Sahā realm in an earlier eon.

## Vijitāvin
*rnam par rgyal chen*, Skt. *vijitāvin*, The 85th buddha in the first list, 85th in the second list, and 86th in the third list.

## Vijitāyus
A king in the distant past, during the time of the Buddha Mahāskandha.

## Vijṛmbhamānikā
*rnam par bsgyings ma*, Skt. *vijṛmbhamānikā*, The name of a female Buddhist deity that is difficult to translate but could approximately mean “Haughty”; here used as an epithet of Sitātapatrā.

## vijñāna
*rnam par shes pa*, Skt. *vijñāna*, Consciousness, the fifth of the five skandhas, generally classified into the five sensory consciousnesses and mental consciousness.

## Vijñānavāda
*rnam par shes pa smra ba*, Skt. *vijñānavāda*, The school of “Consciousness-Only” founded by Maitreya and Āryāsaṅga, which shares with the Mādhyamika most of the philosophical techniques of the Mahāyāna, while differing on the interpretation of the profound meaning of voidness, or the ultimate reality.

## vijñānāparyanta
*rnam par shes pa mu med pa*, Skt. *vijñānāparyanta*, Lit. “limitless consciousness.”Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Viṣkaṭā
*biSh+ka TA*, Skt. *viṣkaṭā*, A town in Videha.

## Vikaṭa
*ma rungs pa*, Skt. *vikaṭa*, A yakṣa general.

## Vikaṭaṅkaṭa
*mi bzad ’gro ldan*, Skt. *vikaṭaṅkaṭa*, A group of yakṣas.

## Vikaṭamukhī
*mi sdug gdong ma*, Skt. *vikaṭamukhī*, ‟One with Contorted Face,” one of the eight demonesses who inhabit the eight great charnel grounds.

## Vikala
*rdzogs byed*, Skt. *vikala*, One of the twelve great yakṣa generals who protect and serve those who bear, read, recite, copy, or commission a copy of the Bhaiṣajya­guru­vaiḍūrya­prabha­rāja­sūtra.

## Vikaṭānana
*gtsigs zhal ma*, Skt. *vikaṭānana*, A yakṣa appearing in some of the paintings of Amoghapāśa. See .

## viṣkandaka
*thod rgal*, Skt. *viṣkandaka*, Lit. “in leaps.” Name of a meditative stabilization. See also .

## Vikaraṇoṣṇīṣa
Skt. *vikaraṇoṣṇīṣa*, One of the mantra deities.

## Vikarāla
*rnam par g.yengs byed*, Skt. *vikarāla*, A king of piśācas.

## Vikasita
*kha bye ba*, Skt. *vikasita*, One of the rāśis.

## Vikasita­kamalotpala­gandha­ketu­rāja
*pad+ma rgyas pa dang ut+pa la’i dri’i tog gi rgyal po*, Skt. *vikasita­kamalotpala­gandha­ketu­rāja*, The name of a buddha.

## Vikasita­netrotpala­gandha­ketu­rāja
*spyan rgyas pa ut+pa la’i dri’i tog gi rgyal po*, Skt. *vikasita­netrotpala­gandha­ketu­rāja*, The name of a buddha.

## Vikasitojjaya
*rgyas pa dang rgyal ba*, Skt. *vikasitojjaya*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the twenty-second) when he becomes a buddha.

## Viśākhā
*sa ga*, Skt. *viśākhā*, The name of a lunar asterism. Its chief star is known as Alpha Librae in the occidental tradition.

## Viśākhā Mṛgāramātā
The main female disciple of the Buddha. She was the daughter-in-law of the chief minister of Śrāvastī named Mṛgāra and also his teacher, which led him to call her “mother”.

## Viśākha
*sa ga*, Skt. *viśākha*, Son of King Prasenajit’s minister Mṛgāra, betrothed to the non-returner Dharmadinnā. His fiancée fled their imminent marriage by a display of miracles at what was to be their wedding, receiving his assent for her to go forth instead. The text also tells of a certain female lay vow holder with a similar name Vaiśākhā on vol. 73, F.15.b.

## Viśākhadeva
*sa ga’i lha*, Skt. *viśākhadeva*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Viśākhamitra
*sa ga’i bshes gnyen*, Skt. *viśākhamitra*, Name of a former incarnation of the Buddha while he was a practicing bodhisattva.

## Vikhyāta
*rnam par bsgrags pa*, Skt. *vikhyāta*, A buddha realm.

## Vikhyātaketu
*rnam grags tog ma*, Skt. *vikhyātaketu*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Vikhyātamanasa
*rnam par grags pa’i yid*, Skt. *vikhyātamanasa*, One of the vidyārājas dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Vikhyātarāśi
*rnam par grags pa’i phung po*, Skt. *vikhyātarāśi*, One of the uṣṇīṣa kings attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Vikhyātaśriyā
*rnam par grags pa’i dpal*, Skt. *vikhyātaśriyā*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## vikiraṇa
*rnam par ’thor ba*, Skt. *vikiraṇa*, Lit. “strewing.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vikrama
*mthu rtsal*, Skt. *vikrama*, The 526th buddha in the first list, 526th in the second list, and 519th in the third list.

## Vikramaśīla
one of the most famous Buddhist universities of India, destroyed in the 12th century.

## Vikramapūri
The name of a town.

## Vikramaraśmi
*rnam par gnon pa chen po’i ’od zer*, Skt. *vikramaraśmi*, A buddha in a northeastern realm who sends bodhisattvas to pay homage to Śākyamuni.

## Vikrama­saṃdarśa­kacintin
*rtsal brtan por sems pa*, Skt. *vikrama­saṃdarśa­kacintin*, The name of a bodhisattva. “Capable Steadfast Intention.”

## Vikramāditya
A king.

## Vikrīḍamāna
*rnam par rtse*, Skt. *vikrīḍamāna*, The name of a bodhisattva. “Playful One.”

## Vikrīḍita
*rnam rol*, Skt. *vikrīḍita*, The 276th buddha in the first list, 275th in the second list, and 275th in the third list.

## Vikrīḍitāvin
*rnam par rol par ldan*, Skt. *vikrīḍitāvin*, The 111th buddha in the first list, 111th in the second list, and 112th in the third list.

## Vikrāmin
*rnam par gnon*, Skt. *vikrāmin*, A great bodhisattva.

## Vikrāntadeva
*lha yi mthu rtsal*, Skt. *vikrāntadeva*, The 444th buddha in the first list, 443rd in the second list, and 437th in the third list.

## Vikrānta­deva­gati
*rnam par gnon pa’i lha stabs*, Skt. *vikrānta­deva­gati*, The twenty-ninth buddha in a kalpa in the distant past.

## Vikrāntagamin
*mthu rtsal stobs*, Skt. *vikrāntagamin*, The 568th buddha in the first list, 568th in the second list, and 561st in the third list.

## Vikrāntagāmin
*stabs kyis gshegs pa*, Skt. *vikrāntagāmin*, The 156th buddha in the first list, 155th in the second list, and 155th in the third list.

## Vikrānta­gāmin
*rnam par gnon pas gshegs pa*, Skt. *vikrānta­gāmin*, A tathāgata mentioned here as one of the thirty-five buddhas of confession.

## Vikāsinī
*bi kA si ni*, Skt. *vikāsinī*, A mantra deity associated with the mudrā of the same name.

## Vikurvāṇa
*rnam par ’phrul*, Skt. *vikurvāṇa*, A nāga prince. One of the sons of the nāga king Anavatapta.

## Vikurvāṇarāja
The buddha that Bhadra is prophesied to become in a future life in the world system called Great Array. Coincidently, there is a sūtra in the Kangyur called The Questions of Vikurvāṇarāja (Toh 167), but there is not likely to be any connection with the Vikurvāṇarāja prophesied here.

## Vikurvita­prabha
*rnam par ’phrul pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vikurvita­prabha*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## viḍāla
An unidentified ritual substance.

## Viśālabuddhi
*yangs pa’i blo*, Skt. *viśālabuddhi*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Viśālakīrti
Skt. *viśālakīrti*, The name of a tathāgata

## Viśālamati
A bodhisattva in the Buddha’s retinue.

## Vilambā
*rnam par ’phyang ma*, Skt. *vilambā*, A rākṣasī known only from this sūtra.

## Viśālanetrī
Skt. *viśālanetrī*, ‟One with Elongated Eyes,” one of the six kinnara queens.

## Vi­śāla­netra
*yangs pa’i mig*, Skt. *vi­śāla­netra*, A great bodhisattva.

## viḍālapada
*pho sum gang*, Skt. *viḍālapada*, A measure of weight.

## Viśālaśrī
*yangs pa’i dpal*, Skt. *viśālaśrī*, A buddha.

## Viśālākṣa
*mig yangs pa*, Skt. *viśālākṣa*, A yakṣa general.

## Vilocana
*rnam par gzigs*, Skt. *vilocana*, The 74th buddha in the first list, 74th in the second list, and 75th in the third list.

## Vilokitā
*rnam par blta ba*, Skt. *vilokitā*, One of the worlds in the distant past.

## Vilokita
*rnam par lta ba*, Skt. *vilokita*, One of the vidyārājas dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## vilokita­mūrdhā
*spyi gtsug rnam par lta ba*, Skt. *vilokita­mūrdhā*, Lit. “seeing from the top of the head.” Name of a meditative stabilization. (Kimura has avalokita­mūrdhā)

## vilokita­mūrdhan
*spyi gtsug rnam par lta ba*, Skt. *vilokita­mūrdhan*, Lit. “seeing from the top of the head.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vilokiteśvara
*rnam gzigs dbang phyug*, Skt. *vilokiteśvara*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Vima
*bi ma*, Skt. *vima*, A goddess.

## Vimalā
*dri ma med pa*, Skt. *vimalā*, Lit. “Stainless.” The second level of accomplishment pertaining to bodhisattvas. See “ten bodhisattva levels.”

## Vimala
*dri med*, Skt. *vimala*, one of the first to join the [Buddha](#buddha)'s order of monks. He followed his friend [Yaśas](#yaśas) into the Buddhist order.

## Vimalaṭī
*dri ma med par ’gro ba*, Skt. *vimalaṭī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Vimalaśaṅkha
*dri med dung*, Skt. *vimalaśaṅkha*, A prominent merchant in the past.

## Vimala­bāhu
*dri ma myed pa*, Skt. *vimala­bāhu*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vimala­buddhi
*dri ma myed pa’i blo*, Skt. *vimala­buddhi*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Vimalacandra
*dri med zla ba*, Skt. *vimalacandra*, A bodhisattva; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Vimala­candra­mati
*zla ba dri med blo gros*, Skt. *vimala­candra­mati*, A king.

## Vimala­candra­prabhātejo­rāja
*dri ma med pa’i zla ’od gzi brjid rgyal po*, Skt. *vimala­candra­prabhātejo­rāja*, A buddha.

## Vimaladattā
*dri ma med pas byin pa*, Skt. *vimaladattā*, A queen in the distant past.

## Vimaladatta
*dri ma med pas byin pa*, Skt. *vimaladatta*, A king in the distant past.

## Vimala­dharma­parvata­jñāna­śikha­rābha
*chos dri ma med pa’i ri bo ye shes kyi rtse mo’i ’od*, Skt. *vimala­dharma­parvata­jñāna­śikha­rābha*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vimala­dhvaja
*dri myed rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *vimala­dhvaja*, In chapter 1 it is the name of one of the bodhisattvas in the presence of the Buddha at Śrāvastī (translated as dri myed rgyal mtshan). In chapter 44 it is the name of a bodhisattva in another world in the distant past (translated as rgyal mtshan dri ma med pa).

## vimalagarbha
*dri ma med pa’i snying po*, Skt. *vimalagarbha*, Unidentified jewel, literally “stainless essence.” Possibly moonstone.

## Vimala­garbha
*dri ma dang bral ba’i snying po*, Skt. *vimala­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## Vimalagati
*dri med ’gros*, Skt. *vimalagati*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Vimala­ghoṣa­tejeśvara­rāja
*dri med dbyangs kyi gzi brjid dbang phyug rgyal po*, Skt. *vimala­ghoṣa­tejeśvara­rāja*, The name of one thousand buddhas prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha.

## Vimalajvala­ratna­suvarṇa­raśmi­prabhā­śikhin
*dri ma med par ’bar ba rin chen gser gyi ’od zer snang ba’i tog*, Skt. *vimalajvala­ratna­suvarṇa­raśmi­prabhā­śikhin*, A tathāgata. (Toh 555: dri ma med pa’i ’od zer rin po che’i tog (Vimala­raśmiratna­ketu); Toh 556: dri ma med par ‘bar ba rin chen ‘od zer snang ba’i tog (Vimala­jvala­ratna­raśmiprabhā­ketu); Sanskrit ms.: Ratnaśikhin)

## Vimalaketu
*dri ma med pa’i tog*, Skt. *vimalaketu*, One of the tathāgatas attending the delivery of the MMK; one of the pratyeka­buddhas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Vimalakīrti
*dri ma med grags pa*, Skt. *Vimalakīrti*, The wealthy Licchavi layman, from the city of Vaiśālī, ranked as one of the great bodhisattvas. The main protagonist of this sūtra.

## Vimalamati
*dri med par ’gro ba*, Skt. *vimalamati*, One of the sixteen great bodhisattvas. The content of the list varies from text to text.

## Vimalamitra
*dri med bshes bnyen*, one of the most learned Indian Buddhist masters. He went to Tibet in the 9th century, where he taught extensively, and composed and translated numerous Sanskrit texts. The quintessence of his teaching is known as the *Vima Nyingtig*, one of the *Heart-essence* teachings of the [Great Perfection](#great-perfection).

## Vimalanetra
*dri med spyan*, Skt. *vimalanetra*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vimala­netra
*dri ma myed pa’i myig*, Skt. *vimala­netra*, In chapter 1, dri ma myed pa’i myig is the name of a bodhisattva present with the Buddha Śākyamuni in Śrāvastī; in chapter 43, mig dri ma med pa is the name of the precious minister of a cakravartin.

## Vi­mala­netra
*dri ma med pa’i mig*, Skt. *vi­mala­netra*, A great bodhisattva.

## Vimala­nirmala­kara­śrī
*dri ma med pa*, Skt. *vimala­nirmala­kara­śrī*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Vimala­padma­jvala­raśmi
*dri ma med pa’i pad+ma ’od zer ’bar ba*, Skt. *vimala­padma­jvala­raśmi*, One of the tathāgatas.

## Vimalaprabhā
*dri ma med pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vimalaprabhā*, The future realm where five hundred thousand bhikṣus in the Buddha’s saṅgha will become buddhas.

## Vimalaprabha
*dri ma med pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vimalaprabha*, The 484th buddha in the first list, 483rd in the second list, and 477th in the third list.

## Vimala­prabha
*dri ma myed pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vimala­prabha*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Vimalaprabhāsa
A bodhisattva who is one of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s sons in this sūtra and predicted to be the future buddha Sunetra. His name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Vimala­prabhāsa
*dri ma med pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vimala­prabhāsa*, A thus-gone one.

## Vimala­prabhāsa­śrī­tejorāja­garbha
*’od dri ma med pa’i dpal gyi gzi brjid bzang po’i snying po*, Skt. *vimala­prabhāsa­śrī­tejorāja­garbha*, A bodhisattva mahāsattva.

## vimalapradīpa
*dri ma med pa’i sgron ma*, Skt. *vimalapradīpa*, Lit. “stainless lamp.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vimalaśrī
*dri ma med pa’i dpal*, Skt. *vimalaśrī*, A great bodhisattva.

## Vimalaśraddhā
*rnam dag dad pa*, Skt. *vimalaśraddhā*, “Completely Pure Faith.” The daughter of King Prasenajit.

## Vimalaraśmi
*dri ma med pa’i ’od zer*, Skt. *vimalaraśmi*, A buddha.

## Vimalarāja
*dri med rgyal po*, Skt. *vimalarāja*, The 507th buddha in the first list, 507th in the second list, and 500th in the third list.

## Vimala­śrī­megha
*ye shes dri ma med pa phun sum tshogs pa’i sprin*, Skt. *vimala­śrī­megha*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vimala­saṃbhava­prabhā
*dri ma med pa skyed pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vimala­saṃbhava­prabhā*, A queen’s nurse in another world in the distant past.

## Vimalateja­guṇa­rāja
*dri med gzi brjid yon tan rgyal po*, Skt. *vimalateja­guṇa­rāja*, A buddha in an eastern buddha realm. He sends two bodhisattvas to pay homage to Śākyamuni.

## Vimala­tejaḥ­prabha
*gzi brjid dri ma myed pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vimala­tejaḥ­prabha*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Vimalatejas
*dri med gzi brjid*, Skt. *vimalatejas*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vimala­tejas
*dri ma myed pa’i gzi brjid*, Skt. *vimala­tejas*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Vimalavaiśāyana
*bgrod bya’i bu dri ma med*, Skt. *vimalavaiśāyana*, The fourth of the thousand young Veda-reciting brahmins. The Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies that he will be the Buddha Maitreya, the fifth buddha in the Bhadraka eon. Note that the Tibetan translation differs from the name found in the extant Sanskrit.

## Vimala­vakrabhānu­prabha
*nyi ma ltar bzhin mdog dri ma med pa*, Skt. *vimala­vakrabhānu­prabha*, A cakravartin king in another world in the distant past.

## Vimala­vatsa
*dri ma myed pa’i sras*, Skt. *vimala­vatsa*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vimalaviśuddhi
*dri ma med par dag pa*, Skt. *vimalaviśuddhi*, A lay woman in Śūrpāraka.

## Vimalavāsinī
*dri ma med pa’i gnas ma*, Skt. *vimalavāsinī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Vimalābha
*mdog dri ma med pa’i ’od*, Skt. *vimalābha*, “Stainless Light of Color.” The name of a kalpa in the past.

## Vimalendra
*dri med dbang po*, Skt. *vimalendra*, A bodhisattva who praises the brahmin Samudrareṇu.

## Vimalāṅganetra
*spyan dang yan lag dri med*, Skt. *vimalāṅganetra*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vimalākarī
*dri med byed ma*, Skt. *vimalākarī*, One of the goddesses associated with Amoghapāśa.

## Vimalāntakarī
*dri med mtha’ yas ma*, Skt. *vimalāntakarī*, One of the vidyārājñīs dwelling with Śākyamuni in the realm of the Pure Abode. The Tib. is not an accurate translation of the attested Sanskrit.

## Vimalottara­jñānin
*dri myed dam pa’i ye shes*, Skt. *vimalottara­jñānin*, A bodhisattva.

## Vimalāsya
*dri ma med pa’i zhal*, Skt. *vimalāsya*, A buddha.

## Vimatijaha
*yid gnyis spong ba*, Skt. *vimatijaha*, The 227th buddha in the first list, 226th in the second list, and 226th in the third list.

## Vimatiprahāṇa
*yid gnyis spong*, Skt. *vimatiprahāṇa*, A bodhisattva.

## Vi­mati­samuddhāṭin
*the tshom kun bcom*, Skt. *vi­mati­samuddhāṭin*, A prince in the distant past.

## Vi­mati­samud­ghātin
*yid gnyis yang dag sel ba*, Skt. *vimatisamudghātin*, A bodhisattva whose name appears only in the Sanskrit of this text (see ).

## vimativikaraṇa
*nem nur rnam par sel ba*, Skt. *vimativikaraṇa*, Lit. “eliminator of doubts.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vimativikiraṇa
*yid gnyis rnam par sel ba*, Skt. *vimativikiraṇa*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vimoharāja
*gti mug med rgyal*, Skt. *vimoharāja*, The 825th buddha in the first list, 824th in the second list, and 814th in the third list.

## Vimokṣacandra
*rnam par thar pa’i zla ba*, Skt. *vimokṣacandra*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vimuktacūḍa
*rnam grol gtsug*, Skt. *vimuktacūḍa*, The 665th buddha in the first list, 664th in the second list, and 656th in the third list.

## Vimuktaketu
*rnam grol tog*, Skt. *vimuktaketu*, The 624th buddha in the first list, 623rd in the second list, and 616th in the third list.

## Vimukticandra
A bodhisattva and interlocuter in The Dharma Council.

## Vimukti­candra
*rnam par grol ba’i zla ba*, Skt. *vimukti­candra*, The interlocutor for Vajra­garbha in The Ten Bhumis. He appears in passing in a few other sūtras, but not in any tantras. On two occasions in verse he is referred to as Mokṣa­candra.

## Vi­mukti­candra
*rnam par grol ba’i zla ba*, Skt. *vi­mukti­candra*, A great bodhisattva.

## Vimuktighoṣa
*rnam par grol ba’i dbyangs*, Skt. *vimuktighoṣa*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vimuktilābhin
*grol brnyes*, Skt. *vimuktilābhin*, The 608th buddha in the first list, 607th in the second list, and 601st in the third list.

## Vimuktisena
*rnam grol sde*, Skt. *vimuktisena*, Indian commentator on the Abhisamayālaṃkāra (fl. early sixth century).

## Vi­mukti­sena
*rnam grol sde*, Skt. *vi­mukti­sena*, Indian commentator (fl. early sixth century).

## Vinardita
*rnam par sgra ’byin*, Skt. *vinardita*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vinarditarāja
*sgrogs pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vinarditarāja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vinatā
The mother of eagles (suparṇa). According to the brahmanical tradition, she is one of the daughters of the creator god Dakṣa Prajāpati, who gave her and twelve of her sisters in marriage to the sage Kaśyapa.

## Vinataka
*rnam par ’dud*, Skt. *vinataka*, One of the seven golden mountains.

## Vinaya
*'dul ba*, one of the Three [Piṭakas](#piṭaka), containing teachings about monastic discipline and ethics in general.

## Vinaya specialist of Gya
Full name Wangchuk Tsultrim (dbang phyug tshul khrims, 1047–1131), he was a holder of the lower Vinaya lineage (smad ’dul) and a member of the Gya clan.

## Vindhyā
*bin+d+hA*, Skt. *vindhyā*, One of the two auxiliary pīlavas.

## Vindhya
*bin d+ha*, Skt. *vindhya*, A mountain range, actually a series of mountain ranges, which extends across central India. The usual translation is bigs byed.

## Vindhyas
*’bigs byed*, Skt. *vindhya*, An Indian mountain chain.

## Vindhyācala
*ri byin t+ya*, Skt. *vindhyācala*, Another term for the Vindhya mountain range; a synonym for Vindhyagiri.

## Vindu
*thigs pa*, Skt. *vindu*, A mountain king.

## Viniścitamati
*rnam nges blo gros*, Skt. *viniścitamati*, The 346th buddha in the first list, 345th in the second list, and 340th in the third list.

## Vinipāta
*rnam par ltung byed*, Skt. *vinipāta*, One of the grahas.

## Vinirbhoga
*tha dad du gnas pa*, Skt. *vinirbhoga*, “Detachment.” The name of an eon in the distant past.

## Vinīta
*rnam par dul*, Skt. *vinīta*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vinītabuddhi
*shin tu dul ba’i blo*, Skt. *vinītabuddhi*, A sea goddess who prays to become the Buddha Śamudrareṇu’s mother when he is the Buddha Śākyamuni, i.e., Māyādevī.

## Vinīteśvara
*dul ba’i dbang phyug*, Skt. *vinīteśvara*, A god.

## Viṣnumati
*khyab ’jug blo gros*, Skt. *viṣnumati*, A king.

## vināyaka
Here, a class of demons who create obstacles, “those who lead astray” or “mis-leaders.” In other contexts the name can be interpreted as “remover [of obstacles],” referring to a class of semidivine beings, or as an epithet meaning “leader” or “guide.”

## Vināya­kānta­kṣepa
*log ’dren gyi nang du ’phen ba*, Skt. *vināya­kānta­kṣepa*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Viṣogra
*dug drag*, Skt. *viṣogra*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Viśoka
*mya ngan bral*, Skt. *viśoka*, A Magadhan king, possibly the successor of Udayin.

## vipakṣa
Skt. *vipakṣa*, Technical term in Buddhist logic.

## Vipara­dharmakīrti­ghoṣa
*grags pa’i dbang phyug dbyangs*, Skt. *vipara­dharmakīrtighoṣa*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Vipaśyā
*zhags bral*, Skt. *vipaśyā*, A river queen.

## vipaśyanā
*lhag mthong*, Skt. *vipaśyanā*, An important form of Buddhist meditation focusing on developing insight into the nature of phenomena. Often presented as part of a pair of meditation techniques, the other being śamatha.

## Vipaśyin
*rnam par gzigs*, the first of the six [Buddhas](#buddha) who preceded [Buddha](#buddha) [Śākyamuni](#śākyamuni).

## Vipaśyinī
*rnam gzigs*, This translation and identification is conjectural.

## Viprasanna
*rnam par dag pa*, Skt. *viprasanna*, The name of a past eon.

## Vipula
*rgyas pa*, Skt. *vipula*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Vipulabuddhi
*rgya chen blo*, Skt. *vipulabuddhi*, The forty-first buddha in a kalpa in the distant past, and also the eighty-eighth buddha in another kalpa in the distant past.

## Vipula­dharmādhimukti­saṃbhava­tejas
*chos rgya chen po la mos pa yang dag par ’byung ba’i gzi brjid*, Skt. *vipula­dharmādhimukti­saṃbhava­tejas*, A buddha in the distant past; the name as given in the prose passages. In verse he is called Adhimuktitejas.

## Vipulagātra
*sku ’byam klas*, Skt. **vipulagātra*, Name of a tathāgata; lit. “vast body.”

## Vipula­guṇa­jyotiḥprabha
*yon tan rgya chen po gzi brjid kyi ’od*, Skt. *vipula­guṇa­jyotiḥprabha*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vipulakīrti
*grags yangs*, Skt. *vipulakīrti*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vipula­mahā­jñāna­raśmi­rāja
*ye shes chen po’i ’od gzer shin tu yangs pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vipula­mahā­jñāna­raśmi­rāja*, A buddha in the distant past.

## Vipulamati
*blo gros rgya chen*, Skt. *vipulamati*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Vipula­praha­sita­vadanamaṇi­kanakaratnojjvalaraśmi­prabhāsābhyudgata­rāja
*rgya cher rab tu bzhad pa’i zhal nor bu dang gser dang rin po che ’bar ba’i ’od zer snang ba mngon par ’phags pa’i rgyal po*, Skt. *vipula­praha­sita­vadanamaṇi­kanakaratnojjvalaraśmi­prabhāsābhyudgata­rāja*, A buddha from the distant past whose name means “Widely Smiling, Exalted King Whose Widely Smiling Face Shines with the Splendor of Gems, Gold, and Jewels.”

## Vipāśyin
*rnam par gzigs*, Skt. *vipāśyin*, “Discerning One.”

## Viraṭī
*dga’ bral ma*, Skt. *viraṭī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Virajā
*rdul dang bral ba*, Skt. *virajā*, Virajā (Dustless) is a buddhafield inhabited by the Buddha Dharmadhvaja.

## Viraja
*rdul bral*, Skt. *viraja*, The 776th buddha in the first list, 775th in the second list, and 765th in the third list.

## Virajadhvajā
*rdul med pa’i rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *virajadhvajā*, A world realm in the distant future. (Toh 555: rnam dag tog, Viśuddhaketu, where it is the name of Rūpyaketu in the lifetime that he attains buddhahood)

## Virajadhvaja
*rdul myed rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *virajadhvaja*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Virajamati
*rdul dang bral ba’i blo gros*, Skt. *virajamati*, A buddha realm.

## Virajaprabha
*rdul dang bral ba’i ’od*, Skt. *virajaprabha*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Virajasamādhibalavikrāmin
*ting nge ’dzin rdul dang bral ba’i stobs kyi rnam par gnon pa*, Skt. *viraja­samādhi­bala­vikrāmin*, One of the tathāgatas.

## Viraja­vīreśvara­rāja
*byang chub rdul bral rgyal po*, Skt. *virajavīreśvara­rāja*, One of the hundred names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for 2,500 buddhas, presumably the name of twenty-five of those buddhas.

## Virajomaṇḍala
*rdul dang bral ba’i dkyil ’khor*, Skt. *virajomaṇḍala*, “Domain Free of Dust.” The name of a kalpa in the distant past.

## Virajottara­jñānin
*rdul myed dam pa’i ye shes*, Skt. *virajottara­jñānin*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Virajovatī
*rdul dang bral ba*, Skt. *virajovatī*, A four-continent world realm.

## Virajovatī­śrī­garbhā
*rdul dang bral ba’i dpal gyi snying po*, Skt. *virajovatī­śrī­garbhā*, “The Essence of the Splendor That Is Free of Dust.” The name of a ray of light.

## Viśrambhikā
*dbugs ’byin ldan ma*, Skt. *viśrambhikā*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Virata
“Ended.” The name of a muhūrta.

## Virati
*rnam par dga’ ba*, Skt. *Virati*, One thousand intermediate eons after Acintyamatiguṇarāja has passed into parinirvāṇa and his dharma has come too an end, the buddha realm Meruprabhā will be named Virati. The Tathāgata Raśmi will reside in this buddha realm and give teachings.

## Virgo
*bu mo*, Skt. *kanyā*, See “Kanyā.”

## Virūḍhadhvaja
*’phags skyes rgyal mtshan*, Skt. *virūḍhadhvaja*, The name that the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies will be that of one of his eighty brothers (the fifty-fifth) when he becomes a buddha.

## Virūḍhaka
*'phags skyes po*, Skt. *virūḍhaka*, a son of King [Prasenajit](#prasenajit) of Kosala, who first served as a general in his father's army, but later usurped the throne. As a boy he discovered that his mother, who had been offered to his father by the Śākyas, had originally only been a servant rather than a noblewoman as the Śākyas had claimed; and later, as king, in revenge he attacked and destroyed [Kapilavastu](#kapilavastu), slaughtering most of the Śākya inhabitants. However, he then died there in a flood. Not to be confused with the Virūḍhaka who is one of the [Four Great Kings](#four-great-kings).

## Virile One
*dpa’ bo*, Skt. *vīra*, Closely associated with notions of virility, this term can denote the male deity of the maṇḍala (whose consort is the vidyā) or the yogī who practices this mode of tantra.

## Virility of a Lion
The name of a bodhisattva.

## Viśrāntin
*ngal bso po*, Skt. *viśrāntin*, An epithet of Vaiśravaṇa, one of the Four Great Kings. See Negi 1995, vol. 3, p. 945.

## Virocana
*rnam par snang byed*, Skt. *virocana*, The father of the asura king Bali.

## Virūpa
one of the eighty-four [mahāsiddhas](#mahāsiddha) of India. An important source of the teachings of the [Sakyapa](#sakyapa) tradition.

## Virūpa (the king)
*mi sdug pa*, Skt. *virūpa*, A certain jealous king of Mithilā who lived before the time of Buddha Śākyamuni. Not to be confused with Virūpa (the ugly one), the householders’ son.

## Virūpa (the ugly one)
*mi sdug*, Skt. *virūpa*, Son of householders on Mount Śiśumāri who cast him out of their home because of his extreme ugliness. When later he felt joy toward an emanation of the Buddha, the Buddha made his ugliness disappear. Then, hearing the Dharma from the Buddha, he manifested the resultant state of a non-returner, went forth, and went on to manifest arhatship. Not to be confused with King Virūpa.

## Virūpakṣa
*mig mi bzang*, Skt. *virūpākṣa*, The name of the great king who presides over the western direction.

## virūpiṇī
Skt. *virūpiṇī*, “Misshapen one,” a class of female spirits.

## Virūpākṣa
*mig mi bzang*, Skt. *virūpākṣa*, One of the four mahārājas. He is the guardian of the western direction and traditionally the lord of the nāgas, though in this sūtra that appears to be Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

## Virtue
*dge ba*, Skt. *dge ba*, A country prophesied by the Buddha. It refers to the country of Khotan.

## Virtue Gift
*dge bas byin*, Skt. *dge bas byin*, Father of the buddha Amoghadarśin.

## Virtue of Light
*’od dge*, A buddha. In Toh 555, his name is given as “Sublime Light” (dam pa’i ’od).

## virtues of ascetic practice
*sbyangs pa’i chos*, Skt. *dhūtadharma*, The qualities associated with the observance of ascetic practices.

## virtuous
*dge ba*, Skt. *kuśala*, The term kuśala can function both as a qualifier or as a noun in its own right, which makes it difficult to resort to a single translation (I have resorted to “virtue” and “virtuous”). It refers to something beneficial or virtuous and is sometimes etymologized as something that keeps badness in check (kutsitaṁ śalate); when the sense of kuśala is more akin to “skillful” or even “virtuoso,” the etymology is that it is “someone who can cut the kuśa grass” (kuśān lāti), a type of grass that is very sharp and thus requires remarkable skill to cut it without being cut in turn.

## Virtuous Abiding
*dge gnas*, Skt. *dge gnas*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Nāgadatta.

## virtuous attributes
*dge ba’i chos*, Skt. *kuśaladharma*, Also translated here as “virtuous phenomena.”

## Virtuous Castle
*mkhar dge ba can*, Skt. *mkhar dge ba can*, A castle in the country of Virtue.

## Virtuous Eye
*mig bzang po*, Skt. *mig bzang po*, A buddhafield in the southwestern direction of the Tathāgata Gazing at All Beings with Great Compassion.

## virtuous friend
*dge ba’i bshes gnyen*, A spiritual teacher who can contribute to an individual’s progress on the spiritual path to awakening and act wholeheartedly for the welfare of students.

## Virtuous Glory
*dge ba’i dpal*, Skt. *dge ba’i dpal*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Siṃhaketu.

## Virtuous Incense
*dge ba’i spos*, Skt. *dge ba’i spos*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Āśādatta.

## Virtuous Intelligence
*dge ba’i blo gros*, Skt. *sāgaramati*, A bodhisattva prince who was a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Virtuous Joy
*dge ba dga’*, Skt. *dge ba dga’*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Guṇendradeva.

## Virtuous Mind
*blo dge*, Skt. *blo dge*, Foremost in terms of insight among the followers of the buddha Vibhaktatejas.

## Virtuous Occurrence
*’byung ba bzang po*, Skt. *’byung ba bzang po*, A past world where the Tathāgata Glorious Secret lived along with the bodhisattva Smṛtibuddhi, a past incarnation of the bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa.

## Virtuous One
*skyes bu dam pa*, Skt. *satpuruṣa*, An epithet for the Buddha. Also the ideal man, a good or wise man.

## virtuous phenomena
*dge ba’i chos*, Skt. *kuśala­dharma*, Also translated here as “virtuous attributes.” For a listing of the mundane virtuous phenomena, see . (See also ).

## virtuous roots
*dge ba’i rtsa ba*, Skt. *kuśala-mūla*, Wholesome actions that benefit others.

## virtuous spiritual friend
*dge ba’i bshes gnyen*, Skt. *kalyāṇamitra*, A general term to denote a qualified spiritual teacher.

## Virtuous Vision
*dge ba’i mig*, Skt. *dge ba’i mig*, Name of a past king in a story the Buddha tells.

## Virupākṣa
*mig mi bzang*, Skt. *virupākṣa*, One of the Four Great Kings, he presides over the western quarter and rules over the nāgas.

## Viruta
*khyad par sgra*, Skt. *viruta*, One of the kinnara kings.

## Viśruta
*rnam grags*, Skt. *viśruta*, One of the pratyeka­buddhas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Viśrutaśrī
*dpal grags*, Skt. *viśrutaśrī*, One of the Buddha’s former rebirths.

## Visṛṣṭa­dharma­rāja
*chos sbyin rgyal po*, Skt. *visṛṣṭa­dharma­rāja*, One of the two names prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha for a group of a thousand buddhas, with presumably five hundred buddhas having this name.

## visage that resembles the full moon
*zhal zla ba nya ba lta bu*, Skt. *pūrṇondu­vadanā*, Twenty-seventh or thirty-first of the thirty-two major marks.

## Visarpa
*’go ba’i nad*, Skt. *visarpa*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## visibly manifests awakening
*mngon sum du byang chub snang ba*, Skt. *mngon sum du byang chub snang ba*, An absorption.

## Visimonya
*bi si mo nya*, Skt. *bi si mo nya*, A temple on Mount Gośṛṅga.

## Vision
*shin tu mthong*, Skt. *shin tu mthong*, Vision (the faculty of sight, or a thing seen), also the name of the one both foremost in terms of insight and foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Dharmeśvara.

## Vision Aggregate
*gzigs pa’i phung po*, Skt. *gzigs pa’i phung po*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Prahāṇakhila (239 according to the third enumeration) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

## vision of awareness
*ye shes mthong ba*, Skt. *jñāna­darśana*, The Nibandhana explains that awareness itself is vision, as it functions as direct perception.

## Vision of One Thousand Lotuses
*pad+ma stong mthong*, Skt. *pad+ma stong mthong*, Alternative name of the current eon, also known as the “Fortunate Eon.”

## vision of phenomena
A genuine understanding and realistic view of the state of things.

## Vision of the Noble
*’phags pa gzigs pa*, Skt. *’phags pa gzigs pa*, Birthplace of the buddha Śuddhaprabha.

## Vision of Unobscured Love
*sgrib med byams pa mthong*, Skt. *sgrib med byams pa mthong*, Mother of the buddha Brahmagāmin.

## Vision of Vast Bliss
*bde ba rgya chen po dmigs pa*, Skt. *bde ba rgya chen po dmigs pa*, A mountain in Moving in Mixed Environments.

## Vision through the View
*lta bas mthong*, Skt. *lta bas mthong*, Foremost in terms of miraculous abilities among the followers of the buddha Bhīṣaṇa.

## visiting monk
*dge slong glo bur du ’ongs pa*, Skt. *āgantuko bhikṣuḥ*, A distinction is made between monks who are visiting a monastery and those who are long-term residents (i.e., Tib. gnyug mar gnas pa, Skt. naivāsika) and familiar with the inner and outer workings of the community. See Kalyāṇamitra (F.313.b.4–5).

## Visphoṭaka
*rnam par ’joms*, Skt. *visphoṭaka*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Visphūrja
*rnam par ’phrul pa dang ldan pa*, Skt. *visphūrja*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Visphūrjita
*mthu bsgyings*, Skt. *visphūrjita*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vistīrṇabheda
*’od rgya chen*, Skt. *vistīrṇabheda*, A buddha in the past.

## Vistīrṇavatī
*yangs ldan*, Skt. *vistīrṇavatī*, The realm where in the future there will be Buddha Śālendrarāja.

## vital energy
*mdangs*, Skt. *ojas*, A term for vitality, strength, and vigor. It is widely believed that this vital energy can be targeted and stolen by various classes of demonic beings, causing a person to experience mental and physical decline.

## vital energy heart mantra
*srog gi snying po*, A phrase describing a mantra syllable in the “selection of mantra syllables” (Tib. sngags btu ba; Skt. mantroddhāra) instructions in The Tantra of Great Gaṇapati.

## vital wind
A term for the life force in the subtle body.

## Vitality
*tshe ldan*, Skt. *tshe ldan*, Vitality (energy, life force), also the name of a son of the buddha Lokacandra.

## Vitara
*bi ta ra*, Skt. *bi ta ra*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vitastā
*rgyas ’bab*, Skt. *vitastā*, A river queen.

## vitasti
*mtho gang*, Skt. *vitasti*, A measure of length that equals the distance from the tip of the extended thumb to the tip of the little finger.

## Vitateśvara
*sna tshogs sgra’i dbang phyug*, Skt. *vitateśvara*, One of the bodhisattvas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## vitiligo
*sha bkra*, Skt. *citra*, A medical condition in which the skin loses pigment, resulting in patches of discoloration.

## Vitimira­jñāna­tathāgata­pradīpā
*ye shes rab rib med pa de bzhin gshegs pa’i sgron ma*, Skt. *vitimira­jñāna­tathāgata­pradīpā*, “The Tathāgata Lamp of Unclouded Wisdom.” The name of a ray of light.

## vitimirāpagata
*rab rib med pa*, Skt. *vitimirāpagata*, Lit. “free from eye disease.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Śvitraroga
*sha za gu nad*, Skt. *śvitraroga*, A vidyārāja from the personal retinue of Vajrapāṇi.

## Viṣṇu
*khyab ’jug*, Skt. *viṣṇu*, One of the central gods in the Hindu pantheon today. He had not yet risen to an important status during the Buddha’s lifetime and only developed his own significant following in the early years of the common era. Vaishnavism developed the theory of ten emanations, or avatars, the ninth being the Buddha. His emanation as a dwarf plays an important role in this sūtra. The Sanskrit etymology of the name is uncertain, but it was already in use in the Vedas, where he is a minor deity, and has been glossed as “One Who Enters (Everywhere).”

## Viṣṇudatta
*khyab ’jug gi byin*, Skt. *viṣṇudatta*, A brahmin.

## Viśuddha
*rnam par dag pa*, Skt. *viśuddha*, One of the gods from the realm of the Pure Abode.

## Viśuddhabuddhi
*rnam par sangs rgyas pa’i blo*, Skt. *viśuddhabuddhi*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Viśuddhacārin
*rnam dag spyod pa*, Skt. *viśuddhacārin*, A bhikṣu who was a pupil of Śāriputra.

## Vi­śuddha­cāritra
*spyod pa rnam par dag*, Skt. *vi­śuddha­cāritra*, One of the four principal bodhisattvas who emerged from the ground at the time of the teaching of the Lotus Sūtra.

## Viśuddha­cāritra
*spyod pa rnam par dag pa*, Skt. *viśuddha­cāritra*, A bodhisattva of a past eon.

## Viśuddhaśīla
*tshul khrims rnam par dag pa*, Skt. *viśuddhaśīla*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Viśuddhamati
A bodhisattva who in this sūtra is said to be one of the sons of King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and whose name is attested in Upholding the Roots of Virtue (Toh 101).

## Viśuddhanandin
*rnam par dag pas dgyes pa*, Skt. *viśuddhanandin*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Viśuddhanetra
*rnam par dag pa’i myig*, Skt. *viśuddhanetra*, A bodhisattva present in Śrāvastī.

## Viśuddha­netrābhā
*mig rnam par dag pa*, Skt. *viśuddha­netrābhā*, A night goddess in the distant past.

## Viśuddhaprajñā
*shes rab rnam par dag pa*, Skt. *viśuddhaprajñā*, Name of a bodhisattva.

## Viśuddhasiṃha
*bi shud d+ha sing ha*, Skt. *viśuddhasiṃha*, An Indian paṇḍita active in Tibet in the late eighth to early ninth century.

## Viśuddhavyūharāja
A bodhisattva who is a prince predicted to become the buddha Guṇāgradhārin, and whose name is attested in the Sanskrit manuscript of this sūtra.

## Viśuddhi
“Purity,” one of four kings who support the earth.

## Viṣṇulā
*khyab ’jug dga’ ma*, Skt. *viṣṇulā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Viṣṇuvatī
*khyab ’jug ’dzin ma*, Skt. *viṣṇuvatī*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Viśva
The name of a deity.

## Viśvabhū
*thams cad skyob*, Skt. *viśvabhū*, one of the six [buddha](#buddha)s who preceded [Śākyamuni](#śākyamuni) in this Fortunate Eon.

## Viśvabhu
*thams cad skyob*, Skt. *viśvabhu*, In early Buddhism the first of the seven buddhas, with Śākyamuni as the seventh. The first three buddhas—Vipaśyin, Śikhin, and Viśvabhu—are in an earlier eon than the Bhadraka eon, and therefore Śākyamuni is more commonly referred to as the fourth buddha. In The White Lotus of Compassion Sūtra, those three Buddhas are the last of thirty of countless buddhas preceding Śākyamuni, and when the Buddha Ratnagarbha prophesies the buddhahood of Samudrareṇu’s thirty million pupils, the last three pupils, unnamed, are prophesied by the Buddha Ratnagarbha to become the Buddhas Vipaśyin, Śikhin, and Viśvabhu.

## Viśvabhuj
*sna tshogs za*, Skt. *viśvabhuj*, One of the seven kings mentioned in the story of Govinda.

## Viśvabhuk
*thams cad mnga’ ba*, Skt. *viśvabhuk*, In early Buddhism the third of seven buddhas, with Śākyamuni as the seventh. The first three buddhas—Vipaśyin, Śikhin, and Viśvabhuk—appeared in a kalpa earlier than our Bhadra kalpa, and therefore Śākyamuni is more commonly referred to as the fourth buddha.

## Viśvadeva
*lha thams cad pa*, Skt. *viśvadeva*, The 878th buddha in the first list, 877th in the second list, and 868th in the third list.

## Viśvagupta
*kun gyis bsrungs*, Skt. *viśvagupta*, The third of the thousand young Veda-reciting brahmins. The Buddha Ratnagarbha names him the bodhisattva Vidvagañja­karuṇāśraya and prophesies that he will be the Buddha Kāśyapa, the third buddha in the Bhadraka eon.

## Viśvakūṭa
*sna tshogs brtsegs*, Skt. *viśvakūṭa*, A great bodhisattva.

## Viśvakarma
*las sna tshogs can*, Skt. *viśvakarman*, Literally “maker of sundry things,” Viśvakarma is the architect of the gods. He was an important deity in early Hinduism. In the Ṛg Veda, he is regarded as the personification of ultimate reality, the abstract creative power inherent in deities and in living and nonliving beings in this universe.

## Viśvakarman
*las thams cad pa*, Skt. *viśvakarman*, A god.

## Viśvamitrā
*kun gyi bshes*, Skt. *viśvamitrā*, A river queen.

## Viśvamitra
*kun gyi bshes*, Skt. *viśvamitra*, A great ṛṣi.

## Viśvantara
*thams cad sgrol*, Skt. *viśvantara*, A prince who was the Buddha in a former life.

## Viśvapurī
*thams cad ces bya ba’i grong rdal*, Skt. *viśvapurī*, The city of King Viśvāmitra.

## Viśvarūpā
*gzugs sna tshogs can*, Skt. *viśvarūpā*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## Viśvarūpa
*sna tshogs gzugs can*, Skt. *viśvarūpa*, “Omnifarious One” is the name/epithet of various deities, but in particular of Viṣṇu in his viśvarūpa aspect.

## Vivasvatāvartā
*gshin rje ’khyil ma*, Skt. *vivasvatāvartā*, One of the dhāraṇī goddesses present at the delivery of the MMK.

## Viśvavarṇa
*thams cad kha dog*, Skt. *viśvavarṇa*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vivṛddhi
*rnam par skye ba ma*, Skt. *vivṛddhi*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī. (The stog pho brang Kangyur has rnam par ’phel ma.)

## Viveśacintin
*khyad par sems*, Skt. *viveśacintin*, A king in the distant past.

## Vividha­vicitra­maṇi­mauli­dharā
*nor bu rnam pa sna tshogs kyis mdzes par byas pa’i cod pan thogs pa*, Skt. *vividha­vicitra­maṇi­mauli­dharā*, One of the names of Śrī Mahādevī.

## viviparous birth
*mngal nas skyes pa*, Skt. *jārāyuja*, First of the four modes of birth.

## Viśvāmitra
*kun gyi bshes gnyen*, Skt. *viśvāmitra*, In chapter 44 it is the name of one of the future buddhas of this kalpa. It is also the name of the kalyāṇamitra in chapter 46, the teacher of children.

## Vivṛta
*phye ba*, Skt. *vivṛta*, A legendary realm in which Śiva will attain buddhahood.

## Viyogā
*sbyor bral ma*, Skt. *viyogā*, One of the subtle channels in the body.

## vājapeya
The Vedic ritual that involves offering several cups of Soma, “the drink of strength” (vājapeya).

## Vājasaneyin
One of the lineages within the Yajurveda branch of the brahmanical tradition.

## Vṛji
The land and people of Vṛji or Vaji (Pali Vajji), a country situated on the northeastern Gangetic plain, and one of the sixteen mahājanapada (“great countries”) of ancient India. It was run as a confederacy of eight or nine clans, including the Vṛji, Licchavi, and Videha, who sent representatives to an administrative council led by an elected ruler. Its capital was Vaiśālī. See Edgerton, s.v. Vṛji and Vaji.

## Vāṣkala
One of the lineages within the Ṛgveda branch of the brahmanical tradition.

## vākkali­vidhvaṃsana­gagana­kalpa
*ngag ki skyon rnam par ’jig pas nam mkha’ ltar gyur pa*, Skt. *vākkali­vidhvaṃsana­gagana­kalpa*, Lit. “destroying verbal flaws, it is like space.” Name of a meditative stabilization.

## Vṛkodara
*spyang lto*, Skt. *vṛkodara*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vākyaccheda
*tshig gcod pa*, Skt. *vākyaccheda*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vākyanuda
*gsung sgrog pa*, Skt. *vākyanuda*, One of the future buddhas of this kalpa.

## Vāli
*’khri byed*, Skt. *vāli*, A yakṣa king. (Toh 555: rgyal po)

## Vālin
A monkey king who was a major character in the Rāmāyaṇa.

## Vālmīki
*grog mkhar*, Skt. *vālmīki*, Ancient Indian rishi who is renowned as the author of the Rāmāyaṇa.

## Vāmā
*g.yon pa ma*, Skt. *vāmā*, One of the subtle channels in the body.

## Vāmadeva
*g.yon phyogs lha*, Skt. *vāmadeva*, A ṛṣi in the past.

## Vāmadevaka
*g.yon phyogs lha*, Skt. *vāmadevaka*, A great ṛṣi.

## Vāmakī
*mi’u thung ma*, Skt. *vāmakī*, One of the great dūtīs attending upon Lord Vajrapāṇi.

## Vāmaka
*g.yon phyogs*, Skt. *vāmaka*, A ṛṣi in the past.

## Vāmanī
*thung ngu ma*, Skt. *vāmanī*, One of the subtle channels in the body.

## Vāmana
*bA man*, Skt. *vāmana*, The dwarf incarnation of Viṣṇu, who deceived the king of the asuras.

## vīnā
*pi wang*, Skt. *vīnā*, A stringed instrument, similar to a lute, that is used in Indian classical music, especially of the Carnatic (South Indian) style.

## Vānara
Skt. *vānara*, One of the rāśis.

## Vṛndakaṭa
*khyu ’gro*, Skt. *vṛndakaṭa*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## Śvānāsyā
*khyi gdong ma*, Skt. *śvānāsyā*, One of the goddesses in the retinue of Heruka.

## Voice as Delightful as the Songs of Cuckoos, Parrots, Grouse, Pheasants, and Kalaviṅka Birds
*khu byug dang ne tso dang ri skegs dang ku na la dang ka la ping ka skad ’byin pa lta bur yid du ’ong ba’i nga ro’i gdangs nges par sgrogs pa*, Skt. *khu byug dang ne tso dang ri skegs dang ku na la dang ka la ping ka skad ’byin pa lta bur yid du ’ong ba’i nga ro’i gdangs nges par sgrogs pa*, One of the bodhisattva great beings.

## voice endowed with the sixty qualities
There are slightly varying lists of the sixty qualities or aspects of the buddha’s voice. Often an additional four are added, extending the list to sixty-four. One such canonical source for the list can be found in the Tathāgatācintya­guhya­nirdeśa­sūtra (Toh 47), . This list is further elaborated by Daśabalaśrīmitra in the Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛta­viniścaya (Toh 3897), folio 306.a.

## voice is deep [like the trumpet of an elephant or the rolling of thunder]
*dbyangs zab pa*, Skt. *gaja­garjita­jimūta­ghoṣa­tā*, Twenty-fifth of the eighty minor marks; the additional simile comes from the Sanskrit term used in this list in other sūtras.

## voice like Brahmā
*tshangs pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *brahmaghoṣa*, The voice endowed with the sixteen perfect qualities of Brahmā, the king of the gods. A common description of a buddha’s speech (Rangjung Yeshe Dictionary, “tshangs pa’i dbyangs”).

## Voice like the King of Swans
*ngang pa’i rgyal po lta bu’i dbyangs*, Skt. *ngang pa’i rgyal po lta bu’i dbyangs*, A queen of King Sarvārthasiddha.

## voice like the trumpeting of an elephant or the roar of a dragon
*glang po’i nga ro dang / ’brug gi dbyangs dang ldan pa*, Skt. *gaja­garjita­jīmūta­ghoṣa*, Fifty-first of the eighty minor signs.

## Voice More Majestic Than Brahmā’s
*tshangs pa’i sgra gzi brjid mngon par ’phags pa*, Skt. *tshangs pa’i sgra gzi brjid mngon par ’phags pa*, The name of a bodhisattva in the Buddha’s audience.

## Voice of All Sounds
*sgra thams cad kyi dbyangs*, Skt. *sgra thams cad kyi dbyangs*, A buddha.

## voice of Brahmā
*tshangs pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *brahmaghoṣa*, A voice that has the qualities of the voice of the god Brahmā. This is one of the thirty-two major marks of a great being.

## Voice of Jambū
*’dzam bu’i mgrin*, One of the fourteen rākṣasīs.

## Voice of Mahābrahmā
*tshangs pa chen po dbyangs dang ldan pa*, Skt. *tshangs pa chen po dbyangs dang ldan pa*, A bodhisattva in the Buddha’s retinue.

## voice of the tathāgatas endowed with sixty aspects
*gsung yan lag drug bcu dang ldan pa*, See .

## Voice of Victory
*rnam par rgyal ba’i dbyangs*, A great bodhisattva present at this discourse.

## Voice Proclaiming the Cloud of Dharma
*chos kyi sprin mngon par bsgrags pa’i dbyangs*, Skt. *chos kyi sprin mngon par bsgrags pa’i dbyangs*, A buddha.

## void
*dben pa*, Skt. *vivikta*, “Void” renders dben pa (vivikta); alternatively, “isolated,” in the sense that there is nothing else beside it.

## voided urine
*bkus te bor*, Skt. *pūtimukta*, the medicine of first resort for monks, as identified in the [Four Supports](#four-supports) [section](#section) of the ordination ritual.

## voidness
*dben pa*, Skt. *vi­vakta*, Also translated here as “void.”

## voidness of all phenomena
*chos thams cad rnam par dben pa*, Skt. *sarva­dharma­vivikta*, The second of twenty-four aspects of the perfection of wisdom taught by Dharmodgata, and realized as meditative stabilities by Sadāprarudita, in chapter 75.

## voidness of voidness
*stong pa nyid kyi stong pa nyid*, Skt. *śūnyatāśūnyatā*, The voidness of voidness, an important concept that indicates the ultimate conceptuality of all terms, even those for the ultimate, to avoid the major error of absolutising the ultimate.

## Vokkāṇa
*po ka*, Skt. *vokkāṇa*, A geographical location in this sūtra.

## volition
*mos pa*, Skt. *adhi­mukti*, Also translated here as “inclination,” “will,” and “intent.”

## volitional factors
*’du byed*, Skt. *saṃskāra*, Fourth of the five aggregates and the second of the twelve links of dependent origination. These are the formative factors, mental volitions, and other supporting factors that perpetuate future saṃsāric existence.

## vomiting and diarrhea
*gsud pa*, Skt. *viṣūcikā*, symptom of a cholera-like illness considered an impediment to ordination.

## vow
*sdom pa*, Skt. *saṃvara*, Restraint from unwholesome deeds, generally engendered by observance of the three levels of vows, i.e., the prātimokṣa and bodhisattva vows, and the tantric commitments (samaya).

## vow holder
*brtul zhugs can*, Skt. *vratin*, Indicating someone who has adopted a mode of religious conduct, often associated with a specific deity or maṇḍala. This type of commitment is usually time or practice specific.

## vow restoration
*gso sbyong*, Skt. *poṣadha*, A twice-monthly ceremony performed by monks, nuns, and novices in which the ordained confess and repair any transgressions, thereby purifying and restoring their vows.

## Vowed to ascetic discipline from youth
*gzhon nu’i brtul zhugs*, Skt. *kumāravrata*, May also refer to practitioners who deliberately act like children; see .

## vowels and consonants
*yi ge gnyis*, Skt. *svaravyañjana*, A dvandva compound signifying (in this text) linguistic expression in general and the basic components of the Sanskrit alphabet in particular.

## Voyager
*slong ldan*, Skt. *slong ldan*, Voyager (one who travels on a long journey), also the name of a captain; a former incarnation of the Buddha.

## Vāṣpa
*rlangs pa*, Skt. *bāṣpa, vāṣpa*, one of the Five Excellent Companions, with whom Siddhārtha Gautama practiced asceticism near the Nairañjanā River and who later heard the [Buddha](#buddha) first teach the Four Noble Truths at the Deer [Park](#park) in Sarnath.

## Vāpikātīra
*rdzing bu’i ’gram*, Skt. *vāpikātīra*, One of the auxiliary charnel grounds.

## Vīrā
Skt. *vīrā*, One of the female śrāvakas attending the delivery of the MMK.

## Vīra
*dpa’ ba*, Skt. *vīra*, A nāga king present in the assembly of the Buddha Śākyamuni.

## Vīrabāhu
*lag pa dpa’*, Skt. *vīrabāhu*, A yakṣa general.

## Vīradatta
*dpas sbyin*, Skt. *vīradatta*, A king.

## Vīramatī
*dpal ldan ma*, Skt. *vīramatī*, One of the great yakṣiṇīs.

## Vīranandin
*dpal dgyes*, Skt. *vīranandin*, A tathāgata mentioned here as one of the thirty-five buddhas of confession.

## Vīrapravīṇa
*dpa’ mkhas*, Skt. *vīrapravīṇa*, A bodhisattva.

## Vīraśrī
*dpa’ bo dpal*, Skt. *vīraśrī*, A householder in this sūtra.

## Vārāṇasī
*wA rA Na sI*, Skt. *vārāṇasī*, also known as Benares, one of the oldest cities of northeast India on the banks of the Ganges, in modern-day Uttar Pradesh. It was once the capital of the ancient kingdom of Kāśi, and in the [Buddha](#buddha)'s time it had been absorbed into the kingdom of Kośala. It was an important religious center, as well as a major city, even during the time of the [Buddha](#buddha). The name may derive from being where the Varuna and Assi rivers flow into the Ganges. It was on the outskirts of Vārāṇasī that the [Buddha](#buddha) first taught the [Dharma](#dharma), in the location known as Deer [Park](#park) (Mṛgadāva). For numerous episodes set in Vārāṇasī, including its kings, see The Hundred Deeds, Toh 340.

## Vīrasena
*dpa’ bo’i sde*, Skt. *vīrasena*, “Heroic Rank”; two different individuals in this sūtra: (1) a universal monarch of the past and (2) a bodhisattva disciple of King Who Transcends the Light of Mount Meru.

## Vratamaṇḍala

## Vratanidhi

*kyi hud zer ba*, Skt. *hāhārava*, Wailer (one who wails or laments), also the name of one of sixteen realms that surround the Crushing Hell. Literally, “Cries of Woe” or “Lamenting.”

## Wailing
*ngu ’bod*, Skt. *raurava*, Wailing (loud crying or lamentation), also the name of one of the great hells; see also .

## Wailing Hell
Name of one of the great hells (Skt. mahānaraka). The Tibetan translation reflects an interpretation of the source term containing the word -rava (“cry” and so forth). The Pali sources attest to two versions of the word: roruva and rorava. The Purāṇas explain Sanskrit raurava as a derivation of the word ruru. See also in the translation. One of the meanings of the Sanskrit word raurava is “dreadful” or “terrible.” Elsewhere translated as “Howling Hell.”

## Wailing Hell of Flames
One of the two Wailing Hells, it is filled with fire. Denizens of this hell experience red hot blazes of fire entering their orifices and burning them from the inside. This hell is described in the commentary on the Pali Saṃkiccajātaka (Jātaka no. 530).

## Wailing Hell of Smoke
One of the two Wailing Hells, it is filled with hot caustic fumes. Denizens of this hell experience these fumes entering their orifices and boiling them from the inside. This hell is described in the commentary on the Pali Saṃkiccajātaka (Jātaka no. 530), the Saṃkiccajātakavaṇṇanā.

## wanderer
*kun tu rgyu ba*, Skt. *parivrājaka*, Pali paribbājaka. Refers to a class of Indian religious mendicants holding a variety of beliefs who wandered in India from ancient times, including during the time of the Buddha. These peripatetic ascetics, who included women in their number, engaged with one another in debate on a range of topics. Some of their metaphysical views are presented in the early Buddhist discourses of the Pali Canon.

## wandering
*kun tu rgyu ba*, Skt. *kun tu rgyu ba*, A class of gods associated with the Four Great Kings.

## wandering being
*rgyu ba*, Skt. *rgyu ba*, A class of nonhuman beings associated with misfortune and disease.

## wandering mendicant
*kun tu rgyu*, Skt. *parivrājaka*, a non-Buddhist religious mendicant who literally "roams around." Historically, they wandered in India from ancient times, including the time of the [Buddha](#buddha), and held a variety of beliefs, engaging with one another in debate on a range of topics. Some of their metaphysical [view](#view)s are presented in the early Buddhist discourses of the Pali Canon. They included women in their number.

## Wangchen Gönpo
Wangchen Gönpo was nominally the ninth Degé king although the actual political power was exercised by his elder brother, Sönam Phuntsok.

## Waning Light

## ward
*lhan gcig gnas pa*, Skt. *sārdhaṃvihārin*, For at least five years after ordination, monks and nuns must live with or near a monastic mentor or “support” (Tib. gnas; Skt. niśraya). Generally, the preceptor (Tib. mkhan po; Skt. upādhyāya) serves as the new monk or nun’s “support,” in which case the newly admitted monastic is called a “ward.” But if the mentored monastic wishes to travel while the mentor does not (or vice versa), the ward must take a new support from among the saṅgha elders. The new support is known as the “support instructor” (Tib. gnas kyi slob dpon; Skt. niśrayācārya) while the new monk or nun is known as their “apprentice” (Tib. nye gnas; Skt. antevāsika). See The Chapter on Going Forth (Toh 1, ch. 1, 1.628–1.678).

## wealthy noblemen
*tshong dpon bu*, Skt. *śreṣṭiputra*, The term śreṣṭhin and its Pāli equivalent seṭṭi have undergone a particular development in Buddhism. The Tibetan translation “merchant” or “owner of merchandise” (tshong dpon) reflects that śreṣṭhin later came to be associated with traders, merchants, and also moneylenders. However, in Sanskrit the term literally means “distinguished,” and an older survey of the term shows that it implies a kind of nobleman of influential social standing who has both access to wealth and a close association with the king. For a more detailed history on the development of this term, see Chakravarti (1996), chapter 3, particularly pp. 73–79.

## well disposed
*dang ba*, Skt. *prasāda*, From the root sīd (to “sit” or “settle”), this term is connected to a metaphor of water settling down and becoming clear, and thus prasāda can often mean “clarity” in the physical sense. This is contrasted with kaluṣa (“turbidity”), which is also used in a metaphorical sense, in this case of looking unfavorably upon someone/something. When we translate it as “good disposition,” or “being well disposed,” it is in contexts where the term has meanings akin to faith and devotion, or generally looking upon someone/something else in a positive light.

## well-gone one
*bde bar gshegs pa*, Skt. *sugata*, One of the standard epithets of the buddhas. A recurrent explanation offers three different meanings for su- that are meant to show the special qualities of accomplishment of one’s own purpose (svārthasampat) for a complete buddha. Thus, the Sugata is “well” gone, as in the expression su-rūpa (“having a good form”); he is gone “in a way that he shall not come back,” as in the expression su-naṣṭa-jvara (“a fever that has utterly gone”); he has gone “without any remainder” as in the expression su-pūrṇa-ghaṭa (“a pot that is completely full”). According to Buddhaghosa, the term means that the way the Buddha went (Skt. gata) is good (Skt. su) and where he went (Skt. gata) is good (Skt. su).

## Western Continent
*ba lang spyod*, Skt. *aparāntaka*, The western continent of the human world according to traditional Indian cosmology, characterized as “rich in the resources of cattle.” It is named Aparāntaka (or sometimes Aparagodānīya or Aparagoyāna). It has a circular shape and is about 7,500 yojanas in circumference. Humans who live there are very tall, about 7.3 meters on average, and live for 500 years.

## western world system
*nub phyogs kyi ’jig rten gyi khams*, This likely refers to the world system of the Buddha Amitābha, Sukhāvatī. Hayagrīva, referred to here as the “King of Horses,” is a member of the lotus family and the wrathful emanation of the bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.

## what is free of intoxication

## Wheel
*'khor lo*, Skt, *cakra*, one of the centers of [energy](#energy) at different points on the [central channel](#central-channel), from which radiate the small subtle [channel](#channel)s going to all parts of the body. Generally there are considered to be four or five of these wheels.

## Wheel of Dharma
*chos kyi 'khor lo*, Skt. *dharmacakra*, the symbol of the [Buddha](#buddha)'s teaching. To turn the [wheel](#wheel) of the [Dharma](#dharma) [means](#means) to teach the [Dharma](#dharma). During his lifetime, the [Buddha](#buddha) gave three major series of teachings, which are referred to as the first, second, and third turnings.

*’khor lo ltar bsdus pa’i mdo*, Skt. *cakravatsamuccayasūtra*, This title only appears in The Hundred Deeds. It may be a shortened title for one of the various versions of the Dharmacakrapravartanasūtra .

## wheel-turning emperor
*’khor los sgyur ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *cakravartin*, A cakravartin is a king who rules over at least one continent, and gains his territory by the rolling of his magic wheel over the land. Therefore he is called a king with the revolving wheel. This is as the result of the merit he has accumulated in previous lifetimes.

## wheel-turning king
*’khor los sgyur ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *cakravartin*, An ideal monarch or emperor who, as the result of the merit accumulated in previous lifetimes, rules over a vast realm in accordance with the Dharma. Such a monarch is called a cakravartin because he bears a wheel (cakra) that rolls (vartana) across the earth, bringing all lands and kingdoms under his power. The cakravartin conquers his territory without causing harm, and his activity causes beings to enter the path of wholesome actions. According to Vasubandhu’s Abhidharmakośa, just as with the buddhas, only one cakravartin appears in a world system at any given time. They are likewise endowed with the thirty-two major marks of a great being (mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa), but a cakravartin’s marks are outshined by those of a buddha. They possess seven precious objects: the wheel, the elephant, the horse, the wish-fulfilling gem, the queen, the general, and the minister. An illustrative passage about the cakravartin and his possessions can be found in The Play in Full (Toh 95), 3.3–3.13.

## wheel-turning king of power
*stobs kyi ’khor los sgyur ba’i rgyal po*, Skt. *bala­cakravartin*, A kind of inferior wheel-turning king.

## wheel-turning monarch

## White Conch Protectress
*dkar mo dung skyong ma*, Skt. *dkar mo dung skyong ma*, A goddess who eventually becomes known as the Dharma protector Śrīdevī Mahākālī. Her parents are the goddess Umadevī and the god Mahādeva. She received her name by protecting a nāga called Conch Excrescence (dung gi mdzer ba can) from being killed by a garuḍa.

## white coral
*mu sa ra gal pa*, Skt. *musalagalva*, In other translations, this is translated into Tibetan as spug. White coral is fossilized coral that has undergone transformation under millions of years of underwater pressure. Tibetan tradition describes it being formed from ice over a long period of time. It can also refer to tridacna (Tridacnidae) shell, which is also presently referred to by the name musaragalva. Attempts to identify musalagalva have included sapphire, cat’s eye, red coral, conch, and amber. It appears in one version of the list of seven jewels or treasures.

## Wisdom Samantabhadrī
Samantabhadrī is usually the primordial female Buddha, consort of the primordial Buddha Samantabhadra. Her role in this text is somewhat confusing, however, because she seems here to be a type of malevolent spirit, which is very much in contradistinction to her usual role.

## wishless
*smon pa med pa*, Skt. *apraṇihita*, Emptiness (stong pa nyid), signlessness (mtshan ma med pa), and wishlessness (smon pa med pa) are known as the “three doors to deliverance” (triṇi­vimokṣa­mukhāni) or the “three concentrations” (trayaḥ samādhyaḥ) and as a set appear in both mainstream Buddhist sūtras and Mahāyāna sūtras. See Conze 1962, pp. 59–69; Lamotte 1944, pp. 1213–15; and Deleanu 2000, pp. 74–78.

## Wishless Ones
*smon pa med pa*, Skt. *smon pa med pa*, The collective name of five hundred future solitary buddhas.

## wishlessness
*smon pa med pa*, Skt. *apraṇihitatā*, Third of the Three Doors of Liberation (see glossary). Objectively, it is equivalent to voidness; subjectively, it is the outcome of the holy gnosis of voidness as the realization of the ultimate lack of anything to wish for, whether voidness itself, or even Buddhahood. See “emptiness.”

## wishlessness as a gateway to liberation
*rnam par thar pa’i sgo smon pa myed pa*, Skt. *apraṇihita­vimokṣa­mukha*, Third of the three gateways to liberation.

## witchcraft
*bon mo*, Skt. *bon mo*, The activity of a female sorcerer (bon). The term bon mo has been translated here as “witchcraft,” given that it is used to translate the Chinese shimu 師母 and does not refer to the pre-Buddhist religion of Tibet, despite the similarities they may share. For more on this translation choice, see Stein 2010, pp. 248–50.

## with a dustless and dust-free principle
*rdul med cing rdul dang bral ba’i tshul dang ldan pa*, Skt. *arajī­virajonaya­yukta*, A meditative stability.

## with outflows
*zag pa dang bcas pa*, Skt. *sāsrava*, See Edgerton 1953, p. 102.

## without a self
*bdag med*, Skt. *ātmāsadbhūtatva*, Selflessness denotes the lack of inherent existence in persons and also, more subtly, in all physical and mental phenomena. Also translated here as “nonself.”

## without apprehending anything
*mi dmigs pa’i tshul du*, Skt. *anupalambha­yogena*, The expression “without apprehending anything” suggests that bodhisattva great beings should teach without perceiving anything as inherently existing. Lamotte, The Treatise on the Great Virtue of Wisdom, vol. IV, p. 1763, note 564, renders this term as “by a method of non perceiving.”

## without attachment or impediment
*chags pa dang thogs pa med pa*, A meditative stability.

*rgyal mtshan bral*, Skt. *rgyal mtshan bral*, Buddha in the presence of whom the buddha Vaidya (34) first gave rise to the mind of awakening.

*sprin med*, Skt. *anabharaka*, First of three heavens of gods on the fourth concentration level.

## without clumsiness
*’khrul pa myi mnga’*, Skt. *nāsti skhalitam*, First of the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas.

*kha dog med*, Skt. *kha dog med*, A buddha realm.

*khengs med*, Skt. *khengs med*, Son of the buddha Abhyudgata.

*spros med*, Skt. *spros med*, Also translated here as “absence of conceptual elaborations.”

*’du shes sna tshogs myi mnga’*, Skt. *nāsti nānātvasaṃjñā*, Fourth or fifth (depending on the list) of the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas.

*chos kyi rang bzhin the tsom med pa*, The name of a bodhisattva.

## without false memories
*dgongs pa nyams pa myi mnga’*, Skt. *nāsti muṣitasmṛtitā*, Third of the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas.

*’jigs pa med pa*, Skt. *[vivṛta]*, The 48th meditative stability in chapter 6. The translation here follows the Tibetan; in the Sanskrit texts, this meditative stability is vivṛta, “uncovered.”

## Without Fighting
*thab bral*, Skt. *Yama*, name of a god [realm](#realm) of the World of Desire, so called because it is high enough for the [gods](#gods) there not to have to fight with the [demigods](#demigod). See [three worlds](#three-worlds).

## Without Fixation
*’dzin med*, Skt. *’dzin med*, A householder in this sūtra.

*bar chad med pa’i ting nge ’dzin*, Skt. *ānantarya­samādhi*, A meditative stability.

## Without Pretense
*tshul mi ’chos pa*, Skt. *tshul mi ’chos pa*, Attendant of the buddha Arhadyaśas.

## Without Reference
*dmigs med*, Skt. *nirālambana*, A bodhisattva who comes from the buddha field called Joy (dga’ spu) far to the west of Jambudvīpa and incarnates as a child in the household of a merchant in Vārāṇasī. The name refers to ultimate reality, meaning “Without Objectifying Perception” or “Without Reference Points.”

## without settled focus
*gnas su bya ba med pa*, Skt. *niradhiṣṭhāna*, The 87th meditative stability in chapters 6 and 8.

## without signs
*mtshan ma med pa*, Skt. *animitta*, Emptiness (stong pa nyid), signlessness (mtshan ma med pa), and wishlessness (smon pa med pa) are known as the “three doors to deliverance” (triṇi­vimokṣa­mukhāni) or the “three concentrations” (trayaḥ samādhyaḥ) and as a set appear in both mainstream Buddhist sūtras and Mahāyāna sūtras. See Conze 1962, pp. 59–69; Lamotte 1944, pp. 1213–15; and Deleanu 2000, pp. 74–78.

## Without Suffering
*mya ngan bral*, Skt. *mya ngan bral*, Attendant of the buddha Guṇaskandha.

*so sor ma brtags pa’i btang snyoms med pa*, Skt. *a­prati­saṃkhyāyopeksā*, Sixth of the eighteen distinct qualities of the buddhas. Also rendered here as as “without indifference that does not make distinctions.”
